body:
## Release v0.14.0

User chose a minor release from main, including merged PRs #130 (test-registry isolation), #131 (pre-compaction checkpoints), and #132 (private per-step routing, quiet notices, containment repair, coverage).

### Release preparation
- Cargo package and lockfile version 0.14.0; no dependencies changed.
- Add dated changelog and release notes with accurate feature costs, limits, separate installation paths, reload and rollback guidance.
- Update alone refreshes managed LGTM hooks; it does not install/refresh the separate checkpoint extension. Jev auto remains a manual two-file personal extension.

### Prevent the recurring macOS notice-test failure
Main's macOS job initially failed the real-notice producer: a single script shared a 60-second watchdog across unrelated scenarios. The parent retried that failed job once; it passed, but a passing rerun is not treated as the repair.

This patch runs all seven named scenarios in fresh processes and temporary projects. Each retains the existing 60-second fixture watchdog, 75-second Rust supervisor, and 12-second synchronous subprocess limits. Denial cases first prove the eligible notice path works, including classifier participation, silent presentation and scanner revalidation. All prior hard/private/mixed/custom/capability/review-warning and no-confirmation assertions remain. Failures name the scenario and child exit status. No production timeout or security gate changes.

### Verification
- `cargo test --locked --all-targets --all-features`: **1,206 passed** under isolated HOME and build directory; outer HOME registry entries **0**.
- Formatting, strict all-target/all-feature Clippy and locked build passed; candidate reports `lgtm 0.14.0`.
- All seven real notice scenarios passed locally.
- Execution coverage passed: **97.82% lines / 87.88% branches**, covering Jev and checkpoint JavaScript/TypeScript, not whole-Rust coverage.
- Authoritative published v0.13.1 binary/archive checksum verified. Initialized project/global hooks with it, replaced the binary at the same temporary executable path, and refreshed with the candidate: both hooks upgraded and exact initial backups were retained when absent.
- Fresh independent Sol 6.1 high and Astra high reviews: no blockers. Only the UTC publication date was corrected after review.
- Rust, Biome and TypeScript LSP clean. No Markdown/TOML/lockfile LSP configured.

### Security / limits / rollback
No new provider calls were made. No paid replay or full native UI conformance is claimed. Hard findings and command requirements remain deterministic. Timeouts still bound each scenario; forced process termination can retain its temporary fixture directory, a pre-existing cleanup limitation. More fixture initialization may increase total integration runtime.

Notes explain model cost, redaction limits, backup non-rotation, nontransactional refresh, manual Jev setup and rollback to v0.13.1. No live binary or user hook was changed. User checkout and local edits are preserved.

The owner approved one local commit-gate exception after runtime diagnostics blocked the ordinary commit; hook settings remain unchanged. This PR must pass all CI, including the repaired macOS integration, before merge. Then tag the checked merge commit as v0.14.0 and let the existing release workflow build, test, checksum and publish assets.

author: mikemcdougall
body:
Refs #688 (canonical source-pinned MCP consumer and exact-candidate render proof remain).
Refs #652 (broader promise audit and qualification remain).

## Summary

The installed MCP render oracle could accept a PNG with a bad CRC, missing IEND, invalid scanline filter or excess decompressed data. It now checks bounded PNG framing, CRCs and pixel-bearing chunks, requires `image/png`, and judges painted and transparent pixels against independently authored geographic samples.

## Changes Made

- Move the PNG decoder and map-render assertion into a pure release-owned module that canonical client producers can pin by protected source revision.
- Reject malformed chunk order, CRC, IEND/data after IEND, critical chunks, palette/transparency, dimensions, zlib length and filter modes with typed reasons.
- Keep the genuine `seed_sql`/`publish_harness` area-layer path, installed proxy request and existing raw-result/global-gate behavior; use the strict decoder for raster tiles too.
- Add positive and typed negative controls for media, shifted/blank/solid images, malformed containers and bounded inflate, plus authored multirow grayscale/RGB/RGBA filter vectors and a documented consumer contract. Follow [PNG Third Edition](https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/#11IDAT) for permitted final-IDAT padding and masked 8-bit transparency keys.

Ancillary metadata is CRC-checked and ignored when it does not affect image samples, as allowed by [PNG Third Edition §13.2](https://www.w3.org/TR/png-3/#13Error-checking); this helper does not claim full PNG metadata conformance.

## Breaking Changes

Malformed PNGs and missing or incorrect media types now fail the render step.

## Gate Impact

- [x] Strengthens the installed-client MCP/interop oracle without changing governed rows, candidate pins or gate policy.

author: jox36
body:
## Novedades
- **Se acabaron los cierres por memoria llena en el TV Box**: la app ahora lee los catálogos grandes (canales, películas, series) poco a poco mientras llegan, y no todos de golpe.
  - **Buscador universal**: los catálogos de tus otros servidores se preparan de a uno.
  - **En TV Box con poca memoria**: esos catálogos solo se cargan cuando abres el buscador, no al encender la app.
  - **Más memoria**: la app pide a Android más memoria cuando el equipo lo permite.
- **El audio avanzado (FFmpeg) ya no se apaga por error**: si la app se cierra por otra causa, como la memoria, el audio avanzado sigue activo.

## Detalles técnicos
- Causa: `OutOfMemoryError` en el hilo de OkHttp, con un heap de 256 MB. Se juntaban varias cosas:
  - `XtreamApi.array()` hacía `body.string()` y luego `JSONArray`, así que tenía en memoria el texto completo (UTF-16) más todos los objetos JSON.
  - Al arrancar, `ServerHub.ensureIndexes()` descargaba en paralelo canales, películas y series de cada otro servidor, y `TvRepo.searchIndex()` hacía lo mismo con el actual.
- Arreglos:
  - `streamList()` usa `android.util.JsonReader` sobre `byteStream()`, guarda solo los campos usados y salta el resto. Lo usan `channels()`, `movies()` y `series()`.
  - `ServerHub` usa un `Mutex` de cola, así que carga los catálogos uno por uno y cada lista en serie. `TvRepo.searchIndex()` también va en serie, con su propio `Mutex` para no armarse dos veces.
  - `ServerHub.lowMemory()` detecta `isLowRamDevice` o `memoryClass` de 256 MB o menos; en esos equipos no hay precarga al iniciar.
  - Se agregó `android:largeHeap="true"` y la caché de imágenes en la TV baja del 20 % al 12 % del heap.
  - `App`: un cierre con traza Java que no menciona ffmpeg ahora borra la marca de "arrancando" (`PlayerSafety.clearStarting`), así no se desactiva FFmpeg al reabrir.

author: kimseungcheol4589
body:
## 개요

**종료·정지된 인스턴스와 이미 한 번 줄인 인스턴스가 다운사이징 후보로 서지 않게 합니다.** `evaluate_ec2` 가 상태를 보지 않아, 종료된 인스턴스가 CloudWatch 에 남은 지난 지표(14일 창)로 `COST_CANDIDATE` 가 되고 승인 버튼까지 열렸습니다. 같은 함수가 다운사이징 이력도 보지 않아, 줄인 인스턴스가 창에 남은 옛 타입의 낮은 CPU 로 다시 후보가 되어 스캔마다 1/4 씩 내려갈 수 있었습니다(#434 5-2). 이슈의 「정해야 할 것」 ⓐ–ⓔ 는 아래처럼 정했고, ⓕ 는 이슈에 적은 대로 범위에서 뺐습니다.

**리뷰 요청**: @SehyeokKim — 코드 리뷰·브랜치 관리 담당이고, FE 라벨 질문이 하나 있습니다(아래 「리뷰 확인 항목」 2번). `SKIP_LOW_UTIL` 이 화면에 어떻게 보이는지가 이 변경의 사용자 쪽 결과입니다.
**리뷰 요청**: @DanzzaN-il — `packages/schemas/api/assets.py` 의 `SkipReasonCode` 주석을 고쳤고(enum 값은 그대로), 담당 파일 `ai/evaluation/cases.py` 의 `evaluate_ec2` 호출에 골든의 `state` 를 넘기도록 한 줄 바꿨습니다. 평가 케이스가 「rule_engine 과 정답지가 같은가」를 세우는 자리라 실제 상태를 넘겨야 그 대조가 실제 경로와 같습니다.

## 변경 사항

**결정**

| | 정한 것 | 이유 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ⓐ 어떤 상태를 거르나 | **`running` 만 판정**한다. `pending`·`stopping`·`stopped`·`shutting-down`·`terminated`·미상은 보류 | 종료 계열은 대상이 사라지는 중이다. 정지 계열은 RIGHTSIZING 실행이 정지 → 타입 변경 → **기동** 순서라 꺼 둔 인스턴스를 켜 버리고, 정지 구간은 관측치가 비어 정지 자체가 저활성으로 읽힌다 |
| ⓑ 사유 코드 | **`SKIP_UNSUPPORTED_STATE` 재사용** — EBS 와 같은 보류 코드 | enum 을 늘리지 않아 FE↔BE 계약이 바뀌지 않는다. 「EBS 전용」으로 적힌 주석만 「EBS·EC2」로 고쳤다 |
| ⓒ 어디서 거르나 | **판정 단계** — 자산 목록에는 그대로 남는다 | 수집에서 빼면 「거른 것」과 「AWS 응답에서 사라진 것」(`absent_since`)이 같은 칸이 된다 |
| ⓓⓔ 연쇄 하강 | **한 번만 줄인다** — 이미 줄인 인스턴스는 저활성이어도 `SKIP_LOW_UTIL`(다운사이징 부적합) | 누적 하강이 1회분(1/4)에서 멈춰 1/8 하한을 자동으로 지킨다. 수집 창·`rightsizing_policy` 는 건드리지 않는다 |

**「이미 줄였다」의 기준 — RIGHTSIZING 실행 중 `FAILED` 만 뺀 전부.** 원복(REVERT_SIZE)이 끝나면 원본이 `ROLLED_BACK` 으로 닫히므로(`workflows._ORIGIN_STATUS_AFTER_ROLLBACK`), `SUCCESS` 만 보면 되돌린 인스턴스가 다시 후보가 되어 같은 제안 → 원복이 반복됩니다. `ROLLBACK_INITIATED`·`ROLLBACK_FAILED`·`UNVERIFIED`(바뀌었을 수 있음)·`IN_PROGRESS`(바꾸는 중)도 같은 이유로 넣었습니다. `FAILED` 는 크기를 바꾸지 못하고 끝난 것이라 다시 제안해도 연쇄가 아닙니다.

**코드**

- `services/rule_engine.py` — `evaluate_ec2(..., *, state, already_rightsized=False)`. **`state` 는 기본값 없는 키워드 인자**입니다 — 기본값을 `running` 으로 두면 호출부가 상태를 빠뜨려도 조용히 판정됩니다. 상태 검사는 관측치·운영 보호보다 앞입니다(판정 대상이 아니면 다른 사유를 내지 않는다). `run_rule_engine` 은 실행 기록에서 이미 줄인 ARN 을 한 번 조회해 넘깁니다(`_rightsized_instance_arns`)
- 호출부 5곳이 실제 `state` 를 넘깁니다 — `run_rule_engine` · `ai/evaluation/cases.py` · `tests/test_golden_dataset.py` · `ai/tests/test_evaluation_cases.py` · `services/tests/test_seed_dataset_verdicts.py`(시드는 전부 `running`). **골든 EC2 14건이 전부 `running` 이라 정답지는 바뀌지 않습니다**
- 주석 — `packages/schemas/api/assets.py`(`SkipReasonCode`) · `apps/web/src/lib/enum-labels.ts`(라벨 문구는 그대로) · `rule_engine.SkipReason`

**테스트**

| 수용 기준 | 고정한 테스트 |
| --- | --- |
| 종료·종료 중이 후보가 아니다 | `test_non_running_state_is_not_a_candidate`(7상태 · 관측치 300 · 평균 1.0 — running 이면 후보가 되는 조합) |
| 사유 코드·주석이 맞는다 | 같은 테스트 + 주석 3곳 |
| `stopped`·`stopping` 처분과 이유 | 같은 테스트 + `evaluate_ec2` docstring |
| 회귀 — 48개 이상 · 5.0 미만 · 종료 | `test_non_running_ec2_stays_listed_but_is_not_a_candidate`(DB · 3상태) |
| 목록에서는 보인다 | 같은 테스트 — `list_assets` 포함 · `absent_since` 없음 |
| `evaluate_ebs` 와 기준이 갈리지 않는다 | `test_ec2_and_ebs_share_the_hold_code` |
| 줄인 인스턴스가 다음 스캔에 다시 후보가 되지 않는다 | `test_rightsized_instance_is_not_a_candidate_on_next_scan`(DB · `SUCCESS`·`ROLLED_BACK` → 보류 / `FAILED` → 후보) |
| 누적 1/8 아래로 내려가지 않는다 | 같은 테스트 — 두 번째 후보가 서지 않으므로 누적은 1회분(1/4)이다 |

**뮤테이션 5종이 전부 걸립니다** — 상태 검사 제거(12 실패) · 이미 줄인 집합 비움(2) · `SUCCESS` 만 봄(1) · `FAILED` 도 포함(1) · 호출부가 `state` 대신 `"running"` 을 넘김(3).

**하지 않은 것**

- **ⓕ 48개 게이트의 분포 검사** — 이슈에 「AWS 가 실패 쿼리에 일부 값을 주는지 선행 확인이 안 되면 범위에서 뺀다」로 적어 둔 그대로입니다
- **SSOT** `docs/PROJECT_STATUS.md` 241행이 `SKIP_UNSUPPORTED_STATE` 를 「EBS 가 `available`·`in-use` 외」로만 적습니다. PM 갱신 몫이라 이 PR 에서 고치지 않았습니다 — 다음 SSOT 갱신 때 「· EC2 는 `running` 외(#453)」를 더해 주세요
- 가드레일 ④ 의 대상 존재 검사(ADR-0006 이월 8행)는 **다른 층의 방어**라 이 PR 범위가 아닙니다
- `test_persistence_pipeline.py` 의 `import os` 미사용(ruff F401)은 `dev` 에도 있던 것이라 그대로 뒀습니다

**리뷰 확인 항목**

1. **「이미 줄였다」를 `FAILED` 제외 전부로 넓힌 것**이 맞는지 — 특히 `ROLLED_BACK` 을 넣은 이유(원복 루프)에 이견이 있으면 말씀해 주세요. 반대 안은 「`SUCCESS` 만」이고, 그러면 되돌린 인스턴스가 다음 스캔에 다시 후보가 됩니다.
2. **(FE)** `SKIP_LOW_UTIL` 의 화면 라벨이 「저사용 임계 미달」(`enum-labels.ts` 105)인데, 백엔드의 뜻은 원래부터 「다운사이징 부적합 — 스파이크 등」입니다. 이 PR 로 「이미 한 번 줄인 인스턴스」도 이 코드가 되니, 라벨을 「다운사이징 부적합」 쪽으로 바꿀지 봐 주세요. 이 PR 에서는 문구를 건드리지 않았습니다.

## 테스트

- [x] `pytest` 통과 — Docker(`db`·`localstack`) + `scripts/seed_localstack.py` 뒤 CI 와 같은 경로로 **3794 passed / 0 skipped / 0 failed**. 이 PR 이 추가·수정한 테스트 파일의 skip 0
- [x] `docker-compose up`으로 로컬 기동 확인 — (해당 없음) 판정 함수·테스트 변경이고 기동 구성은 바뀌지 않음. DB·LocalStack 은 위 pytest 를 위해 띄웠다
- [x] (`apps/web` 변경 시) `npm run lint` · `npm run build` · `npm test` 통과 — (해당 없음) `enum-labels.ts` 주석 한 줄이고 코드·라벨 문구 변경 없음. CI `web` 잡이 확인한다
- [x] (API 변경 시) FE↔BE 계약 동기화 확인(`packages/schemas/api/` ↔ `apps/web/src/types/api.ts`) — (해당 없음) `SkipReasonCode` enum 값 불변 · 주석만 변경

author: kwitsch
body:
## Summary

Performance pass over `universal-format` (→ 0.18.0), driven by measurements against the committed bundle and validated with a headless Claude Code 2.1.303 session, followed by a `/simplify` pass and a `/taskflow:changes-audit --fix` pass (26 candidates, 22 verified, 4 refuted; 10 applied by the fix-applier, 2 more applied by hand, 2 skipped — see below). Three performance changes, four bug fixes:

- **Lazy, per-language bundled plugins** (`prettier.ts`): the java/php/shell prettier plugins are now memoized dynamic imports that `bun build` keeps behind lazy init wrappers. java/php/shell load their own plugin; Markdown and every host prettier embeds Markdown in (JS/TS `md` tagged templates, HTML `<script type="text/markdown">`, Vue `lang="markdown"` blocks) load all three so fenced blocks keep formatting (pinned by tests); JSON/YAML/CSS/SCSS/LESS/GraphQL load none. Server start no longer evaluates mvdan-sh's GopherJS runtime or kicks off java's wasm init.
- **Changed-lines Edit swap** (`handlers.ts`, `shrinkSwap`): the whole merged file is still formatted, but the Edit `updatedInput` now covers only the run of whole lines that differs, widened line by line until `applyEdit` (the in-process mirror of the Edit tool's contract) reproduces the formatted file, bounded at 32 widenings so repetitive text cannot go quadratic (worst case = the old whole-file swap). When the formatted file equals the pre-edit file (a format-only edit), the handler hands the Edit tool a deliberate no-op (`old_string == new_string`) plus a notice, so the file stays formatted instead of the raw edit landing. CRLF files are handled in LF space (the Edit tool matches LF-normalized content and writes CRLF back), fixing a pre-existing failure where every single-line Edit on a CRLF file was refused. Fuzzed on 132k string pairs.
- **Node compile cache in the launcher** (`bin/mjs-launch.sh`): the node branch exports `NODE_COMPILE_CACHE` as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}/node-compile-cache` when Claude Code has exported that variable (a user-set value wins; nothing is exported otherwise; fail-open, ignored by Node < 22.1). The plugin's persistent data dir is the repo convention for runtime state, so nothing is written outside the project. `server.ts` now exits 0 on SIGINT/SIGTERM — Claude Code stops MCP servers by signal, not stdin EOF, and node writes the compile cache only on a normal exit (the audit found it was never persisted before). The cache is process-wide (a project's prettier config and plugins land in it too, never pruned) — documented.
- **Fix: the bundle always reported version `0.0.0`.** `bun build --env` only rewrites the global `process.env.X`; `server.ts` imports `process` from `node:process`, so the inlining never matched. The server now reads `../.claude-plugin/plugin.json` relative to the bundle at startup (the manifest ships next to `mcp/` in every install), so there is no build-time version at all and a release bump needs no rebuild; `runtime-detect.test.mjs` asserts the startup line carries `plugin.json`'s version.
- **Fix: prettier-plugin-sh's `experimentalWasm: true` path never worked in the bundle.** sh-syntax's `package.json` lists `vendors/wasm_exec.js` as side-effectful but `lib/index.js` imports `vendors/wasm_exec.cjs`, so bun tree-shook the import that defines `globalThis.Go` and every wasm format failed with `Go is not defined` (silently, as `{}`). The shell loader now imports the exported subpath explicitly; `sh-syntax` is pinned as a root devDependency at the version prettier-plugin-sh resolves. New test formats a `.sh` file with such a config through the built bundle — the first test to reach the committed `main.wasm` sidecar (also verified from a relocated copy of `mcp/`).
- `build.mjs`: `containShSyntaxDirname` now locates bun's baked-in `var __dirname = "<build path>"` literal by VALUE (the script resolves `main.wasm` itself, so it knows the directory) and replaces it with an `import.meta.url` lookup through two import aliases it prepends to the body — no dependence on bun's statement shape or alias names; throws unless exactly one occurrence.

## Measurements

Harness: a JSON-RPC driver spawning the server, per language first-call + warm p50/p95 over 20 calls (speed is read from the **second** format of a type onward, so lazy loading does not distort it), node 24.22 / bun 1.3.14, this WSL2 box. Baseline = `main`'s committed bundle.

**node 24.22** (`main` → this branch): server start **308 ms → 188 ms**, RSS after start **107 MB → 97 MB**.

author: lucasmatuszewski
body:
## What

A new public skill, `web-performance-audit`. It measures a live page with the Chrome DevTools CLI/MCP and Lighthouse, then writes two reports to `docs/<site>-performance/`:

- `report.md`: written for coding agents
- `report.html`: an interactive report for reviewers

Contents:

- `SKILL.md`: the workflow, the rules that keep the numbers honest, and the output contract (always `docs/`, `raw/` git-ignored)
- `references/setup.md`: CLI, MCP and upstream skills install; attaching to the user's Chrome with `--autoConnect`; pnpm PATH and consent-prompt pitfalls
- `references/methodology.md`:
  - the run matrix and emulation presets
  - recreating the consent state in an isolated context
  - verifying an LCP root cause, INP per interaction, memory
  - common pitfalls
- `references/report-structure.md`: the 11-section report and writing rules
- `scripts/`:
  - `run-lighthouse.mjs`: sequential runs per form factor
  - `summarize-lighthouse.mjs`: medians and ranges, failing audits, main thread, third parties, LCP subparts
  - `render-html-report.mjs`: report-data.json to self-contained HTML
  - `lcp-candidates.init.js`: LCP candidate logger for root-cause checks
- `assets/`: report CSS, client chart code, and a synthetic `report-data.example.json` (schema reference and test fixture)
- `tests/web-performance-audit.test.cjs`:
  - summarizer medians and first/third-party split
  - runner argument validation
  - renderer sections, escaping/XSS, `</script>`-safe JSON, `[hidden]` rule, no controls inside `<summary>`, optional sections

The upstream ChromeDevTools skills are installed from their source and not copied here.

## Why

Built from a real production-site audit. The lessons that shaped the skill:

- **The MCP `lighthouse_audit` tool excludes the Performance category**, so the score comes from the Lighthouse CLI.
- **Browser extensions polluted the real-profile traces.** They used about 8.7 s of CPU at 4x slowdown, so the skill measures in isolated contexts instead.
- **A plausible LCP hypothesis turned out to be wrong.** A slider looked like it was gating the image; it was main-thread contention. The skill now requires a verification step before recommending a fix.
- **Hand-writing the HTML report was the most expensive step and shipped three bugs.** The renderer replaces it.

## Checks

- `npm test`: 117/117 locally, including the 5 new tests.
- Manual trial: rendered the example report and checked it in headless Chrome (desktop 1280 px and phone 390 px):
  - no console errors
  - all 8 tabs switch
  - charts and tooltips render
  - no horizontal page scroll
- Reviewers: please check the public wording and that nothing client- or machine-specific remains (`grep` found none).

author: h1994st
body:
## Problem

When `load::read_module` cannot find a module on the production load path (`load_catalog` → `session_from_loaded`), the module is meant to be recorded as failed rather than abort the session, and no test covers that branch.

## Cause

The existing test for that window rewrites the module, which only reaches the hash-mismatch error and never the read error.

## Fix

- Add `a_module_deleted_after_verification_is_failed_not_fatal`: it deletes the module after `load_catalog` (reusing `write_catalog_with_one_module`). It then asserts that the session still builds, that the module is `Failed` with the OS not-found message, and that an answer reports `failed: 1, analyzed: 0`.

## Verification

- Fails if the branch propagates the error (`unwrap` on `Io(NotFound)`) or drops the failure record (status stays `Verified`).
- `cargo test -p rllvm-query`, `cargo clippy -p rllvm-query --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy -p rllvm-core -p rllvm --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`

author: steipete
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory-session adapters copy registration inputs, reset entries, fork inputs, and participant snapshots a second time even though their actor owner already provides isolation. These extra deep copies do no useful work.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Memory-session adapters retain input and snapshot isolation with fewer deep copies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove five immediate caller copies before `actor.storage.mutate`, whose executor synchronously captures the complete mutation before admission callbacks or queuing. Return the participant array from the already deep-cloned memory snapshot directly. The durable branches, callback-facing copies, reset compare-and-swap expectation, and live authority checks remain unchanged.

Production: +5/-12 lines, net -7 across four files; six deep-copy operations removed. No SQL statement, worker request, transaction envelope, schema, public API, or PostgreSQL bookkeeping changes. SQL/request/MAIN delta is estimated, unmeasured 0/0/0. No latency claim.

<details>
<summary>Candidate ledger</summary>

| Candidates | Decision and reason |
| --- | --- |
| C16300, C16301 | REMOVE: registration identities and query are synchronously captured by the mutation executor. |
| C16396 | REMOVE: the reset entry immediately enters that same executor capture. |
| C17757, C17758 | REMOVE: fork data and patch immediately enter that same executor capture. |
| C16804 | REMOVE: the memory actor snapshot already deep-clones participants. |
| C16299, C16303, C16304, C16308 | KEEP: caller-owned durable inputs must survive asynchronous worker admission. |
| C16302 | KEEP: the eligibility callback must not receive mutable owner records. |
| C16307 | KEEP: synchronous authority callbacks run before selection and can mutate the caller-owned query. |
| C16395 | KEEP: a mutating reset builder must not alter the compare-and-swap expectation. |
| C16397 | KEEP: the callback receives the same immutable environment contract as the durable lifecycle path. |

14 inventory candidates reviewed: 6 removed, 8 kept, all category f.
</details>

## Evidence

Existing production-path memory suites cover registration eligibility and private returned records, intervening reset writes and a mutating builder, patched parent forks, and participant reads. No test assertion is weakened. The actor's sole request capture and snapshot copy remain in their original owners.

The simplify pass retains only the six duplicate copies. One independent Codex review completed with no actionable P0–P2 findings, with full capture, snapshot, storage-consumer and existing test context. Focused formatting, lint, and `git diff --check` pass. Exact-head CI [39185955670](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185955670) passes all type, lint, source-contract, architecture/Madge, T1, dialect and worker-ratchet checks. All three PostgreSQL conformance shards pass. The ordinary run finished with 78 successful checks, 26 skipped checks, and three failing test groups plus their aggregate gate. Knip [117848875212](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185961436/job/117848875212) reports zero new findings: all eight distinct symbols across production/full scans match main [117846593700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39185301352/job/117846593700). The frozen dependency install passed after SSD clearance; dependency inputs match the previous successful install. Under the campaign WAVE-28 SSD-stall policy, the warm pair is deferred to the combined census; all counts above remain estimated and unmeasured.

CI failure attribution: the chat MAIN-count failures match main run 39176649118/jobs 117820741687 and 117820741767; recovery borrower cleanup matches main 39172446197/job 117808338765; the session-row-delta timeout and resource cleanup match main 39176649118/job 117820741627. Candidate jobs are 117848939466, 117848939406 and 117848939582 respectively.

The archive-lifecycle drain-start ordering failure (job 117848939466, assertion at line 680) reproduces on the unchanged base `8cd41d4d3e7832ba19b812b6bb046e6acc19cbf6` with the same reversed order. The focused default-Bun run executed the exact failing case and reported one failed test after worker preparation; this is a behavioral result, not a setup failure. The owner prepares targets concurrently, while the test separately checks release order later. Exact-head CI supplies the matching candidate failure; the redundant local candidate replay was cancelled during setup after the baseline result. All test processes have stopped and the candidate checkout is clean. No assertions were changed. The queued remote alternative never executed a test, and its lease/workflow are stopped; the supplemental workflow was cancelled after Knip completed. Optional supplemental UI/plugin failures are not represented as passing.

```
Author: Ylarod <me@ylarod.cn>
Date:   Mon Oct 19 10:19:27 2026 +0800
```

Blocking a module through the native `module_blacklist` (https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU/pull/3881) makes it
fail with `EPERM`. First stage init treats that as fatal for anything in
`modules.load` / `modules.load.recovery` that is not in
`modules.blocklist`, so blocking the wrong module bootloops the device
or breaks recovery (MediaTek `mkp` in https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU/pull/3883, `oplus_secure_guard_new` in https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU/pull/3908).
Install screen users cannot be expected to know which modules
are safe to block, and both proposed mitigations (https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU/pull/3908, https://github.com/tiann/KernelSU/pull/3889) only
cover part of the problem.

- Manager: remove the "Block kernel modules" option, its pre-fill from
`/proc/modules` and the `--block-module` flag from the install screen
(Material + Miuix), plus the strings (en / zh-rCN / in).
- ksud: keep `boot-patch --block-module`, mark it as developer only in
the help text and document the first stage risk.
- Kernel: unchanged apart from a comment; the blacklist is still
installed at init.

Developers who use it are responsible for choosing safe modules. Note
that `--block-module` clears the list when omitted, so re-patching from
the Manager drops a list set via the CLI.

- `./gradlew :app:compileDebugKotlin` passes.
- ksud `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo check` pass.

 -manager: drop block-modules UI -> Jetpack (Install.kt, Flash.kt)

body:
## Linked Issues or Issue Description

Production deploys are dispatched by hand while staging already has the canary and error-rate checks, and roughly a third of production deploys have failed. This change promotes a green staging commit to production with nobody dispatching it, and gates production on the same REST 5xx error-rate verdict staging runs, with automatic rollback on failure.

## What Changed

- `deploy-production` starts on a completed `deploy-staging` run on `main` plus a daily schedule backstop; it soaks 30 minutes past the staging-green time and skips green when the run is held, already live, or not green.
- The guard presets takeover on automatic runs and refuses rollback inputs there; every existing check (CI verdict, staging history, environment, schema and roles gates) still applies.
- The `production` job ends with the staging-parity error-rate gate over live production metrics; a failed gate auto-rolls back Worker version and container image.
- The gate script accepts a `--user-agent` override so production scrapes identify as the production rollout.

## Verification

- `python3 scripts/test-deploy-production.py`: 112 tests OK (includes 12 new automatic-promotion guard cases).
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/ci -p 'test_workflows.py'`: 54 tests OK (new production error-rate mirror pins plus mutation cases).
- `npm test --prefix wrangler`: 1061 tests pass, including 2 new user-agent gate tests.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean (no Rust changes).
- Not run: live staging drill and the forced error-rate rollback; those need operator dispatches after merge.

## Notes for reviewers

- Operator setup needed before live enforcement: `PRODUCTION_METRICS_SCRAPE_TOKEN` secret (else the gate records a skip) and optionally `PRODUCTION_AUTO_PROMOTE_HOLD_UNTIL`.
- Automatic runs need `PRODUCTION_AUTO_APPROVE=true` or Environment reviewers, same as manual dispatches.

## Summary by Sourcery

Promote verified staging releases to production automatically with soak, safety rechecks, live error-rate gating, and rollback protection.

New Features:
- Automatically promote the latest green staging commit to production after a 30-minute soak, with workflow completion and daily backstop triggers.
- Gate production promotion on live REST 5xx error rates and automatically roll back the Worker version and container image when the gate fails.
- Add a dispatch-only error-rate rollback drill and production-specific metrics user-agent support.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent automatic runs from deploying failed, held, already-live, stale, or older-than-live staging revisions.
- Prevent automatic promotions from competing with active operator recovery dispatches or deploying after cancellation.

Enhancements:
- Preserve existing CI, staging-history, schema, roles, environment approval, readiness, and rollback safeguards for automatic promotions.
- Add pre-deploy hold, live-revision, and operator-dispatch rechecks to fail closed before entering the production deployment lane.

CI:
- Extend workflow policy and deployment tests to cover automatic promotion, soak and recheck behavior, production error-rate gating, and rollback-drill safety.

Documentation:
- Document automatic promotion controls, operator holds, production error-rate enforcement, required secrets, and rollback-drill usage.

Tests:
- Add coverage for automatic promotion guard cases, workflow policy mutations, production error-rate gate bindings, user-agent overrides, and live scrape behavior.

body:
## 效能優化摘要

將多個 API 端點從秒級延遲優化至 200ms 以內。

## 根本原因與修改

### Fix 1: 移除 UserRepository.findById 的 \@EntityGraph\
- **問題**: \ indById\ 被 \@EntityGraph\ 覆寫，每次查單一 User 都強制 JOIN FETCH roles + role，\ indAllById\ 底層逐一呼叫導致 \ atch-query\ 耗時 10s
- **修改**: 移除覆寫；新增 \ indAllByIdsWithRoles\ 供批量場景使用
- **影響**: \GET /api/users/{id}\ 1.5s→~10ms，\POST /api/users/batch-query\ 10s→大幅改善

### Fix 2: UserDataAccessImpl.searchUsers 二次批量查詢
- **問題**: \ indAll(Specification, Pageable)\ 無預載 roles，\UserMapper.fillRoles\ 存取 \user.getRoles()\ 觸發 N+1 LazyLoad
- **修改**: 取得分頁結果後，以 ids 批量呼叫 \ indAllByIdsWithRoles\ 重建 Page
- **影響**: \GET /api/users/search\ 6.2s→~30ms

### Fix 3: RoleDataAccessImpl.searchRoles 二次批量查詢
- **問題**: 同上，\RoleMapper\ 存取 \ole.getRoleFunctions()\ 觸發 N+1
- **修改**: 新增 \ indAllByIdsWithFunctions\，\searchRoles\ 改為二次批量查詢
- **影響**: \GET /api/role/search\ 6.1s→~20ms

### Fix 4: FunctionQueryService.searchFunctions 改走快取記憶體篩選
- **問題**: 每次請求均查 DB，無快取利用
- **修改**: 改從 \getFunctionListCache()\（Redis \@Cacheable\）取全量資料，於記憶體做篩選、排序、分頁
- **影響**: \GET /api/function/search\ 6s→~5ms（暖快取）

### Fix 5: AquarkDataQueryService.getColumnNameList 改為靜態常數
- **問題**: 每次請求執行 3 次反射（含 \getFields()\），\getFields()\ 與 \getDeclaredFields()\ 重疊導致欄位名稱重複
- **修改**: 改為 \private static final List<String> COLUMN_NAMES = buildColumnNames()\，移除 \getFields()\ 迴圈
- **影響**: \GET /api/aquarkData/getColumnNameList\ 764ms→<1ms

### Fix 6: UserJobLinkRepository 移除 @EntityGraph + 二次批量查詢
- **問題**: \ indAll(Specification, Pageable)\ 帶 \@EntityGraph\ 導致 Hibernate HHH90003004 in-memory pagination
- **修改**: 移除 \@EntityGraph\ 覆寫；新增 \ indAllByIdsWithJobPosting\；\searchUserJobLinks\ 改為二次批量查詢
- **影響**: \GET /api/user-job-link/search\ 911ms→~50ms

body:
- Closes N/A. This is mechanical follow-up to #35083, which added the opt-in `jsonConfig` and opted in only `@packages/errors`.

### Additional details

Packages on the flat ESLint config haven’t been linting any JSON, even though most of their lint-staged globs include `.json`. This PR opts all of them in and tidies some `package.json` metadata while we’re in there.

**1. Opt every flat-config package into `jsonConfig`**
- **Configs:** all 15 packages on the flat config now spread `...jsonConfig` after `...baseConfig`. I dry-ran it on each one first: one `--fix` pass left no parse errors and no remaining violations.
- **Autofix:** the fixes only reorder each `package.json`’s top-level keys into `sort-package-json` order and add missing final newlines. I parsed every changed JSON file and compared it to the base: no values changed, and no `exports` map changed order.
- **`cli`:** it keeps ignoring its own `package.json`, since `sync-exported-npm-with-cli` rewrites its `exports` map. It now lints the rest of its JSON, such as `types/tslint.json`.
- **lint-staged:** `json` added to the globs for `@cypress/react`, `@cypress/svelte`, `@cypress/vue` and `@packages/electron`, the four that lacked it.
- **Migration guide:** the checklist now includes the opt-in, so packages that migrate later don’t skip JSON.

**2. Remove `contributors` arrays**
The hand-maintained lists in `@cypress/angular`, `@cypress/react` and `@cypress/vue` are removed. Nothing in the repo reads the field. The git history and GitHub’s contributor graph already record who contributed.

**3. Sharpen npm keywords**
npm search matches on keywords, and its `keywords:` filter matches whole terms, so these are about discoverability:
- **Component testing adapters:** `component-testing` plus the framework name and version. This replaces `component testing`, which has a space and can’t be matched by the filter.
- **Plugins:** `cypress-plugin`, the community’s tag for Cypress plugins.
- **Feature terms:** grep gets tags, filtering and burn. Puppeteer, which had no keywords, gets chromium and multi-tab. Schematic gets `angular-cli` and `ng-add`. The batteries-included preprocessor gets typescript and babel.
- **`@cypress/mount-utils`:** left without keywords, since it isn’t meant for direct use.

These use the `chore:` prefix, so the keyword and `contributors` changes reach npm with each package’s next release. No changelog entry is needed.

**What this means going forward:** the pre-commit hook now autofixes JSON layout and key order in all of these packages. JSON that can’t be autofixed (invalid syntax, duplicate keys, comments) blocks the commit. Anything that skips the hook fails `linux-lint`, which `all-jobs-passed` requires. Because this PR clears every existing violation, a red JSON lint check now points at the PR that introduced the problem.

**Known follow-ups, not in this PR:**
- **Root lint-staged:** the root `package.json` still has entries for `npm/react`, `npm/svelte` and `npm/vue` that leave out `json`. lint-staged 16 uses the closest config, so the package-level globs win and those root lines do nothing. They could be deleted.
- **Grep fixtures:** `npm/grep/cypress.config.ts` writes `expected-json/*.json` without a final newline when `OVERWRITE_EXPECTED` is set, so regenerated fixtures need a lint-staged pass on commit.

### Steps to test

1. `yarn lint` passes.
2. In any opted-in package, break a JSON file, for example by moving a dependency out of order or deleting the final newline, and run `yarn workspace <pkg> lint --fix`. It gets corrected.
3. Add a duplicate key to a `package.json` and try to commit. The pre-commit hook blocks it.

### How has the user experience changed?

No change for Cypress users. The published adapter and plugin packages get better npm keywords and lose their `contributors` lists on their next release.

### PR Tasks

- [na] Is there an associated issue with maintainer approval for PR submission? Mechanical follow-up to #35083.
- [na] Have tests been added/updated? This is lint config and JSON formatting only. `yarn lint` covers it.
- [na] Has a PR for user-facing changes been opened in [`cypress-documentation`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress-documentation)?
- [na] Have API changes been updated in the [`type definitions`](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/blob/develop/cli/types/cypress.d.ts)?

The original full browser run once closed Settings after editing Display name and immediately pressing Escape. The unchanged scenario subsequently passed, including a separate 10/10 baseline repeat. That intermittent failure is preserved as an observation, not presented as a deterministic causal trace.

Three new Profiler probes independently reproduced the guard-publication gap: the edited Display name, edited current password and saving form had committed while their dirty/busy callbacks still exposed the prior value. All three failed before the change and pass afterward. The probes observe child layout completion before passive effects; they do not inject dismissal into an unfinished render or wait for the old effect to settle.

[React's layout-effect guarantee](https://react.dev/reference/react/useLayoutEffect) makes the guard and its parent update complete before paint/another user event. The fix does not claim to make arbitrarily nested programmatic events inside an uncommitted batch synchronous, or prove the publication gap was the sole cause of the original intermittent failure.

## Verification

- 39 focused profile/proof/operation/routing component tests passed. Existing clean-revert, overlapping saves, failure draft retention, hidden proof-time completion, explicit discard, late receipt and account/session-isolation coverage remains intact.
- Full frontend gate passed: design tokens, typecheck, lint (zero errors; existing warnings retained), and 2,047 unit tests across 200 files.
- 31 existing Settings/composer/layout Chromium cases passed. The final 17-case account Settings suite also passed, including three new password scenarios at 375×812 light, 1440×900 dark and 812×375 dark with reduced motion, immediate Escape, Keep editing/focus restoration, unload protection and clean revert. These runs overlap and are not summed as unique cases.
- The complete fixed-source Chromium suite passed: 399 passed, zero failed, 17 conditional skips. This includes the real local signup/profile smoke; UI network fixtures are not represented as live backend coverage, and the separately opted-in lifecycle scenario remains the #766/#767 evidence below.
- Independently reviewed the source and commit-order probes; no actionable regression found. Mobile/landscape screenshots were visually checked. Changed-file secret scanning and diff checks passed; no new exception was introduced.
- An additional opt-in real account-security lifecycle test reached session revocation (both old sessions rejected; PAT retained) but then failed on its stale exact `Username` sign-in selector. The current form is labelled `Username or email`. That unchanged test is separately tracked in #766 and fixed by #767. Its complete real lifecycle scenario passed on that independent branch; it is not reported as passing on this product-fix branch or mixed into this diff.

## Delivery

Deploy the frontend after review/merge; this change requires no backend replacement or migration. No production system was accessed or modified. All browser work targeted local isolated endpoints/fixtures. All seven hosted checks passed on head `e267cf9d`, including the repository-runtime shell, live PostgreSQL, static/secret, backend unit, frontend mock, real Keycloak theme and image-build lanes.

author: ignaciohermosillacornejo
body:
# Summary

Closes #842. This is a v3.0 release blocker. `delete_transaction` refused a split parent only while the parent still had children. The #822 guard dropped its session record as soon as a freshly fetched row for the id came back, on the assumption that a split parent never reappears. That assumption is false. Once all of a parent's children are deleted, Copilot returns it as an ordinary row with no split marker, and deleting it still credits its amount back to the account a second time. Three changes close the gap:

1. **No evidence counts as negative any more.** The retirement branch is gone. A recorded split parent is refused for the life of the record, whatever the server returns for the id. The record is now a plain `Set`, because the window-cache generation stamp only existed to support retirement. The cheap path that refuses without any request is kept.
2. **Local-cache evidence from soft-deleted children.** Deleting a split child leaves its document in the desktop app's Firestore cache, with `user_deleted: true` and `parent_transaction_id` still set. `decodeAllCollections` now collects, in the same single pass, every id that any transaction document names as a parent (deleted documents included), plus the owners of a non-empty `children_transaction_ids`. The result is `AllCollectionsResult.splitParentIds`. The decode worker already returns `decodeAllCollections`' result, so it carries the new field with no worker change. No row is built from a deleted document. `CopilotDatabase.getSplitParentIds()` exposes the set, and `splitParentEvidence` checks it in **both** live and cache-only mode.
3. **Persisted split records.** Records are written to `split-parents.<uid>.jsonl` next to the routing-id index (`~/.claude/copilot-money/`). The new store follows `TransactionMetaStore`'s conventions: append-only JSONL keyed by the authenticated uid, the same `COPILOT_DISABLE_PERSISTENT_INDEX=1` opt-out, and failures that never fail the caller. Records are never retired, so the file never needs rewriting and the atomic-rewrite path is not needed. `CopilotMoneyServer` creates the store when `--write` is on and passes it in through a new `options` argument on `CopilotMoneyTools`. Tests pass a temp dir or nothing, so they never touch the real home directory. The directory is now one helper, `src/core/persistence/dir.ts`, which both stores use.

**Decode in live mode (design choice).** Before this change, live mode never triggered a LevelDB decode for this check. Now the first delete in a process decodes the local cache when no read has loaded it yet. That is the same cached batch decode every cache read uses: a few seconds, once per cache TTL, and free after that. Delete is rare and destructive, and after a restart the soft-deleted children are the only evidence of a split made in the app or by an earlier process, so the cost is worth paying here. An unreadable or absent cache still never blocks a delete (tested). The cost notes in the `deleteTransaction` and `splitParentEvidence` docblocks are updated.

Check order is now: record → cached child row → local cache → window fetch. A hit at any step refuses, and the window fetch only runs when nothing earlier refused.

Run against the real local cache (counts only, read-only): 3 ids are known as split parents only from soft-deleted children, and 1 of them decodes as an ordinary row. That one is the probe's childless ex-parent, which the old guard would have deleted.

The refusal no longer says "run refresh_cache … and retry". It now says the parent stays hidden while it has children, reappears as an ordinary transaction once they are all deleted, and still cannot be deleted safely. The `delete_transaction` and `split_transaction` descriptions say the same. The `delete_transaction` description is trimmed to stay within its context budget, so the budget is unchanged.

Docs:
- `docs/bugs/842-childless-split-parent-deletable.md` (post-mortem) and its index row
- the 822 post-mortem's forward reference
- the CHANGELOG entry
- `hidden-mutations.md`
- parity row W-23, which now expects the parent to reappear and adds a reconnect step
- the round-trip smoke's ledger marker

## External assumptions

Two new assumptions, both **probe transcript**: the live probe of 2026-10-18, recorded in #842's comment and not re-probed here. Both are filed `verified-once` in `src/conformance/ledger.ts`:

- `Transaction.parentId:childlessParentReappears`: GraphQL `Transaction` has no split marker (`hasSplitError` is false on parent, children and ex-parent). After its children are deleted, the ex-parent comes back as an ordinary row from both `transactions` and `transaction(id)`. This replaces `Transaction.parentId:childlessParentHidden` (unverified), which the probe refuted. There is no `refuted` class, so the old entry is replaced rather than reclassified, and its key survives only in the new entry's evidence text.
- `FirestoreTransaction.parent_transaction_id:survivesSoftDelete`: a deleted split child stays in the local cache with `user_deleted: true` and keeps `parent_transaction_id`.

Every `ledger:` marker that cited the old key (`src/tools/tools.ts`, `scripts/smoke/roundtrip-checks.ts`) now cites the new keys.

## Bug fix?

```text
Root cause:       splitParentEvidence treated a freshly fetched row for the id as proof it was no longer a split parent and retired the record, but Copilot's Transaction has no split marker and returns a childless ex-parent as an ordinary row, which still double-credits when deleted (an unverified ledger assumption deciding a destructive write).
Bug class:        aggregation-double-count (recurrence of #822's class: a write that makes Copilot's server count the same money twice across a parent/child hierarchy)
Detector added:   tests/unit/delete-split-parent.test.ts: the exact #842 sequence (split, both children deleted, fresh window returns the parent with parentId null → refused, nothing sent); a real-LevelDB fixture with soft-deleted children refusing the parent in live mode with an empty session (restart) and in cache-only mode; a restart test across two tool instances sharing a SplitParentStore. Four new mutation-guard rows, each passes unmutated / fails mutated under `bun run check:mutation-guards`: "a fresh row never retires a split record", "split-parent records survive a restart", "delete reads the local cache's split evidence in live mode", "soft-deleted split children still name their parent" (decoder: collecting only from decodable documents is detected). The existing "delete_transaction refuses a split parent" row now also names the #842 test.
Siblings checked: The smoke harness already leaves split parents behind (comment and ledger marker updated). Cache-only mode had no retirement but also could not see soft-deleted children (fixed by the same decoder evidence). Other write tools that accept a parent id (update_transaction amount/date, add_transaction_to_recurring, review_transactions, bulk_edit_transactions) are still unguarded, as in #822, because their server-side effect on a parent has not been observed. decoder-coverage, dedup-identity, parent-pointer-documents and `bun run smoke:cache` (11 pass, 2 skip, 0 fail on the real cache) still hold.
Ledger updated:   Transaction.parentId:childlessParentHidden (unverified) replaced by Transaction.parentId:childlessParentReappears (verified-once) and FirestoreTransaction.parent_transaction_id:survivesSoftDelete (verified-once); markers in src/tools/tools.ts and scripts/smoke/roundtrip-checks.ts updated.
```

`bun run check`: 3999 pass, 0 fail (4019 tests, 202 files, after five review rounds and the rebase onto #851). Mutation guards: 18 of 18 proved — 18 rows in the registry (counted with `MUTATION_GUARDS.length`), 8 of them new in this PR (four here, plus `split-parent evidence honours the cache TTL`, `local split evidence only accumulates`, `a login change re-reads split evidence` and `the split-evidence latch waits for the decode` f

author: mojeeq
body:
**Opened as a draft on purpose.** #242 and #243 both merged while the fix for a review finding on them was in flight - #243 by 42 seconds - so each time the finding's fix missed `main` and had to come back as a new PR. A draft cannot be merged, so this one can take its review pass without closing underneath it. I will mark it ready once it is green with nothing outstanding.

This is the fix for the P1 Codex raised on #243, which merged without it.

## What is wrong in `main` now

#243 made the script box follow a newer saved script while nobody has touched it, so a colleague's save cannot be silently overwritten. It decided "nobody has touched it" by asking whether the box matches the saved text, and that is the same question only when the box opened *on* the saved text.

It does not always. A project with nothing saved and a run on record opens on the run:

- the box holds the run, the saved text is empty, so they differ before anybody has touched a key;
- read as an edit, the box is the person's from that moment and ignores every later answer;
- so a script a colleague saves stays invisible, and **Save overwrites it** - the exact path #243 was for.

## The fix

The editor remembers what it last put in the box, and an edit is the box no longer holding that. Saving moves the marker, because what was kept is the box again rather than a draft. Deleting clears it. Typing and "Put it in the box" do not, because both are the person acting.

That also forced out a guard the old comparison had been doing by accident: **an untouched box is left alone when nothing has been saved since it was filled.** Without it, following would write the saved text over a recovered run on every refetch, and over a box somebody had deliberately cleared and saved. Removing the wrong comparison removed that protection too, so both had to land together.

Codex suggested either tracking edits or comparing against the last answer. It turns out both are needed, and they do different jobs.

## Saving does not write the box either (`0ea9c2a`)

Codex found that the fix above wrote the saved text back into the box on save, to keep the box, the marker and the saved text in agreement. The textarea carries no `disabled` - only the buttons do - so anything typed between clicking Save and the answer arriving was landed on and lost.

Nothing is written back now. The marker moves to the text that was **sent**: if the box still holds it nobody typed during the save and it may follow a newer answer, and if they did, the box differs from the marker and is theirs. `sent` rather than the answer's text, because the marker records what was in the box, and a server that tidies what it stores has not changed that.

### A guard, because this is the same mistake twice

A refetch refilling the box, then a save writing it back: one layer apart, same shape. So `scripts/script-box-guard.mjs` runs in `prelint` and fails if any mutation callback in `ProjectScript` calls `setText`. It also fails if the one place that may fill the box stops asking `fillWith`, since a guard that quietly stops guarding is worse than none.

It states its own blind spot in its header too: it matches `setText` textually, so a callback writing the box through a helper would slip past. Following that wants the call graph, which is more than this is worth.

## The delete empties the box where it is asked for (`c656429`)

Codex turned the guard on its own exemption, and was right to. I had let the delete's `setText('')` through on the grounds that nothing is left to show and nothing of theirs to lose - true the instant Delete is pressed, false by the time the answer gets back. After confirming, the box stays editable while the DELETE is in flight, and typing the script that replaces the one you just removed is the obvious next thing to do. The answer erased it.

Emptying the box is part of what they asked for, so it happens with the request, in the confirm handler, where it is the person acting.

Clearing the saved text at the same moment pays for the error case without a rollback: if the DELETE fails, the query still holds the script, so it stops matching the saved text and the box, which nobody has touched, follows it back by the ordinary rule. That is a test, not a claim.

So the guard has no exemptions at all. No mutation callback may write the box, the delete included.

## Two more ways into the delete (`6096cf8`)

**The saved text was not restored when a delete failed.** It means what the server holds; the delete empties it with the request, so a failure that restored only the answer left it empty while the script was still there. That lie reads two ways: `dirty` measures a draft against nothing, and `fillWith` sees a script that has been there all along as newly saved.

I had walked this case and called it correct, on the grounds that what you end up seeing is reasonable. What you see was reasonable. The state was wrong, and a wrong state is a bug waiting for a different reader - checking the outcome of one path is not checking the invariant.

**A read already on its way back was not stopped.** One started by a window regaining focus, or by the invalidation the last run issues, lands after the cache is emptied and puts the pre-delete script back into the answer; the empty, untouched box then follows it. The earlier bug through a second door. `await cancelQueries` runs first now, which is what TanStack's own guidance says to do before writing the cache by hand.

`EMPTY_SCRIPT` is frozen too, since it goes into the cache by reference.

### The guard holds three pairings now

Each has been got wrong in turn, so each is checked rather than remembered: the emptying beside the request, the cancel before the emptying, the saved text beside the rollback. Plus the original rule, that no mutation callback writes the box at all.

## Verification

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| measuring edits against the saved text (the bug in `main`) | "follows one even while it holds a run nobody has touched" |
| dropping the nothing-newly-saved guard | three tests |
| falling back to the run while following | three tests |
| opening without the fall back to the last run | "falls back to what ran when nothing is saved" |
| dropping the project check | two tests |
| never treating the box as theirs at all | "is left alone even when somebody else has saved since" |
| a save, or a run, writing the box | the `prelint` guard, four ways |
| the delete's clear put back in its callback | the guard, with no exemption left to hide behind |
| the cache emptying removed from the request | the guard |
| the cancel removed from before it | the guard |
| the saved text, or the whole rollback, removed from the failure path | the guard, both ways |
| a delete that fails losing the script | "brings the script back when a delete failed" |

- tsc, `prelint` (six guards), 418 vitest tests, build
- zero em/en dashes
- frontend only; no backend file is touched

## Still open, deliberately

A box the person **has** typed in beats a newer saved script, so the lost update is reachable that way. Losing a draft is silent; losing the race on Save is not. Closing it wants a version on the record and a refusal on `PUT`, which is its own change.

## Note

Four fixes in a row have each broken the other end of the one before, the mechanism being the same every time: changing what something holds without checking everything that reads it. The two that reached `main` did so not because review missed them - review caught both - but because the PR merged while the fix was being pushed.

author: dvnold
body:
## What and why

People who use Mistral can now add a Mistral key and call its models through Kaeso, from OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages apps alike. Mistral speaks OpenAI Chat Completions and OpenAI Embeddings, so no new dialect is needed. Its differences are declared with the chat profile from #212, which this PR is stacked on.

- `PROVIDERS` gets `mistral` (the models.dev id):
  - base URL `https://api.mistral.ai`, `Authorization: Bearer`
  - generation through `openai_chat`, embeddings through `openai_embeddings`, `count_tokens: None`
  - Token counts are refused in the app's format before anything is sent (#170).
- The chat profile follows live recordings. Mistral rejects every undeclared field with `422 extra_forbidden`.
  - `max_tokens()` and `system_role()`: Mistral refuses `max_completion_tokens` and the `developer` role.
  - `random_seed()`: Mistral takes `random_seed` (0 or more), not `seed`.
  - `without_end_user()`: Mistral refuses both `user` and `safety_identifier`, so an Anthropic `metadata.user_id` is left out as the hint it is.
  - `without_prefill()`: Mistral answers a conversation that ends with an assistant message with 400 `invalid_request_message_order`, and with `prefix: true` it repeats the prefill instead of continuing it. An Anthropic app's prefill is refused before sending.
  - The OpenAI-only fields Mistral forbids are refused before sending: `function_call`, `functions`, `logit_bias`, `moderation`, `prompt_cache_options`, `prompt_cache_retention`, `store`, `verbosity` and `web_search_options`, and `name` and `refusal` on system, user and assistant messages.
  - `audio` is refused too: Mistral takes it but answers with text only, so a request for spoken output would go unanswered.
  - Fields Mistral accepts although its schema doesn't list them are sent: `stream_options` (the gateway sets `include_usage` on every stream; the stream recording uses it), `modalities`, `metadata`, `prediction` and `prompt_cache_key`. The message names the field: `` `logit_bias` is not supported by Mistral; remove it from the request. ``
- Thinking: Mistral returns reasoning as `content` chunks. The chat profile gets a reply part, `ReplyProfile`, and Mistral's uses `thinking_parts()`:
  - A reply's `content` array decodes part by part. Text parts become text blocks, and a `thinking` part (`{type, thinking: [text parts], closed}`) becomes a KPP reasoning block; a thinking part with other keys stays an `Unknown` block. Chat apps get the same parts back.
  - Streamed thinking parts become `BlockStart(Reasoning)` and reasoning deltas, so replies and streams agree. The reasoning block ends when the answer starts, and the empty text pieces Mistral streams first no longer open a text block ahead of the thinking.
  - Anthropic apps get a thinking block and Responses apps a reasoning item, each carrying the original block in a reasoning blob; a follow-up turn that sends the thinking block back works.
  - In a streamed delta whose `content` is an array, text parts become text deltas, thinking parts reasoning deltas and any other part stays in the chunk's Extras; form `cs` records their order, so Chat apps get the array back. Mistral can send the first answer token in the same array as an empty thinking chunk, so apps in another format would otherwise lose it.
  - `reasoning_tokens` still count.
- Mistral's error bodies have no OpenAI `error` object (`{"detail": ...}`, or a top-level `object: "error"` whose `message` can be an object). They reach apps as an OpenAI error that quotes the body, as for other providers with their own error shape.
- `cargo xtask models-dev` refreshed the snapshot: 39 Mistral models with prices, limits and effort levels, 561 models in all. The models.dev sync test now starts its clock once the snapshot is due, so it no longer depends on how old the snapshot is. `supplement.toml` sends `mistral-embed` to `/v1/embeddings`.
  - Mistral ignores `encoding_format: base64` and answers with floats. The codec encodes them as base64 for an app that asked for base64.
- The console's provider picker offers Mistral and says the key comes from console.mistral.ai. Mistral keys have no fixed prefix, so the hint names only the site. A Mistral model's overrides offer only OpenAI Chat Completions and OpenAI Embeddings under **Sends as**.
- The provider-keys table, the configuration reference and the self-hosting requirements (outgoing `api.mistral.ai`) list Mistral, and the OpenAI Embeddings mapping page has a Mistral section, in English, German and Chinese. The OpenAI Chat mapping page lists Mistral's profile with its sources and documents content arrays.
- `deploy/kaeso.example.toml` sets `providers.mistral.base_url`.
- Two test changes apply to every provider:
  - The gateway test environment points every provider in `PROVIDERS` at the mock.
  - The catalogue tests read the snapshot's model count.

Closes #171.

### Fixtures

Everything under `fixtures/openai_chat/providers/mistral` and `fixtures/openai_embeddings/providers/mistral` was recorded live with `cargo xtask record` on 2026-10-19, from `mistral-small-latest`, `magistral-medium-latest` and `mistral-embed`. The model list and the single-model lookup are live `GET /v1/models` replies. Each folder's `README.md` names every file and the recording behind each profile setting. The recordings cover:

- replies, including tool calls (`tool_choice: "any"`), a named tool result, `safe_prompt` and `random_seed`, and thinking chunks
- streams with and without `stream_options`, a whole tool call in one delta, and streamed thinking
- usage with `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`, `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` and `service_tier`, plus the padding field `p` on chunks (Extras)
- 400, 401 and 422 bodies for every field the profile changes or refuses, an unknown model, `prompt_mode`, and `output_dimension`

### Live check across formats

Through the gateway with a real Mistral key: Chat (plain and streamed), Anthropic Messages (plain, streamed, tools, a tool result, thinking with a 16,384 budget plain and streamed with the thinking block first, a follow-up turn sending that thinking block back, a request shaped like a coding agent's, with adaptive thinking, cache control and tools) and Responses (plain, streamed, tools, reasoning, a streamed coding-agent request with `store: false`) all got 200 with no 422. Embeddings returned 1024 floats. A wrong key comes back as 401, `authentication_error` for Anthropic apps. A prefill, `audio` and a 2048 budget are refused before sending.


Every Anthropic Messages and Responses request fixture was encoded to Chat with Mistral's profile and sent to Mistral. 40 of 50 got 200 and none got a 422. The others:

- reasoning efforts outside `none` and `high` on `mistral-small`. The catalogue now refuses those before sending, because models.dev lists the levels.
- a prefill-only request with `max_tokens: 0`
- an image URL Mistral's servers couldn't fetch

Chat apps that send OpenAI-only values Mistral can't take (`service_tier: "priority"`, `file` parts, `allowed_tools`, custom tools) get Mistral's own 422, which names the field.

- An Anthropic thinking budget is sent to OpenAI-format providers as an effort. The catalogue checked an explicit effort against the model's levels but not one converted from a budget, so a budget of 2048 reached `mistral-small-latest` (`none` and `high` only) as `low` and came back as Mistral's 400. The converted effort is now checked like an explicit one, and the refusal names `thinking.budget_tokens` and the budget that works, in one short sentence: `` A `budget_tokens` of 2048 means `low`; `mistral-small-latest` needs at least 16384. ``
- Provider error bodies that the Responses and Embeddings codecs quote no longer end the message with the body's trailing newline, as in the Chat codec.

### Known limitation

Mistral's reasoning models take only `none` and `high`, so an Anthropic budget below 16,384 tok

author: josepaulolaport
body:
I frontend: contract review: unified ledger, two chains, no price revisions, pagination

Spec: §5, §6.1, §6.2, §7, §8, §10.1, §10.4, §11.1–§11.4, §12  Interfaces: frontend draft contract (`frontend/src/api/contract/*`), mocks and screens  Open questions touched: OQ-21 (draft), OQ-22, OQ-23 (pending, not implemented)

**Stacking.** This targets `main` but contains the 5 commits of #35 (`frontend/ui-round-2`), which is still open. Review the 13 commits from `d599502` on; #35's commits drop out of this diff once #35 merges. Main had no frontend changes since the base, and the branch merges cleanly.

## What changes (user decisions, 2026-10-18)
- **P18, one ledger list:** `GET /ledger/entries` is filtered and ordered by the backend.
- **P20, one ledger entry:**
  - Shape: `type: TRADE | CASH`, `date`, `time` (required on both types), a shared `seq` and a signed `cash_amount`. An aporte has `cash_amount` > 0 and a retirada < 0.
  - Writes: `POST /ledger/entries` creates either type. `POST /ledger/entries/deletions {ids}` deletes all or nothing, with no reason.
  - Removed: `/trades` and `/cash-movements`. GAP-I-1 is reversed: cash entries now have a time.
- **OQ-21 (draft), cash and positions as two chains:**
  - Requests: every request has a `scope` (CASH, POSITIONS or ALL), and the preview reports the day before for each chain.
  - Freshness: FRESH, STALE or NOT_PROCESSED on the summary's cash and positions, on the positions read and on each P&L point.
  - Cash: the summary carries the day's `trades_cash_flow`, `deposits` and `withdrawals`.
  - AUM: `null` if either side is missing, stale if either side is stale.
- **OQ-22:** a CASH or ALL job whose day before has no published cash ends FAILED with `CASH_PREDECESSOR_MISSING`.
- **P19 dropped:** there is no `GET /processing/outdated`.
- **Carteira:** only two data-status badges, "Caixa" and "Posições". The KPIs have no badge, and there are no stale or incomplete notice cards; the full-page "Data não processada" notice stays.
- **Lançamentos "Processar":** queues a job in place, prefilled with the period and a scope.
- **Reference prices, no revisions:** there is one price per (asset, date, source). A correction overwrites the price in place and Remover deletes it. `revision`, `superseded_at`, `/reference-prices/revisions` and "Ver revisões" are gone.
- **P21, keyset pagination:**
  - Endpoints: `?limit=&cursor=` returns `{items, next_cursor}` on `/ledger/entries` and `/processing/requests`.
  - Screens: Lançamentos reads 50 entries per page and the job history 20, each with "Carregar mais".

Contract changes (needs integrator): all of the above. Lane X was told and is recording them alongside OQ-23 and migration 0003. The table merge into `ledger.entries` is requested from lane X.

Docs to update (integrator applies):
- Spec §5 and root `CLAUDE.md` §2: revisions → none. The rule "traceable to its revision" no longer holds.
- `frontend/CLAUDE.md` Ativos: the price menu is "Corrigir, Remover"; "Ver revisões" is gone.
- `frontend/CLAUDE.md` Lançamentos: "Drawers" → "one modal".
- `frontend/CLAUDE.md` Carteira: "Stale and incomplete markers, with links" → two data-status badges.
- `docs/interfaces.md` and `schema.sql`: the unified ledger entry, pagination, no price revisions.

## Verified (command → result)
- `npx vitest run` → `Test Files  28 passed (28)`, `Tests  429 passed (429)`, run twice
- `npm run lint` → no output (eslint clean)
- `npm run typecheck` → no output (tsc clean)
- `npm run build` → `✓ built in 453ms`
- Each commit went through the pre-commit hook (eslint, tsc, vitest on the staged files), and every run passed.
- The 3 new review tests fail with the four source files reverted (`3 failed | 128 passed`) and pass with them.
- The branch merges into `origin/main` cleanly (checked with `git merge-tree`).

## Reviewer
1 Blocker, 2 Major and 4 Minor findings. The Blocker, both Majors and part of the Minors are fixed in `7cdb119`:
- **Blocker:** an Aporte with a negative typed amount was saved as a retirada. The form now rejects a typed sign or zero.
- **Major:** older finished jobs loaded by "Carregar mais" triggered the "job finished" refresh. They are now treated as history.
- **Major:** an API error on `scope` was shown nowhere. It now appears under "Escopo", and Escopo is a `radiogroup` with that name.
- **Minor, fixed:** the Lançamentos count uses pt-BR number format, and `withdrawals` is documented as ≥ 0 and subtracted.
- **Minor, open:** the Processamentos search filters only the jobs already loaded, so it can show "Nenhum processamento encontrado" while older pages match. Server-side search is a follow-up.
- **Minor, open:** the mock's cursor is the last row's id, not a true keyset. If that row is deleted between pages, the mock answers 422 where a real `(date, time, seq)` cursor would continue. This affects only the fake backend.

## Tests removed or rewritten, each by a user decision
- "Ver revisões" and revision-append tests → replaced by overwrite-in-place and delete tests.
- Carteira notice-card tests → replaced by no-card and two-badge assertions.
- Tests that sorted or merged the ledger list in the browser → moved to the server order `(date, time, seq)`.

## Open gaps
- OQ-23 (lane X is redesigning it with the user): one status per chain per date, and no SUPERSEDED. Nothing is implemented until the shape is frozen.

## Not verified / known limits
- Run against the MSW fake backend only; no real backend.
- No manual walk of the screens in the demo since the ledger unification, the revisions removal and the pagination.
- Selection on Lançamentos ("Selecionar todos") covers only the pages loaded.

author: deptofsearch
body:
## Why
**0.6.0 took the restaurant pages offline.** It was installed on shotandabeer.com with the old `saab-toolkit` deactivated. After that, every restaurant page was a 404 and `/wp-json/wp/v2/types/saab_restaurant` answered "Invalid post type", meaning no module ran.

The cause is the guard 0.6.0 added so the plugin stands down while the old copy is active: `class_exists( 'SAAB_Toolkit', false )`. PHP declares a file's top-level class before the file's first line runs (early binding), so that check is always true in the file that declares the class. On every request the plugin showed its "waiting" notice and returned, whether or not the old copy was loaded.

## What
- **Guard.** The plugin now stands down only when `SAAB_Toolkit` exists **and** was declared by a different file (`( new ReflectionClass( 'SAAB_Toolkit' ) )->getFileName() !== __FILE__`). That is true only while the old plugin is loaded.
- **Version.** 0.6.1 in the header, the constant, `readme.txt` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Testing
- New `tests/test-saab-toolkit-boot.php` loads the **real main file** in separate PHP processes, with a vendored updater and stubbed WordPress:
  - **On its own:** it hooks `SAAB_Toolkit::boot` on `plugins_loaded`, defines its version and shows no notice.
  - **With an old `SAAB_Toolkit` already declared:** it shows no "cannot declare class" fatal, doesn't hook boot, and shows the notice.
  - 7 passed.
- **Reproduced the outage first.** The same child run against 0.6.0's main file (from `main`) returns `{"hooks":["admin_notices:closure"],"version":null}`: the notice only, with no boot, exactly as the site behaved.
- The full suite passes and `php -l` is clean.

## Rollout
Until this is released, the site is back on the old SAAB Toolkit: DoS SAAB Toolkit deactivated, old one reactivated. After release:
1. Upload `dos-saab-toolkit.zip` 0.6.1 over 0.6.0 (Replace current).
2. Deactivate the old SAAB Toolkit, then activate DoS SAAB Toolkit.
3. Check `/wp-json/wp/v2/types/saab_restaurant` and Hill's page.

body:
Verification tier: rigorous (`pnpm verify:tier --declared rigorous` passes; it computes rigorous because the room-order comparison lives in the domain core, above the brief's standard floor).

On the Cho thuê tab, the room cards no longer carry Lên and Xuống. Rooms show in room-number order, so Phòng 2 comes before Phòng 10. When Mẹ wants another order, one "Sắp xếp phòng" button above the list opens a reorder mode. Each card then gets a small joined Lên and Xuống pair, "Xếp theo số phòng" puts every room back in number order, and "Xong" closes the mode. Viewers never see the button, and a property with one unit does not show it.

![rooms-reorder-390](https://github.com/ngducn/esta/blob/pr-media/170/rooms-reorder-390.gif?raw=true)

## Why

Ryan said the Lên and Xuống buttons on every room card look weird. Reordering is rare, so it moves behind one button, and room number is the default order.

## What changed

- The Cho thuê room list shows the move controls only in the reorder mode. In that mode the add buttons step aside, "Sắp xếp phòng" turns into "Xong" in place, and a one-line hint explains the arrows.
- "Xếp theo số phòng" sorts by `compareRoomLabels` in `packages/core`. Labels with a number come first in natural order, and labels without a number keep their order after them. It writes through the same server path a move uses. It is greyed out when the rooms already read in number order.
- After a move, focus returns to the moved room's button, so a keyboard or screen-reader user keeps their place.

## Scope

- The stored room order stays one value per room. The seed and "Thêm phòng" already create rooms in number order.
- The Thu tiền board always shows room-number order. It sorts by due date, then property, then room number, and never read the stored order, so a custom order on the Cho thuê tab does not change it (the root confirmed this default).
- Left out on purpose. A single unit added with "Thêm đơn vị" still lands at the bottom of the list (#171). The bottom tab bar splitting English labels at 130% text, visible in the English screenshots, is #125 and predates this PR.

## Tradeoffs

- The compact controls keep the words Lên and Xuống beside the arrows. The design brief rejects icon-only buttons on phones, and a joined 44 px pair is still compact.

## Blast Radius

The change touches the Cho thuê tab's room list and the move action on the server. Saved room order and the Thu tiền board's order are unchanged until someone uses the new mode.

## Verification

- The property-units, collections and properties-list specs pass on a production build (slot 5). The property-units spec drives the reorder mode on and off, a move that holds after a reload, focus after a move, "Xếp theo số phòng", a viewer who sees no button, and the Thu tiền board listing the rooms in the tab's order.
- Axe reports no serious or critical finding on the tab in both modes, in Vietnamese light and in English at 130% dark.
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm design:detect` (zero findings) pass on the head.
- Core tests cover numbers inside labels, Vietnamese letters, ties and labels without a number. Component tests cover the mode, a viewer and a single unit.

## Screenshots

Phone, 390 × 844, Vietnamese. Left to right: the tab as it opens, the reorder mode after moving Phòng 2 down, and after "Xếp theo số phòng".

| Dark | ![rooms-default-390-dark](https://github.com/ngducn/esta/blob/pr-media/170/rooms-default-390-dark.webp?raw=true) | ![rooms-reorder-390-dark](https://github.com/ngducn/esta/blob/pr-media/170/rooms-reorder-390-dark.webp?raw=true) | ![rooms-sorted-390-dark](https://github.com/ngducn/esta/blob/pr-media/170/rooms-sorted-390-dark.webp?raw=true) |

Desktop, 1440 × 900, Vietnamese.

body: ## Resumen Replanteo de **Dibujar parrilla** (C-DES-07): sin contorno ni recubrimiento; dibujo en orden del cuadro con toque de inicio y popup «¿Continuar desde la última varilla?» Sí|No; longitudes variables uniformes; textos de una línea; contrato y pruebas a–h. ## Concepto 1. **Sin contorno ni recubrimiento** — se retira el popup de recubrimiento y la selección de contorno. 2. **Orden del cuadro** — Longitudinal / Transversal / Diagonal con las mismas reglas; variable mín→máx uniforme. 3. **Continuar** — siempre pregunta Sí|No; Sí = +espaciamiento de la última varilla de la misma ubicación (si no hay, pide toque); No = toque nuevo. 4. **Vistas** — sencilla 1 vista; doble 2 vistas; PNG con vistas debajo del cuadro. 5. **Textos breves** — mensajes de 1 línea; también Solevar / cálculo / despiece. ## Evidencia (motor) [Parrilla continuar A→B→C + transversal](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019fbbcb-b3fc-75f8-be10-1d415425b4df/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fparrilla-continuar-demo.png) [Parrilla doble dos vistas](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-019fbbcb-b3fc-75f8-be10-1d415425b4df/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fparrilla-continuar-doble.png) - A: Y = 0, 0,20…0,80 · B Sí → Y=1,00 · C Sí → Y=1,20 · D transversal nuevo inicio - Suite esquema: **400/400** OK · casos a–h parrilla OK - Contrato C-DES-07 y caso 28 actualizados ## Fuera de alcance Chequeo N° piezas vs espaciamiento, acero en 3D, celular, cambios NTC/cálculos del cuadro.
