author: justschen
body:
> [!NOTE]
> **Draft prototype for discussion.** This brings back Keep and Undo for Agent Host (Copilot SDK) chats behind an experimental setting that is off by default. It isn't ready to merge: Undo isn't recorded by the agent host yet, so Session Changes keeps showing undone edits.

## What this does

Agent Host chats lost the local harness's per-change review when their editing session was reduced to checkpoints (fe781b70ab4, 5bb2223128a). This brings the old UX back without new protocol or SDK surface:

1. **Getting the edits.** The agent host already snapshots each file before and after every edit tool call, using the Copilot SDK's `onPreToolUse` / `onPostToolUse` hooks (`FileEditTracker`). Both snapshots reach the workbench with the tool result as `IChatExternalEdit` parts.
2. **Building the review.** A new `AgentHostEditReview` creates one entry per edited file, using the same `ChatEditingModifiedDocumentEntry` local chat uses. The baseline is the "before" snapshot. The modified side is the live document, which reloads as the agent writes to disk.
3. **Showing it.** `AgentHostSnapshotController`, the chat's `IChatEditingSession`, used to be always empty and now exposes those entries. The existing UI reads from it unchanged: the editor overlay (Keep / Undo / n of m), hunk Keep/Undo, keybindings, the legacy working set, the "Suggested Edits" multi-diff and the Undo All confirmation.

Behavior:

- **Attribution:** during a turn, including a subagent's turn that runs on after its parent's, only model changes that come from reloading the file from disk (`EditSources.reloadFromDisk()`) count as the agent's. Typing, refactorings and formatters stay the user's, even mid-turn.
- **Keep** only moves the review baseline, because the agent already wrote the file.
- **Undo** reverts the change as a user edit and saves right away without save participants, because the agent reads from disk. File-level Undo of a created file deletes it, unless the user kept or wrote text in it; then it restores that text.
- **User edits of agent changes:** editing part of an agent change keeps that whole change, as the editor shows it, so Undo never discards the user's text or mixes it with the agent's. The shared change service gets an opt-in flag for this; the local harness and notebooks are unchanged.
- **Safety:** notebooks, files with unsaved changes in any editor, non-UTF-8 files, and files whose "before" snapshot is missing are not reviewed. Unsaved changes and other chats' reviews are checked again after the edit is read. A file leaves the review when it's deleted or renamed, or once the user's edits leave nothing to decide. One chat reviews a file at a time, and restoring a checkpoint clears the review.
- **Scope:** `chat.editor.keepUndo.enabled` (experimental, default off, read-only off in the Agents window). Only chats in the chat view or an editor on the local agent host. Inline chat keeps its own review.

### Session working set

With the opt-in session working set on, a **Session Changes | To Review** tab row appears under the "N files changed" heading while something waits for review. It uses the modern tab colors and the same layout as the in-progress Viewed tabs.

- **To Review** lists the pending files. Hovering a row shows the local working set's per-file actions (`ChatEditingWidgetModifiedFilesToolbar`: Keep, Undo, Open Changes in Diff Editor), and the heading shows Keep / Undo / View All Edits (`ChatEditingWidgetToolbar`). Opening a row opens the file and reveals its first change.
- **Session Changes** is the existing list, unchanged. With nothing to review, the working set looks exactly as before.

## The gap: Undo isn't recorded by the host

Undo reverts the file on disk, but the host doesn't record it. Session Changes and This Turn are computed from the host's edit records (per file, from the first recorded "before" to the last recorded "after"), not from disk. An undone change therefore keeps showing in Session Changes until the agent edits that file again. Refreshing the changeset doesn't help, because it recomputes from the same records. Uncommitted and Branch changes do update, because they read git.

To close it, Undo has to go through the host so the revert is recorded:

- **Whole-file Undo** could use the existing Session `discard-changes`, as long as nothing in that file was kept earlier.
- **Hunk-level Undo** needs range-level discard (`ChangesetOperationScope.Range` / `ChangesetOperationTargetKind.Range`). The protocol reserves it, but the host doesn't implement it. The in-progress work on revertable Session Changes could plug in here: the review's Undo would call it instead of writing the file.
- **Either way, the revert should only undo changes still under review,** not ones the user already kept.

## Research findings

- **The SDK hooks are already in place.** `CopilotAgentSession` drives `FileEditTracker` from `onPreToolUse` / `onPostToolUse`, so no new SDK surface is needed. `onPostToolUse` only fires on success, so failed tool calls aren't reported.
- **Session Changes and This Turn use `FileEditTracker` records in production,** not git checkpoints. The git strategies only run when explicitly requested, such as for compare views.
- **Created files were reported as edits.** The live payload always carried a "before" state, while restored history omits it. `fileEditTracker.ts` now omits it for created files too, so live and restored payloads agree. Deletes still arrive as edits; the review skips them.
- **A later host discard usually still works after a partial Undo.** The host's 3-way revert treats changes the user already reverted as already applied.
- **A bug that only the live run found:** `ChatServiceImpl._startSession` creates a chat's editing session before it registers the chat model, so the provider couldn't look the chat up and never attached the review. `IChatEditingSessionProvider.createEditingSession` now receives `isGlobalEditingSession`.
- **Independent reviews:** Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon and GPT 6.1 Sol each reviewed the research and plan. Their findings shaped the prototype:
  - reload-only attribution instead of a turn-wide window, which could have let Undo delete user typing
  - the create-payload fix and saving hunk Undo
  - replacing settled entries, and failing closed when a baseline is missing
  - a separate review list
  - no review for inline chat or remote hosts

## Limitations

- Review state lives in the window's memory: it's lost on reload, isn't shared with the Agents window or other clients, and only works on the local agent host.
- Terminal writes, deletes, renames, notebooks, and files with unsaved changes aren't reviewed.
- Only UTF-8 files are reviewed, because the host decodes its snapshots as UTF-8. Keeping the snapshot bytes end to end and decoding them with the document's encoding would lift this.
- Editing part of an agent change keeps that whole change, so it can no longer be undone on its own.
- During a turn, any reload of a reviewed file from disk counts as the agent's, including the user's own git operations.
- The agent isn't told about Undos and may re-apply an undone change. `request.editedFileEvents` or an outgoing-turn contribution could pass them along.
- Only the Copilot provider was validated live.

## Open questions

- **Naming:** Keep/Undo, or something like View/Revert? "Viewed" already means "I've looked at this file" in changesets.
- **Viewed tabs:** when the Session Changes | Viewed tabs land, To Review should become a third tab in that row.
- **Heading counts:** the heading shows whole-session totals, while its Keep/Undo act only on the files to review.

## Changes

| Area | Files |
|---|---|
| Review layer (new) | `agentHostEditReview.ts` |
| Wiring | `agentHostSnapshotController.ts` (delegation), `agentHostSessionHandler.ts` (attach to chat-view and editor sessions, turn bracket, edit

author: yelintong
body:
## What

The Design panel's sections now lay their rows out on one grid, taken from the design file (`Frame 29`, 240 pt wide):

```
16 │ 88 │ 8 │ 88 │ 8 │ 24 │ 8
```

- panel 240 pt, content **16 pt** in from the left and **8 pt** from the right (it was 16 / 16)
- two field columns, 88 pt each at the default width, **8 pt gutters** and a **24 pt column** for the buttons at a row's end (flex tracks, so they share a wider panel)
- rows **24 pt** in a 32 pt track, captions **9 pt** over them; section titles **11 pt regular** (were semibold)
- a row's two buttons (eye, minus) are **one group on the row's right edge, 4 pt apart** (was the 8 pt column gutter)
- the export preview frame takes the same 16 / 8

## Why the right margins were out

1. `block()` — the wrapper every field row goes through — inset rows by `PAD` on **both** sides (`r.shrink2(vec2(PAD, inset_y))`), so every row ended 16 pt from the panel's edge while section headers ended 8 pt from it.
2. The panel's frame carried a 1 pt **stroke**, and egui counts a frame's stroke as margin (`content = inner_margin + 2 × stroke`): the content was 238 pt wide, not 240, so even the 8 pt margin landed 1 pt out. The edge is drawn inside the panel now.
3. The paint, effect and layout grid rows reserved 56 pt for their buttons but the group is 8 + 24 + 4 + 24 = 60, so the buttons were squeezed 4 pt into the margin (or 4 pt out of it).

## Numbers, measured in the app (panel 240, right edge at 1440)

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| field column | 84 | **88** |
| row content right edge | 1424 (16 pt from the edge) | **1432 (8 pt)** |
| header button box | 1408..1432 | 1408..1432 |
| a row's two buttons | 28 pt apart, second box at 1436 | **1380..1404 / 1408..1432, 4 pt apart** |

## Screenshot

![The Design panel on the grid](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yelintong/figcraft/feat/panel-grid/docs/images/shot-design-panel.png)

## Tests

`cargo test -p figcraft-ui-egui` — 549 passed. `field_tests`'s glass field width follows the wider column (98.5 → 99.5). The sections' 12 pt bottom margin from the design is left for a follow-up: it moves the lower sections (effects, layout grids) past the 900 pt test window and needs that drag test reworked.

  * Improved responsive sizing for layout, alignment, gap, stroke, effect, grid, and brush controls.

## Summary

#3686 (P3, docs and comments only) follows #2787's D2-K1 slice (merged as #3687), which added a `**Window.**` note to 23 §6.1: the read behind a `bars` snapshot takes at most what its SR-E12-02 window holds, and a series the server keeps also keeps the bars closed since its read, up to 1 000, so a later snapshot of it can hold more than its window holds. Several places still stated only the read's bound, or used examples a read cannot reach. This change makes them agree with the note: 21 §9.5; the `MAX_TAIL` comment, the `read_tail` docstring and the docstring of the test that pins `MAX_TAIL` (the series store reads `MAX_TAIL` whatever a subscriber's `history`, a 0 included, so "the caller skips a 0" was wrong); 23 §8.4's frame sizing, with the 1w case; and the two "1 000 daily bars" examples in 23, which now use six-hour bars, an interval a read can reach (1 000 of them take 6 kind-4 frames and span 21 578 400 000 ms, over 2³²−1). Every figure was run on the real encoder before it was written. No schema, constant, generated file or code path changes: 23 counted lines (13 added, 10 deleted) in five files, and an AST compare shows the three `.py` files differ only in a comment and two docstrings.

## Related issues

Ticket key: E12-T06 (#399), follow-up of #2787 D2-K1

Closes #3686

Related: #2787 (D2-K1, D2-K2); #3687 (added the §6.1 Window note); #399 (E12-T06); #2894 and #2801 (put the window text in `bars/limits.py` and 21 §9.5); #2652 (the tail read).

**Base:** `main` `b3fd759ba`, one commit, head `6b0a976b9`. Round 1 approved `e9fc94f4b` (on `9e5076527`) twice with text-only minors; they are folded in this head (Test plan).

## Ticket brief checklist

- [x] I read #3686 in full, 23 §3.6, §6.1 (the `**Window.**` note) and §8.4, 21 §9.5, `bars/limits.py`, `bars/reader.py`, `bars/series_store.py`, `ws/permissions.py`, `ws/bars_source.py` and `ws/bars_wire.py`
- [x] Repo paths touched: `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md`, `services/api/candleviewer/bars/limits.py`, `services/api/candleviewer/bars/reader.py` and the docstring of one test in `services/api/tests/unit/bars/test_reader_tail.py`; nothing else
- [x] Interfaces unchanged: no schema, constant, generated file or code path changes; no table row is touched (every changed line is a paragraph, a bullet, a comment or a docstring)
- [x] Commands: the doc gates and tests that read these files (Test plan), not substitutes
- [x] Done means: the places #3686 names agree with §6.1, every figure is checked on the encoder, Prettier and the doc tests pass, docs and comments only
- [x] `blocked_by`: none (#3687 is merged)

## Type of change

- [x] `docs` — documentation (all other types: not applicable)

### Acceptance criteria

| #3686 "Done means" | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| **21 §9.5 agrees with §6.1** | `21-database-schema.md:3472`: "a snapshot holds at most what the window holds" is now "the read behind a snapshot takes at most what the window holds", and the §6.1 held-series sentence follows (a series the server keeps also keeps the bars closed since its read, up to 1 000, so a snapshot of it can hold more than its window holds) |
| **The `MAX_TAIL` comment agrees with §6.1, and "(the caller skips a 0)" is gone** | `bars/limits.py:23-29`: the window sentence says "the read takes at most what the window holds"; a new sentence says the series store's read takes `MAX_TAIL` whatever a subscriber's `history` (a 0 too); the held-series sentence follows. The same words go from the docstring of `test_the_tail_cap_is_the_ws_history_maximum` (`tests/unit/bars/test_reader_tail.py:101`), which repeated the old comment |
| **The `read_tail` docstring is true** | `bars/reader.py:336-339`: "Callers skip a `history` of 0" is now "The series store, the one caller, asks for `MAX_TAIL` whatever a subscriber's `history` (a 0 too)"; "a `limit` below 1 raises" is now "a `limit` outside 1..`MAX_TAIL` raises"; the timeout sentence is kept |
| **23 §8.4 agrees with §6.1** | `23-ws-protocol.md:1292`: the window now "bounds the read behind a snapshot to about 400 days, so about 9 frames"; a new sentence gives the held-series case (up to 1 000 bars, 20 frames at 1d); both figures are compared with the 500 and 64 frames of the share, and the 1w case is stated (1 000 bars would take 125 frames, more than the 64 at the floors, held only after 943 weekly closes) |
| **The two "1 000 daily bars" examples are ones a read can reach** | `23-ws-protocol.md:276` (§3.6) and `:712` (§6.1): "1 000 six-hour bars take 6 kind-4 frames" and "(1 000 six-hour bars do)" span more than 2³²−1 ms |
| **Every figure is checked against the encoder** | the table under "Verified figures" (real `bars_frames`, real `tail_window_us`, real `SeriesStore`) |
| **Prettier and the doc tests that read these sections pass** | Test plan |
| **Docs and comments only** | AST compare of the three `.py` files (Test plan); `git diff --numstat`: 5 files, 13 added, 10 deleted |

What each changed sentence states, and where it is true as built:

| Text | True as built in |
| --- | --- |
| 21 §9.5, `limits.py` and 23 §8.4: the read takes at most what the window holds (about 800 bars for 12h, 400 for 1d, 57 for 1w; the last 31 d of a non-time kind) | `bars/reader.py`: `read_tail` looks back `tail_window_us` (for a time kind `TAIL_SPAN_FACTOR` times the span of `limit` bars, within `MAX_TIME_WINDOW_US`; any other kind `MAX_NON_TIME_WINDOW_US`), and `build_tail_query` refuses a `from_us` past the cap. Run: `tail_window_us` at `MAX_TAIL` is 400 d for 6h, 12h, 1d and 1w (1 600, 800, 400 and 57 bars fit), 333 d for 4h and 83 d for 1h |
| A series the server keeps also keeps the bars closed since its read, up to 1 000, so a snapshot of it can hold more than its window holds (21 §9.5, `limits.py`, and 23 §8.4) | `bars/series_store.py`: `_apply` appends a close and drops the oldest only `if len(s.closed) > MAX_HISTORY` (never by age); `MAX_HISTORY: Final = MAX_TAIL`. Run on the real store: a 1d series read at 400 bars and given 600 closes held 1 000; a 12h series read at 800 and given 400 held 1 000; a 1w series read at 57 and given 5 held 62 |
| `limits.py` and `read_tail`: the series store's read takes `MAX_TAIL` whatever a subscriber's `history`, a 0 too | `bars/series_store.py`: `ensure(self, symbol, spec)` takes no `history`, and `_hydrate` calls `self._tail(symbol, spec, MAX_HISTORY)`. `ws/permissions.py`: `sub.series_hold = await self.services.series.ensure(symbol, spec)` is not gated on `history`. `ws/bars_source.py`: `history` only reaches `self._store.latest(symbol, spec.spec_hash, history)`, which trims what is sent. `tests/unit/bars/test_series_store.py`: the fake reader asserts `(spec, limit) == (SPEC, MAX_HISTORY)`. Run: through the real `handle_sub` (the suite's fakes at its edges), a `bars` subscribe with `history` 0, 10 and the default each called `ensure`; on the real `SeriesStore` with a fake reader the read limit was `[1000]`, `latest(history=0)` gave 0 bars and `latest(history=10)` gave 10 |
| `read_tail`: the series store is the one caller; a `limit` outside 1..`MAX_TAIL` raises | `app.py`: `SeriesStore(bars_reader.read_tail ...)` is the only place `read_tail` is handed to code (`git grep read_tail` finds no other call outside tests). `bars/reader.py`: `build_tail_query` raises `ValueError` outside 1 to `MAX_TAIL`. Run on a real `BarReader` with a fake connection: limits 0 and 1001 raised, 1 and 1000 returned |
| `read_tail`: the store bounds every read with a timeout, degrading when it expires (SR-E12-01) | kept from the old text; `bars/series_store.py` `_hydrate`: `async with asyncio.timeout(self._timeout_s)`, and a failed read leaves the series as it was |
| 23 §8.4: about 9 frames for what a read takes; 20 frames for 1 000 bars at 1d | 400 d is 8.05 spans of 2³²−1 ms (49.71 d), so 9 is the upper bound; on the encoder a full 400 d read takes 8 frames at 1d (400 bars), 12h (800) and 1w (57). 1 000 daily bars take 20

## What

Shows the REPL on a 4.3 inch display plugged into the ESP32-S31-Korvo-1.

## Why

CircuitPython did not use the board's LCD connector.

| `CIRCUITPY_DOTCLOCKFRAMEBUFFER=1` on S31 | Result |
|---|---|
| Before | Link fails: undefined `soc_lcd_rgb_signals` and `lcd_hal_*` |
| After | Builds |

The ESP32, S2, S3 and P4 builds already list `esp_hal_lcd`.

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Panel | 4.3 inch 800x480 RGB565 (ESP32-S3-LCD-EV-Board SUB3, ST7262E43), no init commands |
| Timing | From Espressif's esp-bsp `bsp/esp32_s31_korvo_1/include/bsp/esp32_s31_korvo_1.h`: 18 MHz, pclk on falling edge, h 40/40/48, v 23/32/13, about 35 Hz |

body:
Fixes #40227.

Binding a Go string such as `"48"` to a MySQL `BIGINT` column can return no rows through Proxy when the backend uses `useServerPrepStmts=false`, while the same query succeeds directly against MySQL.

`MYSQL_TYPE_STRING` parameters are initially read as `byte[]`. The existing decoding logic converts them to Java strings only for character target columns, so numeric-column parameters reach Connector/J as binary values.

Extend the target-column check to numeric types and express the character and numeric groups with a switch. This preserves string semantics and lets MySQL perform numeric conversion. Preserve existing character decoding, binary parameter handling, NULL handling, and behavior when column metadata is unavailable.

### Validation

- Passed all 487 tests in the MySQL protocol module, including 49 tests in `MySQLComStmtExecutePacketTest`.
- Achieved 100% line and branch coverage for `MySQLComStmtExecutePacket`.
- Passed Spotless and Checkstyle for both changed Java files.
- Rebuilt Proxy and verified the packaged protocol classes match the current compilation output.
- Verified against MySQL 8.0.37 with Connector/J 8.4.0, manually installed in Proxy's `ext-lib`.
- With backend `useServerPrepStmts=false` and `true`, passed all 12 original Go/GORM query cases per Proxy configuration, covering string and integer parameters with `Find`, `Count`, and `RawFind`.
- Verified the #37993 regression path using a BIGINT/VARCHAR composite sharding key with `interpolateParams=false`. This covers the same sharding-value `Comparable` check using an existing table, rather than reproducing the original topology.
- Rolled back all fixtures, confirmed no test rows remained, and stopped both temporary Proxy instances.

author: daniyalmlk
body:
Closes #7.

The page opened with the pipeline's own output, which is better than most front
pages and still the easiest kind of number to produce and the hardest to
believe. Nothing on it said which lines are identities, which are measurements
against a known answer, and which are simply what the code prints.

Seven rows above the install line now, each produced by
`paper-to-live run --json` — which CI already runs against the built wheel, so
the gate is the command line rather than a new script.

### The row the project exists for

The generator's drift term is zero, so the simulated market has nothing in it
to find and whatever wins a search over 322 rules won by luck. That makes the
deflated Sharpe ratio a measurement against a **known answer**: the true Sharpe
ratio is zero, and the honest report of a 0.82 winner is a coin flip's worth of
evidence that it is not worthless. Coming back with 0.70 is the library being
right, not the library emitting a number — and that is a much stronger claim
than the page was making.

The row under it is the guard on that one. An assertion no input can violate
tests nothing, so 0.95 has to be shown attainable on the same 1008 days at the
same trial dispersion, otherwise "never above 0.95" is a statement about the
threshold rather than about the market. Both of those tests already existed and
the page never mentioned them.

### Identities, said to be identities

Two rows are exact zeros and the distinction from "small" is the point. The
erosion column either adds up — 0.8226 less 0.2039 less 0.2732 is 0.3455,
residue `0.0` — or the four figures printed at the top of the page are not a
decomposition of anything. The recovered holdings either reproduce the series
they were derived from, to zero over 1008 days with none ambiguous, or every
cost below them was computed for a strategy nobody ran, which is why that check
raises rather than warning.

The repricing error is quoted as a bound rather than digits, because the last
bits a root finder lands on are not portable: the same quantity in `tenor` is
-8.3e-14 on CPython 3.12 and +1.3e-13 on 3.11.

### Pinned in three directions

`tests/test_readme_evidence.py`, 16 cases. A figure that moves fails, a row
that is deleted fails, and a row in the table that is not among the pinned ones
fails — the last so that a row added later cannot be free. The table is located
by its heading rather than by scanning every pipe in the file, since this
README carries two other tables (the four stages, and the module layout) and
counting all of them would make the check pass for the wrong reason.

The value direction is deliberately not attempted. This page quotes 0.82, 0.70,
0.35 and 0.27 within a few lines of each other, so a check that looks for "some
number near here" and compares it to the measurement can pass against the wrong
one — the failure mode is a green suite defending a wrong figure.

The seed sweep's width is counted out of `tests/test_selection.py` rather than
restated, because "under 0.95 at every seed swept" is only worth reading if the
sweep is wider than one.

This repository is a worse place than the libraries to let a figure drift. It
depends on four of them and CI builds each from its default branch at job time,
so the numbers can move without a commit landing here. That liveness is the
whole point — it is how the day they stop fitting together gets noticed — and it
only works if something is reading the document.

### Tested

- Suite **94 passing**, up from 78, verified on 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 against the
  four libraries installed from their current mains.
- `ruff check .` clean; `mypy` clean over 10 source files.
- All three directions of the pin confirmed to fail before being relied on:
  deleting the 322-rules row fails three cases, editing `deflated to 0.70` in
  the README alone fails one, and narrowing the seed sweep to `[11]` fails one.
- The suite-size claim is bounded a quarter either way and counted by asking
  pytest, since an exact count fails on every commit that adds a test and
  trains people to update the number without reading it.

Phase 9 added to `ROADMAP.md`. The one remaining open item there is still
depending on released versions of the four libraries, which waits on them
having releases.

author: pournasserian
body:
Closes #2554

## What

The pre-flight slice of F-CHK (#2420), CHK-04: an agent runs the site's active checks on a draft without storing it or opening a change set. It comes before the change set run (the epic's fifth slice), which waits on a decision about who the check engine acts as. The runner here is the one that run will use.

- **Core** (`FluentCMS.Core.Checks`):
  - `ICheckRunner` runs every active check whose scope applies to a piece of content, at its active version and in name order. Each check sees the fields its scope names, and calls are charged to the caller. `CheckSelection.Deterministic` leaves out LLM-judged checks, and the run names the ones it left out (`CheckRun.Skipped`).
  - `CheckResult` holds the check, version, type, kind, severity, description, status, findings and model call.
  - `CheckStatus` is pass, warn (a failing check of warn severity), fail or needs review. `CheckResult.Overall` is fail if any check fails, then needs review, then warn, then pass.
- **Tool `check_draft`** (`FluentCMS.Core.Builtin.Tools.CheckTools`):
  - Arguments: `content_type`, `fields`, optional `sources`, `checks` (`all` or `deterministic`), and `id` for a draft of an update.
  - It returns `status`, `results` (each with its findings and model call), `skipped`, and `fieldErrors`, the errors `create_entry` would give the draft.
  - With `id`, a check that asks about changes, such as `sources`, sees only the fields whose value differs from the entry's latest draft.
  - A draft with field errors fails. An unknown content type or entry is refused, with a hint for the call that finds one.
  - It stores nothing and opens no set.
- MCP-01 coverage: "Run the checks on a draft before proposing it". CONTRIBUTING.md: the runner and the tool.

## Why

CHK-04 asks for a pre-flight tool, so an agent fixes what the checks find before it proposes the change, instead of after a set fails. S2 is that loop: three findings, three fixes, a pass.

Choices worth a look:

- **Before the change set run.** The run on every set (CHK-03) must move a set from checks running to checks failed or awaiting review. `AgentPermissions` refuses those moves for agents, and a job (#2536) runs as whoever enqueued it, the submitting agent. Initiators today are only users and agents, so the run needs a decision on whom it acts as in the audit log. I have asked; this slice does not depend on the answer.
- **Not read-only.** The tool stores nothing, but an LLM-judged check spends the agent's model budget, so it does not carry the read-only annotation that clients may approve without asking. `checks: "deterministic"` makes a free, instant call.
- **Field errors fail the draft.** A draft the content type refuses cannot be proposed, so it never reads as a pass, whatever the checks say.
- **Updates.** Without `id`, every field counts as changed, as for a new entry. With it, a headline edit on a priced page does not ask for a source for the unchanged price. The entry is read through `IEntryDirectory`, so the agent's scope applies.
- **Scope.** The content type is read through `IContentTypeDirectory`, so a type outside the agent's scope is refused, and the result shows no check's settings or examples.
- **Not in this PR**: the check run on every change set with results stored on the set, the tool that reads a set's results, and checks that read entities (F-ENT).

## Tests

Unit:

- `CheckToolsConformanceTests` (`ToolProviderConformanceTests`).
- `CheckRunner`:
  - every active check that applies gives its status and evidence, in name order; a warn check's failure only warns
  - scope by content type and field, and an untyped draft
  - the deterministic selection asks no model and names what it left out
  - without a model the run needs review unless something fails
  - status mapping, and the overall status of none
- MCP-01 coverage row.

Integration over MCP, each on SQLite and PostgreSQL:

- S2: a draft with "best in class", an image without alt text and an unsourced price fails three checks with their findings. The fixed draft with a source passes, and nothing is stored.
- An active LLM-judged check needs review without a model, and the run does too. With `deterministic` it is listed under `skipped` and the run passes.
- A draft of an update is checked for what it changes: a headline edit passes and a price change without a source fails.
- A draft the content type refuses lists its field errors and fails.
- Unknown content types, entries, arguments and selections are refused with what to change, and a type outside the agent's scope is refused.
- The built-in tool list includes `check_draft`.

The full suite ran locally against a `postgres:17` container as well as SQLite, and markdownlint passes. No new package and no migration.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked to an issue a maintainer has confirmed
- [x] Targets `v2`
- [x] Tests or docs updated where behaviour changed
- [x] No tool-generated co-author trailers or footers

author: wilfreddenton
body:
## Summary

- Bound table entries across nested contract calls with a shared root limit of 16,777,216 slots (16 Mi slots), alongside the existing per-table and per-Store limits.
- Reserve slots before table creation/growth and release each Store's admitted slots on teardown. Keep normal `table.grow` failure behavior and avoid reservations for requests beyond the declared maximum.
- Stop nested `ExecutionError` formatting from repeatedly expanding its causal chain. Preserve sources and detailed top-level logging, simulation errors, and view responses.

This is a Kontor-only change using the existing Wasmtime dependency. It contains no upstream lifting-metering patch, dependency upgrade, or trial gas/pricing configuration.

## Why

Adversarial nested contracts can accumulate table entries outside the shared linear-memory/GC byte limit. Active table segments can also add entries without incremental call fuel. Counting shared table slots places a portable aggregate limit on this resource without relying on Rust layouts.

Nested error formatting previously expanded the same causes repeatedly. A 17-deep test produced about 19 MB of error text; ordinary formatting of each wrapper prevents that recursive expansion while explicitly requested alternate formatting still traverses the preserved source chain.

## Limits and compatibility

The new table-slot limit is consensus-relevant and must be adopted consistently. Previously valid calls exceeding it will now fail, which must be considered for historical replay and activation. It allows 256 maximum-sized 65,536-entry tables in aggregate, including adapter tables. Slots are logical units, not a whole-process RSS guarantee. Compilation/cache memory and concurrent-view headroom remain separate work.

Wasmtime 49 can fail table backing allocation without a matching failure callback. Admitted slots are therefore conservatively retained until Store teardown rather than attempting an unsafe refund.

## Validation

- Final head: 42 runtime-call tests passed with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`; 2 manual benchmarks ignored.
- Focused guest-memory validation covers shared table admission, initial quota rejection, growth denial, zero growth, clone/drop ownership, declared-max failure without reservation leakage, real published nested table-limit failures with cold/warm gas consistency and sequential-child release, and existing memory/GC regressions.
- Error regressions cover both variants through Wasmtime error wrappers, source classification, preserved causes, direct and wrapped alternate Display, and outer ExecutionError Debug, with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`.
- Indexer library/test Clippy passed with `-D warnings`.
- Formatting and diff checks passed.

Validation so far is Linux aarch64. Actual table allocator failure injection and concurrent Store stress were not run locally; platform CI will run after opening the PR.

## Review

Reviewed locally by Codex and Claude `/code-review`, with a focused follow-up on the final formatter and integration tests. No remaining actionable correctness findings. The review added real published nested table-limit coverage and preserved direct detailed error formatting.

author: omatheusmol
body:
Fixes #324

## Problem
The voice-note recorder disabled Record while the microphone request was pending but left the status at 'Ready to record.', so a slow permission grant looked like a stalled page (issue #324, from #320).

## What changed
- web/recorder.ts: set the status to 'Waiting for microphone permission…' before getUserMedia is called; Record stays disabled as before.
- e2e/recorder.spec.ts: new Playwright tests that hold the microphone request open and check the pending status, the success hand-off to 'Recording…', and the refusal error status with Record re-enabled.

## Tests
- 'shows a pending microphone status and keeps Record disabled until the request resolves' fails without the change (status reads 'Ready to record.') and passes with it, on phone and desktop.
- 'shows an error status and re-enables Record when the microphone is refused' covers the error path; it fails without the change at its pending assertion and passes with it, on phone and desktop.

## Watch out
- Pending text uses the Unicode ellipsis '…' to match the page's other status messages; the issue example uses '...'.
- The issue asks to 'restore Ready to record.' on success; the change moves to the existing 'Recording…' message instead, since 'Ready to record.' would contradict an active recording. The owner may want the literal text, which would be a separate change.
- The error text is the existing 'The microphone is not available. Allow it in the browser and try again.' message, unchanged.
- The tests replace navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with an init script that holds the request until the test settles it; the real grant still runs through the fake device.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`: passed (tsc for the root and web projects completed with no errors.)
- `pnpm test:ui e2e/recorder.spec.ts`: passed (4 of 4 passed (both tests on phone and desktop) with the change.)
- `pnpm test:ui e2e/recorder.spec.ts (change temporarily removed)`: failed (Both pending-status tests failed on phone and desktop with 'Ready to record.' received, confirming they fail without the change; the change was then restored.)

author: glade-team[bot]
body:
The GitHub link watcher now polls every linked PR until it merges or closes and every linked issue until it closes, whether or not its todo is done, and a link whose todo is done keeps its state current without ever waking its task.

Because:
- The watcher stopped a link the moment its todo was marked done (`stopDoneLinks`), without fetching it again, so a link whose todo finished while it was still open kept that state — usually Open — forever (#738; the 0.35.0–0.35.1 token bug left some links never fetched before their todo was done).
- Jared, Oct 18: "our periodic gh sync should include anything that's marked open regardless of the state of the todo; it can stop syncing PRs when they're merged and issues when they're closed".

This commit:
- Drops the "todo done → stop" rule (`stopDoneLinks`) and the skip of stored `watching = false` rows in `watchCandidates`.
- The poller now fetches every linked PR and issue whose stored state is open, or that was never fetched, whatever its todo says; it stops a link once its stored state is closed or merged.
- A change found on a link whose todo is done still updates the stored watch and emits `GithubWatchChanged`, but never produces a `LinkChange`, so no task is woken; one info log per poll says how many such links were refreshed quietly.
- Rows the old rule left `watching = false` while still open are picked up again on the next poll, decided from the stored state alone — no migration.
- Updates `docs/product.md`'s GitHub watching bullet and the `GithubLinkWatch.watching` doc comment.

Calls made without Jared:
- The quiet-refresh log line's wording (`github watch refreshed links whose todo is done, without waking their tasks`, with the count) — the issue asked for the count once per poll, not the words.
- `watchCandidates` now returns closed and merged links too, with the poller deciding from the stored state which to fetch; the alternative was filtering there as well.

Closes #738

No UI changes, so there are no screenshots.

author: giswqs
body:
## Summary
- While the 3D globe is dragged or zoomed, it shows a drape: the map drawn flat once and laid over the sphere. Since #522 the drape bounded its texture size by drawing at a coarser **camera scale**, and zooming out drew it at twice the scale. Point symbols and strokes are sized in points, so they were baked in 2–6× too large, and everything blurred until the settled frame arrived.
- The drape now draws at the camera's scale and lowers its **pixels per point** instead, both in `globe_drape` and in `render_globe_drape`'s per-side size limit (whose pixel-density floor drops from 0.25 to 1/64 so it can do so).
- The drape's pixel budget goes from 1M to 2M pixels, so the moving globe stays near screen density. 4M was barely sharper and doubled the rebuild hitch.

## Validation
- [x] `a_coarse_globe_drape_keeps_point_symbols_their_size` (render): a marker in a drape forced over its size limit covers the same ground as in a full-density drape. Without the fix it drew 6.6× wider.
- [x] `a_drape_keeps_the_camera_scale` (ui-egui): the drape view keeps the camera, including while zooming out, and stays within the pixel budget.
- [x] `ui_shot` screenshots of the World Atlas sample on the globe mid-drag and mid-zoom: cities keep their settled size and the map is sharp.
- [x] `planet_bench`: globe navigation mean frame 0.8 → ~1.0 ms. The worst drape-rebuild frame and layer-toggle latency go from ~13 ms to ~27 ms at the 2M-pixel budget (the scale fix alone costs nothing).

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Globe drapes now better preserve map scale when rendering large areas, including at lower detail levels.
  * Improved point-symbol sizing consistency when globe drapes are constrained by rendering limits.
  * Globe drapes now stay within a bounded rendering area across different zoom levels.

## Was sich für die Spieler ändert

- **Spieler bestätigen ihre Version vor der Schlacht.** In „Who fought“ steht unter jeder Warband entweder „Version not confirmed yet“ oder „✓ Version N goes in · confirmed by …“. Der Knopf „Confirm my warband for battle N“ speichert den Stand des Geräts als Version „before battle N“ und friert dessen Zahlen ein.
- **Leiter können für andere bestätigen** („Confirm for <Spieler>“, die neueste Version auf dem Server) und eine neuere Version nachziehen („Take version N instead“).
- **Nichts blockiert eine Schlacht.** Ohne Bestätigung steht nur „Went in without a confirmed version“.
- **Vorher/Nachher für Leiter:** Abschnitt „Before and after“ in der Schlacht (Rating, Gold, Models, Fallen, mit Unterschied). Der Spieler sieht seine eigene Warband in der Nacharbeit unter „What changed“.
- **Home und Kampagne:** „Open for you“ zeigt „Confirm your version“, bis es erledigt ist; die Schlachtenliste zeigt „live · n/m confirmed“.
- **Schutz:** Eine Warband kann nach der Schlacht nicht mit einer älteren Version markiert werden als der bestätigten (409 `older`), z. B. von einem veralteten Gerät.

- Migration `0025_battle_confirm.sql` (`before_confirmed_at`, `before_confirmed_by`, `before_totals`).

body:
## 概要

为 Skill 新增可选的 Openverse 自动音效。口播计划的 `sfx` 里可以写英文关键词的 `openverse` 事件；`from-compiled` 之后运行 `scripts/openverse_sfx.py add`，联网挑选 Freesound 音效，处理成本地 WAV 后写入独立音轨。草稿 build/publish 仍不联网，引擎代码与固定值不变。

## 改动

- `scripts/edit_plan.py`：新增 `openverse` 事件，按剪后时间映射编译到 `openverse_sfx`；校验兼容不含该字段的旧编译结果，`from-compiled` 行为不变。
- `scripts/openverse_sfx.py`（新增）：`add` 为编译结果里的每个提示挑选、下载、处理并写入音轨，同时生成 `report.json` 与 `credits.md`；`search` 只检索不下载。
  - 只经 HTTPS 访问 `api.openverse.org` 与 `cdn.freesound.org`，拒绝其他主机和指向其他主机的重定向；短暂限流会等待后重试，需等待超过 60 秒时报错。
  - 挑选：标题和标签对不上关键词的结果不选，音乐、循环类排在后面；CC BY-NC 只在没有合适的 CC0 / CC BY 时选用，`--commercial` 完全排除。
  - 处理：剪掉起音前静音，按 `max_duration` 截短；最响 50 ms 窗口统一到约 -20 dBFS，峰值不超过 -1 dBFS，输出 48 kHz PCM WAV；时间重叠时另开音轨。
- `tests/test_openverse_sfx.py`（新增 13 项）：编译映射与输入检查、旧编译结果兼容、排序与许可、响度处理、网络白名单与限流、计划写入与报告。网络全部使用假数据；需要 FFmpeg 的用例在缺少 FFmpeg 时跳过。
- 文档：`SKILL.md`、计划格式、无界面命令、运行依赖与来源、Skill README，以及 `docs/VERIFICATION.md`。

## 联网与许可

- 这一步是可选的，会联网；请求里只有关键词和筛选条件，不上传素材、草稿或账号信息。Openverse 匿名额度约为每分钟 20 次、每天 200 次。
- 第三方音效不随项目分发，保留各自的 CC 许可。CC BY / CC BY-NC 需要署名，CC BY-NC 禁止商用；交付时须转述 `credits.md`。

- `python3 tools/check_package.py` 通过；`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v` 172 项通过。
- `engine/test_headless.py`（本机保留夹具）24 项通过，包括不带 `openverse_sfx` 字段的旧编译结果。

author: wolvever
body:
for Pep

Small behavior-preserving review+simplify pass on `origin/main` (43d2e5b). Does not touch any file that draft #32 changes (runner/mod.rs, runner/remint.rs, transport/jsonl.rs, runtime.rs, DESIGN.md), and leaves the parked host-lifecycle work alone (SoftExpiring / Flush-before-dispatch / Stage / Evidence / EffectId, Runtime::wake → host_wake).

## What changed
- **`HostAttach::decide`** (host.rs): one private helper now records the Host `PermissionDecided` (`Session::decide_permission_rpc`, which does the occupancy check) and stashes `(Event, allowed, optionId)` on the pending ask. `answer_permission` and `cancel` both call it; before, each had its own inline copy of append + `pending.get_mut(..).decided = ..`. The `permission_rpc` helper was only used in those two places, so it moved into `decide`.
- **`adapters::fixture(agent, name)`** (`#[cfg(test)]`, adapters/mod.rs): replaces five identical fixture loaders in acp / codex / grok_build / opencode / pi. Each test module keeps a one-line `fixture(name)` wrapper, so no call site changed.

## Why it's behavior-preserving
- `decide` does the same steps in the same order: build `PermissionRpc` → `decide_permission_rpc` (`?` returns early, so nothing is stashed and nothing is sent) → stash on the `(binding, rpc_id)` key → return the same tuple. `answer_permission` still validates `optionId` first and still sends only after deciding. `cancel` still decides every ask before sending any reply. The stash-reuse path (`Some(stashed)`) is unchanged.
- The fixture change only affects tests and loads the same paths.

## Verification
- `cargo test --workspace`: **279 passed**, 0 failed (same as main).
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets`: no new warnings. The 3 existing warnings (runtime.rs:572, jsonl.rs:118/300) are in files #32 changes, so I left them.

A RPC `ordax_resolve_owner_project_scope_v1` rejeita corretamente antes de consultar grants; a interface MCP, porém, exibia erro pouco acionável.

## Mudanças
- Para ações **project-scoped**, o MCP apresenta uma resposta **sanitizada e fechada**: `error=product_project_scope_not_found`, `setup_required=space_project_repository_device_binding` e `owner_action=register_project_and_device_in_ordax_owner`. Isso informa qual registro precisa ser concluído sem inventar ou criar projeto/grant.
- Não promove grants globais Windows nem caminhos locais como projeto. Não altera o executor, o SQL, o grant nem o catálogo de 37 ferramentas.
- Testa a cadeia inteira: o gateway PostgreSQL/Owner nega antes de consultar grants/enqueue; MCP suprime dados privados e difere claramente entre erro de cadastro e `product_grant_not_resolved`.
- Documenta a origem canônica e o bloqueio de onboarding na issue #220, preservando OrdaX OS/Platform como autoridade e Studio como consumidor.

## Escopo deliberado
**Ainda não cria Spaces/projetos/associações.** A ausência de cadastro precisa ser corrigida no fluxo Owner da issue #220, com confirmação explícita de vinculação e grants específicos. Criar registros diretamente por SQL administrativo seria bypass da segurança e da fonte de verdade.

Relacionado a #220. Catálogo já resolvido em #216.

author: peterwind6174
body:
The root Makefile still uses the old source and package layout. Following `CONTRIBUTING.md` fails with `No rule to make target 'native/metalq.m'`, and the test target tries to enter the nonexistent `metalq/python` directory. The working native build already lives in `native/Makefile`.

## Changes

- Delegate root `make` and `make install` to `native/Makefile`, keeping one compilation definition and copying the outputs to `metalq/lib/`.
- Run tests with `$(PYTHON) -m pytest` from the repository root. Add configurable `PYTHON` and `PYTEST_ARGS` instead of requiring `uv` and the obsolete directory layout.
- Have `make clean` remove both the native build directory and the two copied binaries. Preserve other files in `metalq/lib/`.
- Add PyYAML to the `dev` extra for documentation security tests, without adding it to runtime dependencies.
- Update the README, installation guide, contribution guide, and repository build guidance. Document Metal Toolchain checks and per-command selection using the installed component's identifier.

`make install` builds and copies native binaries; Python package installation remains a separate pip step. This PR is based directly on `main` and does not depend on #12 or #13. Simulator and adapter logic are unchanged.

## Validation

Validated on Apple Silicon using the project Conda interpreter and the installed Metal Toolchain:

- Exported a fresh source archive into a directory containing a space, with no prebuilt binaries. Confirmed the original root build fails before applying these changes.
- Built through the new root `make -j2` and `make install` targets. Verified matching hashes for the native build outputs and their package copies.
- Loaded the native library independently from `native/build/` and `metalq/lib/`. Both GPU Bell-state checks matched the reference with a maximum amplitude error of approximately `1.21e-8`.
- Ran the following tests through `make test`, using `PYTHON` to select the Conda interpreter and `PYTEST_ARGS` to select the files: `test_backend_cpu`, `test_fusion`, `test_fusion_extras`, `test_secure_expression`, `test_backend_mps`, `test_gpu_correctness`, `test_qiskit_adapter`, and `test_docs_security`. **170 passed, no skips.** Existing deprecation warnings remain.
- Ran `make clean`, checked that the build directory and both packaged binaries were removed while an unrelated package file survived, then rebuilt successfully using `make install -j2`.
- Checked `pip install --dry-run --no-index --no-build-isolation -e '.[dev]'` and its metadata: PyYAML is declared only for the `dev` extra. The existing Conda environment was not modified.
- `git diff --check` passed.

These are scoped build/backend checks. Previously observed unrelated full-suite failures are outside this change.

author: code-yeongyu
body:
Fixes #10543 (engine part; the service intake and the desktop dialog land in their own repos)

One feedback core in the omo-senpi extension, used by both the TUI and the desktop app.

- `components/feedback`: collects the report (identity block, app and system, this session's last 50 messages with long tool results shortened, omo/senpi config with headers, env, keys and URL userinfo blanked structurally), redacts every free-text section with senpi's one upload redactor (`pi.redactForUpload`, code-yeongyu/senpi#3674, PR code-yeongyu/senpi#3679, the same function `/share` uses), and sends it to the private intake (`POST /v1/reports`). Memory entries and custom extension entries are never collected.
- TUI: `/feedback` (alias `/bug`): one description, a plain notice of what is included, then Send / See exactly what is sent / Cancel.
- Desktop: extension RPC `omo.feedback.prepare` (the desktop adds its own log, crash and identity sections, which go through the same redactor) and `omo.feedback.submit`.
- No new consent flag: the telemetry install and session hashes are attached only when telemetry is allowed (`shouldDisableTelemetry` + `telemetry.enabled`); `OMO_DISABLE_FEEDBACK` turns uploads off and saves the report as a private local file. A signed-out report's delete token is kept on the device (0600).
- A host without `redactForUpload` reports feedback as unavailable; nothing is ever sent unredacted.

Product decisions (Q): collect as much identity and debug information as possible; no checklist: one Submit sends everything, with a one-line notice and a collapsed read-only view. Open decisions taken at their recommended defaults: keep an optional public GitHub path; link sharing last; share links 30 days + sign-in.

Design: internal design doc (v3, Fable 5.1 reviewed).

## Bundle size (canonical linux/amd64 build, bun 1.4.3)

The feedback core is a lazy sidecar (`extensions/omo-feedback.js`, imported behind `#omo-feedback-runtime` on the first report), and the `/feedback`, `/bug` TUI flow runs from it too. The entry bundle keeps only the component registration, session tracking, the command and RPC shells, and the redactor check.

| Build (same container) | `omo.js` |
|---|---|
| dev `48c3f53a06` alone | 1,396,636 B |
| this PR at `3f2065ebd0` | 1,399,226 B |
| this PR's share of the entry bundle | **+2,590 B** |
| budget (`bundle-size.test.ts`) | 1,424,569 B (PASS) |

`omo-feedback.js` is 232,787 B and loads only when someone sends a report.

Earlier numbers in this thread (1,549,365 / 1,554,141 / 1,556,475 B) were measured on merges with older dev heads, before #10640 moved the PostHog SDK out of `omo.js`, without a same-container dev-only build; they are not comparable with the table above, which is.

## Tests
- RED first for each module (draft, submit, collect, component) and for both QA-found defects, then GREEN: `bun test packages/omo-senpi/src/components/feedback` 24/24.
- `tsgo --noEmit -p packages/omo-senpi/tsconfig.json`: exit 0.
- `bun run test:senpi`: 5799 pass / 0 fail, then 10 pass / 0 fail, exit 0.


## Review round 1 (REQUEST-CHANGES at e82deb49ad) -> fixed at 2cddcb5867
Each fix has a RED test first.
- `packages/omo-senpi/changes.md` history restored; the feedback entry is added on top (+4 lines vs base).
- Client identity is no longer accepted as free text: the desktop sends named fields (`identity: {accountId, userId, email, displayName, plan, deviceId, deviceName}`); the engine validates ids/email and redacts free-text fields. Only engine-built lines skip the text redactor.
- `prepare` names the session (`sessionId`: a live id, `null` = attach no conversation, omitted = latest live); sessions are tracked per id and dropped on `session_shutdown`.
- Engine logs keep only allowlisted, content-free fields per line (time, level, event, ids, durations, outcome).
- `/bug` sends `bug`, `/feedback` sends `feedback`; token-limit config keys stay readable; at most 8 drafts; write failures are refusals, not crashes; a draft survives a retryable refusal.
- Every upload carries `idempotency-key: feedback-<draftId>` so a resend after a timeout cannot duplicate a report (the intake dedupes on it).
- At 2cddcb5867: `bun run typecheck` exit 0, feedback tests 35/35; test:senpi and the official bundle check run in the local heavy queue before READY.

## Depends on
- senpi PR #3679 release + omo senpi pin bump before the upload path is live (until then the component answers "unavailable").
- omo-service report intake PR (in progress).


## QA & Evidence (live senpi, exact heads)
**What was tested:** the real senpi CLI (`--mode rpc`, mock provider, isolated agent dir and HOME) built from senpi PR #3679 at 44ff8f825d, with this omo plugin at e82deb49ad, and a local mock intake (`POST /v1/reports` -> 201). The seeded session had fake secrets (an `sk-` key in a user message, a `ghp_` token in a tool result with the HOME path on the next line), a custom memory entry with a marker, and engine log lines in `<agentDir>/logs` (including a 1h-old line, a content-keyed line, a non-JSON line and a rotated `.log.1`).
**What was observed (54/54 checks):**
- Desktop RPC path (`omo.feedback.prepare` + `submit` with a desktop log section): exactly 1 POST, `{"kind":"sent","reportId":"rpt_qa1"}`, sections description/identity/environment/session/logs/config, no fake secret, no memory marker, no raw HOME (`workdir ~/projects/demo ok`), stale/content/non-JSON/rotated log lines dropped.
- TUI `/feedback`: select offered `["Send report","See exactly what is sent","Cancel"]`, 1 more POST with the same properties; the notice names only the sections present.
- `OMO_DISABLE_FEEDBACK=1`: 0 POSTs, report saved as 0600 under the agent dir (not under HOME).
- Installed senpi 2026.10.16 (no `redactForUpload`): prepare answers `unavailable`, 0 POSTs.
- Real `~/.senpi/agent` and `~/.omo/agent`: unchanged (changed=0).
**Why it is enough:** it drives both real entry points through the real engine and redactor and checks the bytes that reached the intake; the first run (r1) found two defects (save location, overclaiming notice), both fixed with RED tests and re-proven here.
**What was omitted:** evidence files stay local (they contain the machine name in the identity block). Intake error responses and the real desktop app are covered by the service and desktop PRs.

Evidence (local, `.omo/evidence/omo-senpi-adapter/20261019-feedback-core-live-r2/`):

author: aadehamid
body:
Fixes #251. `epm_facts.py quotes` paired quote marks across paragraphs in a decision record's "Hamid's recorded words" section.

## The bug

`recorded_words` joined the section's blocks into one string. The quote pattern then matched across the joins. The real case was in EPM-DEC-001-0028: a nested quotation ended in an empty pair, `""`. The pattern skipped that pair's first mark and paired its second with the opening mark of the next paragraph's quote. The checker then reported the words in between as an unsaved quote. The workaround was to keep the affected paragraph last.

## The fix

- **Pairing:** `recorded_words` returns one string per block, and `quote_problems` pairs quote marks within each block only.
- **Unclosed quotations:** a paragraph whose quote marks don't pair (an odd count of straight marks, or unequal curly ones) is reported. Without this, an unclosed quotation could go unchecked (Pi round 1).
- **Workaround undone:** EPM-DEC-001-0028's recorded words are back in date order, and the quote check still reports 0 problems.

Pi's review confirmed one more effect. On main, the bad pairing used up an opening mark, so a 41-word quote in 0028 was never checked. It is checked now, and it passes.

## Tests

Four new tests, in `scripts/test_epm_facts.py`:
- the #251 shape;
- an unsaved quote after an empty pair;
- an unclosed quotation;
- unequal curly marks.

The first three fail against main's checker (verified). All 69 tests pass.

## Checks and reviews

- `scripts/check.sh` passes. Figures are unchanged (`commit be7fd39`).
- **Pi round 1 (full, independent):** MERGE-READY with one finding, F1. A paragraph with an unpaired mark yielded no span and no report. Fixed in 624bef5.
- **Pi round 2 (focused on 624bef5):** no blocking findings, and four notes:
  - a dead assertion;
  - a test name that no longer matched its fixture;
  - two docstrings;
  - no test for the curly-quote case.

  All four are fixed in be7fd39, which had no third review (EPM-DEC-001-0028). It passed `check.sh`.
- **Limits Pi named, which stay open:**
  - A paragraph with two unclosed quotations (an even mark count) can still hide unsaved words.
  - Reversed curly marks and fullwidth marks are not seen.
  - The unpaired-mark report covers decision records only, not review CSVs.
  - A lone quote mark inside a code span is reported. That can only block a clean record, never pass an unclean one.

  None affects a current record.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes quote-validation logic and one decision doc ordering only; no runtime or auth paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#251**: the `epm_facts.py quotes` checker no longer pairs quote marks **across paragraphs** in decision records' "Hamid's recorded words" sections.
> 
> **`recorded_words`** now returns **one displayed block per string** instead of joining the section into a single line. **`quote_problems`** runs quote extraction on each block separately, so an empty `""` in one paragraph cannot steal a closing mark from the next. It also **flags paragraphs with unpaired marks** (odd straight `"` count or mismatched curly quotes), so unclosed quotations are not silently skipped.
> 
> **EPM-DEC-001-0028** restores chronological paragraph order in recorded words (the extension quote no longer has to stay last as a workaround).

> **Tests:** four new cases in `test_epm_facts.py` cover the #251 shape, unsaved quotes after `""`, unclosed straight quotes, and unequal curly quotes.

author: samuelloranger
body:
## What

The shared Rawkoon UI kit, the base for the player, details, home/library and nav/settings work. Everything is new code under `rawkoon/ui/kit/`; no Wholphin composable is edited or removed.

- `RawkoonTokens` (colors, radii, focus ring metrics) and `RawkoonMotion` with `rawkoonEnter()` / `rawkoonExit()` (220ms fade + 8dp rise in, 120ms fade out, 150ms color changes, no springs or looping animation).
- `Modifier.rawkoonFocusRing(shape, focused)` and an interaction-source variant: 2dp gap in the app background, then a 2dp apricot ring outside the shape. Controls built on it do not scale on focus.
- `RawkoonButton` (Primary / Secondary / Ghost, optional icon and mono meta), `RawkoonIconButton`, `RawkoonPlayButton`.
- `RawkoonChip`, `TypeChip`, `GenreChip`, `RawkoonStatus` / `RawkoonTone` and `StatusPill`.
- `SectionHeader`, `Kicker`, `RawkoonMonoText`, `UnderlineTabs`.
- `RawkoonPosterCard` (2:3, scrim panel, year and status pills, status bar) and `RawkoonLandscapeCard` (16:9, progress track).
- `RawkoonDialog` / `RawkoonDialogItem` and `RawkoonToast` (with countdown bar).
- Fira Code Regular and Medium as `RawkoonMono` (static instances cut from the upstream variable font, SIL OFL 1.1), listed on the licenses screen.
- Fix: the request and episode pills on the Rawkoon home rows use `StatusPill` (pending amber, approved/downloading sky, ready emerald, denied rose, episode pill in the returning tone) instead of `AppColors.Discover.*`.

## Why

The Rawkoon look (focus ring, status colors, chips, section headers, motion) was only partly applied and each screen would otherwise redo it. Keeping the kit in new files keeps later upstream Wholphin syncs conflict-free: later PRs swap call sites one identifier at a time.

## Wholphin composables the kit replaces (for upstream ports)

Nothing is swapped in this PR yet except the home-row pills. The kit components are the intended replacements for: `ui.components.Button` and `ExpandablePlayButton` (RawkoonButton), `DialogPopup` / `DialogPopupContent` (RawkoonDialog), the plain card/image cards in `ui/cards` (RawkoonPosterCard, RawkoonLandscapeCard), and the plain row title in `ItemRow` (SectionHeader). Each Rawkoon composable's KDoc names what it replaces where that is known.

## Notes

- Fira Code is only published as a variable font in the upstream fonts repo, so the two static weights were instanced from it with fonttools.
- The poster card uses a scrim and gradient instead of a real blur, as blur is unavailable on older TVs.

## How verified

- `JAVA_HOME=<JDK 21> ./gradlew :app:compileDefaultDebugKotlin :app:testDefaultDebugUnitTest -q` passes. New unit tests cover the status tone mapping and colors, the request-chip-to-status mapping, button variant colors and the motion constants.
- `uvx pre-commit run --from-ref origin/rawkoon --to-ref HEAD` passes (ktlint 1.8.0).
- Every component has a `@PreviewTvSpec` preview.
- Visual check on a TV device is still pending (no device attached to the build host).

author: mikeysklar
body:
## What

`refresh()` now flushes the frame buffer with ESP-IDF's cache call.

## Why

On P4 and S31 the old ROM call got the wrong arguments.

| Chip | ROM `Cache_WriteBack_Addr` | Old call |
|---|---|---|
| ESP32-S3 | `(addr, size)` | Correct. Build-tested only, now reached through `esp_cache_msync`. |
| ESP32-P4, S31 | `(map, addr, size)` | Wrong arguments |

| Tested, ESP32-S31-Korvo-1 800x480 | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `refresh()` after writing all 768 KB | 0.06 ms (median of 5) | 0.26 ms (median of 10) |
| Pixels written to `display.framebuffer` | Shown | Shown |
| Plasma demo | 54.3 fps (1 run) | 53.9 to 54.3 fps (3 runs) |
| Builds: Korvo-1, Qualia S3 RGB666 | | Compile |

No visible bug today: the bounce buffers copy the frame through the same cache.

Scope: mipidsi has the same two-argument declaration but never calls it; left alone.

AI assistance: written with Claude Code. I ran the tests above on hardware.

author: demianli
body:
Refs #1629

## 摘要

```text
run.start { client_time_zone? }
  wire-handler：canonicalClientTimeZone（UTC 或 Area/Location，Intl 認得；別名收成正規名）
    壞的 → invalid_argument「run.start 的 client_time_zone …」，先於重送判斷，不進佇列
    好的 → ThreadPump.submit / turnStartOf / userMessageSourceOf
        inbox/spliced 那一件 source.clientTimeZone
        turn/start(kind:'message').clientTimeZone
        user/message(source.kind:'user').clientTimeZone      ← 格式 49
  time-context.foldTimeContext
    deriveBrowserTimeZoneContext(這一輪的 turn/start ＋ user/message)
      resolved → 第一行時鐘換成該時區；第二行 "…Interpret … in this zone."
      mixed    → 第一行用回退時區；第二行 mixed [...] 請模型確認
      missing  → 與 #1625 逐字相同（unavailable）
```

照 dsh `session-controller/src/index.ts:467-482`（驗證）與 `time-context/src/request-zone.ts`（三種讀數、字樣逐字），dsh 在 `687f282e`。web 真的送出是 #1630，在那之前實際跑出來仍是 `unavailable`。

另補 #1625 審查的四項後續：重啟後 9 分鐘內沒有新讀數的常駐格、G 格釘住查找回 `ok`、gap-survey 重判註記、測試註解。

## 證據

- **Before:** `run.start` 帶 `client_time_zone` 被 handler 略過；time-context 第二行永遠 `unavailable`。
  **After:** 新增 `run-start-client-time-zone.test.ts`（10 條：有效／UTC／別名／沒帶位元組相同／無效 6 種字串＋4 種非字串都回 `invalid_argument` 且訊息含 `client_time_zone`／壞時區先於重送判斷／三個位置／舊日誌讀回）、`steer.test.ts` 一條（插話三個位置）、time-context 單元 8 條、宿主 K 組 4 條（resolved／mixed／missing／下一輪不外溢）。
- **突變（每個都跑過、都紅、已還原）：**
  M1 handler 不驗證 → 2 紅；M2 handler 不傳給 start → 3 紅；M3 `turn/start`／inbox source 不帶 → 6 紅；M4 `userMessageSourceOf` 不帶 → steer 1 紅；N1 `turnStartOf` 不帶 → 6 紅；N2 `submit` source 不帶 → 6 紅；N3 wire client 不送 → 5 紅；M5 fold 固定 missing → 3 紅；M6 第一行不換時區 → 1 紅；M7／M8 derive 各忽略一個來源 → 6／3 紅；M9 derive 不驗證 → 1 紅；M10 mixed 不排序 → 2 紅。
  後續項：節流不讀日誌（`last = null`）→ 新的 9 分鐘格紅（單獨跑確認是它）；把 `sessionLookup` 服務對子代理回 `not-attached` → G 兩格紅。**限定**：只在插件那一端把 `ok` 改成 `not-attached` 不會紅（兩條路輸出同一行字，錄的是服務的回答）；G 格釘的是「服務查得到子代理自己那份日誌」，不是「插件有用它」。
- 本機：`pnpm -r --no-bail run typecheck` 0；harness 全套 vitest 414 檔 4751 條全綠；wire／core／time-context／goal／session 各自全綠；eslint（harness、wire、core、time-context）0；prettier 0；`verify-package-invariants`、`verify-tsconfig-paths`、`verify-lib-manifests`、`gen-known-event-types` 0。Node 只有 25.9（沒有 Node 22）。

## 合併風險

**Door:** one-way（日誌格式 49，判準見 `session-store.ts` 32 那段）

**Blast Radius:** run.start 協定、會話日誌格式、time-context 的讀數

- **日誌格式 48 → 49，單向**：既有事件上多的選填欄位，沒有 `ignorable` 可標。**一台 48 的 runtime 讀不了 49 的檔**（`parseHeader` 拋 `SessionFormatUnsupportedError`，`jsonl-session-store.ts:734-741`；只有 `eval/session-scan.ts` 開了 `acceptNewer`），續接時 header 會被改寫成 49。**回滾的後果：發版後退回前一版，被新版碰過的 thread 在舊版打不開**（先前 PR 與註解寫「48 讀新檔照常重建」是錯的，已更正）。沒帶 `client_time_zone` 的送出，日誌與以前位元組相同（有測試）。#1624、#1579 也要升版：誰先合誰拿下一號，後合的 rebase 時把 `session-store.ts` 那段編號往後挪。
- **版本夾具延後到 #1529**：49 還沒出貨、夾具機制還不存在（#1529 OPEN），#1529 已記一筆「49 出貨時補它的版本夾具」。「舊日誌讀回」那格（`run-start-client-time-zone.test.ts`）是**用今天的寫入器造出來的**，不是真正舊版寫的檔，所以它證明的是「不帶時區的日誌今天讀得回」，不是跨版本相容。
- **發版**：#1625、#1629、#1630 同一版出（#1625 合併到 #1630 合併之間不發版）。
- **子代理不繼承時區**：子代理的日誌沒有 `turn/start`，那則讀數第二行是 `unavailable`。dsh 派子代理時同樣沒帶（`manager.ts:464` 給 `{ kind: 'user' }`）；dsh 有的是人直接對子代理說話時 `subagent.prompt` 帶時區，`subagent.send` 帶時區另開 #1734。
- 不在這張：web 送出（#1630）、使用者在設定裡指定時區。

## 偏離 dsh

- **沒有偏離。** 先前的「偏離 1／檔頭偏離 6」（讀日誌時不要求等於本執行期正規名）依 PM 審查**已撤回**，插件讀日誌的驗證回到 dsh 的 `canonical !== value` 就拋（`request-zone.ts:36-37`，`request-zone.spec.ts:52`）。跨 Node／ICU 版本正規名可能不同的風險（Node 25.9 把 `Asia/Kolkata` 收成 `Asia/Calcutta`）另開 #1733 等 demian 決定，發版產物升 Node 之前要有結論。
- 驗證函式放 `@nexus/wire`（`canonicalClientTimeZone`），插件另抄一份格式正規式（插件不 import wire）；dsh 兩邊也是各抄一份。
- 與 dsh 的一處形狀差：dsh 只認帶 `rpcId` 的 user 來源；我們讓時區與 `requestId` 各自獨立（只帶時區沒帶編號也記），讀的時候只看「人話來源上的時區」，結果等價。

## 審查後補強（第二版）

- 插件單元測試補「查找回 `ok`、位址是子代理、日誌有帶時區的 `turn/start` → 第二行 resolved」。**突變：把插件改成只認 root 位址，這一條紅**（其餘 39 條綠；改之前 27 條全綠分不出來）。宿主的 G 格改註明它釘的是服務端。
- 別名測試改成逐字照 dsh：不等於本執行期正規名的別名拋、正規名那個照收（用 `Intl` 自己的回答分辨，不寫死字面）。
- 其他小更正：dsh 行號 `:205-213`、gap-survey 指標 `:454`、`toStrictEqual`、`cordis.patch.yml` 註解。
- 本機：typecheck 0、harness 全套 414 檔 4751 條綠、eslint／prettier 0。

author: jacktheclown91
body:
E10 implementation stacked on E9, focused on anatomical evolution and functional cold/parental-care ecology. `main` unchanged.

### Functional biology
- **`endothermic-core`**, enabled only after ancestral `fur-mantle`, mounts on a real flank organ socket, has body mass, mutation and upkeep costs. It reduces the existing actual thermal loss in sufficiently cold environments when funded with energy; the metabolic energy surcharge is higher in hot climates.
- **`mammary-gland`**, gated on *both ancestral endothermy and live birth*, requires a third finite organ slot and costly upkeep. This necessitates evolving a higher-capacity torso rather than making mammalian anatomy a one-click trait.
- At the **existing funded live-birth authority**, a child is linked to the true birth parent's milk anatomy. Eggs never gain a milk lineage bond even if their parents are lactating. The existing animal body plan inheritance passes the necessary anatomy to the next generation, not living adults.
- The canonical `FamilyController.phaseCare()` now provides anatomically gated nursing. **All milk calories and water are withdrawn from maternal reserves** at greater than 1:1 metabolic energy conversion cost; no parallel milk reserve, free child healing or fabricated nourishment. Maternal reserve floors, actual near-surface contact and a juvenile weaning age gate apply. This complements existing manual mouse-driven 'Tend' action, which becomes **'Nurse'** when the real mother and infant qualify.
- All newborns incur an extra cold-exposure penalty in real low-temperature cells until the young grow, representing a meaningful selection pressure for fur, warmth and contact care. Endothermy and actual nearby nursing parents can partly mitigate that cost but at a real food energy expense. Young from a previously solitary wild lineage receive normal care behaviors if inherited nursing anatomy unlocks them.
- Pure functions live in `src/ecology/mammalian-care.js`; unchanged world objects and the existing fauna metabolism, existing care, existing heredity and existing save serialization remain authoritative.
- **Top-down silhouette art** for new organs uses the same editable procedural part sprite pipeline. No forced side views or extra species templates.

### Testing and limits
Feature-only syntax and focused lifecycle tests in `tests/e10-mammal-cold.mjs`, `.github/workflows/e10-mammal-smoke.yml`. Covers anatomy registry/tissue/sprites, torso socket validity, live-birth ancestry, exact parent relation, finite milk and hydration, cold and hot thermogenic tradeoffs, actual family phase feeding, distance, weaning, saved lactation binding and inability to nurse egg-born young.

**Not delivered by E10:** huge traversable continents, fully ecological tundra vegetation, specialized mammal wild founding populations, true mammalian placentation, automated species derivation, full browser acceptance. These are later distinct milestones. See `docs/e10-mammal-cold.md`. Draft and stacked; do not merge yet.

### Verified targeted result
**PASS:** [E10 GitHub Actions run #39191667262](https://github.com/jacktheclown91/GenVo/actions/runs/39191667262). Feature-only syntax and targeted actual Simulation family-phase smoke passed, including maternal paid milk, warmth in cold, body socket validation, save/load, no egg-born nursing, no remote nursing and weaning. No browser rendering playtest/full regression/performance test yet.

author: k9ksu
body:
Before: the only way to hide a box was to unlock the page and press its Hide button. A box popped out into its own window also stayed on the main page, so it showed twice.

After: the Menu has **Choose which boxes show**, next to Unlock. It lists every box that can be hidden, each with a tick box. Unticking hides the box and ticking shows it again, and the choice is saved to the operator's callsign like Hide is. A map the current kind of logging doesn't use, or a box that's open in its own window, says so in the list. The journal and a QSO's detail aren't listed, because they appear on their own when needed (Principle XV).

A box popped out with ⧉ Pop out now leaves the main page while its window is open. A line above the boxes says "World map is open in its own window. Bring it back". Closing the window, or pressing Bring it back (which closes that window), puts the box back.

How: in `app.js`, the picker is added next to the Unlock button by script, so it follows that button wherever the Menu puts it. A popped-out window announces itself every second over a `BroadcastChannel`, and announces when it closes. The main page leaves out any box it has heard from in the last 3.5 seconds. This is not saved anywhere.

## How to see it working
1. Open Menu, then **Choose which boxes show**. Untick **Log**: the Log box disappears. Reload the page, and it stays hidden. Tick it again to bring it back.
2. Press **⧉ Pop out** on the World map. It opens in a window of its own and leaves the main page, and the line "World map is open in its own window. Bring it back" appears.
3. Close that window. The World map comes back on the main page within a second or two.

## Checks run in this session
- ruff format, ruff check and strict mypy are clean.
- pytest: 561 passed.
- In Chromium: unticking Log hid it and saved `hidden`, and ticking it brought it back. Popping out the World map hid it from the main page and showed the line. Closing the window brought it back. Bring it back closed the window and restored the box. There were no page errors.

Rebased onto #32, so this keeps main's newer Oxy versions: @oxy.so/bloom 13.0.0 (newest 13.x, no Bloom major migration here), @oxy.so/services 11.16.0, @oxy.so/core 6.0.0, @oxy.so/contracts 5.0.0 and @oxy.so/protocol 1.4.0. They are all SDK 58 ready. The rebase also dropped two stale root lock entries (`expo-modules-core` 57.0.20 / `expo-modules-jsi` 57.1.1) that expo-doctor flagged as a duplicate native module.

## Code changes for SDK 58
- `app/_layout.tsx`: expo-router 58 removed `Stack.Screen redirect`; the root Stack swaps `(auth)`/`(app)` with `Stack.Protected guard` (same single authority).
- `app/(app)/index.tsx`: Alia SDK 21 has voice built in; dropped `voiceSession` and the `@alia.onl/sdk/voice` import.
- `app.config.js`: `asyncRoutes: { web: false }` keeps SDK 57's single eager web bundle (`web.output: 'single'` was already explicit).
- CI / deploy: `actions/setup-node` pinned to Node 24 in the jobs that run the Expo CLI (lint, web export, frontend deploy); SDK 58's CLI needs Node 22.13+ / 24.3+.

Checked and not applicable: ImageBackground, InteractionManager, deep `react-native/Libraries` imports, `File.write()`, expo-notifications, custom native modules / AppDelegate subscribers, `@react-navigation/*`. The backend's `NODE_ENV=test bun test` runs under Bun, not the Expo CLI, so SDK 58's per-command NODE_ENV doesn't affect it (the suite passes with it). The frontend has no NODE_ENV scripts and commits no `.env*` files apart from `.env.example`.

GIF/WebP decoders stay ON: OxyProvider's account surfaces include @oxy.so/services' FileViewer / JustifiedPhotoGrid, which render arbitrary files with RN `Image`.

## Verified locally
- `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after the lockfile update; a plain `bun install` leaves `bun.lock` unchanged.
- `bun run typecheck` (backend + frontend, typed routes generated), `biome ci .`, `expo lint .`, `validate:gates`, `validate:agents-md`, the reviewed-image / base-digest / deploy-head gate tests, `bun run build`.

- `expo-doctor`: 19/20. The one remaining check is the Metro `unstable_enableSymlinks` warning, which comes from @oxy.so/app-preset 3.3.0 (accepted fleet-wide).

Compared with an SDK 57 prebuild of main: Android permissions, services and iOS entitlements are identical. Info.plist only gains the generated UIScene manifest, so no plugins were added.

body:
Moves mypy from 1.15.0 to 2.4.0 (published 2026-10-01). No advisory. `mypy src tests scripts` is still clean (21 files).

mypy 2.x adds three dependencies:
- ast-serialize: held at 0.12.1 (2026-10-03) with `--upgrade-package ast-serialize==0.12.1`, because the newest, 0.13.1, came out 2026-10-17 and is inside the 14-day release cooldown. A plain pip-compile later would move it up.
- librt 0.16.0 (2026-09-29).
- pathspec 1.1.1.

Supply-chain checks (Greptile is out of credits this period, so this review stands in for it):
- Fetched the sdist and wheel of mypy 1.15.0 and 2.4.0, and of each new dependency. Every sha256 matches PyPI, and every lock hash is a published digest.
- Diffed old against new and sdist against wheel. The sources match apart from `mypy/version.py`, which the build rewrites as usual. ast-serialize's wheel-only `__init__.py` is the standard maturin shim.
- New code paths are mypy 2's parallel workers, which pass options to a local subprocess over a socket. Nothing calls out to the network.
- ast-serialize and librt are owned by the mypy core devs (jukkal, ilevkivskyi) and published by trusted publishing from mypyc/*. pathspec comes from cpburnz/python-pathspec with provenance. mypy itself has no provenance on either version (consistent), and its owners are unchanged.

Only requirements-dev.in and requirements-dev.txt change.

Gate run locally on a fresh Python 3.12 venv, mirroring the CI job: hash-checked installs, `pip check`, a pip-compile dry run, the secret scan, ruff check and format, mypy (clean), pytest (66 passed), and pip-audit on the dev lock (clean).

body:
Add private daily/weekly scan schedules that dispatch the same typed source handlers and durable runner as manual imports. Users can create/edit/pause/resume schedules, choose local time and IANA timezone, inspect next-run time and open the last run. Dispatch and next-due advancement are atomic; restart produces one latest catch-up, overlaps are skipped, and changed local Gmail grants require explicit resume.

Also record the user's early-visibility rule: push a meaningful planning commit when starting each feature branch, then retain the final verified commit/push/PR/merge/cleanup sequence. Applied on this branch in 5742bdb before finished implementation.

Validation: 354 backend / 133 frontend tests; Ruff, strict mypy, TypeScript, Oxlint, Prettier, wheel/frontend builds and refreshed code graph. Covers DST gaps/folds, half/quarter-hour zones, concurrency, replay, quotas, isolation, stale edits, frozen scopes, changed grants, snapshot restore and UI retry/edit/pause. Migration 0019 adds schedules; first-party tzdata supports Windows and Linux.

Gmail is mocked only. No live personal-data/AI requests or Docker deployment. Remote provider failures remain visible on runs. Chat scan-start tools and automatic extraction from imported email are outside this slice.

author: danbradbury
body:
## Summary

Windows gets its own process discovery, login service, window switching, installer, release archives and CI, so setup matches the other platforms:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DanBradbury/firekeeper/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

- **Discovery:** `ps` and `lsof` are answered natively on Windows (Toolhelp snapshot; command line and cwd read from the process environment block) behind the existing `Run` test seam. Windows-quoted command lines and either path separator are parsed identically on every platform. Codex falls back to matching recent threads by cwd, since open files can't be listed.
- **SQLite:** new `internal/sqlitejson` runs `sqlite3` when present and reads read-only in-process otherwise, so Windows needs no `sqlite3`.
- **Daemon:** `LockFileEx` locks; a per-user Task Scheduler logon task (no admin, hidden console, restart on failure). Status uses exit codes and the lock file, never localized `schtasks` text.
- **TUI:** `s` raises the terminal window hosting the runtime (`internal/winterm`); tabs inside Windows Terminal are not addressable.
- **Redaction:** `C:\Users\x`, `C:/Users/x` and `/c/Users/x` count as home.
- **Install/release:** `install.ps1` (checksum-verified, no admin, upgrades a running binary), Windows zips for amd64/arm64 in GoReleaser, self-update runs `install.ps1`.
- **CI:** new Windows job (build, vet, tests, Windows-only tests that must run, real Task Scheduler round trip, installer under PowerShell 7 and 5.1), `GOOS=windows go vet` in the Linux job, `.gitattributes` for LF checkouts.
- **Docs:** README Windows section; AGENTS.md platform rules.

## Verification

- Linux: `gofmt`, `go build`, `go vet`, `go test -race ./...` all pass; `GOOS=windows|darwin go vet ./...` clean; Windows amd64/arm64 binaries build with `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- `scripts/test-install.ps1` passes under PowerShell 7 on Linux.
- **Not run on Windows.** The Windows-only code (`*_windows.go`, the `schtasks` registration, PATH editing, replacing a running exe) has only been compiled and vetted; the new Windows CI job is its first real run.

## Known limitations

- Logon-task creation without elevation relies on the trigger naming the current user; unverified on a real standard account.
- Codex-on-Windows matching is by cwd among threads from the last 24h, so a just-closed session in the same directory can be misattributed.
- Window switching raises the window, not the tab.
- Windows binaries are not code-signed.
- Claude Desktop install paths excluded from discovery are a best guess.
