author: elemperor1
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"Elemperor1"} -->
_Requested by **Jacob** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01J5Wo2baMAqpqr4eWLBCTmk?thread=cmsg_01J5Wo2baMAqpqr4eWLBCTmk69cauTTdUuXDyVnm3iZBo7)_

Before: a saved game kept nothing of the Fallout side of the game. Loading one reset the quests, the global variables, the variables of every script and the clock shift as for a new game, and the save had no version of its own for any of it.

After: a save carries a `FOSV` record for each section of the state of Fallout (`format`, `globals`, `quests`, `objects`, `controls`, `talking`, `packages`), each with its own version, the first one with the version of the whole. Loading puts them back: the stage of each quest, the stages done, the objectives, the journal, the timer and delay and the variables of the quest script, the globals and the clock shift, the variables of object scripts, the controls the player was refused, the characters that talking activators speak for and the packages scripts gave. A save from a newer engine is refused with the "requires a newer version" message, a section this engine does not know is skipped with a warning, a save with no `FOSV` record starts the scripts as a new game does, and a damaged section stops the load with a message instead of a crash.

This is the first slice of M7 (the roadmap paragraph has the plan in its text). The ESM4 references, the characters and the rest of the state follow in the next slices.

How: `FalloutScript::SaveWriter` and `SaveReader` (`components/falloutscript/savestate.*`) write little endian numbers, size-prefixed lists in key order (so a state read and written again is the same bytes) and form ids that the reader maps through the same map of plugins the other records use; every read is checked against the bytes left. Each class of the state names `FalloutScript::SaveAccess<T>` as its friend, so a section's code lives in a file of its own and the headers do not change again when a section does (that is the header sweep in this diff: one friend declaration and one include in each class). `OFScript::FalloutScripts::saveSections()` lists the sections; `StateManager` writes them after the world and hands `REC_FOSV` records back on load. The section bytes are a raw subrecord (a text subrecord is re-encoded and ends at the first zero byte, which the smoke run caught).

Tested: 3,020 component tests (13 new: round trips, byte-equal write-read-write, plugins that moved or are gone, a script that changed, truncated and absurd sizes) and 736 host tests pass. `fallout_start_smoke_test.py --only saves` saves a running game from a Lua menu script, changes a global and a quest, loads it in the same engine, then starts a second engine with `--load-savegame`: stages, stages done, the objective and the global are the saved ones in both and still are three seconds later (the quests that ran before the save do not run again).

author: vkehfdl1
body:
## Problem
The Quick Look TIFF viewer decoded in the page with UTIF, synchronously on the page's only thread.
- A 21MB scan took **0.4-7.3s run to run**, and the page was unresponsive meanwhile.
- A TIFF over the 32MB whole-file cap was **never shown** (the panel said it was too large).

## Change
- `node/tiff.ts` (new): on macOS `sips` decodes the file to a PNG in the main process and the panel shows it. This is the route HEIC already takes.
  - A picture longer than 2048px on its long side is shrunk to it.
  - A smaller picture is **not** resized. Found by testing: sips's `--resampleHeightWidthMax` scales *up* as readily as down (an 8px TIFF came back 2048px wide), so the option is only passed when the picture is larger than the cap. My first version passed it always, and a test written against that behaviour had to be rewritten.
- Off macOS the in-page decoder stays, but a TIFF over 8MB now arrives without bytes and the panel shows the file's info instead of freezing.
- `node/sips.ts` (new): the sips runner, scratch folder, and failure handling that `heic.ts` carried, now shared by both. `heic.ts` shrinks to its own options. HEIC behaviour is unchanged (its 4 real-app checks and 10 unit tests pass).
- `byteNeed("tiff")` becomes `"decode"`; `TiffView` takes the PNG without UTIF.

## Measured in the built app
M4 Max, production build, Space to picture shown. 2 rounds x 3 runs, before/after interleaved.

| file | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 21MB scan, 3000x2500 | median **3.76s** (0.41-7.29s) | **0.26s** (0.26-0.28s) |
| 35MB TIFF, 12MP (past the 32MB cap) | **never shown** (6/6) | **0.27s** (6/6) |
| 3MB, 1200x900 | 65ms | 93ms |

- The small file gets **28ms slower** (a sips process start). I am not hiding that.
- The old decoder's own stall was only 0.07-0.25s in this harness. The time was spent after the stall, so the stall figure understates the delay; the 3.8s median above is the user-visible number.
- Not measured: Windows or Linux (unchanged, in-page decoder plus the 8MB limit), multi-page TIFF (only the first page is shown, as before), CMYK/16-bit/odd TIFFs beyond the 24-bit RGB ones I generated.

## Verification
- TDD: `test/preview-tiff.test.ts` (16 tests) was written before the modules and failed first. It covers routing, the sips arguments, scratch cleanup, fallback on tool failure or empty output, never shelling out off macOS, the 8MB cap, and real-sips cases (own size kept, shrink to 2048, pixel size probe).
- `bun run test`: 2105 passed. `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- Live E2E / manual QA: new lane `quick-look-tiff` (real Space on the built app, registered in `run-all.mjs`): 11/11. It checks time, page stall, decoded size, no enlargement, and that left is red and right is blue. Run on the pre-change build it fails: `long side is shrunk to 2048` gives 6000x800, and it then crashes on the 5000x4000 scan because no picture is shown. So it catches the regression.
- Existing lanes: `quick-look-heic` 4/4, `quick-look-reference` 122/122.
- Screenshot of the 5000x4000 result reviewed: red/blue halves, title, "Open with Preview".

## Not in this PR
Spreadsheets (#236).

author: sargunv
body:
Gabled and gambrel roofs on L/T/U footprints now follow the arms, with valleys at reflex corners and vertical gables at inferred arm ends. This builds on #5, now merged into `main`.

The Zig and TypeScript twins identify terminal hips with the ordinary skeleton, then build a second wavefront with those eaves stationary. Unholed footprints filling at least 98% of their bounding rectangle retain the frame profile; existing rectangle, rotated-rectangle, square and full-vertex rectangle fixtures are unchanged. Direction and orientation are ignored on the arm/courtyard skeleton path. Other unholed outlines without a qualifying end retain the frame.

Courtyards now work for every frame shape: gabled/gambrel use skeletons; the other frame shapes clip their height fields around holes and raise courtyard walls to the roof. Radial courtyard roofs stay flat. The shapes gallery and contact sheet add T, U and courtyard footprints, and native rendering adds eight close views.

## Decisions and remaining work

- Half-hipped and saltbox-family arms retain their frame profiles. Half-hips need a height-dependent change in edge motion; asymmetric/flat-top profiles need explicit rules at arm junctions.
- Mansard retains its profile after comparing renders, the OSM wiki drawing and OSM2World's profile. The two-thirds-height break matches; hip/ridge placement differs.
- Keep the 192-vertex cap. Gable inference may build two skeletons, and no complexity improvement justifies increasing it.
- No host patch for cut copies. The gap ledger now distinguishes cut metadata, complete GeoJSON geometry, source-supplied roof data, and cross-worker stitching. Bounds alone cannot reconstruct a skeleton.

Stationary edges keep arm junctions in the existing event solver. Moving unweighted apexes would require repairing shared junctions; rectangle decomposition would introduce separate overlap, valley and hole rules. Gable-end selection is an inference; arbitrary irregular outlines can retain the frame, and a closed courtyard wing can have a continuous hipped ridge.

## Review fix

Band clipping now uses the existing tolerant break-line classification in both twins. On the seed-2 comb, a collapse at `6.5000000000000036` coincides with the slope break at `6.499999999999993`. Exact comparisons discarded collinear event vertices and generated slivers that vanished in float32, leaving unmatched horizontal roof edges. Retaining vertices on the break in both bands closes the gambrel and mansard roofs without a fallback or a new watertightness pass. A shared comb fixture checks both shapes with along/across orientations and explicit/default directions, including closed-surface invariants.

Both twins share one skeleton height helper between roof vertices and stationary-wall stops and name the rectangle-fill threshold. TypeScript now shares the radial-shape predicate too; Zig already did. The geometry notes are removed, with rationale here and the float32 limitation in the README. The benchmark script is unchanged.

## Measurements

Whole polygons rounded to the zoom-16 grid, no source cuts, Node 24.21.0 on macOS arm64; median of three passes after warmup. Tagged passes use roof:shape with default direction/orientation. Times are totals for the dataset, not frame times.

- Bamberg tagged non-flat (1,319 polygons): flat fallbacks 3 -> 2; about 33 -> 71 ms.
- Bamberg forced gabled (3,091): 14 -> 0 fallbacks; 30 -> 212 ms. Forced gambrel: 14 -> 0; 50 -> 211 ms.
- Invalides forced gabled/gambrel (3): 3 -> 0 fallbacks for each; about 0.7 -> 86 ms and 0.5 -> 74 ms. The baseline only triangulated flat roofs.
- Rounded 192-vertex polygon: about 25 -> 35 ms. A 1,000-vertex input is rejected by the cap immediately.

## Validation

- `mise run test`, `mise run check`, `mise run build` pass.
- `mise run //plugins/building/native:render-test`: 39 Metal frames pass pixel and query checks, using the existing FFI install read-only.
- Shared fixtures cover L/T/U, courtyard cases and Invalides; independent tests check gable ends and roof coverage. Both twins test near-coincident gable wall stops.
- Fuzz seed 1, 300 iterations: zero failing layouts; the separate touching-courtyard test retains the same 7/3,000 triangulation failures as the baseline.
- Fuzz seed 2, 300 iterations: parent `b328f0a` 12 failing layouts, reviewed head `c2f9805` 16, fixed head 8. All four new comb gambrel failures and four existing comb mansard failures are closed; the remaining eight layout failures and 10/3,000 touching-courtyard failures persist.
- Inspected the contact sheet, native arm/courtyard close views and Bamberg. Very thin roof strips retain the documented subpixel float32 rounding limitation.

Local review renders: `/tmp/building-contact-sheet.svg.png`, `/tmp/building-native/shapes-gabled-t.png`, `/tmp/building-native/shapes-gambrel-u.png`, `/tmp/building-native/shapes-gabled-courtyard.png`, `/tmp/building-native/osm-inselstadt.png`. Baseline renders are in `/tmp/building-native-before/` and `/tmp/building-before.svg.png`.

author: etanhey
body:
## Summary
Etan, live on 2.2.46: "the scrub doesn't work at all." The teleprompter scrubber was unmounted in ended/idle readback, showed 0:00/0:00 during Replay, and stuck on a stale "so far…" total during long reads. Readback and replay also looked like a different panel from live speaking.

**Part 1: scrubber**
- Ended/idle readback keeps the scrubber, showing the **retained, seekable** duration and the stop position. Drag or click seeks through SEEK2's existing `scope: "readback"` + `readback_id` path; there's no new seek protocol.
- Idle history Replay: the probed file duration becomes the job's own `durationMs` before retention. Live seeks, the retained readback and the advertised `duration_ms` now agree, which fixes 0:00/0:00.
- Long reads broadcast `playback_duration {long_read_id, duration_ms, final}` as chunks synthesize. Once all chunks exist, `long_read.estimated_total_ms` is set, and the "so far…" label clears.
- Speaking edges carry `readback_duration_ms`: the contiguous retained span (`RetainedReadback.seekableMs`). A long read stopped before its lookahead plays therefore never offers unreachable time.

**Part 2: readback/replay layout parity** (QA 2026-10-19 03:48, Findings 1–2)
- Readback uses the speaking chrome: fixed `Theme.teleprompterViewportHeight` viewport, scrubber, spacer. The dismiss control is kept.
- The reserved trailing wing shows the same `VoiceBarNotchWaveform` as a dimmed, still bed (`TimelineView` paused: no idle clock).
- Short text sits vertically centred; long text still scrolls from word 0.
- Equal teleprompter label slots centre the track on the panel axis. "so far…" hangs under the total, and wider spacing clears the knob.
- No scroll indicators in either mode. A legacy scroller gutter was shifting readback text 8.5 pt left.
- Sub-second reads label `0:01`. Labels hide without a duration and dim when the row can't seek.

No recording, F5, capture or admission changes. `docs/tts-seek.md` is updated.

## Review loop (2 rounds)
Implementer: Claude Opus 5.5. Reviewers: Codex gpt-6.1-sol (code) + Claude Opus 5.5 with `frontend-design` (UI renders).
- **R1 @ 4f0c6895: CHANGES.**
  - Sol (2 blocking): (1) the history-Replay scrubber couldn't seek, because the duration was broadcast-only and not job/retained metadata; (2) a stopped long read advertised unretained lookahead time.
  - Opus UI (1 blocking + 5 minor): the scrub row sat 24 pt left of centre (blocking); long readback jumped 8.5 pt and showed a legacy scroller; sub-second 0:00/0:00; no text counterpart for the readback position; the knob overhung the labels; meaningless edge rows.

body:
The upload workspace previously retained only the first 200 table rows, and single-cell exploration was limited to synthetic teaching views. This change adds bounded workflows for inspecting actual processed data and tracing measurements to sample metadata.

Changes:
- Import gene-by-cell CSV/TSV with exact cell-ID metadata joins, 10x-style Matrix Market bundles, and versioned dense/CSR single-cell packages.
- Add an optional H5AD API reader for dense/CSR/CSC X, obs/var annotations, categorical/nullable metadata, and supplied embeddings. Files are bounded and temporary uploads are deleted.
- Explore supplied UMAP/t-SNE/PCA/spatial coordinates, gene values, cell/gene annotations, and descriptive group summaries. Export and reopen the complete loaded single-cell package.
- Retain all accepted table rows with pagination, full-table search, and CSV export. Link long/wide omics tables through unique sample IDs and expose missing or ambiguous links.
- Include a reproducible PBMC3k marker subset (2,638 cells, 16 genes) with source checksum/licensing, and reuse the existing documented TCGA matched RNA/protein subset.
- Add sample metadata templates and workflow/format documentation. Phylogenetic features remain removed.

Validation:
- 28 frontend tests, TypeScript checks, JavaScript syntax check, and production build pass.
- 22 backend tests and Ruff pass, including a compatibility test using AnnData's own H5AD writer.
- Chromium browser checks pass for public datasets, gene coloring, embedding selection, cell views, export/reimport, TCGA links, desktop/mobile layouts, guided CSV/Matrix Market input, and H5AD import through the configured API. No browser runtime errors were observed.
- The removed workspace still returns HTTP 404.

Scope:
These are processed-data exploration workflows. Embeddings/clusters are supplied, not recomputed. Raw-data readers for BAM/CRAM, Cooler, vendor MS/mzML, FCS and microscopy images remain external conversion routes. H5AD requires the optional API; no durable server storage or live-site deployment is included.

See docs/REAL_DATA.md and docs/FORMAT_SUPPORT.md for supported formats, bounds, and source provenance.

```text
    PageList: retained rows, tracked positions, resize

```

Adds screen cursor operations, attributes, clearing, scrolling, resize and lazy alternate-screen state. Reuses page-list storage and typed partial-failure handling; no new dependency or printer.

Closes #1358.

## Evidence

- **Before:** screen operations were absent; the initial coding witnesses failed to compile. The final resize witnesses also exposed missing wide-cell support in the test fixture.
- **After:** all 149 planned cases and the added ownership/boundary regressions pass. `cargo nextest run --locked -p maestro-terminal --no-fail-fast`: 753 passed, zero skipped. Doctests: one passed.
- The installed signed-commit hook passed workspace formatting, Clippy, strict rustdoc and conventions through `just check`.
- Committed production change: 1,160 added code lines, 10 deleted. No manifest or lockfile changes.
- Graph check flags increased use of the existing `StorageError` owner (degree 40 to 56). New screen methods reuse this typed storage boundary rather than introducing another error model; affected callers remain in the terminal crate.

## Root cause

| Missing behavior | Owner | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| Screen state and cursor operations | `screen`, `screen_set`, `kitty::key` | Full 149-case matrix, including managed values and page crossings |
| Duplicate hyperlink admission required spare string capacity | `Page::insert_hyperlink` | Reusing a live identity succeeds without allocating duplicate bytes; direct page and screen regressions pass |
| Cursor references could outlive rewritten page storage | `Screen` cursor migration | Both erasure routes have failing root/linked-write witnesses before the fix and pass afterward; managed background, style, link and reset controls pass |

| Wide-cell resize fixtures treated every scalar as narrow | Integration-test writer and reader | Wide heads/tails, wrapping, removal and cursor reflow now pass |

## Docs

Public items have rustdoc. `docs/terminal-emulator.md#screens` describes defaults, cursor operations, managed clearing/scrolling, resize/prompt policy and alternate state. HUMANIZER docs/terminal-emulator.md: 0 fixes.

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** terminal.

The page hyperlink-admission and zero-byte allocation fixes also affect managed page copies. Existing page/history tests pass. Shared CI owns full-workspace tests and coverage; independent review and those results remain pending. No merge is requested here.

author: bunnysayzz
body:
## Checklist

 - [x] Read the [contributing guide](https://github.com/mockito/mockito/blob/main/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)
 - [x] PR should be motivated, i.e. what does it fix, why, and if relevant how
 - [x] Avoid other runtime dependencies
 - [x] Mention `Fixes #<issue number>` in the description _if relevant_
 - [x] At least one commit should end with `Fixes #<issue number>` _if relevant_

## What

`verify(mock, after(x))` busy-spins: `VerificationOverTimeImpl.verify()` only sleeps `pollingPeriodMillis` on the delegate-failure path (`handleVerifyException`). On the success path with `returnOnSuccess=false` it just sets `error = null` and loops again, so the delegate gets polled back-to-back for the whole duration (measured ~4.6M polls in 200ms in the issue).

## Fix

One line: sleep the polling period on the success path too, so `after()` polls at the configured frequency like it does on the failure path. `timeout()` (`returnOnSuccess=true`) is untouched, it still returns immediately.

Fixes #3868

## Tests

Added `should_sleep_between_successful_polls_when_not_returning_on_success` to `VerificationOverTimeImplTest`: runs `after()` with a 200ms duration and always-satisfied delegate, asserts the full duration elapses and the delegate is polled a bounded number of times (`atLeast(2)`, `atMost(20)`). On current code the delegate gets hit millions of times in that window, so the test fails; with the fix it passes.

Honest note: I could not run the suite locally (no JDK on this machine), so CI is the verification gate here. The change is a single added `sleep()` call in an existing `else` branch, matching the failure path right below it.

author: youknowone
body:
Three slices of the `portal-interpret` work (#1942), on current main.

### 1. `co_flags & CO_*`, LOAD_CONST from the promoted `co_consts_w`, cells unwrapped in `locals()`
- `astcompiler/consts.rs` carries the `CO_*` flag words. `PyFrame::co_flags()` returns `self.code().flags.bits()`, and frame-flag reads become `co_flags & CO_*`. This is the `pyframe.py` / `pycode.py` shape.
- The translator lowers `bits()` on the transparent flags word to an integer read. The `code_flags_method` `bits` arm in `front/mir.rs` does this, so the interpreter source keeps the `bitflags` idiom.
  - Before this, the opaque foreign `bits()` stayed as a residual call with no function pointer inside `fast2locals`. That residual miscompiled `locals()`.
- `constant_at` reads `co_consts_w` from `jit::promote(self.pycode)`, so LOAD_CONST returns the same object identity each time. This matches `pyopcode.py LOAD_CONST` / `getconstant_w`.
- `locals()` now unwraps cellvar and freevar slots by position and always calls `cell.get()`, as `pyframe.py fast2locals` does.
  - This fixes a bug on main: with `PYRE_NO_JIT=1`, `locals()` could return the `cell` object itself.
  - Cause: a nursery collection during the snapshot made the `is_cell` test miss.
- Tests:
  - `constant_at_returns_same_identity_for_nested_code_tuple_and_str`
  - `locals_returns_cellvar_and_freevar_values_not_cells`
  - the `bits` / `fast2locals` cases in `code_flags_methods_lower_to_integer_ops`

### 2. A promoted-const initializer call lowers to the global or literal it copies
- `lower_global_initializer_call` handles a call whose callee is a promoted-const initializer that only copies a global or a literal. The call becomes a read of that global or a constant op, instead of a residual call.
- `const_lit_to_op` now maps enum discriminants to `ConstInt`.
- Four tests in majit-translate.

### 3. A portal guard failure traces from the rebuilt resume framestack
- `PyreJitState::trace_from_guard_resume_position` passes the framestack rebuilt from the resume data to `trace_jitcode_at_resume_framestack`. Each frame keeps its own jitcode, as in `pyjitpl.py MetaInterp.handle_guard_failure` → `resume.py rebuild_from_resumedata`.
- Test: `portal_guard_resume_hands_framestack_to_trace_walk`.

### Verification
- Hand-fold census is unchanged: 50 rows / 43 functions.
- fmt, citation and boundary checks pass.
- Full `cargo test --all --no-default-features --features dynasm,pyre-module` passed before the rebase: 12766 tests.
- After the rebase onto d2f965af16f: `cargo test -p majit-translate`, `-p pyre-interpreter --features dynasm` and `-p pyre-jit-trace --features dynasm,prepass --lib` pass.
- The second rebase, onto e33de85e231, touched no common files, and patch-ids are unchanged.
- `pyre/check.py --synthetic-only` (dynasm, cranelift, wasm): every `locals_*` row and `recursive_forced_frame_kept_stack` pass on all three backends. The only red rows are ones that are already red on main.

### Not included
Callees without a function pointer still become residual calls with a symbolic address hash. A report-only census across the prepass found 1168 such callees in 3656 graph/callee pairs. Making each one nameable, then turning the refusal on (`jtransform.py handle_residual_call` needs a real funcptr), is left for a separate change.

author: albertodeluigi
body:
Roadmap item E7, "reconnected own node tSEQ" repeating in the console.

## Cause
`pruneDeadOwnLegs`, run by the 12-second liveness sweep and on focus, treated an own node's signer link as dead unless `connected === true`. During a slow start (handshake, waiting for the node id) every sweep therefore dropped the leg, and the next `reconnectOwnNodes` "reconnected" it. `connectProvisioned` returns early while a signer exists, so there was no second WebSocket. Each pass still re-ran the node checks after it: `waitNodeReady`, `/status`, and up to ten `/node/onchain` reads. It also logged another *reconnected own node*.

## Fix
A link in the SDK's `connecting`, `handshaking`, `authenticated` or `node_id` phase counts as alive. A link that fails ends in `error` within 30 s (`whenNodeId`) and is retried as before. Wake signals (online, a long background) still force a rebuild.

## Also checked
- **Repeated WebSocket closes:** the closes seen in the local proxy, after 40 to 160 s, were page reloads. Without reloads a link stayed up for 3 hours; the relay pings every 15 s.
- **Failing WebSockets:** the `/lsp-ws-asset` and `/lsp-ws-btc` failures are the retired demo signers, which answer 502 on the box (#87).
- A clean load does one provision, one WebSocket and one on-chain read.

`node --test`: 678 passed, 0 failed.

body:
This PR introduces live currency rate integration via Frankfurter, refines contact detail and GST validation warnings (making them non-blocking for exports/issuances), and improves PDF/Excel layout styling for proforma invoices (PI) and single-SKU scenarios.

Key Features & Updates
1. Live Currency Rates & Background Scheduler
Frankfurter API Integration: Added automated syncing for USD-based reference rates (INR, AED, GBP, EUR) using official central bank sources via [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev/).

Background Scheduler & Configuration: Implemented a background thread with adjustable intervals (1 to 168 hours) to keep rates updated automatically.

Stale Rate Protections: Added rate-staleness detection (excluding rates older than 10 days from new conversions) while ensuring historical invoices retain their recorded amounts.

UI Updates: Modernized the currency rates configuration panel with live health indicators, last-fetch timestamps, manual Refresh now controls, and interval settings.

2. Non-Blocking Contact & GST Warnings
Flexible Validation: Missing contact details (Tel/Phone, PIC, Email) and GST No. (for INR) now trigger advisory bottom-right warnings and inline red *required prompts in the editor and exports without blocking PDF/Excel generation or saved downloads.

Smart Parsing & Cleanup: Improved parsing logic for party blocks and calling codes (ITU E.164).

3. PDF & Excel Export Layout Enhancements
Single-SKU Layouts: Refined row heights, spacing, and vertical alignment for single-SKU items and compact tables.

Table Borders: Updated section borders to keep summaries open above initial amounts and ensure clean vertical dividers across tables.

Excel Formatting: Enhanced numeric and currency formatting (#,##0.00) alongside rich text support for required field markers.

author: apoorvdarshan
body:
## Problem Raw HTML in package READMEs is printed as literal text: `

` badge rows, `` badges, `

`, HTML comments. The server-rendered https://database.dev/kiwicopple/supa_audit contains `<p`, `<a href=` and `<img src=` as text. react-markdown keeps README HTML as `raw` nodes, and with no plugin to parse them it turns each into a text node. ## Fix - Parse the HTML with `rehype-raw`, then run `rehype-sanitize` with its default (GitHub-style) schema. It keeps `align`, `width`/`height`, http(s) image `src`, `details`/`summary` and tables, and removes `script`, `iframe`, `on*` handlers, `javascript:` URLs and `class`/`style`. Sanitizing is required: READMEs come from any publisher, pages are server-rendered, and the CSP allows `script-src 'unsafe-inline'`. - Sanitize runs before `rehype-highlight`, so highlight.js classes survive. - Sanitize prefixes ids with `user-content-` (DOM clobbering). remark-rehype already prefixes footnote ids, so it now uses `clobberPrefix: ''`, and a small plugin gives in-page `#…` links the same prefix. Footnotes keep GitHub's `#user-content-fn-1` fragments. ## Tests New `website/__tests__/markdown.integration.test.tsx`: raw HTML renders as elements; unsafe HTML is removed and README ids can't clobber page ids; SQL fences keep highlighting and the copy button; footnote and raw-HTML anchor links resolve. On master 2 of the 4 fail; with the fix all pass, and removing any part of the fix fails at least one. `TZ=UTC pnpm exec vitest run --coverage` (CI's `test:coverage`): 28/28. Prettier as in CI, `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint on the changed files and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` are clean. ## Notes - `rehype-raw` adds parse5: about 54 kB gzipped to the package page's markdown bundle. - CSP `img-src` still limits external images (e.g. to `img.shields.io` and `github.com`), as for markdown images today. - #490 also touches `markdown.tsx` (styling only, no raw HTML); the two changes merge cleanly apart from `pnpm-lock.yaml`. author: outductor
body:
## 概要
`/buckets/$id` に「バケット設定」セクション(オブジェクトブラウザの下)を追加し、クォータ・Website access・CORS・Lifecycle の編集と、未完了マルチパートアップロードの確認 / cleanup を UI から行えるようにしました。

Closes #376

## 変更内容
### backend
- `POST /api/buckets/{id}/cleanup-uploads` を追加。body `{"olderThanSecs": N}` を受け、URL の bucket ID を注入して Garage `POST /v2/CleanupIncompleteUploads` (`{bucketId, olderThanSecs}`) に転送。レスポンス `{"uploadsDeleted": N}` はそのまま返す。
  - `olderThanSecs` の欠落 / null / 負数 / 小数 / 文字列 / 4KiB 超の body は Garage に送らず JSON の 400 (欠落を 0 = 全件削除と解釈させないため)。
  - 成功時は一覧のキャッシュを破棄 (一覧に未完了アップロード数が出るため)。
- 既存の `PUT /api/buckets/{id}` → `UpdateBucket` は変更なし。`websiteAccess` / `quotas` / `corsRules` / `lifecycleRules` を含む body が無変更で転送され、成功時のみキャッシュが破棄されることをテストで固定。

### frontend
- `api.ts`: `BucketDetail` / `UpdateBucketBody` 型を Garage の `GetBucketInfoResponse` / `UpdateBucketRequestBody` に合わせて追加 (`unfinishedMultipartUploads` / `...Bytes` / `...Parts`、`websiteConfig` はキー省略・`errorDocument: null` あり、`corsRules` / `lifecycleRules` はキー省略あり)。`getBucket` / `updateBucket` を型付けし、`cleanupIncompleteUploads` を追加。
- 新規 `components/bucket-settings.tsx` (`buckets.$id.tsx` はローカルの誤った型定義を削除し、import とマウント 1 箇所のみ追加):
  1. **クォータ**: 容量 (数値 + B/KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB) とオブジェクト数、それぞれ「無制限」トグル。既存値は割り切れる最大の単位で表示。
  2. **Website access**: 有効/無効スイッチ、インデックス / エラードキュメント、ルーティングルール JSON (Experimental)。無効化は確認ダイアログで「設定が破棄される」旨を警告。routingRules は編集時のみ送信 (省略で現状維持)。
  3. **CORS ルール** / 4. **ライフサイクルルール**: JSON 編集 (Experimental)、構文・配列チェック、「例を挿入」。変更時のみ送信、`[]` 保存は確認のうえ全削除。
  5. **未完了マルチパートアップロード**: 件数 / パート数 / サイズを表示し、「N 時間/日 以上前」で cleanup。1 時間未満は警告、結果は削除件数をトースト表示。
- 各カードは 保存 (変更時のみ primary) と リセット。失敗時は ApiError のメッセージをトーストとカード内に表示し、フォームは保持。成功時は `['bucket', id]` と `['buckets']` を invalidate (カードはサーバ値で re-key され保存値にリセット)。

## テスト
- `go vet ./... && go test ./...` (新規 `handler_buckets_test.go`: PUT の無変更転送とキャッシュ破棄 / Garage エラー転送時はキャッシュ維持 / cleanup の bucketId 注入 / 不正 body の 400)。
- ローカル Garage v2.4.1 に対する env-gated `TestBucketSettingsIntegration` (i376- バケットを作成・削除): quotas / website + routingRules / CORS / lifecycle の設定、`[]` 削除と省略時の維持、website 無効化で設定が消えること、不正 lifecycle の 400、cleanup のレスポンス形状。
- `npm run lint && npm run build` (tsc 含む)。

## ブラウザ検証手順
テスト用バケット (例: `i376-check`) を作成して `/buckets/<id>` を開き、ページ下部の「バケット設定」で:
1. **クォータ**: 容量の「無制限」を外し `10` `GiB` → 保存が primary になる → 保存 → トースト、再読込後も `10 GiB` 表示。リセットで編集前に戻ること、`0` や空欄で保存が無効になることを確認。オブジェクト数も同様。両方「無制限」に戻して保存。
2. **Website access**: スイッチを有効 → `index.html` / `404.html` を入力して保存。ルーティングルールに `[{"Condition":{"KeyPrefixEquals":"a/"},"Redirect":{"ReplaceKeyPrefixWith":"b/"}}]` を入れて保存 → 再読込で HttpRedirectCode 302 付きで表示される。`[{` など壊れた JSON でエラー表示・保存不可。スイッチを無効 → 保存 → 確認ダイアログ (設定破棄の警告) → 無効にする。
3. **CORS ルール**: 「例を挿入」→ 保存 → 「現在 1 件のルール」。`[]` にして保存 → 削除確認ダイアログ → 削除で 0 件。`{"a":1}` (配列でない) でエラー表示。
4. **ライフサイクルルール**: 「例を挿入」→ 保存。`"Status":"Bogus"` にして保存 → Garage のエラー (Invalid lifecycle configuration) がトーストとカード内に出て、入力が保持されること。
5. **未完了マルチパートアップロード**: 件数 / パート数 / サイズが表示される。`30` `時間` で「古いアップロードを削除」→ 確認 → 「N 件の未完了アップロードを削除しました」トースト。`0.5 時間` にすると 1 時間未満の警告が出る (ダイアログ文にも反映)。(未完了アップロードを作るには `aws s3api create-multipart-upload --bucket i376-check --key x` などで作成し、`0 時間` で削除できる)
6. キーの権限・オブジェクトブラウザ・上部のサマリーが従来どおり動くこと。最後にテスト用バケットを削除。

author: haozeke
body:
Three ljos bugs from the willma-20261018d run (bench a523b77).

- **A named commit leaves the empty issue the hook filed** (ljos-u40m). In 10 of 12 cells, session 2's first edit filed a new issue, and the commit `ID: add kebab_case` then cited the reopened session 1 issue. The new issue stayed STARTED with `deeds: []` and the sha under `elsewhere`. `book_named_in` now treats a row's issue as a placeholder when a hook filed it (new `filed` flag), the row has no deed, the tracker has no deed on it, and the tracker has it STARTED under this holder. The placeholder is released and cancelled before the named issue is claimed, so a one-node claim graph takes the named one. The row moves to the named issue with the sha in `deeds`. A filed issue with a deed, or one another holder has, keeps the old path (`also` and `elsewhere`).
- **`ljos_start` files an issue while the seat holds one** (ljos-6yav). In w1 session 2, the Edit hook claimed work-ipph and `ljos_start` claimed work-8372 four seconds later. With no issue passed, `start_work` now looks for an unfinished row for the checkout whose issue the tracker has STARTED under this holder. It moves that row to the server's book, marked `started`, so the next hook call takes it back through #156's path. A named commit that lands while the row sits in the server's book takes it back first as well. When the task differs from the title a hook filed the issue under, the task goes on the issue as a `vissue note`; vissue has no verb that renames an issue.
- **A row with issue null** (ljos-5a7b). In w5, session 1 timed out before any edit. The `UserPromptSubmit` hook opens the row (`note_start` and `remember_title`), and nothing removed it. Stop and SessionEnd now drop a row with no issue, no deeds, no failures and no asks, and the idle sweep drops one once it is idle. Rows with failures or asks stay, because their lesson and the failures they booked are the record the fails column reads.

Tests: one per shape, built from the w1 and w5 hook sequences, plus the two guards (a deed on the placeholder, another holder). CI runs them; nothing was built on the box.

author: saurabhav88
body:
## What changed

Word correction joined words the user had separated: "still open. AI agents" became "still OpenAI agents" (the full stop deleted), "open, AI" the same, and "a PI" became "API". The multi-word passes stripped every token's punctuation before matching and rebuilt the span from the first prefix and last suffix, so punctuation inside the span was deleted.

`WordCorrector` now only joins or replaces several words when nothing but spaces separates them (`sliceCrossesPunctuation`, Passes 0, 1 and 2). The no-space join (Pass 0) also refuses a span with an everyday small word unless the saved word already has those words (`joinsThroughStopword`): "bank of america" still becomes "Bank of America", and "open a i" (spelled letters) still becomes "OpenAI". `ownerIntercepts` applies the same rules so Self-Learning's claim check still mirrors Pass 0. Saved split aliases ("A P I", "open A I", "in vious wispr") still match.

Help: How Custom Word Correction Works explains the rule and the mishearing workaround.

Scope: part B of the #3892 plan (`docs/feature-requests/issue-3892-2026-10-17-word-correction-boundaries.md`). The word-ending half (#3892) follows separately; it waits on the plan's non-Latin decision.

## Proof

- Focused: 36 tests in 3 suites; switching both rules off fails the shipped-dictionary, hand-built, predicate and mirror rows.
- `scripts/xcode-test.sh` full Debug run on the rebased branch: 11687 tests, PASS.
- Live UAT (Transcribe a File, Parakeet, default dictionary): said "The question is still open. AI agents can help."; raw ASR "still open, AI agents"; delivered "The question is still open. AI agents can help." No OpenAI join.

## Review

- Local Codex: round 1 found that "Bank of America" lost its casing fix (fixed with `joinsThroughStopword`); the full run then found "open a i" no longer joined (fixed: a one-letter "a" beside another single letter is a spelled letter). Final Codex round: no actionable findings.

body:
## 문제
공백↔황혼 전환 시, 특히 공백에 처음 들어갈 때 크게 끊김. 원인은 두 가지임.
- 첫 프레임에 구름 준비 작업이 한꺼번에 몰림.
- 전환하는 2.4초 동안 두 장면을 매 프레임 함께 그림(구름 세트 2벌, 블룸 2번).

## 변경 1: 첫 프레임 작업 분산 (61d7760)
- `cloud-live.js`: 한 번도 안 그려진 스프라이트는 만든 시각부터 10초를 셈. 전에는 만들자마자 GPU 텍스처가 해제됐음. 해제된 스프라이트가 다시 쓰이면 `touch()`는 대기열에만 넣고, `tick()`이 프레임당 1~3장씩 되살림.
- `cloud-overlay.js`: `warm(W, HZ)` 추가. 기본 레이어 형태 고치기와 손그림 레이어 굽기를 그리기 프레임 밖에서 한 레이어씩 처리함.
- `tsukuyomi.js`: `scheduleDay2`가 오버레이 문서를 다 읽은 뒤 `warm`부터 돌림. 그래서 큰 덩어리는 고친 형태로 한 번만 구워짐.

## 변경 2: 스냅샷 페이드 (6f9684b)
**공백↔황혼**
- 전환 순간의 화면(장면 + 물결 + 전경)을 오버레이 캔버스에 떠 두고, 장면은 바로 목표 상태로 바꿈.
- 오버레이는 CSS opacity 전환(`T_DAY`초)으로 걷힘. 합성기에서 돌기 때문에 메인 스레드가 바빠도 매끄러움.
- 전환 중에는 새 장면 하나만 그림.
- 진행 중에 다시 누르면 지금 보이는 화면을 다시 떠서 이어 감.
- 밤 전환, 카메라 모드, 엔진이 정지된 동안에는 기존 보간 방식을 그대로 씀.

**月↔山 세계 전환**
- 이전 세계를 페이드 시작 때 멈춤. 캔버스에 마지막 화면이 그대로 남아 정지 화면으로 걷힘.
- 전환이 실패하면 이전 세계를 다시 시작함.

## 확인
GPU가 없는 헤드리스 크로미움(소프트웨어 렌더링)에서 측정함.

- 연속 입력(황혼 → 공백 → 황혼), 밤 전환, 月→山→月 전환 모두 최종 상태가 정상임. 콘솔 오류 없음.

abstract.inc 1000 tokens per second

Adds Abstract's agent skill to Development & Code Tools (one README line, alphabetical).

**What it solves:** an agent that needs to call the Abstract API (https://api.abstract.inc/v1, OpenAI-compatible) gets the sign-in flow, safe key handling (`$(abstract token)`, never printed), the model ids, and what each error code asks of the user.

**Who uses it:** developers who send LLM work (GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Kimi-K3) or robot action requests (bimanual YAM models) to Abstract from Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or another terminal agent.

**How it ships:** the skill is bundled in the public `abstract` CLI (https://github.com/abstractpbc/abstract-cli). `abstract skill` prints it; `abstract skill install` writes it where each installed agent reads skills.

**Example:** "Summarize this repo with glm-5.3:superfast on Abstract" -> the agent runs `abstract status`, then sends a Responses API request with the key from `$(abstract token)`.

**Prerequisites:** the `abstract` CLI (`curl -fsSL https://abstract.inc/install.sh | bash`) and an Abstract account. Docs: https://abstract.inc/docs. Pricing: https://abstract.inc/pricing.

Submitted by the Abstract team (we are the skill's authors), prepared with an AI coding agent.

## What changed

**#573: a Markdown resume reads as one.** `structure-from-text.ts` now reads Markdown. `# Name` (and a Word Title-style name, which the .docx reader writes as `# Name`) is the name. A heading deeper than its section's, like `### Title — Company` under `## Experience`, is a line of that section. A line that is only the dates (`*March 2021 – Present*`) dates the line above it. Emphasis (`**`, `__`, `*`, `_`, backticks), links and rules are taken off by a new `plainLine`, with look-alikes left alone (`first_last@example.com`, `2*3*4`, `* bullet`). Skill and education bullets lose their markers, and dates taken out of a title leave no `()`. The parsed view and the "contact details found" line now agree. A first line in capitals that names no section is the name too.

**#574: the clean version of a Markdown resume.** With #573 the floor structure already puts the name and contacts on top and the roles under Experience. Two more things were needed:
- the "would this drop a line" gate (`draft-document.ts:missingLines`) now reads a line part by part between separators. The render sets the contact line in its own order ("Berlin · email" for "email · Berlin"), and read whole that sent every such resume to the plainer line-by-line version, which drew each `### role` as a section in capitals.
- that plainer version (`planLines`) strips Markdown marks too.

The fix reaches the render page, Tailor's Document view and its downloads, Save as vN (`cleanDocx`) and application packs.

**#575: the section-order field.** It takes the names its hint lists ("experience") and the keys ("work"), in any case. It shows the names back. A name it does not know is refused with a sentence: the field keeps what was typed and is marked invalid, and no file is drawn. Before, the name was dropped and the section went to the end. A name typed twice is one section.

**#585: a link is never broken in the clean PDF.** pdfkit breaks a line after any hyphen or slash. A text holding a link or an e-mail address (contact line, header lines, paragraphs, bullets, skill values) is now broken at its spaces only and drawn a line per call, so the link moves whole to the next line. A text with no link is left to pdfkit as before. The .docx needed nothing: Word only wraps for display, and the file and every parser keep the link whole (a test checks both).

**#590: resume versions.**
1. Save as vN keeps the file the person uploaded. Three nullable columns on `resume` hold it once ApplyPack has written the file in place, and the next upload clears them. **Download original** returns the upload, and **Download vN** appears next to it once the two differ. The save flash's "Download .docx" still returns the new version. The rule lives in the pure `kept-upload.ts`.
2. Clean version → **Save as a new resume** now runs the same scan run an upload does. You see the progress page, then land on the scanned resume with the flash, so the page never shows "Not scanned yet — press Scan" while a scan is under way. Pressing Scan during the run joins it instead of paying again.

Review pass (code-review-expert): two fixes went in.
- The emphasis and link patterns are bounded. Unbounded, a long line of lone `*` took quadratic time on every page view: 171 ms at 24k characters, about 7 s at 150k. Now 85 ms at 150k.
- The deeper-heading rule applies only under a section of a known kind, so a Word Title further down a .docx cannot swallow the `##` sections below it.

## Verification

- `npm run lint:types` clean; `npm test` 3,605 / 3,605 pass; `npm run exports:audit` 0 dead, 0 over-exported; `npx prisma format --check` clean.
- Route smoke on a fresh database: **156 requests, 156 as expected, 0 failed**; pseudo-language pass **0 runs of English outside the catalog**. It now also requests the new `GET /resumes/:id/download/original` and POSTs an unknown section name, which is refused. `prisma migrate diff` against the migrated database: no difference.
- Live, on a copy of the scratch install (Ukrainian interface):
  - The stored `alex-rivera.md` resume's parsed view now shows the name, email, phone, link and location, with Summary · Skills · Experience (3 roles) · Education.
  - Uploading the tester's shape (`### Title — Company`, italic dates) shows Marta Keller, all four contacts and 2 roles with dates. The clean PDF opens with the name and contacts, has roles under EXPERIENCE and contains no asterisks, and so do Tailor's `/resumes/:id/document` .docx and .pdf.
  - Save as v2: **Download original** returns `markdown-headed-roles.md` (`text/markdown`), and **Download v2** returns the clean .docx with the edit and no `**`.
  - The order `summary,experience,skills,…` puts EXPERIENCE second in the PDF. `summary,experiance,skills` is refused with the field kept.
  - At 12.5 pt body size the contact line wraps with `github.com/mkeller-example` whole on the second line.
  - Save as a new resume goes to the progress page and lands on `/resumes/3`, scanned, with the flash.
- AI: 3 calls on `claude_code` (resume-scan, plan): the upload, Save as v2 and Save as a new resume.

Closes #573
Closes #574
Closes #575
Closes #585
Closes #590

## Schema

- `20261019143719_resume_upload_file`: `resume.uploadFile` (bytea), `uploadName`, `uploadMime` (text), all nullable. They hold the uploaded file once a Save as vN wrote the next version.

## Decisions made (easy to reverse)

- #590.2: the clean save shows the upload's progress page rather than a "scan running" state on the resume page. It is the flow an upload already has and needs no new polling. The alternative is a polling card on the resume page, as the pack tab has.
- #590.1: one kept file (the last upload), not a history of every version's file. A version history would need a table of its own, and it is only worth building if someone needs v2 while v3 exists.
- #585: a justified paragraph that wraps a link is set flush left. pdfkit sets the last line of each call flush left, and drawing line by line is what keeps the link whole.

## Follow-ups (P2/P3)

- Save as vN *with a posting* (Tailor → Save, then re-check) still scans with `scanInBackground`. The resume page can show "Not scanned yet" while that scan runs, and Scan then pays twice. Same fix as #590.2.
- `/resumes/:id/props` takes the candidate's name from the text's first line. For a .docx whose name has Word's Title style, that line is `# Name`, so "Fix document properties" writes "# Name — Resume" (found by reading the code, not run).
- Unused imports: `scanInBackground` and `replaceResumeFile` in `routes/jobs.tsx`, `saveResumeTextVersion` in `routes/resumes.tsx`.
- CLAUDE.md's list of pure resume modules does not name `kept-upload.ts` yet.

## Release notes

### Added
- After you save a new version of a resume, its page offers both the new version and the file you uploaded.

### Changed
- Saving the clean version as a new resume now shows its progress, then opens the new resume already read.

### Fixed
- A Markdown resume is read properly: its name, contact details and roles are found, and no asterisks or hash marks show anywhere.
- The clean version of a Markdown resume, in the Tailor document view, in its downloads and in a saved version, opens with your name and contacts and keeps every job under Experience.
- The section-order field takes the section names it lists, such as "experience", and says so when it does not know a name instead of quietly moving that section to the end.
- A web address or e-mail in the clean PDF is never split across two lines.
- "Download original" returns the file you uploaded, even after you saved a newer version.
- A role title no longer keeps empty brackets after its dates are read.

FixKey is a standalone desktop product. Move its complete implementation from `delinoio/oss` into `delinoio/apps`, including the Rust correction engine, Tauri/React application, bundled dictionaries and third-party notices, product contracts, affected CI and protected release workflow.

Keep the `fixkey` product identity, local-only processing, platform boundaries, signing gates and immutable `fixkey-v<version>` releases. Update support and updater URLs to this repository. Development follows the apps convention: `pnpm dev` for the frontend and `pnpm dev:desktop` for the native shell from `apps/fixkey`.

Source: `delinoio/oss@a445d20e86904dd51f1bf286838ab04afa2a0632`. Destination: `3b3c8c8f014093c7b90a17c924ff54b095a5a1d9`. The companion oss change removes the transferred implementation and its old CI/release ownership. Merge this import before the source removal.

Validation on the destination change:

- Root `cargo test --locked`: passed; FixKey shell 18 tests, engine 101 tests and dictionary integration 6 tests.
- `cargo test --locked -p fixkey --features desktop --lib`: passed, 25 tests.
- `cargo clippy --locked -p fixkey-core --features native --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the equivalent `fixkey --features desktop` check: passed.
- `pnpm test` from `apps/fixkey`: passed, 20 UI tests and production frontend build.
- Root `pnpm test:tooling`: passed, 38 tests including release gates, metadata and affected selection.
- Root `pnpm format:check`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `go tool actionlint -shellcheck=''`: passed. Commit hooks also passed.
- Compared all 72 transferred source/asset files. Differences are limited to development commands, support/update URLs and a dependency-pin comment. All three LFS dictionary hashes match the source pointers; their objects were uploaded to this repository.

Unperformed: actual native input/application acceptance on macOS, Windows and Linux; Windows/Linux execution; signed installer assembly, installation and update delivery; dependency security audits and hosted CI. No release or credentials were published. The protected `fixkey-signing` and `fixkey-publish` environments and their release variables/secrets must be configured before a release; neither repository currently has these environments. Existing dependency security constraints remain documented and are not resolved by this migration. Generated frontend `dist` output was removed after validation.

body:
**Detail bug report:** [View on Detail](https://app.detail.dev/org_befd6425-a158-4e24-9d4d-1e5c08769515/bugs/bug_9ae7e771-c81c-423e-a74d-882564bd92de)

## Summary
Closes #487

`URLPatternFilter` silently dropped every URL for single-star brace-alternation globs that shape as a SUFFIX (`*.{jpg,png}`) or PREFIX (`/blog/{2023,2024}/*`). `_categorize_pattern` short-circuited such patterns into the brace-unaware SUFFIX/PREFIX fast paths, which store the literal unexpanded string (`{jpg,png}` / `/blog/{2023,2024}`) and can never match a real URL. With `reverse=True` the semantics were inverted (every URL passed).

Root cause: brace expansion (`{a,b}` → `(a|b)`) only runs in the PATH branch of `_add_pattern`, but `_categorize_pattern` routed these single-star brace patterns away from it — so the feature added in `810207bd` (PR #426) was bypassed for the two most natural user spellings.

## List of files changed and why
- `crawl4ai/deep_crawling/filters.py` — Guard the SUFFIX/PREFIX fast paths in `_categorize_pattern` with `"{" not in pattern` so single-star brace globs fall through to the PATH branch, where the existing `{a,b}` → `(a|b)` post-processing translates them into a real regex.
- `tests/deep_crwaling/test_filter.py` — Regression tests pinning the four distinct footguns: matches, routing (compiled regex contains the expanded alternation), `reverse=True` semantics, and that non-brace single-star globs still take the fast paths.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- New regression tests (14 parametrized cases) added to `TestURLPatternFilter` covering the two bug-report shapes, >2 alternatives, brace-in-the-middle, the `reverse=True` inversion, and the non-brace fast-path preservation.
- Bug-report reproduction (`/blog/{2023,2024}/*` and `*.{jpg,png}`) verified directly — both now match expected URLs and reject non-matching ones, including under `reverse=True`.
- End-to-end `FilterChain` (the async path BFS/DFS/BestFirst strategies call) verified: include `/blog/{2023,2024}/*` plus exclude `*.{jpg,png}` (via `reverse=True`) admits only matching URLs; `FilterStats` counters are consistent.
- Routine checks all pass: unit tests for `tests/deep_crwaling/test_filter.py` (115 passed) and adjacent deep-crawling caller tests (87 passed) including `test_bfs_filter_mixed_case_host`, `test_deep_crawl_resume`, `test_bfs_start_url_dedup`, `test_bfs_score_metadata_repro`, `test_dfs_metadata_score`; module import and `py_compile` succeed.
- Lint/type-check (not wired into CI for this repo): ran `ruff`, `mypy`, and `black` via `uvx` against the changed files and confirmed zero new errors compared to baseline (both files had pre-existing style drift that exists on `main`).
- Procedures that could not be run: none — every procedure in the test plan ran successfully.

## Checklist:
- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] I have added/updated unit tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

author: semihalev
body:
Two small rules, one commit each.

## 1. A value read as text is its CAST AS TEXT

The rule: wherever a value is read as text, it is the text CAST AS TEXT gives it.

Before this PR, five places turned a value into text, each with its own copy of the rule:
- CAST AS TEXT
- `Value::as_string`
- `Value`'s Display
- `value_to_string`, which CONCAT, CONCAT_WS and the other text functions use
- STRING_AGG

COLLATE and EMBED had copies as well. The copies disagreed:

| Expression | main | here |
|---|---|---|
| `CONCAT_WS('', 1e20)`, `CONCAT(1e20)`, `LPAD(1e20, ...)` and the other text functions | `100000000000000000000` | `1e20` |
| `LENGTH`-style readings of `1e20`, such as `CHAR_LENGTH` | 21 | 4 |
| `STRING_AGG(ts, ';')` | `2024-01-01 12:00:00.123456 UTC` | `2024-01-01T12:00:00.123456+00:00` |
| `STRING_AGG(f, ';')` for `1e20` | `100000000000000000000` | `1e20` |

`Value::write_text` in `core/value.rs` is now the one rule. It writes the value's text into the caller's buffer and returns false for NULL or a value with no text form.

`Value::text_form` gives the same text as a `Cow`. Two helpers serve both functions:
- `stored_text` gives the borrowed text of TEXT, BOOLEAN and JSON.
- `formatted_text` formats a FLOAT, TIMESTAMP or VECTOR once. `text_form` returns that String without copying it.

These now call it:
- CAST AS TEXT
- `as_string`
- Display, which keeps `NULL` and the extension tag for a value with no text form
- `value_to_string`
- STRING_AGG
- COLLATE
- EMBED's number branch

INTEGER, BOOLEAN, TIMESTAMP outside STRING_AGG, and JSON already gave the same text everywhere.

`docs/_docs/sql-features/cast-operations.md` now says that the text functions, `||` and STRING_AGG read a value as CAST AS TEXT does.

Cost: Display writes through `write_text`, so `||` and `Value::to_string` write an INTEGER, BOOLEAN or TEXT into their own buffer with no allocation, as before. TEXT stays borrowed in `text_form`. A FLOAT or TIMESTAMP is formatted once, as before.

## 2. An unaliased window column is named as written

Every unaliased window function column was named after the function alone. `SUM(f) OVER ()` and `SUM(f) OVER (PARTITION BY g)` were both `SUM()`, and `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id)` was `ROW_NUMBER()`.

The column is now named by `expression_to_string`, the stringifier that names aggregate columns. It gains a Window arm:
- The call is written as an aggregate column names it.
- Then comes OVER with its PARTITION BY, ORDER BY and frame as written, or `OVER w` for a named window.
- An ORDER BY key leaves out the default ASC.
- A FILTER and the call's own ORDER BY are not part of the name, as for an aggregate.

| Expression | main | here |
|---|---|---|
| `SUM(f) OVER (PARTITION BY g)` | `SUM()` | `SUM(f) OVER (PARTITION BY g)` |
| `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id)` | `ROW_NUMBER()` | `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY id)` |
| `COUNT(*) OVER ()` | `COUNT()` | `COUNT(*) OVER ()` |

`docs/_docs/functions/window-functions.md` states the rule.

A window function that ORDER BY reads and the select list does not carry is computed into a hidden column. That column was named after the expression's text, and the sort found it by that name. With visible windows named as written, a visible `SUM(v) FILTER (WHERE v > 0) OVER (PARTITION BY g)` would have taken the place of a hidden `SUM(v) OVER (PARTITION BY g)`. The hidden column is now named by its `ExprKey`, as hidden aggregate columns are. ORDER BY and DISTINCT ON both bind it by that identity: `resolve_distinct_on_indices` reads a hidden column's key after the SELECT expressions, as ORDER BY does. The check for a window the select list already carries compares keys too.

`join_consumer_rule_test` asserted `COUNT()` for `COUNT(*) OVER ()` in four cases. It now asserts the new name. I searched `tests/` for names of the form `NAME()`; that test was the only one using the old window name.

## Tests

- `text_form_rule_test` (new):
  - 23 text readings (`||`, CONCAT, CONCAT_WS, UPPER, LOWER, LENGTH, CHAR_LENGTH, REVERSE, LEFT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING, REPLACE, LPAD, RPAD, TRIM, LTRIM, RTRIM, INSTR, STRPOS, SPLIT_PART, STARTS_WITH, ENDS_WITH, REPEAT), plus STRING_AGG.
  - Each runs over FLOAT, TIMESTAMP, BOOLEAN, INTEGER and JSON columns, and over FLOAT, BOOLEAN and INTEGER parameters.
  - Each reading must equal the same reading of `CAST(x AS TEXT)`.
  - 41 wrong for columns and 35 for parameters on main.
- `window_column_names_test` (new): nine shapes.
  - Plain, partitioned and ordered windows, NULLS FIRST, a named window and a frame.
  - The lazy partition path with LIMIT, a window over a GROUP BY aggregate, and an alias.
  - 8 wrong on main.
- Added in the review round, each failing on `5876962d`:
  - `test_a_sort_window_is_not_taken_for_a_visible_one_named_alike`, in `window_column_names_test`. A visible filtered window and an ORDER BY over the unfiltered one, ASC and DESC. The test also checks that the hidden column is dropped. 2 wrong.
  - `text_form_alloc_test` (new). With a counting allocator, writing an INTEGER, BOOLEAN or TEXT value into a buffer must allocate nothing. On `5876962d` an INTEGER allocates once.
    - Like `built_string_alloc_test`, it builds only without the default `jemalloc` feature.
    - I ran it with `--no-default-features --features parallel`.
- The two `text_form_rule_test` tests now open their own DSNs.
- Added in the second review round, each failing on `cc33a681`:
  - `test_distinct_on_reads_a_sort_window_by_identity`, in `window_column_names_test`. DISTINCT ON over a ROW_NUMBER and over a DENSE_RANK that ORDER BY also reads. Both kept one row on `cc33a681`.
  - `test_owning_a_formatted_text_costs_no_more_than_writing_it`, in `text_form_alloc_test`. Owning the text of a FLOAT or TIMESTAMP must allocate no more than writing it into a buffer with room. On `cc33a681`, owning `1e20` allocated 4 times against 3.
- `text_form_alloc_test` is added to the system allocator step in `ci.yml`, beside the other allocation tests that build without `jemalloc`.

I checked each guard in place by reverting only its source change.

## Suites

On `5876962d`, not run again since:
- `cargo nextest run --all-features` over 40 text, function, cast, JSON, vector, float and collate targets: 494 passed.
- Every target that uses OVER, 57 of them: 1089 passed.

On `cc33a681`, not run again since:
- `cargo nextest run --all-features` over every target that uses OVER and the text targets: 1512 passed.

On `ff3c19c6`:
- `cargo nextest run --all-features` over every target that uses OVER or DISTINCT ON, plus the text, function, cast, JSON, vector, float, collate and distinct targets: 1583 passed.
- `cargo test --no-default-features --features parallel --test text_form_alloc_test`, as CI runs it: 2 passed.
- `--lib` tests under `core::`, `functions::`, `utils::`, `query::` and the window modules: 585 passed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` and `cargo clippy --lib --tests --features test-failpoints` are clean.

## Not done

- **LIKE and GLOB with an operand that is not TEXT.** The agreed rule is to read both sides as text, but that is a separate PR. There are three pattern matchers: the VM's `CompiledPattern`, storage's `LikeExpr` and storage's own `CompiledPattern`. The index prefix range and the pushdown rules need the same change. I will verify those paths first.
- **ARRAY_AGG and `generate_series`** build JSON and write a TIMESTAMP differently from each other (`... UTC` and RFC 3339). That is the value-to-JSON rule, which this PR does not touch.
- **An expression over a window**, such as `SUM(f) OVER () + 1`, is still named `expr_N` by the window projection.
- I did not run the whole in-memory suite or the filedb suite locally.

| Empty storage → defaults, setItem never called; `update({volume:30})` returns 30 and writes JSON under `SETTINGS_KEY`; a second store reads 30 | `tests/unit/ui/settings-store.test.ts` › createSettingsStore persistence › returns defaults from empty storage without writing; › writes updates as JSON and a second store reads them back |
| `'{nope'`, `'[]'`, `'42'` → defaults; `{version:1, aimMode:'anywhere'}` → aimMode `anywhere` + defaults elsewhere | `settings-store.test.ts` › createSettingsStore parsing › falls back to defaults for stored {nope / [] / 42; › keeps valid stored fields and defaults the rest |

| Throwing (QuotaExceededError) and null storage: constructs, defaults, update/get from memory, nothing throws, 0 console.error/warn calls | `settings-store.test.ts` › createSettingsStore with broken storage › works from memory and stays silent with throwing storage / null storage |

body:
#### Reference Issues/PRs

Fixes #439

#### What does this implement/fix? Explain your changes.

Avoid intermediate exponential overflow and underflow in `entropic_risk_measure` when `theta` is small. For example, finite returns `[-0.02, 0.01, 0.03]` at `theta=1e-5` currently produce `inf`, whereas the same formula evaluated stably gives approximately `0.02001897119984886`.

- Add prepared log weights to the exponents before applying NumPy `logaddexp.reduce`, and subtract `log1p(-beta)` in log space. Zero weights become negative infinity without a log-zero warning; tiny positive weights remain in log space. This measure no longer calls SciPy.
- Reuse the existing weight validation and missing-return preparation. Preserve column-specific NaN exclusion, zero-weight exclusion, and scalar/vector NaN results for empty usable inputs. Limit intentional `invalid` suppression to the NumPy reduction for no-mass NaN columns; evaluate weighted exponents before that context and the confidence-level arithmetic after it.
- Add eight regression cases covering overflow and all-positive-return underflow, with and without sample weights, for 1D and 2D returns. All eight fail on the unmodified main implementation and pass with the fix. Add two further strict-floating-point preservation checks for tiny relative weights; those pass on upstream and the final fix, but caught a regression in the first local implementation. Add four strict-floating-point NaN preservation cases that fail on an unguarded NumPy reduction and pass with the localized guard.

The public API and mathematical definition are unchanged. Scope: the shared linear weight normalization is unchanged; extreme weight ratios that underflow there, and inputs whose scaled losses or internal reduction differences exceed the floating-point range, are not addressed by this patch. The extreme-exponent warning boundary was also present in the previous SciPy implementation.

#### Does your contribution introduce a new dependency? If yes, which one?

No. The reduction uses NumPy only. Existing SciPy uses elsewhere in the module are unchanged.

#### What should a reviewer concentrate their feedback on?

Numerical stability and preservation of the existing sample-weight and NaN semantics. The change is limited to one measure implementation and its regression tests.

#### Any other comments?

Tested on Windows 11, Python 3.12.14, NumPy 2.5.4, SciPy 1.18.1, CPU only.

Local verification:

- Existing measure tests before the fix: 1,145 passed (new regressions deselected).
- Measure tests after the NumPy review update: 1,159 passed, with no warnings, including eight original-defect regressions, two tiny-weight preservation checks, and four NaN-reduction preservation cases.
- Additional normal-API numerical audit: 200 deterministic cases compared with a 70-digit standard-library Decimal reference, including NaNs, zero weights, and 1D/2D inputs; all passed at `rtol=1e-12`, `atol=1e-14`. Two further normal-API checks combine a `1e-320` weight with `theta=1e-5` and also match Decimal in 1D/2D.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `deptry src`, `ty check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- Complete pytest suite including doctests: upstream baseline 10,667 passed; previous SciPy fix 10,677 passed; NumPy review update 10,681 passed. All runs had zero failures, errors and skips, using two workers and single-thread BLAS. XML testcase sets reconcile exactly: no baseline test missing, fourteen cases added over upstream, and exactly the four NaN cases added since the previous PR head. The full-suite warning count is 1,078, matching both earlier complete runs; the focused measure suite has no warnings. Initial unrestricted local execution encountered native CVXPY worker aborts; incomplete intermediate runs are not included in these totals.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: passed (all six hooks).

AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation, and test preparation. Hosted CI is not represented by these local results.

- [x] New behavior and bug fixes are covered by tests.
- [x] The complete tests and code quality checks pass locally.
- Documentation: no public API or mathematical-definition change.

author: mengwong
body:
## What was done

The skills describe L4 as it is on `unstable`, and `main` is a different compiler.
Encodings are often written with an `unstable` binary and filed in commons, where a `main` build has to read them.
Measured 2026-10-19: `main` build 98 rejects 42 of the 108 documented examples under `doc/`, and the `unstable` shelf build rejects none.
This PR separates two questions, the compiler you run and the dialect you write, and checks the second mechanically.

- **The target comes from the brief, and defaults to `main`.**
  If the brief is silent the target is `main`; it is `unstable` only when the brief says so.
  The default is assumed, not ruled: the brief template says so.
  Running an `unstable` binary does not license `unstable` syntax.
  `writing-l4-rules/SKILL.md` has a step 0 that asks the two questions and reads `l4 --version` (with a probe for a `dev` build).
- **`references/dialects.md`** gives each construct a status on `main`: **reads**, **degrades** (accepted, means something else or less) or **rejects**, with what each compiler does and what to write on `main` instead.
  It is sorted by how the failure shows: seven silent rows, nine where `main`'s message names the wrong thing, and the plain ones.
  It also records what changed between `main` builds 97 and 98: `IS INTEGER` and `WAIT UNTIL` renamed with no alias, the temporal built-ins removed, `DO` made a modal of its own.
  The shelf build has none of that, so for those constructs the two compilers accept different text; for `IS INTEGER` and `WAIT UNTIL` the table gives an idiom both read (`FLOOR x EQUALS x`; an event by another party at that time).
  The page's header says it was measured at build 98, which is the minimum build for a `main` target.
- **`references/dialect-probes/`** holds 105 one-purpose files that back the table.
  `main` rejects exactly the 58 numbered ones and the shelf build rejects exactly nine.
  They are deliberately odd `.l4`, so a repo-wide checker can object: `etc/check-not-precedence.mjs` did, and the NOT probe now carries its `NOT-REACH-OK` marker.
  `etc/dialect-census.sh <l4> [dir]` runs `l4 check` over a tree and prints each failing file with its first error; it is how both numbers were taken, and how to refresh them.
- **`encoding-a-subject/assets/check.sh` makes the target check.**
  With the target `main`, the default, it runs every module with your binary and with a main build and compares the four counts it already prints (errors, satisfied, failed, refused).
  A module whose counts differ, or that errors on main, is red, says "reads differently on main", and shows the first error `main` gives.
  If no main build can be had, or either build prints nothing a real `l4 run` prints, it exits 2: a step not run is not a full check.
  `L4_TARGET=unstable` skips the main check and says so on stderr; stdout and the exit status are what they were.
  It runs `l4 run`, not `l4 check`, on the main build, so it also compares what the assertions say.
  So with the target `main` every module is run twice, once per build, with your environment (the main run without `JL4_LIBRARY_PATH`): a module that fetches over the network, posts, or reads `ENV` does it twice, once with main. For such a module use `L4_TARGET=unstable` and compare by hand, or keep it out of the checked directory (assumed, not ruled; there is no skip list).
  The comparison is of counts, so equal counts can hide a different assertion failing on each side.
- **`fetch-main-l4.sh`** prints the path of a main-build `l4`, taking it out of the platform's VS Code extension package (main releases ship no standalone archive) and caching it.
  The only network calls are to GitHub's release endpoints: the list of releases, to find the newest, one release, and one package.
  **What it trusts:** there is no digest, because the release publishes none for the package, and it runs the downloaded binary (`--version`) before it reports the path.
  It takes only the one zip member, refuses anything but a regular file, does not cache a binary whose `--version` is not a main build's (an empty one is accepted only below build 97), falls back to the newest cached build when offline and to an older release when the newest has no package for the platform, and says on stderr when it does.
- **The brief template** gets a "Target compiler" line (`main`, build 98 or later, by default) and asks for `check.sh`'s output with its main columns.
  `canon-deposit.md` and `encoding-a-subject/SKILL.md` say a deposited encoding states its target in `NOTES.md`, with the check's output and the main build; `encoding.json` is touched only where a row already has a `checks` object with a `note`.
  The skill also loses its claim that `l4` has no `--version`.

## How it helps

An encoder can tell which compiler will read the file, and `check.sh` goes red before the encoding is filed, with main's first error under the module.
What is checked mechanically and what is only documented are different:

- **Checked by `check.sh`:** a module `main` rejects, a module `main` cannot finish in 300 seconds, and a difference that changes an `#ASSERT`'s outcome.
- **Not seen by `check.sh`:** a different `#TRACE` outcome.
  It counts error diagnostics and assertion lines and nothing else; a trace prints neither.
- **Documented only:** which construct to write instead (the table and its probes), the three rows that degrade (an input named in an action, a `MAY` with a `LEST`, a language tag on `@nlg`, each compared by running both builds and reading the trace), and the spellings `unstable` and `main` disagree on.

`@lang`, `REFUSE` and `YMD` were by far the commonest first errors on `main` across the commons encodings checked.
One difference cannot be seen from an error at all: an input named inside a `MUST` action matches any payload on `main` but is compared on `unstable`, so paying a stranger fulfils the obligation.
`check.sh` passes it: `run-must-names-an-input` already contains the wrong-payload trace and the check reads 0/0/0/0 on both builds while the two answer differently.
The page puts it first, with a `PROVIDED` spelling that gives the same traces on both.
A `MAY` with an explicit `LEST` is the same kind of row: a permission that lapses is `DEONTIC BREACHED` on `unstable` and `FULFILLED` on `main`, which ignores a `LEST` after `MAY`.
`unstable` refuses four things `main` accepts without a word: `NOT a AND b` or `NOT a OR b` with no brackets, an infix `EXPONENT` after any `IMPORT` (`prelude`, `daydate`, `math` and `currency` each tried), a `PARTY` that is not the performer of its action (for the obligation of a record-typed action and the events of any action, not for the obligation of a constructor action), and a constructor named like a field of an input (field opening makes the field win).
Run over 2,058 modules, which are the 108 under `doc/` and the 1,950 `.l4` files under `subjects/` of the commons checkout at `b2a0c118` (2026-10-16) outside `il/` and `vn/` (commons has since moved to `02414270`; these were not re-taken), the check found 1,500 that read the same on both builds, 551 that differ in their counts, and 7 that `main` did not finish in 60 seconds (none took longer than 24 seconds on the shelf build).
Of the 551, 8 had no error on `main`: all in one encoding, and the constructor-and-field row above is their cause.

## Controls

Run on darwin-arm64, under bash 5.3 and the system bash 3.2.57, with `main` build 98 and the shelf build `unstable-20261015-8730d3f`:

| Control | Result |
| --- | --- |
| a. a module that reads the same on both | green, exit 0 |
| b. a module using `REFUSE`, one starting with `@lang`, one with a section `GIVEN` followed by a second rule | red, exit 1, one "reads differently on main" line each, and the first error under it: `unexpected BECAUSE`, `unexpected '@'`, `I could not find a definition for the identifier rate` |
| c. no main binary: no `fetch-main-l4.sh` beside `check.sh`; `L4_MAIN` not runnable

Linear: [PET-58](https://linear.app/petka-app/issue/PET-58)

## Why

Expo SDK 58 is out: React Native 0.86 → 0.88, the iOS 27 SDK, and an Expo Router navigation-core rework. This is a native upgrade, so it needs a new build and store submission and can't ship as an OTA update. Bumping to **1.16.0** gives it a new `runtimeVersion` (`${major}.${minor}`), so this JS is never served to 1.15 binaries.

## What

Seven commits, one concern each.

**Expo SDK 58 + version bump to 1.16.0.**
- Expo 58.0.14, RN 0.88.0 and React 19.3.0, aligned with `expo install --fix`.
- **Major bumps:** gesture-handler 2.32 → **3.3**, webview 13 → 14, and `@sentry/react-native` 7 → 8, pinned to the SDK-validated `~8.28.0`.
- **`react-native-unistyles` 3.3.0 → 3.5.3.** This is required: 3.3.0 fails to build on RN 0.88 (`ImageProps::tintColor` became optional; fixed in 3.5.1).
- **Test tooling:** Jest 29 → 30 and `jest-expo` ~58.
- **`pnpm-workspace.yaml`:** Jest 30 pulls in `@parcel/watcher` and `unrs-resolver`, which want install scripts. Both are set to `false` in `allowBuilds`, since they ship prebuilt binaries.

**Expo Router `initialRouteName` removal.**
- **Authenticated stack:** now uses `unstable_settings = { anchor: 'index' }`, so deep links (e.g. from a notification) still have the home screen underneath.
- **History and leaderboards tabs:** the prop is just dropped. Each already declares its default tab first, and all navigation into them uses full hrefs.
- **Unaffected:**
  - `useNavigation().setOptions` / `getParent()` are still supported.
  - The new iOS 26 transparent-header default doesn't apply, because we set `headerStyle.backgroundColor` explicitly.

**RN 0.88 strict types.**
- **Forms** (`create-account`, `restore-account`, `update-nickname`): each now has an extracted `submitForm` handler, so the TextInput submit event is no longer passed to react-hook-form's `handleSubmit`.
- **`posthog.screen`:** the params are cast, because search params can now be typed as `undefined` (JSON drops those keys anyway).
- **`Prompt.provider.tsx`:** removed an obsolete `@ts-expect-error`.

**Tests.** `@shopify/flash-list` 2.3 now ships ESM, so it's added to `transformIgnorePatterns`. The `Share`, `Linking` and `Platform` mocks are updated to the stricter types.

**Other deps.**
- **Convex packages:** convex 1.47, convex-helpers 0.1.128, crons and migrations patches.
- **`@convex-dev/expo-push-notifications` 0.3.1 → 0.4.2.** Its `config` → `logLevel` refactor doesn't affect us: we construct `PushNotifications` with no options, and the methods we call are unchanged.
- **Minor bumps:** posthog, lucide, zod, react-hook-form, biome (plus the `$schema`), testing-library and ts-jest.
- **pnpm:** 12.14.0.
- **Cleanup:** the stale lucide `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` is gone.

**Convex AI files and skills.** Refreshed via `convex ai-files update`.

**`pnpm eas` script.** Runs EAS CLI through `pnpm dlx` with explicit build approvals for `dtrace-provider` and `protobufjs`, so there's no global install and no flags to remember (the same approach as mobileappb2c). Example: `pnpm eas build --profile development --platform ios`. CI is unaffected, since it gets `eas` from the Expo GitHub action.

## Verification

- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck` and all 40 suites / 380 tests pass.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` is clean and `expo-doctor` passes 20/20.
- `expo prebuild --clean` succeeds:
  - it generates the new iOS `SceneDelegate.swift`
  - `android.enableMinifyInReleaseBuilds=true` is now set by default
  - our `expo.modules.kotlin` keep rule is applied

**Dev client builds (EAS `development` profile):** both succeeded. Checked on iPhone 18 Pro (iOS 27) and Android; the app looks and works as before.
- iOS: [build 427c6937](https://expo.dev/accounts/expo.app/projects/petka-app/builds/427c6937-e7a9-4928-8c68-54cd606c599d)
- Android: [build 9a29cac3](https://expo.dev/accounts/expo.app/projects/petka-app/builds/9a29cac3-6141-482c-bcfb-41abf0e07af6)

**Still to do before merge:**

author: goldentechksa
body:
## What

YTD used to be `current × periods elapsed` for every line on the stub, so a one-off bonus or a week of overtime was projected as if it had been paid every period since January 1.

Now each line is one of two kinds:

- **Recurring** (regular pay, every deduction, the withholding on regular pay alone): `per-period amount × periods elapsed as of the stub's pay date`.
- **One-time** (overtime, bonus, and the extra withholding they drew): counted once, at face value, on the stub that pays them.

In a multi-stub run only period #1 (the period the customer entered) pays overtime and bonus. Later stubs get 0 of each and carry period #1's one-time amounts forward in YTD, so `grossYTD = regularYTD + overtimeYTD + bonusYTD` and `netYTD = grossYTD − taxesYTD − deductionsYTD` hold on every stub.

## Worked example (bi-weekly, TX, 3 stubs from 2026-03-02; 80h × $25, 4 OT h × $37.50, $500 bonus, $100 medical)

| Stub | Pay date | Gross | Regular YTD | OT YTD | Bonus YTD | Gross YTD | Taxes YTD | Net YTD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 03/16 | 2,650.00 | 12,000.00 | 150.00 | 500.00 | 12,650.00 | 2,091.13 | 9,958.87 |
| 2 | 03/30 | 2,000.00 | 14,000.00 | 150.00 | 500.00 | 14,650.00 | 2,411.74 | 11,538.26 |
| 3 | 04/13 | 2,000.00 | 16,000.00 | 150.00 | 500.00 | 16,650.00 | 2,732.36 | 13,117.64 |

## Verification

- `npm test`: 52 passed across 8 suites (5 new tests written first, watched fail, then made green).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Deployed to staging from this same commit.

## Not changed

The "periods elapsed" multiplier still rounds up by one on calendar-aligned schedules (a Jan 1–14 period paid Jan 15 counts as 2 periods). Independent of this change; tracked separately.
