author: andreypfau
tristan-stoltz-erc
body:
## Summary

Adds a deterministic synthetic temporal-stability benchmark as the next layer after [multi-fidelity spatial metrology #8087](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/pull/8087), addressing [FDM-STABILITY-001 #8096](https://github.com/Luminous-Dynamics/symthaea/issues/8096).

- Compares five policies: unmonitored negative control, Shewhart, EWMA, two-sided CUSUM and a hybrid persistence guard.
- Exercises six synthetic profiles: stable baseline, abrupt offset, linear drift, range-dependent gain change, variance inflation and a transient single-point outlier.
- Uses three interleaved check-standard values to make range-dependent changes visible; monitors never receive the evaluator-only stress label.
- Separates warning from quarantine; quarantine is sticky within a trace and cannot clear itself after quiet observations.
- Reports first alert, first quarantine, **premature quarantine before a known change**, detection delay, false quarantine under stable conditions, post-change trusted-evidence fraction, transient-outlier quarantine and tail residuals separately.
- Regenerates every reading, chart state, disposition, metric and digest in the exact verifier; altered evidence fails closed.
- Registers the module and documents the measurement-study gates.

## Research grounding

- [NIST gauge R&R and measurement-process characterization](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section4/mpc4.htm) covers stability, bias, drift, resolution, linearity and repeatability/reproducibility.
- [NIST uncertainty from gauge studies](https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section4/mpc46.htm) explains why estimated uncertainty depends on a representative, stable measurement process.
- [NIST control of artifact calibration](https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section3/mpc35.htm) describes check standards and control charts.
- [ISO/ASTM 52902:2023](https://www.iso.org/standard/79683.html) grounds the use of specified AM geometric-capability artefacts and measurement uncertainty.

The references motivate this benchmark but do not validate its threshold choices or synthetic profiles.

## Evidence boundary

All observations, reference values, noise and drift profiles are synthetic. The declared sigma of 0.006 mm and all limits are arbitrary benchmark parameters, not actual instrument specifications or industrial false-alarm guarantees. The synthetic baseline assumes zero residual for every standard before a stress is injected; a physical monitor must derive standard-specific baselines from traceable values and an independent measurement-system study. No instrument or printer I/O, G-code generation, autonomous recalibration, production release or safety authority is added.

Source and branch structure have been inspected. This environment does not expose a Rust toolchain, so formatting, compilation, tests and clippy have **not** been run. A local Python mirror of the detector arithmetic was used only to sanity-check selected deterministic scenarios; that is not a Rust test and is not a validation substitute. In the current environment, skipped CI workflows must not be treated as a pass.

## Next gates

1. Run exact-head cargo fmt, focused module tests, crate tests and clippy from a Rust-enabled checkout.
2. Pre-register a multi-seed panel and publish distributions of false quarantine, detection delay and unsafe post-change trust; do not tune on evaluation seeds.
3. Add explicit missing-check-standard and artifact-instability controls, plus a recovery state that requires independent evidence.
4. Validate actual instrument identity, reference-standard stability, uncertainty budget, time spacing, environment and range coverage in a physical measurement-assurance study.
5. Connect to the spatial/multi-fidelity selectors only after monitor semantics and physical assumptions are independently reviewed.

This is a stacked draft: merge/review order should follow #8072 → #8087 → this PR. No physical improvement claim is made.

author: ishesatoshi
body:
﻿checker(buildable): reject a type name used where a value is required (#778)

`struct holder { n int }` followed by `x := holder` passes `hyb check` and the
emitter prints the identifier verbatim, so `go build` fails with
`holder (type) is not an expression`. Go has no value named `holder`, and the
shape is KNOWN â€” the identifier resolves to a struct declaration â€” so this is
not an `Unknown` fail-open case.

Four value positions, plus a built-in type and a type alias:

    x := holder        assignment
    take(holder)       call argument
    holder + 1         arithmetic operand
    return holder      return value
    x := int           a built-in conversion target as a value
    x := tally         a type alias as a value

All six now reject with HYB-E1002.

The rule has to be NARROW, because a type name is a legal operand in three
other positions. Each is a control in the new accept fixture:

1. The CALLEE of a call â€” `holder(1)` is a struct conversion, `int(3.0)` and
   `u8(200)` are built-in ones.
2. The FIRST argument of `new`/`make` â€” `new(bag)`, `make([]int, 4)`.
   `make`'s later arguments (len, cap) are values and still walk.
3. The BASE of a field access, which is a qualifier position: `color.red` is
   an enum variant and `greeting.build(...)` is a method call on the type.
   A bare `x := colour` is still a value position and still rejects.
4. Anywhere a local binding shadows the type name (`holder := 5`).

Two of those were found by running the corpus and the test suite rather than by
reasoning about the rule, which is the part worth recording:

- `new(bag)` broke `n5-zero-map-first-write.hy`. An early version walked that
  argument as a value. The corpus caught it on the first run.
- `color.red` broke two `shape.rs` tests, and `greeting.build(...)` broke
  `spike6_positive.rs` â€” the Field base is a qualifier, not a value, and an
  enum-only exclusion was not enough because a method call on a type puts a
  type name there too.

Both are pinned in the accept fixture now, so a future widening of the rule
cannot silently reintroduce them.

Verified against main @ aa4a9d9:

  - all 6 value positions: ACCEPT + `go build` FAILS before, REJECT HYB-E1002
    after
  - 8 controls unchanged and building: struct conversion callee, struct
    literal, `int(3.0)`, `u8(200)`, `int(floatVar)`, a shadowing local, a
    field access, and a plain fn call
  - corpus 113 -> 115 (1 reject + 1 accept control), verdict agreement 115/115,
    tripwire not fired
  - differential reject-side 77/77, accept-side 35/38 (the 3 are the known
    cgo-bridge programs, unchanged from the baseline)
  - managed gate PASS, test registration OK, conflict markers none, census OK
  - 13 new tests in `hy-check/tests/type_name_in_value_position.rs`; all 81
    hy-check suites green, including the 173 lib tests

### Adjacent finding, NOT fixed here

`holder(1)` â€” a struct conversion with a positional argument â€” is accepted by
the checker and fails `go build` with `cannot convert 1 (untyped int) to type
holder`. I verified this behaves identically on pristine main, so it is
pre-existing and not a regression from this change. It is a different rule
(validating a conversion's target against its argument) from #778's
(type name in a value position), so I left it alone rather than widening this
PR's scope. Worth its own issue if the maintainer agrees.

Refs #778.

## Summary

**d851e624: fix(mcp): normalize unicode search terms in catalog filtering**

The client-side keyword filter only lower-cased text, so composed and decomposed characters, NBSP and repeated spaces matched differently from server search. Added `normalizeSearchTerm` (NFC, case folding, whitespace collapse) applied to both keyword and searched text. Files: `mcp/src/catalogSearchTerm.ts`, `mcp/src/catalogFilters.ts`, tests, `docs/mcp/catalog-search-normalization.md`.

Added an optional `bypassCache` argument (and `MINDVAULT_CATALOG_CACHE_BYPASS` default) to browse, search and preview. A bypassed call is live-only, never falls back to a snapshot, reports `cache: bypassed`, and leaves the shared cache policy untouched. Files: `mcp/src/catalogCacheBypass.ts`, `mcp/src/index.ts`, `mcp/src/tools.ts`, `mcp/src/validation.ts`, schema snapshot, tests, `docs/mcp/catalog-cache-bypass.md`.

author: yusuke-kurosawa
body:
## 概要
ヒアリングでは、ハードウェアの保守期限と担当者の退職時期から、検討を始める時期を逆算しています。ただ今は、「今は時期でない」と止まった案件を、予算が組まれる前に拾い直す仕組みがありません。保守期限・退職予定・決算月から「動くべき時期」を出し、その数か月前に担当者へ知らせます。

Closes #151（Epic #162）

## 計算（`lib/features/act-timing/compute.ts`）
1. **期限**：保守期限と退職予定のうち早いほう。分からないものは無視する（受け入れ基準）
   - ヒアリングに保守期限がなければ、AX 診断の「保守期限」の回答から目安を出す（過ぎている＝診断の月、1年以内＝半年後、1〜3年＝2年後。3年以上先・不明は使わない）
2. **開始**：期限 − 移行にかかる期間（組織の設定、既定 12 か月）
3. **予算**：決算月が分かれば、開始以前で最も近い「予算策定の月」（決算月の3か月前）に前倒しする
4. **通知**：動くべき時期の N か月前の1日（組織の設定、既定 3 か月）

## 変更内容
- `leads.act_by` に動くべき時期（その月の1日）を持つ
- **通知は #85 の仕組みに乗せた**：種類 `act_timing` の「次の行動」を、通知日を期限にして自動で作る。毎朝の期限通知（前日・期限切れ）がそのまま担当者に届く
  - リードごとに1件。題名に月を入れ、同じ月なら作り直さない（通知も重ねない）。月が変われば同じものを動かす。完了済みの同じ月は作り直さない
- **対象**：受注と、時期以外の理由で失注したリードは外す（次の行動を消す）。失注・保留の理由が「時期」のリードは対象にする
- **再計算のタイミング**
  - ヒアリングの保存・削除のとき（失敗してもヒアリングの保存は失敗させない）
  - 設定を変えたとき（組織のリードをすべて）
  - 毎朝の期限通知の前（直近2日に更新されたリード。診断の回答や状態の変更を拾う）
- **画面**
  - リード詳細の概要タブに「動くべき時期」カード（月、根拠、予算策定への前倒し、次の行動の期限）

Head: 482edfe3711000490dcaf49c2f4468de28cce82a

## Summary

PR CI now runs only the tests a change can reach, in parallel, instead of the
whole cli suite serially on every PR. Pushes to `main` and a new nightly
schedule keep running the full suite as the safety net; a selector failure
selects ALL, never nothing. The affected-tests kit is vendored verbatim from
agent-gateway (source pinned in the kit commit) — the same selection in
production there.

## What changes

- 3f4ade22 ci: vendor the affected-tests kit from agent-gateway 44a2ecce56fd05d87bbe7b823377765064b64a3a
- 0753276e ci: run only the tests a PR can reach, in parallel
- 482edfe3 fix(ci): re-vendor run_parallel.py from agent-gateway 4e609a781346efce347e739034c72bfbd12334d4

`.ci/affected.json` restricts the selector's test globs to the three suites CI
actually runs (cli/tests, scripts, cookbook/tools) and puts `scripts/ci/**` on
the always-run-all list. The kit's default globs also match cookbook-demo test
files that no job executes; with the restriction, a change reached only by a
demo test falls back to ALL instead of selecting a subset nothing runs.

The `cli` job (Python 3.10 + 3.13 matrix):

- checks out depth 2 (the PR merge commit and its base parent — all the diff
  needs),
- on `pull_request`, computes `python3 scripts/ci/affected.py --base HEAD^1
  --format args`; any other event, or a selector failure, yields `ALL`,
- runs the cli-suite files of that selection through
  `python3 ../scripts/ci/run_parallel.py --runner pytest` (one process per test
  file); `ALL` runs the whole suite the same way; an empty cli share prints
  "no tests selected" and passes,
- the selection travels only through the `TESTS` environment variable and
  reaches the shell as positional arguments (`set -f`, no eval, no inline
  `${{ }}` in `run:`) — a file name is never evaluated as shell code.

`on: push` is now limited to `main`: a PR branch push no longer re-runs the
full suite on top of the pull_request run. The new nightly schedule
(`23 4 * * *`) is the full-suite safety net; the weekly contract-drift
schedule is unchanged, and the contract job gets an explicit cron guard so the
nightly schedule does not also make that live check daily. The contract job's
selection logic is otherwise untouched (a separate PR reworks it).

Non-test steps (manifests, slop-gate, version-check, video-gate, contract
checks) are unchanged.

Tests: `scripts/test_ci_wiring.py` pins the wiring — fail-safe selection,
env-only passing, both paths through the parallel runner, no serial full suite
left on PRs, the nightly schedule, the weekly contract cadence; every one of
its assertions fails on the workflow before this change. The kit ships its own
hermetic tests (`scripts/test_ci_tools.py`, each case builds a throwaway git
repo). `docs/acceptance.md` quotes the new cli-job commands, as its CI section
must match the workflow.

## Measured

All on a 32-core dev machine (Python 3.12, pytest 9.1.1; CI's matrix is
3.10/3.13), every run at commit 0753276e:

| run | command | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| serial, the old PR command | `pytest -q` in `cli/` | 610 passed, 16.0 s |
| full suite via run_parallel, 3x | `run_parallel.py --runner pytest ALL` | 610 ran / 0 failed / 0 skipped each time, 9 s / 9 s / 9 s |
| typical subset (a `cli/src/sbx/gpu.py` change: 10 of 14 files) | the committed Test-step script with that selection | 546 ran / 0 failed, 5 s |
| scripts suite (now includes 69 kit tests + 7 wiring tests) | `pytest -q -s scripts` | 117 passed, 48.9 s |

Parallel pass counts equal the serial count (610 = 610, three times). A PR
that changes one cli source file runs ~5 s of tests instead of the whole
suite; CI wall time on hosted runners is not measured here — it lands with
the first real PR run.

## Selection

| change (probe commit on top of 0753276e) | selector mode | what the cli job runs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CHANGELOG.md` only (docs) | none | nothing: `cli: no tests selected for this change` |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | ALL | the whole suite via run_parallel |
| `cli/src/sbx/gpu.py` | subset: 10 files | `cd cli && python3 ../scripts/ci/run_parallel.py --runner pytest tests/test_cli.py tests/test_cp.py tests/test_gpu.py tests/test_just_created.py tests/test_migrate.py tests/test_runner_debug.py tests/test_runner_stats.py tests/test_runners.py tests/test_sdk_contract.py tests/test_templates.py` — the exact committed Test-step script, executed as-is with that `TESTS`: 546 ran / 0 failed, 5 s |

The gpu.py subset is every suite file that imports or names `sbx.gpu`
(`test_bump_version`, `test_release_smoke`, `test_small_gpu_recipe`,
`test_gpu_vram_docs` correctly stay out: they do not touch it). This PR's own
diff also selects ALL (it changes `.ci/affected.json` itself).

## Recall

`RUNNER=pytest TEST_GLOB` over the three CI suites,
`bash scripts/ci/recall.sh cli/src/sbx/cli.py scripts/bump_version.py
cookbook/small-gpu/run.py cookbook/tools/video_gate.py`, twice, identical
results both times:

| probe | selector | failing files | real misses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cli/src/sbx/cli.py` | 10 | 11 | 0 |
| `scripts/bump_version.py` | 2 | 3 | 0 |
| `cookbook/small-gpu/run.py` | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| `cookbook/tools/video_gate.py` | 3 | 2 | 0 |

Every failing file that the mutants actually broke was selected, every time:
all 10 importers/namers of `sbx.cli`; `test_bump_version.py` +
`scripts/test_bump_version_followups.py`; `test_small_gpu_recipe.py`;
`test_video_gate.py`. The one extra "failing" file, `scripts/test_ci_tools.py`
(the kit's own hermetic tests), is a probe-harness artifact, not a selector
miss — it depends on none of the four probed files, and with each mutant
committed it passes run alone (69 passed) and in a rerun of recall's exact
24-way pipeline at -P 1, 2, 4, 8 and 24 (failing set = exactly the true
dependents each time). It only dies while recall.sh's full loop runs during
host-load peaks on this shared machine; it is the most subprocess-hungry file
in the probe set, consistent with transient fork/memory pressure. Re-running
the identical pipeline minutes later loses the artifact.

## Deviations

- `scripts/ci/run_parallel.py` comes from agent-gateway `4e609a7`, while the other kit files come from `44a2ecce`; the files are unchanged between the two. At 0753276e the `contract` job (Python 3.10) failed only the kit's own `test_children_import_from_collection_roots_in_order`: 3.10 has no `-P`, so each child imported from the cwd ahead of the collection roots. Upstream fixed this in agent-gateway #324. With the new runner, `python3.10 -m unittest -q scripts.test_ci_tools` gives 69 tests OK (10 skipped: pytest absent).

- `scripts/test_ci_tools.py` is placed under `scripts/`, not the kit's default
  root `tests/`: no CI job collects a root `tests/` directory in this repo,
  while the contract job collects `scripts/`; the file locates `scripts/ci`
  via `parents[1]`, which resolves identically from `scripts/`.
- The contract job's change-detection is untouched (a separate open PR
  reworks it); the only addition is a job-level cron guard so the new nightly
  schedule does not turn the live contract check daily.
- `on: push` is restricted to `main` (the reference pattern): PR branches no
  longer run the full suite twice per push. This is a behavior change beyond
  the test selection itself.
- Measurements ran on a local 32-core host, not hosted runners (CI matrix
  3.10/3.13 vs local 3.12); pass counts are runner-independent, wall times are
  labeled as local.
- The recall harness artifact above: kit files stay verbatim (no edit to
  recall.sh's hardcoded `-P 24`), documented instead.

body:
Closes #739 (killed and sleeping tabs keep timers and terminals; each Codex tab runs a second process): item 1 is fixed here, item 2 is won't-do by the owner's decision, item 3 moved to #810.

- **What it does** — when a local Claude Code tab's `claude` is killed or crashes (ends without `/exit`), Koloft stops re-reading its transcript every half second, while its row stays in the sidebar as before.
- **What a user sees change** — no user-visible change. The row, its title and status are the same; only background polling stops.
- **Runtime code** — +14/−9 lines under `src/`.
- **How to see it in the shipped app** — no way from the app.
- **Confidence to ship as-is** — high: the only thing that now stops is reading a transcript whose `claude` is gone, and nothing re-reads a dead tab's row (`setAlive` is only ever called with `false`, from `tabLifecycle.ts`; a restart or wake makes a new tracked entry through `track()`).
- **Hand-test before merging** — no.

## What changed

`SessionTracker.setAlive(tabId, false)` — called on every pty teardown — now runs `stopFollowing(t)`, split out of `cleanup()`: it clears the 5 s subagent scan interval and the land timer, and unwatches the transcript and its title sidecar (two `fs.watchFile` polls at 500 ms). The tracked entry and its `info` stay, so the row stays. `watchTranscript` and `stopFollowing` now share one `unwatchTranscript`.

## Measured (before / after)

Scratch vitest (not committed): 20 tabs tracked and bound to transcripts in a temp `HOME`, then `setAlive(false)` on all, counting `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` 1.5 s later.

| | file watchers (500 ms polls) | timers |
|---|---|---|
| 20 live tabs | 40 | 40 |
| 20 killed tabs, before | 40 | 40 |
| 20 killed tabs, after | 0 | 20 |

The 20 timers left are one-shot run-state timers (waiting → idle, `sessionRuntime.ts`), not polls; the sleeping row's status still uses them.

## Each kind of session tab

| Tab | Item 1 (timers after the process ends) |
|---|---|
| Claude Code, local, killed or crashed | fixed here |
| Claude Code, local or remote, put to sleep | already untracked: sleeping goes `sleepTab` → `stopTabProcess` → `ClaudeBackend.stop()`, which calls `tracker.untrack` before the pty exits — unchanged |
| Claude Code, remote | already untracked on pty exit (`backends/claude.ts` `onPtyExit`) — unchanged |
| Codex, Muse, Antigravity — local and remote | no such leak: pty teardown calls `storedSessions.stop()`, which deletes the run; Muse's and Antigravity's single sweep interval stops itself when no live run is left (`museSessions.ts` `sweepRegistry`, `agySessions.ts` `tick`) |

## What ran

| Suite | Result | Why that one |
|---|---|---|
| `format:check` on changed files, `check:comments`, `typecheck` | pass | fast gates |
| `test:unit:changed` (8 files, 516 tests) | pass | import graph of the change |
| `sessionTracker.test.ts` (84 tests), after the test waits for the first parse before killing the tab | pass | the only file the review fix touched (test only, so the e2e round stands) |
| new unit test, red first | failed on `main`, passes here; also fails if `setAlive` only unwatches the files and forgets the 5 s interval | proves both kinds of polling stop |
| e2e `lifecycle`, `idle-auto-close`, `remote-kill`, `restart-session`, `claude-session` (`--workers=2`, 49 tests) | pass | the pty-exit, sleep/wake, remote exit, restart and plain local paths this touches |
| `/code-review low origin/main...HEAD` | no findings | |
| `/simplify` (4 angles) | one fix taken (shared `unwatchTranscript`, test waits past a 5 s scan) | |

Not run: other agents' e2e specs — Codex, Muse and Antigravity tabs do not go through `SessionTracker`.

## Out of scope

- **Item 2 (every sleeping tab keeps a mounted terminal)** — measured, not done; the saving is small. Scratch Playwright run on the built app with fake claude, 25 tabs put to sleep plus 1 awake, renderer read through CDP (`HeapProfiler.collectGarbage`, `Runtime.getHeapUsage`), `app.getAppMetrics()` and each xterm's buffer size:
  - 1 tab: JS heap 10.5 MB, 237 DOM nodes.
  - 25 asleep as left (one screen each): heap +6 MB, +2,150 DOM nodes, buffer cells ≈ 1.1 MB.
  - 25 asleep with 1,500 lines written into each (scrollback full at 1,000): heap +12 MB, buffer cells ≈ 22.6 MB at the test window's ~69 columns (≈ 39 MB at the 120-column cap, computed), renderer working set +60 MB (working set swung 158–197 MB between identical baseline runs, so read it loosely).
  - So about 1.5–2.5 MB per sleeping tab at worst, 25 tabs ≤ ~60 MB — about one Codex app-server (#810). Disposing and restoring from a saved screen risks lost lines, colours and scrollback for that. The e2e build draws with the DOM renderer; WebGL contexts are already capped by `webglPool`. Codex, Muse and Antigravity screens after their TUI ends were not probed (inferred: bounded by the full-scrollback run).
- **Item 3 (each local Codex tab runs its own app-server)** — still true after #755/#765, ~60 MB each idle (codex-cli 0.162.0); sharing one needs a design and a real-codex probe. Filed as #810 with the numbers.
- A killed local Claude tab whose turn had ended still turns idle after 4 min and, 30 min later, runs one `ps` and is turned into a sleeping tab (`sessionRuntime.ts` `tryAutoClose` → `index.ts` `sleepTab`). One-shot, existing behaviour, left as is.
- If a transcript parse is in flight at the moment the tab dies and the transcript is moved at that same moment, `adoptRelocated` could re-attach the watchers — inferred, not checked; not guarded, as nothing makes it likely.
- #609 (a sleeping tab's old screen keeps mouse and focus reports on) — related to item 2, untouched.

No toca `.github/**`, `.devsecops.yml`, dependencias, reglas de Firestore, IAM ni CSP. ## Tipo de cambio - [x] `fix` Corrección de error (accesibilidad / puerta de calidad) ## Cómo se probó - `npx vitest run`: 509 pruebas en verde (2 ejecuciones); `npm run lint` salida 0; tsc y build en verde. `modalesDetalleEstado.test.tsx` sin editar y en verde. - Mutaciones (cada una rompe exactamente 1 prueba): una regla a `warn`; `depth` 2; volver un `` a `div role="status"`; alias `jsx_a11y/...: off`; bloque `overrides`; bloque `ignorePatterns`. - Con el `.oxlintrc.json` nuevo y los tres `role="status"` sin cambiar, `npm run lint` daba exactamente 3 errores `prefer-tag-over-role` (por eso el commit de `` va primero: ningún commit deja el lint en rojo). - Revisión de código y de seguridad (agentes): aprobadas; la de seguridad concluye que endurece el control. ## Checklist de seguridad - [x] Sin secretos, IAM, reglas, dependencias, CSP, workflows ni `innerHTML`/`eval`/RegExp dinámicas. gitleaks sobre los commits: sin fugas. ## Impacto y rollback `git revert`; independiente de F1, F2 y F4. Riesgo: una versión nueva de oxlint puede detectar más casos en una regla existente → fallaría el PR de Dependabot, no `main` (la lista es explícita, las reglas nuevas no entran solas). ## Notas para el revisor - **Deuda conocida:** un `

body:
Request: w1537

Two changes, both asked for by lothsahn:

1. **fff-health gives a freshly started portal 300 s instead of 120 s** before it checks `/api/health` (`HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC`).
2. **`fffctl conf`: the orchestration worker can read and change the VM's own settings, `/etc/fff/fff.conf`.** lothsahn: "It should be able to touch any settings that aren't credentials or keys or secrets", and "Make sure when it prints, it doesn't print any secrets. Just prints the settings that changed."

## 1. The 300 s start grace

When the FFBox host rebooted, nine Actions runners fetching git-lfs at once saturated its two disks (rpool 80-90% busy, ~66 ms reads on the VM's zvol). The portal sat blocked on reads loading its 7.2 GB data folder (event-loop stalls of 32 s, 52 s and 277 s, 0% CPU, D state). fff-health restarted it at 220 s (the 120 s grace plus 4 failed checks) and again at 340 s, 12 s after it had already recovered, and each restart started the load over. A hang later in the portal's life is still restarted after 4 failed checks.

- `deploy/vm/guest/fff.conf.example`: `HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC=300`. Every script loads this file first (`deploy/vm/guest/lib.sh` `load_conf`).
- `docs/portal-on-ffbox-host.md`: "300 s start grace" (the production-timing line) and "5-minute start grace" (the fff-health.timer row).
- `deploy/vm/test/ci-vm-e2e.sh`: the comment that lists the defaults. The fast e2e still sets its own `HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC=20`.

**Effect on a live VM:** a VM whose `/etc/fff/fff.conf` has no `HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC` line gets 300 s at its next update. The installer never rewrites that file: `deploy/vm/guest/install.sh` writes it only when it is missing, and an update runs install.sh without `--repo`. A VM whose fff.conf sets the value keeps its own, and `fffctl conf set HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC 300` changes it.

## 2. `fffctl conf`

- `fffctl conf` (or `conf get [KEY]`): every key `fff.conf.example` defines, one line each, as `KEY=VALUE (set in ... | default)`. A refused key prints as `KEY=<redacted> (a person's: why)`. A value that looks like a token prints as `<redacted>` under any key.
- `fffctl conf set KEY VALUE`: checks the key, then the value (a number range, yes/no, HH:MM, a branch name or a relative folder; never a quote, `$`, space or backslash). It keeps the file before as `fff.conf.prev`, replaces or appends the line, and prints **one line**: `KEY: old -> new (takes effect ...; the file before is ...)`. An unchanged value prints `KEY: no change (...)`. It restarts nothing.
- **Fails closed:** only the keys in `CONF_CHECK` can be set. Refused: any name containing TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASS, CREDENTIAL, AUTH, PEM, CERT, PRIVATE, RECIPIENT, COOKIE or SALT; the backup key, recipients and target; the deploy's code (`FFF_REPO_URL`, `FFF_BRANCH`, `BASE_REPO_URL`); the VM's layout (`FFF_ROOT`, `FFF_USER`, `FFF_PORT`, `BASE_PATH`); the worker's own fences (`OPS_*`); and any key in neither list.
- **When each setting takes effect:** the health and watchdog settings at the next 30 s check, since `fff-health` runs `load_conf` on every run. `NODE_MAJOR` and `BACKUP_TIME` only at the next `fffctl update`. The table is in docs/ops-worker.md, "fff.conf settings (w1537)".
- **Secrets stay out of the logs:**
  - `fff-ops-priv` logs `conf set KEY (value not logged)`.
  - `fffctl` logs the change, redacted.
  - The server's guard (`server/opsWorker.ts`, `FFFCTL_CONF_SECRET_NAME`, kept equal to fffctl's by a test) refuses secret names and token-like values before sudo, so they never reach sudo's log.
- The charter (`docs/ops-worker.md`) and the worker's prompt say it changes a setting only when Lothsahn or Ben asks.
- **Tests:**
  - `deploy/vm/test/fff-conf.test.sh` (new, in lint.sh) runs against a fixture fff.conf that holds secrets. It checks that set prints exactly the changed line, that `fff.conf.prev` is kept, that exactly one line changes, and that `load_conf` reads the new value. It also checks "no change", every refused key and bad value, and that no output or log line carries a secret. It fails when a new `fff.conf.example` key is not classified.
  - `fff-ops.test.sh`: the wrapper's forms.
  - `server/opsFffctlForms.test.ts` and `server/opsWorker.test.ts`: the guard.

**Once deployed**, the worker sets the 300 s grace with `fffctl conf set HEALTH_START_GRACE_SEC 300`. It applies within 30 s and nothing restarts.

## Checks

- **prepush** on lothdesktop, run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-strip-types` (Node 22.17.1 here; the repo wants >=23.6):
  - typecheck OK (web skipped: no web/node_modules)
  - gitleaks OK
  - identity OK
  - shellcheck FAILED, on 50 SC2015 notes (info). Unchanged origin/main gives the same 50 on this Windows machine, with shellcheck 0.9.0 and 0.10.0 alike, and main's Linux lint is green. This change adds no finding. CI's Linux lint is the check that counts.
- Measured locally: `fff-conf.test.sh` 6/6 ok; `opsFffctlForms.test.ts` + `opsWorker.test.ts` 29/29 pass. `fff-ops.test.sh` needs jq and root, so it runs in CI.

author: windoliver
body:
## Issue

Closes #48

Two of #48's criteria moved on Oct 18 to the issues that build what they read: the coexistence run to #18 (the record of a typed permission answer) and the manual evaluation with skill hygiene to #26 (the skill and `deep_claim`). Both now depend on #48. The five criteria #48 holds are all proven below.

## What it adds

- `scripts/agent-harness.mjs run | all | budgets`:
  - **Sessions:** real Claude Code sessions in a pseudo-terminal with `--settings`, never `claude -p`. The held-stop and idle-wake scenarios reproduce the October 4 results.
  - **Read-only jobs:** Claude Code and Codex, launched with exactly what their `adapter.facts@1` files name, the prompt on stdin, and an allowlisted environment.
  - **Run line:** one JSON line per run with verdict, model, tokens, cost and cap.
    - **Cost:** `reported` for Claude Code. For Codex on a plan it's `unpriced`: tokens only, never `$0`, held to a token cap.
    - **Cleanup:** every process a run started is found by ancestry and stopped by PID.
- `scripts/agent-harness-hook.mjs`: the Stop hold and the `asyncRewake` waiter a session's `--settings` runs.
- `adapters/claude-code.facts.json`, `adapters/codex.facts.json`: draft facts files that hold only the launch, sign-in, usage and transcript fields the harness reads. #312 owns the full schema.
- **Preflight lane:** `harness budgets` runs after perf, outside the checks' budget.
  - It runs every session when a change touches the harness, its hook or its launch facts. Otherwise it is `UNTOUCHED` and starts no agent.
  - It holds each session to 60 s and the whole run to 10 minutes, on the reference Mac only.
  - It compares with the merge base's harness, with a 100% margin because model latency is noisy. When the base has none, as now, it reports `INITIAL`.
- The `harness` budget in `benchmarks/budgets.json` joins the frozen budgets, so it can't be changed or removed once it's on main.

## Proof

- **Fails before:**
  - On an export of `1de288c`, all 20 fast acceptance tests fail: no harness, no lane.
  - The new `validateBudgets` test failed with `Missing expected exception` before the freeze.
- **Passes after:**
  - `node --test tests/acceptance/48/harness.test.mjs`: 20/20.
  - `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: 27/27.
  - `DEEP_HARNESS_LIVE=1 node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/acceptance/48/harness.live.test.mjs`: 7/7 on Claude Code 2.1.303 (Haiku) and Codex 0.144.0 (`gpt-reserve`).
  - `npm run preflight`: every lane passes, perf passes against the merge base, and the harness lane is `INITIAL`.
- **Wrong programs:** each of 13 planted twins of the harness or preflight fails the tests tagged for its criterion:
  - no cost cap, no token cap, unpriced printed as `$0`, usage counted per transcript entry, cached input left in input;
  - no descendant tracking, no cleanup on SIGTERM, inherited environment, no pseudo-terminal, `claude -p`;
  - a lane that runs on any change, a hard-coded session limit, a preflight that ignores the lane.
- **Evidence:** the harness run log for both October 4 scenarios, from the preflight's lane on the reference Mac (Mac15,7, M3 Pro, 36 GB, AC power), paths left out:

```json
{"scenario":"held-stop","agent":"claude","verdict":"PASS","stop":"done","elapsedMs":8355,"cost":{"basis":"reported","usd":0.0095},"cap":{"usd":0.5},"processes":{"lingered":[]}}
{"scenario":"idle-wake","agent":"claude","verdict":"PASS","stop":"done","elapsedMs":10447,"cost":{"basis":"reported","usd":0.0043},"cap":{"usd":0.5},"processes":{"lingered":[]}}
{"scenario":"read-only-job","agent":"claude","verdict":"PASS","stop":"done","elapsedMs":6071,"cost":{"basis":"reported","usd":0.0037},"cap":{"usd":0.5}}
{"scenario":"read-only-job","agent":"codex","verdict":"PASS","stop":"done","elapsedMs":7449,"cost":{"basis":"unpriced"},"cap":{"tokens":300000}}
{"lane":"harness budgets","status":"INITIAL","reason":"first measurement: the merge base has no harness","touched":["adapters/claude-code.facts.json","adapters/codex.facts.json","scripts/agent-harness-hook.mjs","scripts/agent-harness.mjs"],"machine":{"model":"Mac15,7","reference":true},"current":{"wholeMs":32323},"over":[]}
```

In the held stop, the session replied `READY`. The Stop hold returned the answer with a fresh code word, and the next reply was exactly that word. In the idle wake, the session sat idle 3.7 s before the waiter woke it with the code word. A live run with a $0.0001 cap stopped at `cost_cap`, and a Codex run with a 1-token cap stopped at `token_cap`. Codex's read-only sandbox rejected its patch, and Claude Code's Write was denied in `dontAsk` mode.

## Still open

- Claude Code's read-only job relies on `--permission-mode dontAsk`, not an OS sandbox. A user allow rule for Bash could get past it until #236's Seatbelt backend lands.
- The lane's comparison against a merge base that already has a harness can't run until this lands.
- The kept transcripts hold the account's email and system prompt. They stay in the run's `--out` folder and are never evidence.
- Size: about 300 handwritten lines, plus 26 in existing files. The 1,458 lines under `tests/acceptance/48/` were written by the blind drafting job.
- This machine runs Node 23.9 against the pinned 22.19. vitest warns about it, and that predates this change.

author: degoke
body:
## What and why

`POST [base]/Patient/$match` answered `405`. A clinic that is sent a person has to find out whether it already holds them, and FHIR R4 has an operation for that. It now takes the R4 `Parameters` (`resource`, `onlyCertainMatches`, `count`) and answers a `searchset` Bundle, best first, with `search.score` and the `match-grade` extension on each entry. The algorithm is the server's own, and is a table (`Rules` in `crates/fhir/src/patient_match.rs`) so it can be read and tuned in one place. It is described for users in [FHIR API](docs/fhir-api.md#finding-a-patient-patientmatch).

| Grade | When | Score |
|-------|------|-------|
| `certain` | An identifier has the same `system` and `value` (exact) | 1 |
| `probable` | The same name, full birth date, and a phone number or email address in `Patient.telecom` | 0.75 to 0.95 |
| `possible` | The same name and full birth date | 0.40 to 0.70 |

- **Names** ignore case, accents (Yoruba dots included), punctuation and word order, so a family name written as a given name matches. A different birth date is never a match.
- **Phone numbers** are compared by what they dial (`+234 803…`, `0803…` and `2348031…` are one number); a number written without a country code is taken as Nigerian.
- **`onlyCertainMatches`** returns one Patient or nothing: when more than one Patient is a potential match, nothing is returned, as R4 says. `count` is applied after.
- **Each entry says what it matched**, in repeated `https://refhir.dev/StructureDefinition/match-evidence` extensions on `search`. The identifier, phone number and email address are the request's own, so a caller with several can tell which one matched.
- **Replaced and inactive Patients.** A Patient with `active` false and nothing that replaced it is never returned. A match on one that another replaced (`link` type `replaced-by`) is the Patient that replaced it: relative `Patient/id` links in this store, up to five, never round a cycle, to a Patient in use. That result is capped at `probable`, so it is never `certain` and `onlyCertainMatches` never returns it, and it carries `replaced-record` evidence. Its other evidence is what the returned Patient itself shares with the request.
- **Candidates** come from the existing `identifier` and `birthdate` search parameters, a page at a time. More than 20,000 sharing an identifier or birth date is a `422` (`too-costly`) rather than a partial answer; more than 50 identifiers, names or telecoms in the request is a `400`.

## How it was tested

- 41 tests in `patient_match.rs` (normalisation, grading, request parsing, paging, the replaced-by walk including chains, cycles and dead ends) and 23 over HTTP in `match_tests.rs`, one shared server seeded with a registration desk's cases. Both run against a small Patient package (`fixtures/patient-match`), not the whole R4 release, so the server test binary stays quick.
- An audit test: the operation is recorded as an operation on `Patient`, with no query and nothing of what it looked for.
- I reverted the scope mapping, the replaced/inactive filter, the one-certain rule, the cap and the other review fixes one at a time; each time the tests written for it failed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace` pass, **except `tests::cluster::healthz_tells_a_balancer_which_processes_can_take_traffic`**, which fails on a loaded machine (it has a 300 ms staleness window): it passes alone every time, and it failed in runs with this module's tests skipped.
- **Not run:** the Postgres tests. "Only the store the request was made to is searched" rests on every read going through the request's own transaction; I did not test it against a shared tenant database.

## Things to look at

- **Access.** A POST operation was judged as `create`. `$match` is now judged as `search` (`auth/scopes.rs`, POST only), so `user/Patient.read` and `user/Patient.rs` can use it and `user/Patient.c` cannot. A patient-scoped token is refused, because the operation reads every Patient there is. It is not available over `/sync`. Replicas answer it themselves.
- **The replaced-by decision** is the one most worth a second opinion: following the link means the server returns a Patient that the request did not itself match. The cap and the evidence are what make that safe to use; `Rules::replaced_by` set to `None` leaves replaced Patients out instead.
- **Request body is JSON.** The server's XML converter does not produce FHIR Parameters, so an XML body is a clear `415` instead of "resource is required".
- **New dependency:** `unicode-normalization` (MIT/Apache-2.0) for accent folding. It was already in `Cargo.lock` through `idna`; the lock only gains it as a dependency of `refhir-fhir`.
- **Fixtures:** `crates/fhir/fixtures/patient-match` copies three search parameters from `minir4` and one from `extra`; a test keeps them equal to the originals.
- The branch merged `main` (release 0.0.2); the CHANGELOG entry is under *Unreleased*, not the released section.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all` and `cargo test --workspace` pass (apart from the load-flaky `healthz` test above)
- [x] I added or updated tests
- [x] I updated the docs and `refhir.toml.example` if a flag, setting, endpoint or behavior changed (docs updated; no setting was added)
- [x] I added a line under *Unreleased* in `CHANGELOG.md`
- [x] A schema change is a new numbered migration in **both** SQLite and Postgres, and no shipped migration was edited (no schema change)
- [x] No secrets, tokens or real patient data are included

## Related issue
Closes #2504

## Summary
The breast-cancer PRS77 model is `source_verified_runtime_blocked`, so `run_cancer_prs` skips it for every sample. It never became a finding, and #2501's `withheld_traits` deliberately excludes models that are not runtime-scored. So the Cancer page showed prostate, colorectal and melanoma gauges and nothing about breast. The only explanation was a `!!! note` in `docs/modules/health-risk/cancer.md`, and the page's own breast absolute-risk overlay made the missing gauge more likely to read as a bug.

**What changed.**
- **API.** `CancerPRSListResponse` gains `unavailable_models`: one `{trait, name, reason}` per bundled model that is not runtime-scored. `reason` is `runtime_blocked` or `scoring_disabled`, taken from the existing `PRSWeightSet.runtime_scoring_blocked` and `is_runtime_scored`, which are not re-implemented. It is kept separate from the sex-gate `withheld_traits`.
- **Never contradicts or duplicates.** A model already shown (a legacy stored row) or already named by the sex gate is left out.
- **One load.** `list_cancer_prs` now loads the weight sets once and passes them to `_apply_sex_gate`.
- **UI.** `PRSWithheldNotice` takes an `unavailable` list and renders it in the same `role="note"`, in the PRS tier and in the empty state:
  - `runtime_blocked`: "… is not shown: this model is not currently scored or reported. Its source is verified, but it cannot yet be scored safely." The wording follows the marker's definition ("exact source is valid but whose runtime representation is unsafe"), so it stays true for any future runtime-blocked model, not only breast.
  - `scoring_disabled`: "… is not currently scored or reported."
- **Docs.** The breast note in `cancer.md` says the page names the model. The docs-consistency phrases are untouched.

## Definition of Done
- [x] One cohesive change, reasonably sized (split if not)
- [x] `lint` is green (Ruff check + Ruff format + Vulture + ESLint + Knip)
- [x] `test-backend` (py3.12 + py3.13) and `test-frontend` (Vitest) pass

Two rows do not apply. There is no carriage-gated finding, and no new scientific claim: the runtime block and its reason are already recorded in the panel and cited in `cancer.md`.

- **Backend tests** (new class `TestCancerPRSUnavailableModels`, 9 tests):
  - breast is named `runtime_blocked` for XX, XY, `manual_review`, `unknown` and none, and no active model is ever named;

  - `GET /api/analysis/cancer/prs?sample_id=2` returns colorectal and melanoma, prostate/`sex_mismatch`, and breast/`runtime_blocked`.
  - The page lists both lines in the PRS tier.
  - axe reports 0 violations in light and dark themes.
- Backend suites pass: cancer/PRS/route 380 and docs 25. `mkdocs build --strict` is clean.

On 11259dbc: ruff check, ruff format --check and vulture clean; backend cancer/PRS/route 380 and docs 25 passed, with 9 new tests; mutation checks fail the new tests; frontend lint, knip and build clean, Vitest 1935/1935; mkdocs build --strict clean; Playwright MCP real-data check on sample 2 with axe 0 violations in light and dark themes; local codex review --base origin/main found no issues. author: chrisshaiman
body:
## What was wrong

The rest of #528's MongoDB item. The host ran `mongodb-org 8.0.21`, which refuses kernels 6.19+ unless `rseq` is forced on (now managed, #809). MongoDB fixed the allocator in 8.0.30 (SERVER-125742) for kernels 7.0.14+, and the host has been on 7.0.0-38 (the 7.0.14 stable series) since tonight's reboot; the 8.0 repository offers up to 8.0.34. The role installed `mongodb-org` with `state: present`, so it would never have upgraded, and it had no pin, so a fresh host would get whatever the repository served that day.

Reading the role for the upgrade found a second thing: it enabled and started **both** `mongod` and `mongodb`. CAPE's installer removed the package's `mongod.service` and runs its own `mongodb.service` (no config file, data in `/data/db`). A package upgrade re-extracts `/usr/lib/systemd/system/mongod.service`, after which that loop would enable and start a second mongod on port 27017 against an empty `/var/lib/mongodb`. Whichever won the port at boot would decide whether CAPE saw its reports.

## Change

- `defaults/main.yml`: `mongodb_version: "8.0.34"`, `mongodb_unit: mongodb`, `mongodb_rollback_dir`.
- Every `mongodb-org*` package installed at the pin, `allow_downgrade: true` so the previous pin is the way back.
- Before a version change: `mongodump --gzip --db cuckoo` to `/root/lamware-rollback/mongodb/cuckoo-<installed>-<date>.archive.gz` (skipped when the installed version already equals the pin).
- `mongod.service` masked. Only `{{ mongodb_unit }}` enabled and started.
- Handlers flushed after the install, then the running server's `db.version()` must equal the pin, or the deploy fails.
- `tests/test_mongodb_upgrade_is_pinned_and_backed_up.py` (structural: seven pinned packages, dump before install and only on a change, mask plus single unit, version read from the server after the restart).

## Scope

- **MongoDB consumers on the host:** CAPE (`cape`, `cape-processor`, `cape-web`) through `127.0.0.1:27017`; nothing in lamware's own services uses MongoDB. The LiteLLM/Keycloak/API containers do not.
- **Unit files:** CAPE's `mongodb.service` (kept, with the rseq drop-in from #809) and the package's `mongod.service` (masked).
- **Data path:** `/data/db` (CAPE's unit passes no config; `/etc/mongod.conf` is unused). The dump targets the live server, so it covers the right data.
- **Unattended upgrades:** the MongoDB repository is not an allowed origin, so the pin is the only thing that moves the version.
- **Roles deployed:** `mongodb`.

## Rollback

Stated before the change, CLAUDE.md §5. A patch release within 8.0 keeps `featureCompatibilityVersion` 8.0, so the way back is `mongodb_version: "8.0.21"` and `make deploy TAGS=mongodb` (the install task allows the downgrade, the handler restarts the unit, the verify task confirms 8.0.21 is serving). If the data ever needed restoring: `mongorestore --gzip --archive=/root/lamware-rollback/mongodb/cuckoo-8.0.21-<date>.archive.gz --drop`. Verified before the change: `mongodump`/`mongorestore` present on the host, 239 GB free for the archive (cuckoo is 7.7 GB of data, 3.7 GB on disk).

## Host evidence

Deployed by the operator from this branch with `make deploy TAGS=mongodb,security-test`: `failed=0`, smoke gate `14 passed, 0 failed`; the deploy's own verify task read `8.0.34` from the running server.

On the host afterwards:
- `mongosh` → `db.version()` **8.0.34**; `ping` ok; `cuckoo.analysis` **275** documents (unchanged); `featureCompatibilityVersion` **8.0**.
- Dump taken before the package change: `/root/lamware-rollback/mongodb/cuckoo-8.0.21-2026-10-18.archive.gz`, 1.03 GB, `0600 root`.
- The package's `/usr/lib/systemd/system/mongod.service` was re-extracted by the upgrade, exactly the hazard the mask is for; `systemctl is-enabled mongod` → `masked`. CAPE's `mongodb` unit active since 22:40:05 (the handler's restart), `NRestarts=0` after it, `Environment=GLIBC_TUNABLES=glibc.pthread.rseq=1` still applied.
- No `SERVER-121912`, `cannot start` or `fatal` line in the unit's journal; `cape`, `cape-processor`, `cape-web` active throughout.
- **A full detonation on the upgraded server** (capture-check sample `42b9c406…`): CAPE task 1304 `reported`, its report written to and read back from MongoDB 8.0.34 (`cuckoo.analysis` 275 → **276**, one document with `info.id: 1304`), analysis 1197 `completed`, `critical`, **16 correlations** (the baseline), 0 tracebacks, the two known `Errno 13` peek lines.

```
==> Merge check passed.
    Provenance commit: 7a200bdea13c0d2d987ee4616d5d25e4bbe9977d
    Branch:            fix/mongodb-upgrade-pinned
    Verified at:       2026-10-19T05:55:03Z
```

## Not verified

- **Rolling back in anger.** The downgrade path is the same task with the previous pin; it was reasoned from FCV semantics, not executed.
- **Whether 8.0.34 still needs the rseq drop-in** on CAPE's unit: the drop-in stays either way (it corrects CAPE's `rseq=0` line), so this was not isolated.
- **A reboot on 8.0.34.** The unit starts under the drop-in as before; the next reboot is the observation.

author: omgitsthedm
body:
The owner said "do and fix it all" about the remaining plan. This is Phase 3 of the customer-experience plan: customer accounts, saved pieces, drop early access and reviews. It also covers two monitoring gaps.

**Accounts** (`/account/`, `server/customers/`, `/api/account/*`)
- Sign in with a passkey only. No password, name or email address is asked for or stored, only each passkey's public key, so the site sends no account email.
- Sessions are random tokens stored as SHA-256 hashes, kept for 90 days in `__Host-aha_account` (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict).
- Every change needs a same-origin request plus the account header. Sign-in attempts are limited to 30 per 15 minutes per IP.
- Deleting an account removes its passkeys, sessions, saved pieces and order links.
- The account page does WebAuthn in about 1 KB of its own code; the server verifies with `@simplewebauthn/server`.

**Saved pieces:** Save for later on product pages keeps a list in the browser. Signing in merges it into the account, and it syncs while signed in.

**Orders:** the order page's Add to my account links the order through its signed link. An order belongs to one account.

**Reviews** (`/api/reviews`, Admin → Reviews)
- Only from an order's private link, only after it ships, one per product per order.
- Every review waits for the owner's approval, and an edit goes back for approval.
- Product pages show approved reviews only, CDN-cached until a moderation purges `reviews-<slug>`. Nothing is seeded or invented.

**Early access** (`src/data/drops.json`, empty today)
- Before `releaseAt`, the checkout quote refuses a drop unless the shopper is signed in and `earlyAccessAt` has passed (`early_access_only`).
- Feeds leave it out until release, and their CDN copy expires at the release.
- The product page shows both times and locks buying for everyone else.

**Also**
- Film plays and account creation reach analytics: GA4 `film_play` and `sign_up`, PostHog `film_played` and `account_created`. No personal data.
- Lighthouse CI now also checks `/shop/` and `/shop/mighty-micks/`. Local mobile runs: LCP 2.1 s and 2.2 s, CLS 0.061 and 0.027, TBT 10 ms and 30 ms.
- Additive migration `20261019100000_customer_accounts`, byte-identical at both discovery paths. The admin overview still loads if it isn't applied yet.
- Privacy page: new sections for accounts and reviews.
- Script budget:

  | Scripts | Size | Cap |
  |---|---|---|
  | Public storefront | 58.3 KB | 65 KB |
  | Private order and account pages | 8.0 KB | 12 KB (new) |
  | Admin | 25.9 KB | 40 KB |

**Checks run locally**
- Production and preview `npm run check`: 228/228 tests.
- Playwright: 76 passed in production; 66 passed and 10 skipped in preview.
- New `tests/browser/accounts.spec.ts` covers:
  - real passkeys with Chrome's virtual authenticator (create, save and sync, sign out and back in, delete; a deleted passkey is refused);
  - order linking and the review form;
  - reviews on product pages and the early-access lock;
  - axe on the account and order pages.
- New `tests/accounts.test.mjs` covers the server: CSRF, the attempt limit, saved-piece validation, order ownership, cascade deletion, review rules and moderation with purge and audit, drop windows, checkout locks and feed exclusion.
- The live renderer stays byte-identical to the built product pages (`tests/live-catalog.test.mjs`).
- `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities.

Not built: one-tap Apple Pay and Google Pay on product pages. It changes the quote-then-pay design, and proving it needs a payment on a real phone, which isn't authorized.

author: lloydcoder
body:
## Security gap
The authenticated World Intelligence query API previously ignored `QueryContext`, did not use the existing tenant policy table or authorization helper, and returned global query pages based only on a shared bearer token. No per-query tenant/capability/purpose decision or access audit was enforced.

## Changes
- Require tenant, subject, and purpose context on every protected query request; missing context fails closed.
- Derive the required capability from the route, not a caller-supplied capability header.
- Enforce per-tenant allowed capabilities and purposes for in-memory and PostgreSQL query paths.
- Filter in-memory rows that explicitly carry tenant/subject ownership.
- Append allowed/denied query audit events; PostgreSQL audit events use the existing append-only table.
- Add HTTP, unit, and PostgreSQL integration coverage for missing context, unknown tenants, capability denial, purpose denial, and audit evidence.

## Boundary
World Intelligence remains a data/query service, not an identity or execution authority. The authenticated Platform service is expected to provide the tenant/subject/purpose context from its verified principal. Canonical global world-state tables remain global by design; tenant-specific candidate source evidence remains separately scoped.

## Acceptance
All CI and security checks must pass before merge. The canonical TADL gate will subsequently run the PostgreSQL policy integration test against the pinned World Intelligence revision.

author: mrauhala
body:
engine-odim serializes cold loads of a PVOL volume file behind a per-file lock, `PixelCache::with_file_load`. A request that found another request's load in flight waited on that lock's `std::sync::Mutex` on its runtime worker. The holder meanwhile downloads the file as a task on the same runtime: the query runtime, for EDR and GetFeatureInfo. With waiters parked on every worker, nothing ran that download or drove the runtime's I/O and timer drivers. The runtime then stalled for good, and every EDR query and GetFeatureInfo on it hung past its deadline.

A one-volume walk loads inside the lock, so one more concurrent cold one-volume walk on a file than the runtime has workers is enough. GetFeatureInfo is such a walk and is admitted by render slots, not by EDR admission, so a burst of GetFeatureInfo requests on one cold volume can reach that count.

## Change

- The per-file lock is now `FileLoad`, a flag under a mutex plus a condvar. The mutex guards the flag only, never the load.
- A free lock is taken at once.
- A waiter on a multi-thread runtime waits inside `block_in_place`, through `off_core`, so the runtime's other workers keep running tasks and driving I/O and timers. On a blocking-pool worker or outside a runtime it waits directly.
- The wait ends at the request deadline in scope. `with_file_load` then returns `DeadlineExceeded` without running the load, and nothing is marked bad, as with any other deadline (#993). Without a deadline, as in the poll-time pre-warm, it waits until the load ends, as before.
- `with_file_load` returns a `Result`, and `load_many`'s error type is `DataServerError`.
- engine-odim now lists tokio's `rt-multi-thread` feature, which `block_in_place` needs. Until now it came only through feature unification.
- Root CLAUDE.md, Critical Rule 7: never wait on a runtime worker for work that needs that runtime, a single-flight cache wait included. The rule names GRIB's field jobs, which already wait for their cache fills inside `block_in_place`. engine-odim's CLAUDE.md describes the lock.

## Tests

- `one_volume_walks_waiting_on_a_cold_file_leave_the_runtime_running` runs four concurrent one-volume walks on one cold remote file, on a 2-worker runtime with a 200 ms GET. All four answer as a walk alone does, and the store sees one GET.
- `walks_waiting_on_a_cold_file_stop_at_their_deadline`: a walk without a deadline downloads the file over 2 s. Three walks with a 300 ms deadline arrive meanwhile. Each returns `DeadlineExceeded` well before the download ends and downloads nothing, and the first walk then answers.
- `file_load_waiter_gives_up_at_its_deadline` checks the deadline at the lock itself, without I/O.
- The walk tests run on a runtime that is never dropped. A stalled runtime fails them at a 20 s watchdog instead of hanging the test binary.

Checked against each half of the fix, by disabling it:
- Without `block_in_place` and without the deadline, as on main, both walk tests stall the runtime and fail at the watchdog.
- With `block_in_place` but no deadline, the deadline test fails: the waiters answer once the 2 s download ends instead of at 300 ms. The lock-level test cannot run, because its holder waits for the waiter to return.
- With the deadline but no `block_in_place`, the walks test fails after 10 s with a walk's error: the waiters held both workers until their deadline. The deadline test still passes there, since a condvar timeout needs no runtime.

Closes #1200
Refs #1127

author: lothsahn
body:
**TL;DR:** A Windows tray app, built and started by the machine daemon, pauses and unpauses all FF Factory work on that PC: by hand, on a work schedule, and when a person types or clicks (90 minutes idle to resume, 30 s grace after a tray unpause). A paused machine counts as held (the existing `placement.hold`), shows amber "Paused" on the machines view, and its workers commit, push and hand their requests back to the dispatcher, which re-places them elsewhere. Shown end to end on beast against a throwaway portal; nothing live was paused or touched. Deploying is lothsahn's call.

Request: w1532

## What it does

- **Tray app** (`machine/tray/FFFactoryTray.cs`, `machine/tray.ts`). The daemon compiles it with the C# compiler .NET Framework 4 puts on every Windows 10/11 PC (no SDK, no binary committed), into `<app_dir>/tray`. It rebuilds whenever the sources change, so a daemon update updates it. The daemon runs in the logged-on user's session (its logon task uses InteractiveToken), so the tray it starts shows in that user's notification area at logon. They talk over stdin/stdout (JSON lines, UTF-8). The icon is the portal's favicon converted to .ico at 16 to 256 px, with a grey F and an orange pause sign while paused (`make-icons.py`). Menu: the state, why, what comes next, agents here; Pause all work / Unpause; Work schedule…; Pause when someone uses this PC; Open FF Factory.
- **Pause rules** (`machine/pauseRules.ts`, pure) and the keeper (`machine/pause.ts`, `<app_dir>/pause.json`), reported to the portal in the hello and in a new `pause` message.
- **Portal** (`server/machinePause.ts`, `Agents.placement()`, `Orchestrators.handBack`, `SessionManager.pauseHeld`): a paused machine joins `placement.hold`, so no new work is placed there, the Capacity block says `HELD`, and nothing resumes there (w1376). Its work is handed back. Standing agents start no run there. The machines view shows "Paused" with the reason.

## Decisions (settled by research and the beast runs)

1. **How the three combine: the latest event wins, and a person at the keyboard wins over both.** The base state is the latest of a tray Pause/Unpause and the schedule's last edge (a window's start unpauses, its end pauses: lothsahn's words). So a tray pause holds until the tray unpauses or the next window starts. A tray unpause outside the window holds until the next edge. With no schedule, the tray's last word holds. A person's input pauses a machine that would otherwise run (inside the window or after a tray unpause), until 90 minutes pass with no input. It also holds across a window's start, because someone is still at the machine. A tray unpause clears it and ignores input for 30 s. Changing the schedule never brings back a tray word the schedule had already replaced (found in the beast run, test added). Why: lothsahn described the schedule as events ("unpause when the schedule begins"), and a thermostat-style "latest event wins" rule never surprises the person who acted last.
2. **Settings live on the machine** (`pause.json`); the portal shows them read-only. Why: the schedule and the activity watch are about the person at that PC. They must keep working while the portal is unreachable and survive daemon restarts and updates. The portal only needs the result, which it already uses to hold the machine.
3. **Hand-back.** A worker mid-turn is told once: finish the current step, commit and push everything unfinished (WIP is fine), release any Unity slot, bench lock or player, and end with `wNNN: handed back: branch <b> pushed; <where it stopped>`. When its turn ends, FF Factory stops the process, saves anything still uncommitted on its branch (w656 `save_work`), takes the request off the worker, sets it Queued with `WorkItem.handedBack`, and tells the dispatcher to `switch_branch` a free sandbox on an unpaused computer to that branch and `start_agent` there. The new worker's handover quotes the note. If a turn ends without the line, the worker gets 60 s for its queued notice to run as a turn of its own (seen on beast). If it is still mid-turn 15 min after the notice, its turn is interrupted, and the process is stopped 2 min later if that does not end it. A lock holder gets no longer: a bench measured while a person uses the PC measures nothing, and the notice asks it to release the lock first. A worker between turns is not woken: its process stops, and its requests move only when something would resume it (check-in, CI, a reply). That message is then carried to the next worker. Built on the existing mechanisms (`placement.hold`, the w1376 resume hold, w656 save_work, `moveOff`, the handover note), not a parallel one.
4. **Standing agents pause; the ops worker's machine updates do not.** A standing run waits on a paused machine, as it does on an offline one, and a run already going finishes. Updates take about a minute, keep the fleet on one daemon commit, and are what update the tray itself.

## Agents' input never counts as a person (measured on beast with the real tray)

Low-level hooks count only key or button presses without `LLKHF_INJECTED`/`LLMHF_INJECTED` (or their lower-integrity forms). On beast, 5 `SendInput` keys, 5 `keybd_event` keys (the way `scripts/agent/osdrive.py` presses keys) and 3 `mouse_event` clicks all arrived flagged injected. `PostMessage` keys (the way `scripts/agent/post_key.py` sends them) never reached the hook. The result was 0 person input, the state stayed RUNNING, and the tray logged "ignored 10 injected key press(es) and 3 injected click(s)". Unity MCP drives the game inside the editor and sends no OS input. Mouse movement does not count.

**Found on beast:** its Left Ctrl is held down (607 non-injected auto-repeats in 20 s, no release, no mouse movement; `GetAsyncKeyState` = 0x8001). Without handling, that would pause beast forever. The tray now counts only a key's first press, and ignores keys already down when the hooks start (the stuck Ctrl gave 340 repeats and 0 person keys). Also found: a **Windows Security firewall prompt for `finalfactory.exe`** (a player started outside the slot pool) is in front on beast. While it is there, Windows drops injected mouse input (UIPI) after the hooks have seen it. So on beast, agents' `mouse_event` clicks do nothing until a person answers that prompt. I left it alone: allowing or cancelling it is a person's call.

## Evidence

Run on beast, 2026-10-19 05:28 to 05:34 UTC (the final run after the UI fixes; earlier runs showed the same). The setup: the real `server/index.ts` on 127.0.0.1:8899 with a throwaway config, plus two in-process test machines from this branch. **testbeast** had the real tray app in beast's desktop session (pid 8736, session 1, both hooks); **testother** had none. The agent was the scripted fake; with the change in `e2e/fakeAgent.ts`, it really commits and pushes when it gets the pause notice. Log: `demo-evidence.log` in the review folder.

- **Tray installed and started by the daemon code:** `tray: built …pp	ray\FFFactoryTray.exe (build 402737eac2fd9cb8) with …\Framework644.0.30319\csc.exe`, `tray: running, pid 8736 in session 1, hooks: keyboard and mouse`, `tray: shown in the taskbar (Windows 11 NotifyIconSettings …)`.
- **Manual pause, worker commits and pushes, request re-placed:** `pause: PAUSED (manual)` → portal `machine testbeast: PAUSED (manual)` → `told worker fc6bcb75 … (w1) to hand back` → Capacity `testbeast … ROOM 91% but HELD (paused from its tray app: paused by hand (w1532))` → `w1 handed back from worker fc6bcb75 on testbeast/slot5 (by its worker); branch sandbox/slot5` → origin `8c47dee WIP: w1 handed back at a machine pause` → `switch_branch testother/slot2: … checked out sandbox/slot5 from origin` → `start_agent` worker ec6aa629 on testother/slot2, whose first message carries `Handed back (w1532): w1 was taken off worker fc6bcb75 on testbeast/slot5 …` → `testother/slot2 is on sandbox/slot5: 8c47dee WIP … half-done.txt there: true`.

Closes #99

## What this changes

`TestLoggedValuesLeaveOutIdentitiesAndCredentials` searched the whole JSON log line for secrets such as `"4455"`. The line's `time` field (`2026-10-19T05:16:50.170044554Z`) can carry the same digits in its nanoseconds, so the test failed now and then with no code change.

**What the tests search now:** tests that search a JSON line for a digit secret of nine characters or fewer (a timestamp can hold a run that long) now log through `untimedJSONLogger`. It is a `slog.NewJSONHandler` whose `ReplaceAttr` drops the top-level `slog.TimeKey`. These tests are:
- `internal/sip/logvalue_test.go`:
  - `TestLoggedValuesLeaveOutIdentitiesAndCredentials` (`4455`, `10.20.30.40`, `192.0.2.1`, …);
  - `TestViaLogsItsHostLikeAURIAndLeavesOutTheReceivedAddress` (`40001`).
- `internal/pii/clientip_test.go`: `TestClientIPAttributeNeverCarriesTheFullAddress` (`40001`, `5061`).
- `internal/hss/keyring/keyring_test.go`: `TestKeyringNeverPrintsItsKeys` (`0707`, the hex of its key bytes). Added in the review round.
- `internal/msrp/limits_test.go`: the path test from #98 (`49152`, the client's port). Added in the review round.
- `internal/pii/pii_test.go`: `TestAttributesNeverCarryTheRawValueIntoALogLine`. Its secrets are 11 digits or more, longer than any digit run a timestamp holds, so it could not fail this way. It changed only so that all of these tests use the same logger.

**What stays the same:**
- Every secret is still checked; none was removed or loosened (see the diff: only the logger lines changed).
- Every one of these tests also fails if the line has a `"time"` key, so the fix cannot be undone by accident.
- Each package has its own small copy of the helper. `internal/pii` cannot import a shared test package that depends on `internal/runtime`, which imports `pii`.

**Other tests I checked** for the same pattern, a raw line searched for digit-only secrets:
- `tools/rcs-sim` already reads the decoded strings (`stringsIn`, #84/#93).
- msrp-relay's control tests search only the `error` field.
- Other secret lists use forms a timestamp cannot hold: 11 digits or more, hex of 16 bytes or more, or text. This covers `internal/sip/digest`, `internal/milenage`, `internal/diameter/cx`, ftserver's awsstore, rcs-as messaging, msrp's handler test, runtime and hss.

author: panghy
body:
## Why
On 2026-10-19 the v0.11.9 release PR (#2493) went through 13 CI runs over 4+ hours without being cut. Root cause: each release-plz refresh needs about 8 minutes (`release-plz release-pr`) plus 14 minutes of CI (all of it `check` at 11 min and `coverage-changed` at 13 min), while main merged roughly every 15 minutes. Every green head was already stale by the time it went green (for example f195da19b0 went green at 06:53, and main moved at 06:50).

The UNKNOWN-mergeability skips at 07:39 and 07:55 were symptoms, not the cause. CI on those heads was still running, and main had already moved past them.

## What
1. **CI fast path for release-metadata PRs** (`ci.yml`): when `release-fast-path` reports `fast_path=true`, the PR skips `check` and `coverage-changed`. CI Gate accepts that skip only when `release-fast-path` succeeded. Merge-queue and push requirements are unchanged. Release PR CI drops to about 2.5 minutes, so refresh plus CI takes about 11 minutes, under the 15-minute cadence.
   - A non-release PR that forges `fast_path` still meets both jobs in the merge queue. Auto-cut's direct `--admin` merge re-classifies the diff with its trusted script, which rejects any workflow or script change.
2. **Auto-cut transient states** (`auto-cut-alpha.yml`):
   - Every run, cron included, re-reads `mergeable=UNKNOWN` up to four times, 30 seconds apart.
   - A missing CI Gate beside queued or in-progress CI jobs counts as running CI and gets the full `AUTO_CUT_CI_WAIT_MINUTES` budget. CI Gate `needs:` every job, so it only appears once CI finishes. Before this change, every push run spent its whole wait in the 5-minute "never started" grace.

No other auto-cut guard changes: hold-release, draft, conflicts, failed gate, threads, freshness, `--match-head-commit` and the throttle all stay as they are.

3. **Hardening, from self-review:**
   - The classifier now requires `Cargo.lock` to carry every bumped workspace version, even when the lockfile is not in the diff. Before this, a stale lockfile would have been accepted, and the fast path no longer runs `check` to catch it.
   - `release-fast-path` runs only on `release-plz-*` branches, so ordinary PRs pay no extra latency before `check`. Its result is advisory: a failed classifier falls back to full CI.
   - The UNKNOWN grace is a 2-minute deadline per episode. A missing gate beside an already-failed CI job keeps the short grace.

Accepted residual risk: a test whose behaviour depends on the specific version number (not just `CARGO_PKG_VERSION` symbolically) would no longer fail on the release PR. It would surface in the next merge-queue run on main. A grep found no such test.

## Tests
- `scripts/test-ci-native-routing.py`: the job scheduler is now dependency-ordered. New coverage for the fast-path gate truth table (fast_path × classifier result × slow-job result), routing per event, and mutations that would widen the skip.
- `scripts/test-release-pr-fast-path.py`: a stale or missing lockfile bump is rejected. The real v0.11.9 head (91d935dadb) still classifies as `fast_path=true`.
- `scripts/test-auto-cut-alpha.py`: a fake `date` clock exercises the budgets. New cases: UNKNOWN re-read for each event; persistent UNKNOWN stops after four reads; the 07:39 shape (UNKNOWN after the push budget is spent); a missing gate with running CI waits past 5 minutes; a missing gate without CI keeps the short grace; and the running-CI wait is still bounded.
- All new tests fail against `origin/main`'s workflows and pass here. `actionlint` is clean.

Docs: monorepo `docs/RELEASING.md` § Guarded direct release merges (companion PR to follow). No assistant-app-guide impact, because this is CI-only and not user-facing.

author: lionsr
body:
Closes #9550. Stacked on #9732 (QICLean pin bump to `594b6e8d`). Held as a draft until #9732 merges in a coordinated window.

### Mathematics

The buffered discount on a chain needs the energy of the filtered vector to be at most `Δ/2`. QICLean now proves two bounds for it:
- `Entropy.two_mul_condEntropy_le` uses `∑_j 4 a_j² ∑_Y d_Y² J`. On the chain this is at most `16 N_R q^{2(R+1)} J / m`.
- `Entropy.two_mul_condEntropy_le_logarithmic` uses `∑_j 8 e a_j² ∑_Y log²(e d_Y) J`. This is the three-lines estimate of Remark 6.3 of the note (`rem:sharper`). On the chain it is at most `32 e N_R ℓ_R² J / m`, with `ℓ_R = log(e q^{R+1})`.

The shell count now uses the smaller of the two energy thresholds:
`m = ⌈max {4, E_R J/Δ, 128 √((1 + J/Δ) B_R)}⌉`, where `E_R = min {32 N_R q^{2(R+1)}, 64 e N_R ℓ_R²}`.
The proof splits on which entry is the minimum and applies the matching QICLean lemma. Since `E_R` is at most either entry, this `m` is never worse than the shell count from either estimate alone; in particular it satisfies the bound of Remark 6.3 (`rem:sharper`). For large `q^{R+1}` it removes the polynomial factor `q^{2(R+1)}`, so `m = O((1 + J/Δ) B_R)` and `C₀ = O(R log q (1 + J/Δ) B_R)`, as the issue asks. For small cases, such as `q = 2, R = 1`, the quadratic entry is smaller, so it is kept.

### Changes

- `Counting.lean`: the bound `log²(e d_X) ≤ log²(e q^{R+1})` becomes the lemma `log_sq_supportDim_le`. `cutLogBudget_interval_le` uses it.
- `BufferDiscount.lean`: new `chainQuadraticEnergyThreshold` and `chainLogEnergyThreshold`. `chainEnergyThreshold` is now their minimum. The discount proof proves both energy bounds and splits on the minimum. The local-fix marker is updated.
- `AreaLaw.lean`: `chainShellConst = 5 + E_R + 128 B_R`, and `chainShellCount_le` is adapted. The statements of `chainAreaLaw`, `regionEntropy_interval_le` and Theorem B are unchanged.
- Blueprint `ch35`, `docs/formalization/one-dimensional-chain.md` and the paper-gap note `docs/paper-gaps/tnlean_one_dimensional_discount_constants.tex` now state the new `m`, `C₁` and `C₀`.

### Overlap with open work

- #9687 (Codex, `codex/generic-prefix-truncation-20261018`, with #9700 stacked on it) also edits `Counting.lean`. It adds `chainBudgetConst_le_mul_log_sq` after `one_le_chainBudgetConst`. This PR adds `log_sq_supportDim_le` after `supportDim_le_real` and edits `cutLogBudget_interval_le`. The hunks are disjoint and `git merge-tree` merges `Counting.lean` cleanly; the conflicts it does report come from main, not from this PR.
- d9's #9599→#9612 stack edits ch35 and `docs/formalization/one-dimensional-chain.md` but none of the three Lean files here. `git merge-tree` against the head of #9612 is clean. This PR waits for that stack and merges main afterwards.

No `sorry` or `axiom`. Not built locally because of the disk hold; CI builds it.

author: e9uuleus
body:
修复 2026-10-19 Supply Chain 定时运行（[run 39208624081](https://github.com/E9uuleus/YumpooPlatform/actions/runs/39208624081)）中 OSV Scan 报出的 13 个包、54 个已知漏洞（3 Critical、27 High）。线上版本 `server-v2026.10.18.1` 与草稿 `server-v2026.10.19.1` 都受影响，本 PR 合入并晋升后才能消除。

## 改动

**后端**：Spring Boot 4.1.x 最新仍是 4.1.1，尚无带修复的补丁版本，因此在 `backend/pom.xml` 中用 Boot 的版本属性覆盖：

- `tomcat.version` 11.0.24 → 11.0.27：修复 GHSA-9xv2-5v5q-p794、GHSA-gcx9-497g-6cp6、GHSA-h3x4-894j-xpx5 三个 Critical；修复下限是 11.0.25，取补丁线中发布满 7 天的最新版；
- `jackson-bom.version` 3.1.5 → 3.1.7：`jackson-core` 与 `jackson-databind`；`jackson-annotations` 仍为 2.21。

**npm**：只涉及开发和打包工具链，以及 `exceljs` 的传递依赖。

- 在依赖范围内刷新锁文件：axios 1.20.0、brace-expansion 2.1.7 和 5.0.12、fast-uri 3.1.8、ip-address 10.7.4、postcss-selector-parser 7.1.6、undici 7.30.0；
- 在 `pnpm-workspace.yaml` 中按父包和大版本限定覆盖：`get-uri@8>basic-ftp ^6.2.3`、`exceljs@4>uuid ^11.1.1`、`minimatch@3>brace-expansion ^1.1.21`。后者在范围内，但 pnpm 11 定向刷新时不会重新解析它。

所有新解析的版本都已逐个核对 npm 发布时间，均满 7 天冷却期。覆盖理由与移除条件见 [依赖漏洞修复覆盖](https://github.com/E9uuleus/YumpooPlatform/blob/fix/dependency-security-2026-10-19/.agents/notes/implemented/process/2026-10-19-dependency-security-overrides.md)。

## 剩余项与风险

- **undici 7.30.1 暂缓引入**：它于 2026-10-15 发布，修复了当天公布的 8 个公告（含 4 个 High）。OSV 本次未收录这些公告，但收录后会再次报出 7.30.0。由于不满 7 天冷却期，本 PR 把锁文件固定在 7.30.0；7.30.1 在 2026-10-22 满 7 天，届时刷新锁文件即可。undici 7 只是 `@electron/get` 的可选依赖，只在下载 Electron 时使用，不随产品发布。
- **jackson 3.1.8**（2026-10-18 发布）不满冷却期，本次不引入；3.1.7 已覆盖 OSV 列出的全部 Jackson 漏洞。
- **uuid 覆盖不改变浏览器产物**：Vite 使用 `exceljs` 预打包的 `dist/exceljs.min.js`，其中内置 uuid 8 的代码。该公告只影响带输出缓冲区调用的 `v3/v5/v6`，而 `exceljs` 只调用 `v4()`，浏览器端不受影响。
- **basic-ftp 5 → 6 是大版本升级**：6.0.0 唯一的破坏性变更是默认禁止单独的传输主机，用于防范 FTP 反弹攻击；只有 OpenAPI 生成器的 PAC 文件地址使用 `ftp:` 时才会用到它。
- 本 PR 不改动部署引擎、数据库迁移、接口或事件契约。

## 验证

- 用 CI 同一镜像 `ghcr.io/google/osv-scanner-action:v2.6.0 --recursive ./` 在本地复现：修复前同样是 54 个漏洞，与 CI 一致；修复后结果为 `No issues found`。
- `mvn dependency:list` 确认 tomcat-embed-core、el、websocket 均为 11.0.27，jackson-core 和 jackson-databind 为 3.1.7。
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` 锁文件稳定，并通过 pnpm 供应链策略检查。
- `pnpm run ci:static` 全部通过，包括文档与 Agent Note、CI/发布策略、OpenAPI/事件/迁移兼容、lint、类型检查、构建、api-client/Web/桌面测试和资产校验。
- 后端 `mvnw clean verify` 通过：单元测试 604 项，其中 1 项既有跳过；集成测试 397 项全部通过；M014 有界堆验证通过。
  - `tools/ci/environment.mjs` 会过滤 `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS`，所以本机没有通过 `pnpm ci:backend` 运行，而是在 backend 目录直接运行 Maven，并设置 `-Djdk.net.unixdomain.tmpdir`。

供人工审查后以 squash 合入 `dev`。

author: michen00
body:
## Summary

Release Publish now attests each artifact's build provenance, so `gh attestation verify` can check a download against this repository, `release-publish.yml` and the tag it was built from. For that check to hold, the publish run has to start on the tag rather than on `main`, and this makes it do so.

## Changes

An attestation, like the Sigstore signatures #8 already makes, names the ref its run started on. Release Tag dispatched Release Publish with `--ref main`, so a check pinned with `--source-ref refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` would fail, and a check without it would accept another release's genuine artifact.

- `release-tag.yml` dispatches Release Publish on the tag.
- `release-publish.yml` refuses to run from any ref but the tag, then attests the wheel, sdist and checksum file with `actions/attest-build-provenance@v4`, holding `attestations: write`.
- `scripts/release/approve.sh` approves a publish run only when it started on the tag it names, by dispatch or by a push of the tag, and on the commit the tag points at. A run's ref name alone cannot tell a tag from a branch named like it, whose workflow file the branch would supply. A dispatch on `main` and a dispatch or push on such a branch are now refused, and new cases in its suite cover each.
- RELEASING.md, SECURITY.md and the CI notes describe the attestation, and RELEASING.md's verification commands pin the tag for both `gh attestation verify` and `cosign`.

## Testing

- [x] `make check` passes locally: every hook and 370 tests, with the approval suite at 38 cases.
- [x] shellcheck passes on every `run:` block of `release-tag.yml` and `release-publish.yml`.
- [ ] CI is green

## Review focus

None of this runs before the first release. The first real evidence is v0.1.0: its Release Publish run should start on `refs/tags/v0.1.0`, and the verification commands in RELEASING.md should pass against its assets.
