author: roed-math
body:
This PR equips pointed simplicial sets with tensors and cotensors by unpointed simplicial sets. It advances `GeneralizedCohomology/README.md`, milestone G2.1 **Pointed simplicial substrate**, specifically its target to construct the mapping simplicial set, tensors, and cotensors. Define `K ⊗ X = K₊ ∧ X` and `X^K = Map_*(K₊, X)`, and prove their characteristic hom-set equivalences with maps from `K` into the underlying pointed mapping simplicial set. This is the next effective critical-path step because the closed pointed smash product and suspension–loop adjunction are already merged, while the model-category layer needs this simplicial tensor–cotensor interface. After this PR, G2.1 still needs the full simplicial enrichment and colimit interfaces used downstream, the Kan–Quillen and pointed model structures, and the realization–Sing Quillen and monoidal comparisons.

Add `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialSet/Pointed/Tensor.lean` with the degreewise disjoint-basepoint functor and its forgetful adjunction, the tensor and cotensor bifunctors, both universal properties, and the fixed-parameter tensor–cotensor adjunction. Reuse Mathlib's `typeToPointed`, Tau Ceti's existing pointed smash and internal hom, the symmetric braiding, and the closed adjunction; no Mathlib infrastructure or external formalization is vendored. The module credits Hovey–Shipley–Smith, *Symmetric spectra*, Section 1.

Self-review against API design, reuse, and generality kept the surface to the constructions and characteristic formulas callers need, confirmed Mathlib still lists simplicial tensors as a TODO and contains no overlapping pointed API, and retained arbitrary universes without unused hypotheses. It also replaced a hand-written degreewise `Option` object with Mathlib's `typeToPointed` inside the explicit functor while preserving transparent computation for the simplex-level API.

Roadmap: GeneralizedCohomology

The Enterprise console needs an authenticated private origin, while OCE creates opaque per-agent hosts that Octelium's fixed Service FQDN cannot represent. This stages `console.oce.stinkyboi.com` through Octelium and limits the native wildcard route to exact `agent-<32 hex>.agents.oce.stinkyboi.com` hosts on the Tailscale-only Traefik listener. The existing `openclaw.stinkyboi.com` route stays on the suspended legacy backend until the final cutover.

The catalog adds an `oce` Namespace, authenticated console Service, and post-authentication legacy redirect. `scripts/openclaw-enterprise-access.py` applies only these three objects from a clean, exact-main checkout after OCE API readiness; it rechecks main before each scoped apply, requires convergence, and reads back the authorization and redirect contracts. DNS inventory, certificate SAN, static catalog checks, runtime route tests, and rollout instructions are updated together.

Validation: targeted Octelium catalog, private DNS, Traefik route, and 108 executable Traefik runtime checks pass. The post-wiki local full gate was stopped after ten silent minutes following Terragrunt generation; an earlier full gate passed and CI passed on this head. This PR is staged; merge does not activate OCE or switch the legacy URL. Final console and native-origin probes require the Enterprise API and network-policy prerequisites.

body:
사이트에 OS 별 터미널 비교 벤치마크를 싣기 위한 **측정 도구**예요. 처리량 · 키 → 화면 지연 · 메모리와 유휴 CPU · 시작 시간 네 지표를 Linux · macOS · Windows 에서 다른 터미널과 같은 잣대로 재요. 앱 코드 (`src/`) 는 바꾸지 않아요.

세 OS 의 결과는 [#756 종합 댓글](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6263077551) 에 있어요.

## 바뀐 것

- **공용 뼈대** — 대상 터미널을 띄우고 닫는 코드를 `tool/stress/terminals.sh` 한 벌로 뗐어요 (처리량에서 분리). 위생 절차 (`hygiene.sh`) 는 끝날 때 측정을 시킨 창을 다시 앞으로 올려요.
- **새 지표 셋** — `compare-latency.sh` · `compare-memory.sh` · `compare-startup.sh` 와 OS 별 측정기.

  | 지표 | Linux | macOS | Windows |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 키 → 화면 | `key-to-screen_linux.c` (portal ScreenCast · uinput) | `key-to-screen_macos.m` (ScreenCaptureKit) | `key-to-screen_windows.c` (DXGI Desktop Duplication · `SendInput`) |
  | 메모리 · 유휴 CPU | `proc-usage_linux.py` (PSS) | `proc-usage_macos.c` (`phys_footprint`) | `proc-usage_windows.c` (Private Working Set) |
  | 시작 시간 | `startup-to-screen_linux.c` (데스크톱 런처) | `startup-to-screen_macos.m` (`open`) | `startup-to-screen_windows.c` (`ShellExecuteEx`) |

- **Linux 대상** — Konsole · GNOME Terminal · COSMIC Terminal 을 더했어요. foot 의 scrollback 을 맞췄어요. 지연 · 시작 시간은 KDE Plasma · GNOME · COSMIC 에서 각각 돌아요 (GNOME · COSMIC 은 창 위치를 안 알려 줘서 마젠타 표식으로 창을 찾아요).
- **`TILDAZ_BIN`** 으로 잴 TildaZ 를 골라요 — 사이트에 실을 값은 릴리즈 판으로 재요.
- 문서 — `tool/stress/README.md` 의 "다른 터미널과 견주기" 절 (쓰는 법 · 밟은 함정), `tool/README.md` 색인, `AGENTS.md`.

## 검증

**Linux** — 미니PC Firebat ZY-A8 · CachyOS · 60 Hz · TildaZ 0.10.5 릴리즈
- KDE Plasma 6.8.0: 네 지표 기록 측정 (9 대상) — [#756 ⑦](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6261441904)
- COSMIC 1.9.0: 지연 · 시작 · 홈 DE 처리량 — [⑧](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6261961905). 이 회차에서 도구 결함 셋을 찾아 고쳤어요 (위생 점검이 늘 멈춤 · 시작 시간이 띄운 앱의 출력 통로 때문에 멈춤 · 지연 2 회차부터 `.go` 가 남아 표식을 놓침)
- GNOME Shell 51.1: 지연 · 시작 · 홈 DE 처리량 — [⑨](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6262848252)
- `sh -n` (스크립트 전부) · Linux 측정기 `cc -Wall` · Python 도구 `py_compile` 통과

**macOS** — MacBook Pro M5 Pro · macOS 27.0.1 · 120 Hz · TildaZ 0.10.5 릴리즈
- 네 지표 기록 측정 (7 대상) — [#756 ⑥](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6261377691). 첫 회차 (10 월 13 일, ①~④) 도 이 도구로 쟀어요

**Windows** — 데스크탑 Ryzen 7 5700G · Windows 11 26200 · 150 % · 60 Hz · TildaZ 0.10.5 릴리즈 zip
- 네 지표 기록 측정 (5 대상) — [#756 ⑩](https://github.com/ensky0/tildaz/issues/756#issuecomment-6262957271). 측정기 넷은 이 기기에서 만들었어요
- 미니PC 에서 `zig cc -target x86_64-windows-gnu` 로 측정기 넷을 다시 빌드해 확인했어요

이 브랜치는 `origin/main` (`2b25ae1`) 위에 있어요. `src/` · `build.zig` 를 건드리지 않아 앱 빌드 · 테스트에는 영향이 없어요.

## 남은 것 (새 이슈에서)

- 듀얼부트 노트북 (Ryzen AI 7 350 · 120 Hz) 에서 Linux · Windows 를 같은 하드웨어로 다시 재요 — #809
- 사이트에 실을 것을 고르고 새 페이지를 만들어요 — #810
- 측정에서 나온 단서 — macOS 지연 회귀 (+4.6 ms, #811) · Linux · Windows 의 CJK · 이모지 처리량 (#812).

Closes #756
Closes #761

author: assem2002
body:
Fixes #15313

## The issue

A WHERE assignment with an array constant as a vector subscript:

```fortran
integer :: arr(3), brr(3)
arr = [1, 2, 3]
brr = [1, 2, 3]
where (brr > 1) arr = brr([3, 2, 1]) + 3
```

GFortran prints `1 5 4`. LFortran stopped at run time:

```
Runtime error: Array 'brr' index out of bounds. Tried to access index 0 of dimension 1, but valid range is 1 to 3.
```

The same happened with `brr([k, 2, 1])`, with an implied-do like `brr([(i, i=n,1,-1)])`, and with an ELSEWHERE mask like `elsewhere (brr([3, 2, 1]) > 2)`.

## Why it happened

The `implied_do_loops` pass turns `[3, 2, 1]` into a temporary array `tmp` and fills it just before the statement that uses it, here inside the WHERE body. Later, `array_struct_temporary` puts every temporary of a WHERE construct before the whole construct. So the copy of `brr(tmp)` ran before `tmp` was filled, and used its old contents (0 here) as indices.

## The fix

In `src/libasr/pass/implied_do_loops.cpp`, `ArrayConstantVisitor` now puts the statements that fill an array constructor of a WHERE construct (in its body, its ELSEWHERE parts or their masks) before the outermost WHERE. That is where `array_struct_temporary` puts its temporaries, and where this pass already puts them for FORALL. The fill also runs once now, not once per element.

A constructor that can see what the construct assigns stays where it was, because before the construct it would read old values. That is a constructor that names a variable the construct assigns, reads a pointer, or calls a function:

```fortran
where (brr > 0)
    arr = 4 - brr
    crr = [arr(1), 2, 3] + brr   ! must use the new arr(1)
end where
```

Not covered: such a constructor still fails when its statement also gets a temporary before the construct, as in `crr = drr([arr(1), 2, 3]) + 1`. That is the same kind of problem as #14901.

## Tests

- `where_21`: an array constant subscript in a WHERE value and in an ELSEWHERE mask, and three constructors that must stay in place (a variable, a pointer, a function). It fails on `main` and passes here.
- Local LLVM 11 suites pass: unit 25/25, integration 5158/5158, reference.

## Other bugs found

- #15595: `where (m) arr = brr(idx)`, with the vector subscript as the whole value, crashes LLVM code generation.
- #15596: in a WHERE construct, the vector-subscript temporary of a later statement (`c = d(a) + 1`) is computed before the construct.
- #15597: the statements of a WHERE construct run as one element loop, so `c = a(3) + d` after `a = 4 - a` is wrong.

author: oscerd
body:
## What

Revisits the security model (`security-model.adoc`, its `security-model.yaml` index and the summary in `AGENTS.md`) in light of the 38 advisories published on 2026-10-15 ([camel-website #1818](https://github.com/apache/camel-website/pull/1818), fixed in 4.18.5, 4.22.1 and 4.23.0).

Some of their lessons were already in the model, but cited by Jira key (CAMEL-24411, CAMEL-24412, CAMEL-24413/24420, CAMEL-24419) or not cited at all, because the CVEs were not public yet. Others were not covered.

## Changes

**Citations.** The Jira keys are replaced by the published CVE IDs. The rules that were added without a citation (unmuted exceptions, CORS, shared state, the HTTP/2 header case, prefix matching, redirects) now name their advisories. All 38 CVEs are cited.

**Adversary model**
- Remote directory listings and HTTP redirects are listed as far-side output that the attacker influences (CVE-2026-79983..79986, CVE-2026-85251). The far side is also untrusted when the service is compromised or shared, or when the protocol leaves its responses unprotected in transit (plain FTP).
- Other local accounts on the host are named as a secondary adversary. They are in scope only for files Camel itself makes readable to them (CVE-2023-34442, CVE-2026-85300).
- A Camel endpoint that manages a component through messages, such as `dynamic-router-control:`, is not a management surface (CVE-2026-83531).
- A configuration that the project's own documentation shows counts as reasonably expected (CVE-2026-78164, CVE-2026-83531, CVE-2026-78163).

**In-scope classes**
- New class: integrity and signature verification that can be skipped (CVE-2026-85243, CVE-2026-85248).
- "SSRF triggered by parsing" becomes "request forgery and credentials sent where the route did not choose". It now covers a message body read as a locator, a destination supplied by the peer, and a redirect (CVE-2026-78163, CVE-2026-80344, CVE-2026-85251).
- Path traversal now covers the remote path that the remote-file consumers retrieve, delete and rename.
- The control-header definition now covers the saga an exchange joins (CVE-2026-85312).
- Mapping sites now include producers that parse a document (CVE-2026-85249).
- Auth: a check whose claim is absent fails closed (CVE-2026-85301), and authentication is never inherited from a pooled thread (CVE-2026-84181; the skip was reachable with `alwaysReauthenticate=false`).
- Expression injection: forwarding messages to an endpoint is not asking for their content to be evaluated (CVE-2026-83531).
- XXE: `FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING` alone depends on the implementation (CVE-2026-91858).
- Disclosure: payload content in the default logs (CVE-2026-85260) and secret files readable by other accounts (CVE-2026-85300).
- Insecure defaults: a library object that Camel builds to do its own work (a serializer, a filter, a parser factory) carries Camel's defaults (CVE-2026-78165, CVE-2026-85313, CVE-2026-91858). The connection, TLS and authentication defaults of a wrapped client stay inherited posture.

**Core invariants.** The dispatch invariant now covers the saga an exchange joins (CVE-2026-85312). The placeholder invariant gets its first concrete instance (CVE-2026-78164).

**Severity tiers.** The "indicative severity" column said its tiers reflect how the PMC has historically scored each class. Several rows read "Critical (9.0-9.8)", but no advisory for these artifacts has been rated Critical since 2014: the three Critical ratings are CVE-2013-4330, CVE-2014-0002 and CVE-2014-0003. The index also lists two Critical Camel K advisories (CVE-2026-80351, CVE-2026-80352); the note and the YAML say they are triaged against Camel K's own scope. The column now gives, for each class, the range published since 2015. The note under the table says Critical remains available for code execution or full compromise with no precondition.

**Triage aids**
- New false friend: a `Camel*` header name is not a trust marker (CVE-2026-78164).
- Two new "inverse error" entries under known non-findings: a message that reaches a control endpoint, and a finding that needs a third-party implementation on the class path.
- The incomplete-fix rule now cites CVE-2026-78162 and CVE-2026-85314.
- The per-option opt-in table adds the options introduced by the fixes.
- Deployment hardening adds egress restriction, the encrypted variant of a protocol where one exists, and the umask.
- Component-author guidance gets new questions on content sniffing, code taken from messages, placeholder resolution at runtime, signature verification, payload logging, secret files and third-party defaults.

Two points need PMC judgement:
1. The severity recalibration changes guidance that triage tooling reads.
2. The heritage-defaults known limitation now lists `signatureVerificationOption=optional` (`camel-crypto-pgp`). CVE-2026-85243 kept that default on purpose, and the change records that position.

Docs only. Rendered with Asciidoctor.js and gave no warnings (as `main`). `security-model.yaml` parses. No new `xref:` links.

author: ivythaophuong
body:
## What
Supabase Auth can require a CAPTCHA on sign-in, sign-up and password reset (Authentication > Bot and Abuse Protection). Once it is switched on, requests without a token fail. Email confirmation alone does not stop automated sign-ups (the 631 junk accounts used a public inbox, mailinator.com), so this adds the check on the page.

## Change
- sb.signUp, sb.signIn and sb.recover send the token in gotrue_meta_security.captcha_token, the field @supabase/auth-js sends (read in the official package source for all three calls). Without a token the requests are exactly as before.
- AuthModal shows the Turnstile widget on the sign-in, sign-up and forgot-password forms only (not the new-password or email-link steps), keeps the button off until it is solved, resets the widget after every attempt (a token is single-use, valid 300 s per Cloudflare), removes it when the form changes, and says so when the script cannot be loaded or the check fails.
- src/lib/captcha.js loads the script from Cloudflare's exact URL with explicit rendering. The public site key is committed (the Docker build does not read .env files). VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY overrides it when defined, even empty: the test setup sets it empty (vite.config.js); a local run on localhost can use Cloudflare's dummy key 1x00000000000000000000AA because the real key allows the production hostnames only.
- The secret key is NOT in the repository and must only be entered in the Supabase dashboard.
- nginx sends no Content-Security-Policy, so the widget is not blocked.

## Rollout order (important)
1. Merge and deploy this.
2. Check that sign-in shows the widget and works (Supabase does not ask for a token yet).
3. Only then enable CAPTCHA in Supabase (Turnstile, secret key). Enabling it before this is deployed locks everyone out of sign-in.
Rollback: switch CAPTCHA off in Supabase (takes effect at once); the widget on the page is harmless.

## Verification
- Tests written first: client tests for the three bodies (with and without a token), loader tests (exact URL, once, load failure, retry), and modal tests with a fake Turnstile (button off until solved, token sent, reset after use, expired and error callbacks, load failure, no widget on the reset and link forms, no widget and unchanged requests when no key).
- npm test: 189 files passed, 1 skipped; 2897 tests passed, 24 expected fail, 4 skipped, 17 todo. npm run build: succeeded; the site key is in the bundle, no secret-looking key is in the source.
- Not run: lint; not tried with the real widget or with CAPTCHA enabled in Supabase.

## Limits
- That Supabase accepts the token for the real project is not yet shown (needs the secret key in the dashboard).
- The real site key is only valid for the hostnames set in Cloudflare (careeraihub.com and www).

author: mshunshin
body:
These are three differential fuzz targets that compare decode paths with libjpeg that `djpeg`, `cjpeg` and `jpegtran` don't expose. They found P4-247 to P4-250 (filed in #685), and the YCbCr one checks the P4-244 fix (#684). I'm offering them in case you want them here. Tell me if you'd rather not take them, or want them in another shape.

## Caveat: the harness needs a C libjpeg-turbo build

The targets don't link C. Instead, each one runs a small C program from `examples/` as a subprocess and compares the output byte for byte. Building those programs needs a **libjpeg-turbo 3.x development install**: headers and the library, with the 12- and 16-bit API for the lossless oracle. The existing `*_diff_c` targets only need the command-line tools.

- `fuzz/build_c_oracles.sh <prefix>` builds the three programs into the git-ignored `fuzz/oracles/` and prints the environment variables the targets read.
- A target whose oracle isn't configured exits with an error instead of comparing nothing.
- **I have not added them to `fuzz-smoke.yml`.** That job would have to build the oracles against the official 3.1.4.1 `.deb` first, which ships the headers. I can add that here or as a follow-up if you want them in the weekly run.

## The targets

| Target | Rust side | libjpeg side (oracle) |
|---|---|---|
| `fuzz_ycbcr_diff_c` | `set_output_colorspace(YCbCr)`, every scale, box/fancy upsampling, crops | `JCS_YCbCr` output (`examples/ycbcr_decode_c_oracle.c`, already here from #684) |
| `fuzz_raw_diff_c` | `Decoder::decode_raw` planes | `jpeg_read_raw_data` (new `examples/raw_decode_c_oracle.c`; builds against the jpeg-6b API, JPEG_LIB_VERSION 62, too) |
| `fuzz_lossless_diff_c` | `precision::decompress_lossless_arbitrary`, precision 2–16 | the lossless decoder (new `examples/lossless_decode_c_oracle.c`) |

- **What counts as a mismatch.** Each target asserts only on inputs libjpeg decodes without a warning. It excuses a mismatch only when it matches a filed class: the scaled IDCT's documented saturation, P4-248, P4-249 or P4-250. P4-66 can't be told apart reliably, so it still fails.
- **Known divergences.** `LTRS_FUZZ_INCLUDE_KNOWN=1` turns the excuses off. `fuzz/known_divergences/<target>/` keeps one input per class, outside the corpora.
- **Lossless sampling factors.** The lossless target hands libjpeg a lone component's sampling factors as 1×1 when they are valid. T.81 A.2.2 makes them irrelevant for a non-interleaved scan, but libjpeg resets prediction at the iMCU row. So a 1×v component with restarts that aren't a multiple of v rows decodes wrong in libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0 and right here.
- **Seeds.** `fuzz/scripts/make_c_oracle_diff_seeds.py <cjpeg 3.x>` writes the seeds, with a small T.81 encoder for lossless layouts `cjpeg` can't write. Its lossless seeds also go into `fuzz_decompress_precision`'s corpus. That README row read 3 but the corpus already held 328 files, so it now gives the 353 tracked files.
- **History.** This is one commit; the work landed as five in our fork (mshunshin/libjpeg-turbo-rs). The library is untouched: the diff is only under `fuzz/` and `examples/`.

## Checked on this branch (main 614898f4, macOS aarch64, libjpeg-turbo 3.2.0)

- All three targets build with `cargo +nightly fuzz build`.
- Each corpus replays clean (`-runs=0`): 198, 36 and 25 seeds.
- Every known-divergence input still fails with `LTRS_FUZZ_INCLUDE_KNOWN=1`. All but the P4-66 one pass without it.
- A two-minute run of each target, from its seed corpus with `-dict=fuzz/jpeg.dict`. `fuzz_raw_diff_c` ran 124,324 inputs with no finding. The other two each stopped on a divergence. Both reproduce identically on an older base (25d6605c plus #684, #687 and #688), so neither comes from the recent merges:
  - **`fuzz_ycbcr_diff_c`**: a 61×45 baseline stream with 4×2 luma and 1×1 chroma, decoded at 3/8 with fancy upsampling and the crop (4, 2, 9, 5). Two Cb samples differ: Rust gives 120 and 40, libjpeg 184 and 231. The same decode without the crop matches. It is none of the filed classes, and I haven't triaged it further.
  - **`fuzz_lossless_diff_c`**: a 61×45 8-bit RGB lossless frame, 18 of 8,235 samples differ. That fits P4-66, which the target can't excuse; I haven't confirmed it.

author: vgabi94
body:
Grok Bot: Part of #38. This covers Core storage, the CLI and MCP. The Radio page's Recent stations section is left for Opus, as Gabriel asked.

## What
- **Core: `StationStore`**, in `stations.json` in the data folder.
  - Recent list: the last 6 started, newest first, no duplicates. The same filters in another order or case count as one station.
  - Saved stations by name, case-insensitive.
  - Stations are stored as filters, never paths, so the file is portable with `.usrdata`.
  - Each change is a read-modify-write under `stations.json.lock` and is published atomically (temp file plus rename), so the player recording a station and a CLI save at the same moment don't lose each other's change.
  - An unreadable file reads as empty with a warning and is moved to `stations.json.bad` on the next change. Damaged entries are dropped one by one.
- **Recording:** `QueuePlayer.RadioStarted` fires outside the queue lock when a station starts. `PlayerHost` adds it to the recent list, so stations started from the CLI, MCP or the app are all remembered. This is best effort: a write failure is logged and radio plays on. Restoring a saved queue doesn't count as a start.
- **CLI:** `radio list`, `radio --recent N`, `radio --station <name>`, `radio save <name> [--recent N] [--replace]` (saves the station on air, or a recent one), and `radio delete <name>`.
- **MCP:** `radio_stations` (read-only), `radio_save`, `radio_delete`, and `radio` with `recent` or `station`.
- **Docs:** cli-reference.md (Recent and saved stations), mcp.md, and getting-started.md (data folder).
- **Also:** the same LiteDB projection-mapper fix as #105 (identical lines, so they merge cleanly). It's included because the race also failed `RadioExcludeTests` locally on this branch.

## Tests
- StationStore: order, dedupe and the limit of 6; order- and case-insensitive identity; save, replace, get and delete; a copied data folder reads the same, and the file has no paths.
- Unhappy paths: bad, too long and taken names, unknown stations, recent numbers out of range, a corrupt file / wrong version / `null` (set aside), damaged entries, a data folder that is a file.
- The lock: a held lock is waited for through a gate hook (released on the 3rd retry, no sleeps). A lock that's never released fails with invalid_state on a fake clock. Two concurrent writers lose no saves.
- `RadioStarted` fires once per started station, and not for failures or restores.
- CLI and MCP end to end with the in-process player: recorded on start, save from on-air and from recent, restart by `--station` / `--recent`, list text and JSON, delete. Exit codes 12, 13, 8 and 2 for each misuse.

## Note
`radio end` (#104) also adds a `radio` subcommand. If #104 merges first, this branch gets a small conflict in RadioCommand.cs and McpCommand.cs, and I'll resolve it with a merge from main (no force-push).

## Left for Opus (UI)
The Radio page's Recent stations section (6 most recent, newest first, "On air" mark, one click to restart). The app can read `StationStore.Recent()` through its library service. The player already records stations the app starts.

author: mdopp
body:
## Symptom
A value that only a template's hook reads (auth's `SMTP_*`, `OPERATOR_EMAIL`, `BASE_DN`) changed no rendered file. `laib set` was therefore followed by an empty plan, and pre-start never ran again. Auth worked around it (#361) by naming the SMTP values in a comment line of `auth-authelia.container`.

## What changed
- **render:** each service also renders `quadlet/<svc>/values.laib`: its values, one per line, sorted, secrets as `!secret NAME` (never a value). Quadlet ignores the extension. A changed value changes that file, so the plan names the service. apply then re-runs its hooks (`hookTargets` follows `p.Services`) and restarts it, as for any other change of the service. No per-template tricks.
- **plan:** when the file first lands in an existing service's folder (a box from before this change), it is written but is no change of the service. So the upgrade does not restart every service and re-run every post-deploy once. A new service is unaffected, because its units are added anyway.
- **review:** the file is skipped as a "unit", since the values are already judged from the state diff above it.
- **templates/auth:** the workaround comment line is gone.
- The golden files of all three cases gain their `values.laib`.

Kernel lines: +23 for this change (render +18, plan +3, review +1).

## Proof
`TestAChangedValueIsAChangeOfItsService` (red without the fix):
- Every service has its values output.
- A box with everything applied except the new file: one change, no service.
- Then `SMTP_HOST` changes: plan names `auth` with exactly that one change.
go vet, go test ./..., gofmt, golden: green.
Not proven on a box: `laib set auth SMTP_HOST=…` then `laib apply auth` re-runs pre-start. That is the owner's check below.

## On the Kraftwerk (after the release)
- `laib apply`: writes the `values.laib` files and should restart nothing.
- Then, to see it, `laib plan auth` after any `laib set auth SMTP_FROM=<the same address>`. If nothing differs, the plan is empty; with a changed value it names auth.

Closes #364

author: shuiei
body:
## What and why

Checked the Workshop support check's "free" pieces (WearNTear `m_noSupportWear` off) against the game: that part already does what the game does. `WearNTear.UpdateWear` only calls `UpdateSupport` when `m_noSupportWear` is on, so the piece never breaks from lack of support. Its `m_support` is set to `GetMaxSupport()` in `Awake` and never changes after that, so `GetSupport()` gives the material's maximum to whatever rests on it. Pieces with `m_supports` off are still left out. Nothing changed there.

The check did turn up one real difference. In `UpdateSupport`, the game skips every collider whose `attachedRigidbody` is set, so nothing rests on such a collider. `SetupColliders` also leaves these colliders out of the piece's own support-search bounds. The editor counted them both ways. The pieces affected are those whose moving part has a Rigidbody: the leaves of doors, gates, drawbridges, iron grates and the window shutter, plus the hulls of `Trailership` and `VikingShip_Ashlands` (I checked against the game's bundles).

- The support scan marks each collider that sits on a Rigidbody or below one, as a 13th element of each box entry.
- `Stability` leaves those boxes out of both a piece's grown boxes and the colliders other pieces see. They still count for the stand-in shapes.
- `tests/fixtures/piece-support.json` remade with `--export-test-data`. Only the new flag changed.

## Where it shows

- [x] Editor (Core / Desktop)
- [ ] WorldEditorBridge plugin
- [ ] Docs only

Modes affected: Workshop (support check, Claude's `support_check`)

## How it was tested

New tests: the scan marks the colliders on a Rigidbody and below it but not the others, `AddBox` writes the flag, and a pole leaning on a door's frame holds while one leaning on its leaf falls. Existing expected JSON updated. I checked the door scenario by hand with a scratch program against the built Core: the pole on the leaf now has support 0 and falls, and before the fix it had 86. The test suite was left to CI.

- [ ] `dotnet test --project tests/Core.Tests` and `dotnet test --project tests/Desktop.Tests` pass

author: mostafabdeir0
body:
## Summary

Adds exam-level integrity checks prompted by the second automatic-generation evaluation (v2 scored 89/100). Its main defects were invisible to single-question checks: one question gave away another's answer, marks didn't match the work, and question text carried marks notes and internal ids. Everything reuses the existing validation, repair and quality-check mechanisms; no new services, dependencies or migrations.

## Changes

**Answer leakage** (`exam_store.answer_leaks`, `leak_messages`)
- Finds an MCQ whose correct answer appears in another question's student-facing text (prompt, choices, subpart prompts):
  - the same mathematics in any notation: LaTeX and plain forms are compared in one canonical form (`\frac{1}{1+e^{-z}}`, `\dfrac{1}{1+\exp(-z)}` and `1/(1 + e^(−z))` match);
  - a close paraphrase: a sentence covering most of the answer's words *and* the words only the correct answer has.
- Not leaks: shared formulas no question asks for, text matching a distractor as well, short answers ('0.5'), options that reuse the same words in another order.
- Used in four places: generation batches and Build with AI and revisions (sent back for repair), and the quality check (`answer_leakage`, run after the reviewer's safe fixes; the reviewer is told what the code found so a minimal rewording can remove it).
- Planner and writer rules: a formula, definition or fact another question asks students to recall is named, never stated.

**Marks and work**
- Planner, writer and reviewer rules: points follow the distinct, non-trivial steps a complete answer needs; degenerate inputs don't earn a whole question's marks; genuine edge cases stay and earn their reasoning's marks. The reviewer reports mismatches (`marks`, describe only; points unchanged).

**Hygiene**
- Rejected in AI-written questions: marks written into question text (`(2 marks)`, `[3 pts]`), and internal ids or sources in concepts / learning objectives.

**Difficulty calibration**
- Shared guidance for Remember at medium/hard and Understand at hard, and an informational quality-check note for those pairs. The professor's setting is never changed.

**Safe reviewer fixes** (second commit)
- A quality-check repair is applied only if the fixed question gains no new problem (garbled maths, internal ids, marks notes…) and no new answer leak involving it; later fixes in the same review see the question as already fixed. A fix still only ever changes its own question.

## Testing

- Backend: Ruff clean; pytest **331 passed**, 2 skipped (17 new in `tests/test_question_integrity.py`: maths in several notations, definitions in biology and history, legitimate exceptions, repair during generation, quality-check reporting and reviewer fix, a leak across generation batches caught by the final check, unsafe reviewer fixes rejected without any change, a safe fix changing only its own question, demanding-pair notes, marks notes, ids in concepts, prompt rules).
- Frontend: TypeScript and ESLint clean; Vitest 72 passed; `next build` succeeds.
- On the stored v2 exam (read-only, offline), the new checks flag exactly its real defects: the Q1→Q4 leak, marks notes in Q3–Q5, ids in Q1–Q2's concepts; nothing else.
- Secret scan of the added lines: no keys, tokens, credentials or private data.

author: nabilfatih
body:
## Summary

`e2e/settings/profile.browser.ts` › "a learner shuffles the animal in settings" failed in two unrelated learner runs (tables4, propsweb2). The triage workflow traced it in both traces, and a refuting agent confirmed it.

- Since #1144 an animal draws a cheek ellipse with an `opacity`.
- `Picture` renders an animal's shapes by position, with no keys, so React redraws a shuffled animal on the shapes of the one before.
- An attribute that a reused ellipse gains is written last. The same animal then lists its cheek's attributes as `cx cy fill rx ry opacity` in the tab that shuffled, but `cx cy fill opacity rx ry` in a fresh tab.
- The test compared raw `innerHTML`, so it timed out whenever the new animal landed on an old one's shapes. That depends on the random draw.

The product draws the right animal; only the comparison was wrong.

**Change:** `animalMarkup` in `e2e/support/avatar.ts` serializes the animal's shapes with each shape's attributes in name order. `drawnAnimal` and every markup comparison in the settings and profile tests use it. No product change: keying the picture would remount the drawing on every shuffle only to hide this.

author: periakteon
body:
## Description

The LibreKO client loads eighteen rank-symbol images from `res://assets/ui/rank_symbol/` (`Client/src/Domain/RankSymbol.cs`), but no pipeline step produced them, so a client built from source showed no national-rank symbol anywhere: not on name plates, not as the character-window medal, not in the ranking window and not in the chat log.

This adds a `rank-symbols` step to the `ui` stage, `bakers/bake_rank_symbols.py`, in the style of `bake_target_symbol`. The art is not in `UI\ui.hdr`. Retail keeps it as loose textures in `symbol_us\`, beside the clan symbols, under clan id 0, and each file's header still carries the artist's original path, which names the tier:

| Retail file | Size | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `s_0_20_0` .. `s_0_25_0` | 16x16, gold border | `knights_0..5.png` |
| `s_0_30_0` .. `s_0_35_0` | 16x16, black border | `personal_0..5.png` |
| `s_0_40_0` .. `s_0_45_0` | 64x64, bar in the top-left | `tier_0..5.png` |

Tier n matches `RankSymbol.TierOf`: 0 rank 1 (Gold Knight), 1 ranks 2-4 (Silver), 2 ranks 5-10 (Mirage), 3 ranks 11-40 (Shadow), 4 ranks 41-100 (Mist), 5 ranks 101-200 (Training).

- The textures are decoded with the existing `ko_texture.decode_ntf`.
- The ladder bars get shorter with the tier, centred on the widest one, so the six bars are cropped to one shared box and all come out 56x14: the chat log draws them at a fixed size, and per-image crops would stretch the shorter ones.
- Missing inputs are reported and skipped rather than failing the bake, as in `bake_target_symbol`: the bar textures are newer than the rest, and an older install may not have them.
- Left out on purpose: `s_0_50..55`, byte-identical to `30..35`, and `ani_0_40..42`, the animated top-three bars, since the client loads static PNGs only.

One mapping is inferred rather than read from the packed retail executable: gold border to `knights_*` and black border to `personal_*`. The permanent national-point symbols are described as the monthly ladder ones with a yellow border, and LibreKO ranks "knights" on all-time points and "personal" on monthly points. If that is backwards, swapping the 20 and 30 in `GROUPS` fixes it; the docstring says so.

The README's `ui` row now lists the rank symbols.

Closes #4

Related: ZeusAFK/LibreKO#191 makes the client draw the symbol on the player's own name plate too.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How it was tested

- `python bake.py --ko <English retail install> --out <LibreKO>/Client/assets --only rank-symbols`: 18/18 symbols, and the `imports` step after it wrote no new and rewrote no existing sidecars.
- `python bake.py --list` shows the step in the `ui` stage.
- Opened every output: the gold and black marks are 16x16, and the six bars are all 56x14.
- In game with LibreKO `a928fbd` on Windows 11 and Godot 4.7.2 .NET: the knights-rank symbol shows beside a ranked character's name and as the character-window medal.
- The repository has no test suite; not run on Linux.

## Screenshots

The eighteen outputs, enlarged five times: `knights_0..5`, `personal_0..5`, `tier_0..5`.

![The baked rank symbols](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/periakteon/LibreKO-Assets/pr-media/rank-symbols-sheet.png)

author: matt-edmondson
body:
Fixes ktsu-dev/Coder#271

## What changed

C#'s shift operators take an `int` count, and a `long` doesn't convert to `int` implicitly. So `x << n`, `x >> n`, `k <<= n` and `k >>= n` with a `long` `n` failed with CS0019.

- `CSharpGenerator` now writes the count of a `LeftShift`/`RightShift` binary expression as `(int)(n)`.
- An override of `GenerateAssignmentStatement` does the same for `<<=` and `>>=`.
- An `int` literal count is still written bare (`(x << 3)`).

The generator has no static-type scope, so every non-literal count is cast. No result changes: an `int` cast to `int` is itself, and C# masks a `long` count to its low six bits, which the cast keeps.

## Tests

- New test `CSharpGeneratedSourceCompilesTests.ShiftsByALongCount_Compile` builds `sh(long x, long n) => x << n`, a `<<=`/`>>=` on a `long` local, and `x << 3`, using `dotnet build`. With the generator change reverted, it fails with four CS0019 errors.
- `LanguageGeneratorBaseTests.CFamilyGenerators_SpellEveryBinaryOperator` now expects the cast on C# shifts. C++ is unchanged.
- The full suite passes: 1317/1317.

author: fridisbredis
body:
Three defects Frida found in the dev scheduling grid after #301 landed. All three are in the same view and surfaced in one sitting, hence one PR.

## 1. A round-the-clock work area was hatched as closed just before midnight

One cell — `23:15` — rendered as "outside operating window, disabled" on a stage where nothing was ever configured as closed.

`expandWindows` stores a recurring window as **one row per calendar day**, so a 24/7 area's windows meet exactly at midnight:

```
16 Oct 00:00 ──────────► 17 Oct 00:00 ──────────► 18 Oct 00:00
                    ▲
            slot 23:15–00:15 fits in neither
```

`isWithinWindow` asked whether any **single** window contained the slot. A slot straddling that seam is too late for the first window and too early for the second, so `.some()` returned false. The coverage was continuous; the check could not see across the join.

Now the windows are sorted and merged into runs before the containment test. **A real gap between two shifts still closes the slots that straddle it** — that is what this check exists for, and a test pins it.

### Same root assumption as #301

That a slot never crosses a day boundary. #301 removed it from slot *generation*; this removes it from the open/closed *check*. They are connected: the seam slot only renders at all once the grid is in phase across midnight, so the bug was almost certainly already there, invisible because the cell was missing entirely.

## 2. The vertical scrollbar clipped the last timeslot column

The final cell sat half under the scrollbar and could not be fully seen or clicked.

The table is `w-full` inside an `overflow-y-auto` box, so its 100% is measured against the box's **border-box** — which includes the scrollbar track. On a platform set to always show scrollbars the bar is painted over the table's right edge. With overlay scrollbars the bug is invisible, which is why it was never caught.

Adds a `scrollbar-gutter-stable` utility on both grids. `both-edges` rather than a bare `stable` so the grid stays optically centred instead of shifting sideways when the bar appears. Tailwind 3 has no built-in utility for this, so the class sits next to the existing `scrollbar-none`.

## 3. Changing day kept the previous day's horizontal scroll

Scroll to the end of Friday, switch to Saturday, and the grid opened parked past its morning on an apparently empty stretch.

Switching day or stage replaces every column, but React keeps the same scroll element, so the offset survives a change that invalidates it. `useHorizontalScrollShadow` already owns that ref, so the reset lives there: it takes a `resetKey`, and both grids pass the first slot's ISO string — identifying day and stage without threading a new prop through two components.

Three things the reset deliberately does **not** do:

- **Skips its first run**, so the browser's restored scroll position on back navigation survives. An existing test caught this — my first version reset on mount and broke the case the mount-time `sync()` exists to honour.
- **Leaves `scrollTop` alone.** The roster of people or work areas is the same list across days, so an admin working down it keeps their place.
- **Does not fire when the same day re-renders.** An autosave or a `router.refresh()` must not yank the view back mid-edit.

## Verification

Each fix was checked by breaking it deliberately and confirming a test noticed:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `isWithinWindow` back to the old `.some()` | 2 tests fail — the seam case and the ordering case |
| reset removed from the scroll hook | 1 test fails — the day-change case |

Unit **1315 passed** (102 files) · lint, format, `tsc`, `npm run build` all clean.

## For review

The merging logic in [`isWithinWindow`](src/lib/scheduling/grid-logic.ts) is the part worth reading closely. Worth confirming the intent: *touching or overlapping windows are one span; a genuine gap still closes the slots across it.*

Fixes 2 and 3 are visual and not covered by any automated visual check — they want a look in the running app.

author: lww0134-ctrl
body:
## Problem

`PUT /api/character` answers `{"ok": true}` even when the agent row was not written. The route calls `runtime.updateAgent(...)` and discards the returned `boolean`; `AgentRuntime.updateAgent` returns `false` when the adapter updated no row (a restored database without this agent, or a deleted row). The route then renames the live character, writes the new name into `eliza.json`, and replies `ok`. The caller cannot tell that storage refused the edit. The same repository already treats that exact result as a failure in `ElizaCharacterPersistenceService.persistCharacter` (`CHARACTER_AGENT_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED`).

Before this change, the new regression test produced:

```text
FAIL  test/character-persistence-receipt.test.ts > refuses a character PUT whose agent row update was not confirmed
AssertionError: expected 200 to be 500 // Object.is equality

- Expected
+ Received

- 500
+ 200
```

The `eliza.json` written by that request already contained the new name `Nova` while the agent row was never updated.

## Approved scope

This repairs the existing character-editor save path (`PUT /api/character`) in [`packages/agent`](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/tree/develop/packages/agent). It restores the persistence contract the repository already defines: `packages/agent/src/services/character-persistence.ts` throws `CHARACTER_AGENT_UPDATE_UNCONFIRMED` when `updateAgent` does not confirm, and `packages/agent/test/character-persistence-receipt.test.ts` is titled "Real config/database/history writes report partial completion honestly".

The repository does not contain a PRD or MVP plan file, as stated in `CONTRIBUTING.md`. This is a reproduced receipt defect in a shipped route. It does not add a feature, route, permission, setting, or UI change. There is no issue because repository rules require a human to write issues.

## Change

- `PUT /api/character` now keeps the `updateAgent` result and answers `500 Character storage update was not confirmed.` when it is `false`.
- The storage write now runs before the live character and the config are changed, so an unconfirmed write leaves the character name and `eliza.json` unchanged.
- `recordCharacterHistory` keeps its own guarded block; a history failure still reports the payload-budget error only for unbounded payloads.
- Test: deletes the agent row, calls the route, and asserts the 500 reply plus unchanged live character and config name.

## Why this implementation

The alternative was to keep the current order and only add the boolean check after `commitStagedCharacter`. That would answer 500 but still rename the live character and rewrite `eliza.json`, so the reply would contradict the state on disk. Persisting the staged character first, then committing it, makes the reply match storage and needs no new helper, error type, or config flag.

## Validation

Exact head: `ab26a25a6063a7d0a3eca154dcf1fb7c5fd2e8a5`

- Before: `bun --bun x vitest run test/character-persistence-receipt.test.ts` -> `Tests 1 failed | 1 passed (2)`, `expected 200 to be 500`.
- After: same command on both character files -> `Test Files 2 passed (2)`, `Tests 5 passed (5)`, 4.69s.
- Focused test file: `test/character-persistence-receipt.test.ts` 2 of 2 passed; neighbour `test/character-rename-config-persistence.test.ts` 3 of 3 passed.
- Package suite: NOT RUN - the focused files plus the rename/persistence neighbour cover the changed route; the full `packages/agent` suite needs more host memory than this 3.7 GB runner has.
- Typecheck: single-file `tsc --ignoreConfig --noEmit --skipLibCheck --moduleResolution bundler --allowImportingTsExtensions --types node src/api/character-routes.ts` -> exit 2, 6 errors, 0 in the changed file. All 6 are `TS7016` for unbuilt `@elizaos/plugin-assistant` dist types in three unchanged files (`config/config.ts`, `services/character-history.ts`, `services/character-persistence.ts`). The `--customConditions eliza-source` variant that pulls monorepo source did not finish in 500s on this host (exit 124, no output).
- `bun run --cwd packages/agent build`: NOT RUN - same host limit.
- `bun run --cwd packages/agent lint:check`: NOT RUN - the local `@biomejs/cli-linux-x64` install is broken.
- `bun run verify`: NOT RUN - the budget for a full repository verify was not available in this run.
- Changed-file Biome check (`biome check` on both files) and `git diff --check`: clean, exit 0.

## Change

A single playlist name or lyrics string could approach the full16MiB response limit and reach Compose; track metadata already had a per-record cap. Bound each playlist ID+name to16KiB UTF-8 before API/library publication, and lyrics to512KiB response bytes,64Ki UTF-16 units and2,048 lines. author: grapp-rapp
body:
Pause voluntary debt sweeps and retain scheduled loan payments so operating cash can fund equipment across the men's and women's gyms. The default combined equipment budget is ₪200,000, split ₪100,000 per gym initially, with editable allocation and an affordability gate. A separate ₪500,000 full-equipment alternative replaces that total; it is additional to the existing purchase and cosmetic budget.

The dashboard and Acquisition Plan compare purchase timing, bank cash, debt remaining and extra upfront funding for no-equipment / ₪200k / ₪500k alternatives. Growth, pricing, staffing, the existing loan, owner salaries and the ₪100k cash target remain unchanged across comparisons. No extra borrowing, sales uplift, rent or staff is invented. Equipment is paid once, including VAT, with eligible credits arriving later.

Existing acquisition browser and cloud models receive the requested policy once. A version marker preserves later edits and any decision to resume sweeps. Original rebuild models and actuals remain intact.

Validation: production build passed; 294 tests passed, one existing skip. Tests cover scheduled loan payoff in month 72, no extra sweeps, aggregate allocation, one-time capex, VAT timing, cash reconciliation, funding gaps and browser/cloud upgrade compatibility. Default equipment purchase is month 14 for ₪200k or month 27 for ₪500k; buying at takeover requires ₪195k or ₪495k extra cash respectively under the unchanged assumptions.

author: csr
body:
This PR fixes the `kibana-elasticsearch-snapshot-build` pipeline, which has failed on `main` and `8.19` on every daily build since Oct 17 because the ES cloud-ess Docker image is no longer found under the name `build.sh` looks up.

- elastic/elasticsearch#161755 fixed a latent `base == base == DockerBase.CLOUD_ESS` typo in `distribution/docker/build.gradle`, so the cloud-ess image is now tagged `docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch-ci/elasticsearch-cloud-ess:<version>` instead of `docker.elastic.co/elasticsearch/elasticsearch-cloud-ess:<version>`. `build.sh` still queried the old name, so `ES_CLOUD_ID` came back empty and `docker tag ""` failed with `invalid reference format` right after a successful Gradle build (e.g. [main build 8895](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-elasticsearch-snapshot-build/builds/8895#01a151e3-b0d1-4148-96fe-6d86d1f0d272), [8.19 build 8893](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-elasticsearch-snapshot-build/builds/8893)).
- There is deliberately no fallback to the old name. The ES change is merged on ES `main` and `8.19` (elastic/elasticsearch#162311), but the ES backports to 9.5 (elastic/elasticsearch#162306) and 9.4 (elastic/elasticsearch#162308) are still open, so this PR is labelled `backport:skip` and backports will be opened manually per branch: 8.19 right away, 9.5 and 9.4 only after their ES backports have merged.
- Only the ES-side lookup changes. The image is still re-tagged and pushed as `docker.elastic.co/kibana-ci/elasticsearch-cloud-ess:<version>-<sha>`, which is what `create_manifest.ts` and `cloud/deploy.sh` consume, so the manifest and the downstream verify/promote steps are unaffected.

author: officeappout
body:
**Stacked on #480** (`feat/route-quality-phase01` — uses `src/lib/route-quality` and `/admin/routes/quality`). When #480 merges, GitHub retargets this PR to `main`.

## What
Route generation on a **self-hosted GraphHopper 11.1** (Cloud Run, `me-west1`, project `appout-1`), behind the new panel flag **`enable_graphhopper_routes` (default OFF)**. Nothing is deployed by this PR — `infra/graphhopper/README.md` has the owner commands.

Loop recipe = the experiment winner **"mix best-of-6 + trimSpurs"**: 3 GraphHopper round trips (calibrated, headings 120° apart) + 3 OUT 3-waypoint loops routed as GH legs, spur-trimmed, scored with `src/lib/route-quality`, top 3 returned. Experiment (6 starts × 3/5 km × 6 runs): **77.8% pass v1 bars vs 58.3% Mapbox v1**, p95 134 ms/generation locally.

### 1. `infra/graphhopper/`
- `Dockerfile`: temurin 21 JRE, jar pinned by **sha256** (Maven Central), Geofabrik `israel-and-palestine` **md5-checked**, SRTM fetched during the **build-time import**, graph baked into the image; non-root runtime.
- `config.yml` + `models/` (foot / out_run / bike / out_bike / mtb), flexible mode, SRTM smoothing; `RouteResource` logging silenced (it logged the whole custom model + caller IP per request), no request log.
- `healthcheck.sh`, `cloudbuild.yaml` (E2_HIGHCPU_8, build → push → optional deploy), `service.yaml` (2 vCPU/4 GiB, min 1/max 3, startup+liveness probes, **ingress all + IAM only, no allUsers**).
- `scripts/`: `setup.sh`, `build.sh`, `deploy.sh`, `smoke.sh`, `weekly.sh` (Cloud Build manual trigger + Cloud Scheduler, Sun 03:00 IL).
- **Auth from Vercel:** the existing `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` SA mints a Google ID token (google-auth-library, dynamic import, cached) and gets `roles/run.invoker` on this one service. No new key. Optional dedicated `GRAPHHOPPER_INVOKER_SA_KEY`.

### 2. `src/lib/routing/graphhopper/` (server)
`types` · `custom-model` (tags → model: quiet streets, avoid unmarked crossings, parks areas; lit = later) · `request-builder` (round_trip / via legs / A→B) · `client` (timeout, 1 retry on 5xx/network, 400 → null, no retry on 401/403) · `id-token` · `config` · `map-response` (path, elevation, max grade, road_class shares, crossing counts).

### 3. `src/lib/routing/loop-service.ts` (+ `loops/`) and `friendly-route.ts`
Parallel 6 candidates, deadline with abort (keeps already-found loops), reseed on "Could not find a valid point". Without the OSM layer the major-road share comes from GH `road_class`; crossing bars need the OSM layer (fetched from our CDN-cached `/api/route-quality/osm-layer`, 500 ms budget).

### 4. `POST /api/routes/generate`
Firebase ID token Bearer auth, per-uid rate limit (`RL_ROUTES_GENERATE_UID_*`, default 40/10 min), `mode: 'loop'` → top-3 loops, `mode: 'ab'` → friendly A→B. 503 when not configured, 502 when GH fails. `/admin/routes/quality` gets a **GH** variant and a **v1↔GH** mode (calls the API directly, no Mapbox fallback, so failures are visible).

### 5. App integration
`generateDynamicRoutes`: a 4-line hook — when the flag is on **and** the request is a plain loop (no commute/corridor/chain/flow/short-route/deviation/fitness stop), call the API; **any error, >2 s, or empty → the existing Mapbox pipeline**. Flag off → the block is skipped entirely (no await, no fetch). `route-generator.service.ts` otherwise untouched.

## Tests
- `src/lib/routing/__tests__`: request builder, response mapping, loop selection (recorded GH geometries from the experiment), calibration/reseed/deadline/down, client auth/timeout/retry, ID-token parsing + caching, API body validation.
- `src/app/api/routes/generate/__tests__/route.test.ts`: 401/400/503/429/200/502/A→B.
- `graphhopper-loops` adapter: eligibility, DTO → Route, fallback (503/429/network/empty/malformed/timeout/not signed in).
- `route-generator.graphhopper.test.ts`: flag off → endpoint never called, Mapbox path; flag on → GH routes, no Mapbox; flag on + 502 → Mapbox fallback.
- `npx vitest run src/lib/routing src/app/api/routes src/features/parks/core/services/graphhopper-loops src/features/parks/core/services/__tests__/route-generator.graphhopper.test.ts` → 8 files, 67 tests pass. Wider `src/features/parks src/lib src/hooks src/app/api src/features/admin`: 2199 pass; the only failures are the emulator suites (no emulator running).
- `bash scripts/ci/tsc-baseline.sh check`: no new errors from this PR (the 9 reported are missing `@sentry/nextjs` / `@capacitor-community/media` packages in the local node_modules, files untouched here).
- `bash scripts/safety-check.sh`: pass.
- **Not verified here:** the Docker build itself (no Docker on this machine) — the config mirrors the experiment's working GH 11.1 config, plus the new `out_bike` profile and the logging block.

## Owner steps (after merge)
`setup.sh` → `build.sh` → `INVOKER_SA=… deploy.sh` → `smoke.sh` → set `GRAPHHOPPER_URL` in Vercel → compare on /admin/routes/quality → flip `enable_graphhopper_routes` → `weekly.sh`. Cost ≈ $50–70/month (1 always-warm instance, request-based billing).

author: javierarrieta
body:
## Symptom

In a Coder workspace, `hm-pull` fails with `cd: The directory ... does not exist` and `hm-update` fails on the same missing path.

```
$ echo $CODE_DIR
/home/coder/code          # set by modules/home-manager/shell.nix
ls /home/coder/code       # does not exist — the repo is at /home/coder/nixos-configurations
```

## Cause

`CODE_DIR` was hardcoded to `${userHome}/code` for every host, and `hm-pull` / `hm-update` use `$CODE_DIR/nixos-configurations` to find this repo's checkout. A Coder workspace has no `~/code`: both templates set the agent `dir` to `/home/coder` (`coder-templates` `templates/podman-template/main.tf`, `k8s-titan` `coder/templates/dev/main.tf`), so a clone from the landing directory lands straight in `$HOME`.

`hm-apply` and `hm-gc` were never affected — `hm-apply` deliberately applies from `github:javierarrieta/nixos-configurations` rather than a local checkout.

## Change

- `modules/home-manager/shell.nix`: `CODE_DIR` comes from a per-host `codeDir` userOption, defaulting to the previous `${userHome}/code`. The aliases themselves are untouched — they resolve `$CODE_DIR` at runtime.
- `home/hosts/coder-workspace/userOptions.nix`: `codeDir = "/home/coder"`, plus the same path correction to `homeManagerConfigDir`. `coder-workspace-titan` imports this file as its base, so it inherits the value.

`homeManagerConfigDir` is read by nothing (no consumer outside the `userOptions.nix` files), so that part is consistency, not behaviour.

## Verification — `nix eval` on the rendered session variable, no switch

| attribute | `CODE_DIR` |
|---|---|
| `homeConfigurations.coder-workspace` | `/home/coder` (was `/home/coder/code`) |
| `homeConfigurations.coder-workspace-titan` | `/home/coder` (was `/home/coder/code`) |
| `homeConfigurations.vps` | `/home/javier/code` — unchanged |
| `homeConfigurations.macbookpro` | `/Users/javier/code` — unchanged |
| `nixosConfigurations.llm01 … home-manager.users.javier` | `/home/javier/code` — unchanged |

`homeConfigurations.llm01.config.home.sessionVariables` does not resolve at all (that standalone attr doesn't import `shell.nix`) and fails identically on pristine `main` — pre-existing, unrelated.

## Notes for the reviewer

- The fix only reaches a workspace once it is on `main` **and** `hm-apply` has been run there, because `hm-apply` builds the pushed commit, not the local checkout. Workaround until then: `cd ~/nixos-configurations; and git pull --ff-only origin`.
- The titan pod layout was measured in a live `dev` workspace; the llm01 podman one is inferred from its template's `dir = "/home/coder"`. If a casa workspace does keep repos under `~/code`, that host needs its own `codeDir` instead of inheriting this one.

author: mmsge
body:
## Summary

The first live StoryGraph import (#134) matched only 170 of 416 books and filled **0** starts. *Ducks*, *Slags* and *Om udregning af rumfang II* came back unmatched, although all three are on BookWyrm with title, author and ISBN cached. The cause is an older bug in `collapseReadingEvents`, which this fixes. The fix also corrects start dates in every reading tool, with no import involved.

## Changes

- **`collapseReadingEvents` keys a book on the union of every title and URL its statuses use.**
  - A generatednote ("started reading *Hysj*") carries title and Edition URL. The "read" comment often carries only the URL (`inReplyToBook`).
  - Keyed separately, one book became a title-keyed half holding the start and a URL-keyed half holding the finish. Live data showed *Hysj*, *Dungeon Crawler Carl* and others as finished with no start.
  - For the import, that meant two candidates per title, which ADR 0063 rightly refuses as ambiguous. Where a book did match, it often landed on the half without the finish.
  - The key is still `normalizeTitle(title) || url` on the collapsed row, so `collapseKey` and every lookup are unchanged. Two editions sharing a title still merge.
- A conflict row names the book by StoryGraph's title when BookWyrm never gave one, instead of "—".
- ADR 0064, an AGENTS.md rule line, version **1.3.1**.

## Deploy impact

- [x] Needs a redeploy: `cd /srv/bot && make deploy`. No migration.
- Then **re-upload the StoryGraph export once**. Matches from the first upload point at the split keys, and the idempotent import rewrites them in place.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (2,092 passing) and `npm run format:check` are clean.
- New tests reproduce *Hysj*'s live shape: a titled generatednote plus a URL-only "read" comment now give one book, started and finished, in either arrival order.
- Ran end to end on Postgres 16, seeded the way BookWyrm actually federates (finishes on URL-only comments):
  - *Ducks* and *Slags* both match.
  - Two starts are filled.
  - *Ducks* returns 2024-09-29 (storygraph) → 2024-10-02 and 2026-05-28 → 2026-05-29.
- The branch carries a no-op merge of the old #134 tip (its content equals `hovud`), because a force push was not available. Squash merging leaves only the fix.

## Decision record (ADR)

- [x] ADR added: `docs/decision-records/0064-a-book-is-one-book-across-its-statuses.md` (README index updated)

## Attribution

- Both: Markus (ran the live import and reported the result) + agent (diagnosed from live MCP data and implemented)

body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"deadjoe"} -->
_Requested by **Joe**_

Before: in Advanced mode the Lyrics card had only section buttons and the Styles card had suggestion chips with a refresh button. There was no undo beyond the text field's own, no way to keep lyrics or styles for later, and no roomier place to write.

After: the Lyrics card has Undo, Redo, New draft, Saved lyrics and a full-screen editor (Saved lyrics, New draft, Undo, Redo, Done). The Styles card has Saved styles, Undo changes, Save styles and Clear styles; the suggestion chips and refresh are gone. Section buttons moved under the lyrics. Nothing here uses AI.

**How**

- `drafts.rs`: saved lyrics and styles in `<app-data>/saved.json`, written atomically, newest first, 200 each; the same words move up instead of repeating. Creating a song saves its lyrics and style under its title.
- `useUndo`: per-field history; typing within 0.8 s is one step; loads, clears and added sections are separate steps; ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y use it.
- `SavedPopover`: searchable list with previews and times; deleting asks first. `LyricsTools`: toolbar and full-screen editor (Escape or Done returns).

**Validation**

- `npm run check` (65 tests), `cargo test` (73), clippy, Prettier.
- Reviewed in a browser preview.

author: tarasgez
body:
## Observed failure (2026-10-19 08:26 UTC)
Real QA1/QA2 Zitadel sign-in PASS, previous-run cleanup PASS (0 found), and E2E ran, but `page.waitForEvent('dialog')` timed out after 12 seconds at the first UI Delete action. The actual UI `UserNotesCard` checks client `useAuth().session.user` before invoking `window.confirm`. The E2E test navigates with `waitUntil: 'domcontentloaded'` then clicks immediately; SSR can render a button before React hydrates its `onClick`, making the click inert. This is a probable hydration race, not yet independently proven as the sole cause.

## Change
- Require the real React 19 `onClick` handler on the selected delete button to have hydrated before clicking. Fail explicitly `REACT_DELETE_BUTTON_NOT_HYDRATED` if it hasn't; no sleeps, production code changes, or mocking confirmation.
- Await native `dialog` handling and `button.click` together to expose click errors rather than masking them with a dialog-only timeout.
- Output `DZVIN_RUN_SCOPED_DIARY_FIXTURE_TEARDOWN=PASS` only when exact-ID cleanup and post-test absence assertions pass.

Existing QA-only protection, pinned users, no new infrastructure. Full real integrated E2E needs another run against the pinned suite SHA.

body:
## Correctif : la section devis ne s'exécutait pas (CSP)

La CSP nginx de `visibleartisan.fr` impose **`script-src 'self'`** (pas de `unsafe-inline`). Le `<script>` **inline** de la section devis était donc **bloqué** → Options, paliers d'abonnement et estimation restaient vides (le CSS inline, lui, passe car `style-src 'unsafe-inline'`).

**Fix :** le JS est sorti dans **`static/demo-assets/devis.js`** (servi depuis `/demo-assets/`, autorisé par `script-src 'self'`). Le slug est lu depuis `document.body.dataset.planSlug`. `connect-src 'self'` autorise déjà le `fetch` vers `/api/quote`.

## Déploiement (après merge)
```bash
cd /opt/waas-factory
sudo git checkout main && sudo git pull origin main

# déployer devis.js au même endroit que demo.css :
ls -la /var/www/sites/demo-assets/        # si c'est un symlink vers le repo -> rien à faire
# sinon :
sudo cp /opt/waas-factory/static/demo-assets/devis.js /var/www/sites/demo-assets/

sudo systemctl restart waas-webhook.service
```
Puis **régénérer une démo** (les anciennes ont encore le script inline bloqué) → la section devient fonctionnelle.

## Summary
Adds a third sequential gate to `examples/marketing/research_publish_agent.py`, and fixes the offline demo the new gate had broken.

## 1. The brand-safety gate (commit 5daf047, written 29 Sep, not previously pushed here)
- `article-brand-safety`: a PreNode between the fact-check Invariant and the compliance PreNode. It's a separate editorial signal, because a draft can be policy-compliant and still be unsafe for the brand (for example, next to a sensitive current event).
- Same `gated_node` / `route_on_denial` chaining as the other two gates, with its own `blocked_unsafe` branch.

## 2. Fix for the offline demo (commit 2dbfd55)
The brand-safety gate uses the same Claude model as the compliance gate, and the offline stand-in answered every call to that model with the scenario's compliance score. So in the **noncompliant** scenario:
- brand-safety blocked first, and
- `_print_result` didn't know about `brand_safety_denial`, so it printed `published=None` as if nothing had been blocked.

Before the brand-safety commit, that scenario was correctly blocked by compliance.

Fix:
- `marketing_fake_providers.py`: each scenario has its own `brand_safety` verdict, told apart by the reviewer's system prompt; a new **unsafe** scenario exercises the brand-safety block.
- `research_publish_agent.py`: reports brand-safety denials, runs four scenarios, and the docstrings and task table include the new review.

| Scenario | Outcome |
|---|---|
| approved | published |
| unverified | blocked by fact-check Invariant |
| unsafe | blocked by brand-safety PreNode |
| noncompliant | blocked by compliance PreNode |

author: marcusds
body:
# What does this implement/fix?

`music/item_by_name` (used for play-by-name, e.g. from voice assistants) only matched names exactly in the library and otherwise returned the first global search result. A typo or a natural language request ("something by the beatls from abbey road") found nothing or an unrelated item. The code carried a todo for exactly this.

This adds an AI fallback to that lookup:

- The plain lookup runs first, unchanged. It now also reports whether its result is a close match: an exact library match, or a first search result whose name (and artist, when given) passes `compare_strings(..., strict=False)`.
- With no close match, and when an AI engine is available, the engine is asked (8 s cap) to correct and structure the request into JSON `{media_type, name, artist, album}`. The same lookup then runs once more with those terms. The AI result is used when it is a close match, or when the plain lookup found nothing. Otherwise the plain result is kept.
- Only the request text (name/artist/album, capped at 500 chars) and the allowed media types are sent. No library metadata is sent. The request is embedded as a JSON value and marked as data in the prompt. The reply is parsed as untrusted JSON: it must be an object, terms are whitespace-normalized and capped at 200 chars, and a `media_type` outside the allowed set is dropped. The reply only feeds the existing search.
- Gating mirrors smart playlists: a new core music option `ai_item_lookup` (bool, default on) and an engine picker `ai_item_lookup_engine` that depends on it. Selection works like the announcement TTS engine: a new `select_core_ai_engine` helper adopts the first engine when none is stored.
- With no engine, the option off, or any engine error, timeout or unusable reply, the behavior is the same as before.

The new logic lives in `controllers/music/ai_lookup.py`. In `controller.py`, the existing body moved into `_lookup_item_by_name`. The media type list is now a module constant.

Config/data: there are two new optional core config entries with safe defaults, and no existing keys are renamed or moved. I don't think a migration is needed. `translations/en.json` was regenerated with `scripts.build_translations`.

## Types of changes

- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) — `bugfix`
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) — `new-feature`
- [x] Enhancement to an existing feature — `enhancement`
- [ ] New music/player/metadata/plugin provider — `new-provider`
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected) — `breaking-change`
- [ ] Refactor (no behaviour change) — `refactor`
- [ ] Documentation only — `documentation`
- [ ] Maintenance / chore — `maintenance`
- [ ] CI / workflow change — `ci`
- [ ] Dependencies bump — `dependencies`

## Checklist

- [ ] The code change is tested and works locally. (Unit tests only. Not tried against a real AI engine or a running server.)
- [x] `pre-commit` passes on the changed files. It was run with a shared venv, because the PyTorch index could not be reached in this environment.
- [x] Tests added in `tests/controllers/music/test_item_by_name_ai.py`, with a fake AI plugin: a typo resolves; a close match and an exact library match skip the engine; an engine exception, a non-JSON or invalid reply, or a timeout falls back; no engine and the option off leave the behavior unchanged; a requested media type restricts the prompt and the search; parser and prompt bounds. 15 passed. `tests/controllers/music`, `tests/helpers/test_plugin_engines.py`, `tests/controllers/config` and `tests/controllers/translations` pass. For the full-suite status, see the session report.
- [ ] For changes to shared models, the companion PR in `music-assistant/models` is linked. (n/a)
- [ ] For changes affecting the UI, the companion PR in `music-assistant/frontend` is linked. (n/a: generic config entries)
- [x] I have read and complied with the project's AI Policy for any AI-assisted contributions.

author: arianvp
body:
A port of hermeticbuild/hermetic-llvm's bootstrap to buck2, for aarch64-linux-musl. The compiler is hermetic-llvm's prebuilt, statically linked LLVM 23.1.2; musl 1.2.6 (libc.a and start files) and compiler-rt's builtins, outline atomics and crtbegin/crtend are built from source with it. Archives are unpacked with a pinned static bsdtar, and musl's generated headers and per-architecture source selection are done in Starlark through dynamic actions, so no action needs a host tool or a shell. toolchains//:cxx selects the toolchain when the target configuration has //toolchains/llvm:musl, which //toolchains/llvm/tests gets as a PACKAGE modifier; it builds a C program there and runs it as an action.

x//platforms:actiond runs actions on actiond, hermeticbuild's local Remote Execution API worker, which runs every action in an empty chroot inside a small Linux VM. It is opted into per checkout from .buckconfig.local, together with the RE client settings, as described in platforms/README.md. Everything the toolchain does runs there, including running the test program.

Archives are unpacked where actions run: the compressed archive is uploaded once, and the extracted files, the 146 MB llvm binary among them, are created in the remote CAS. Unpacking locally made every remote action upload them first. Downloads carry their size, so buck2 needs no HEAD request to defer them.

author: develop-zaone
body:
## 변경 요약

CONTACT 페이지 "공지사항"에서 열리는 사업소식·사업보고 상세 페이지를 만들고, Sanity에 첨부파일 칸을 더했습니다. 본문 사진은 자르지 않고 원래 비율로 보이게 바꿨습니다. 목록은 이메일 폼과 함께 다른 브랜치에서 만듭니다.

- **Studio**
  - 사업소식·사업보고에 첨부파일(Sanity `file` 배열)과 포스터이미지 칸을 더했습니다. 첨부파일은 표시 이름을 선택으로 쓸 수 있고, 비우면 올린 파일 이름이 보입니다.
  - 첨부파일이 있으면 본문을 비운 채 게시할 수 있습니다(예전 사업보고처럼 파일만 올리는 글).
- **상세 페이지**: `/news/[slug]`(사업소식), `/reports/[slug]`(사업보고). 같은 화면을 쓰고 칩 글자만 다릅니다.
  - 구성: 칩 → 제목 → 게시일 → 첨부파일 → 본문 → 포스터 → 다른 소식 살펴보기(같은 종류의 이전·다음 글) → 공지사항 목록 보기 버튼
- **본문 사진**: 16:10으로 자르던 것을 원래 비율 그대로 보입니다. 폭은 그대로이고, 작은 사진은 늘리지 않고 원래 폭으로 가운데 둡니다. 인사이트 본문도 같이 바뀝니다.
- **정리**: 인사이트 상세와 겹치던 포스터·설명 글·주소 풀기 코드를 `PostPoster`·`describePostBody`·`decodeSlugParam`으로 옮겨 같이 씁니다.

## 배경

- 시안: Figma "[1017] CONTACT 작업중" `1555:5653`(1024만 있음). 디자이너 메모상 칩·제목·업로드 날짜는 필수이고, 첨부파일·사진은 있을 때만 보입니다.
- 첨부파일 내려받기: Sanity가 안내하는 `?dl=이름` 방식은 CDN이 이름을 퍼센트 인코딩해서, Safari가 `2025%EB%85%84…`처럼 깨진 이름으로 저장합니다. 그래서 CDN 주소 끝에 원래 파일 이름을 붙이고 `?dl`을 다는 방식으로 바꿨습니다. Chrome·Firefox·Safari(WebKit) 모두 한글 이름으로 저장되는 것을 확인했습니다.
- 예전 사이트(zaone.org/contact)의 공지 18개(사업소식 14, 사업보고 4)는 이미 Sanity production에 옮겨 게시했습니다. 그중 세로 포스터·긴 인포그래픽·가로 표 이미지가 16:10 틀에 크게 잘려서 본문 사진 비율을 바꿨습니다.

## 확인 방법

- `/reports/2022-공익법인-결산서류-등의-공시-연간기부금-모금액-및-활용실적`
  - 첨부파일 2개(PDF·XLS)가 보이고, 누르면 한글 이름 그대로 내려받아지는지
  - 이전 글·다음 글이 2024·2025 공시로 나오는지
- `/news/언론보도-한-자리-모인-비영리스타트업-뉴-필란트로피-변화의-지렛대`: 사진과 캡션이 보이는지
- `/news/모집공고-어린이를-위한-창의적-놀이환경이-필요한-기관을-찾습니다`, `/news/언론보도-비영리-조직을-스타트업처럼-키운다`: 세로 포스터·인포그래픽이 잘리지 않는지
- `/admin`: 사업보고 글에 첨부파일 칸이 보이는지

확인이 필요한 것(임시로 정함):
- 주소를 `/news`·`/reports`로 정했습니다. 사업소식과 사업보고는 글 주소가 서로 겹칠 수 있어서 종류를 주소에 넣었습니다.
- 이전 글 = 먼저 게시된 글, 다음 글 = 나중에 게시된 글입니다. 사업보고에서도 섹션 제목은 시안대로 "다른 소식 살펴보기"입니다.
- 375 시안이 없어서 모바일은 인사이트 상세의 375 크기에 맞췄습니다.
- "공지사항 목록 보기"는 `/contact?notice=news|report#notices`로 갑니다. 목록 쪽에 `id="notices"`와 `notice` 값에 따른 탭 선택이 있어야 합니다. 그 전까지는 CONTACT 준비중 화면으로 갑니다.

_Requested by **Fauxpaw** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017XFzw6pFPZv8xrAeBj1juT?thread=cmsg_017XFzw6pFPZv8xrAeBj1juTJB2sA8K8ji75SHkpf4yxQt)_

Stacked on #330: merge that first. This is the top of the no-playtest stack (#319, #320, #322, #330). It also shares two lines with Slice 29 (#324): whichever merges second takes `main` in and keeps both sides.

**The levels, agreed by the owner on 2026-10-20 as proposed** (design only: nothing is built until after Slice 30, #148):

| Warning | Level | From |
|---|---|---|
| A needs gene is being lost | more than half the hatched sprites alive lack it | #237's decision 4, its line for careful copying |
| A gene value has run to the end of its range | its middle has gone nine tenths of the way from the starter's value to that end | #274's list; why not "within a tenth of the end" is below |
| Too few to judge | no warning with fewer than 10 hatched sprites alive | A4's "fewer than 10 deaths" |
| Flaws and broken genes | reported, with no warning yet | #221 |

For the starter, the range warnings come at `GrowsUp` 1,800 or 12,600 ticks, `GrowsOld` 7,650 or 56,250, `Speed` 4.3 or 11.5 and `SenseRadius` 6.4 or 13.6. The brain parameters work the same way; `trace_decay`, which starts at the bottom of its range, warns only at 0.941.

## What changes

Before: the baseline report and the end of a fast-forward give the gene numbers, but nothing says when the species' genes have gone somewhere bad unless someone reads the tables.

After, once it's built: both end with **gene warnings**, lines that ask for a look and never change a verdict. A fast-forward that ended badly would say:

```
The hatched sprites alive carry 6.8 hidden flaws and 1.2 broken genes each, on average.
Gene warnings:
  drank Level → thirst: lacked by 62% of the hatched sprites alive, a needs gene (warns past half)
  GrowsUp: trait: 4500 → 1500, all the way to the end of its range (warns at 1800)
```

The calls made in the design, each with its reasoning in `docs/design/changes/2026-10-19-gene-warnings.md`:

- **Measured from the starter's value,** not "within a tenth of the end" as the brief said: three brain parameters start that close to an end and would warn from the first tick.
- **The needs genes are found from the data,** not listed in the code. The rule finds exactly #237's eleven on `main`, and a test pins them. After Slice 29 it also counts `fullness Level → hunger`, which eases hunger as the gut fills, making twelve, and Slice 29's `act_threshold` gets range warnings at 0.025 and 1.825.
- **No warning for values with no range** (an instinct's weight, a half-life) or for the starter's other genes the species loses: moving and losing is evolution (#237's decision 1). They're still listed.
- **Fast-forward's genes table gains two columns,** flaws and broken genes each hour, so the 220-hour runs show where they level off before anyone sets a warning for them.
- **One measure in the simulation's library.** Slice 30's 220-hour report counts lacking genes first, as the generations run does, and the build takes that count over unchanged.
- **Named "gene warnings",** in plain words. The owner's notes called it a genetic canary; the name is theirs to change.

**What it would have said today: nothing.** On `main` at `ce9cfc7`, the viability run (seeds 1–10, 50,000 ticks) with a scratch build of the measure gave no warnings. No needs gene was lacked by more than 2%, and no ranged value got more than a fifth of the way to an end (`GrowsOld` in seed 4, 21%). The levels were set before it ran, and it changed none. #225's 220-hour check would have warned on `GrowsUp` in seeds 3 and 8, the short childhoods it found.

Where: M2 design §16.3, §16.4, a new §16.6 and §16.7 (was "Later", §16.6); M1 design §7.6; `CONTEXT.md` (**Needs gene** and **Gene warning** are new, **Gene value** says which values have a range); the change file.

author: wasnertobias
body:
Closes #1287

## Motivation

Worker auto-placement (`_pick_best_gpu_subset`) ranked candidate GPU subsets only by the current snapshot: TP>1 collocation, awake lanes, awake VRAM and free VRAM. Sleeping lanes were left out on purpose, so the score never asked which lanes can still be loaded **together** after the placement. In practice that let a second TP=2 lane take GPUs `1,2` next to a TP=2 lane on `0,1`. That partial overlap blocks the first lane through GPU 1 and strands GPU 2, which lowers how many lanes can be co-resident on the node.

## Changes

- `_auto_place_gpu_devices` now collects every placed vLLM lane on the node, **awake or sleeping**, with its per-GPU footprint (`_estimate_lane_vram_mb / len(gpus)`).
- `_pick_best_gpu_subset` scores each feasible subset by the layout it would create. Two terms come before the existing ones:
  1. **`conflicts`**: placed lanes that could never be loaded together with the new lane, because on some shared GPU their share plus the new lane's per-GPU threshold exceeds the card's total.
  2. **`misaligned`**: multi-GPU lanes that overlap the candidate only partially. When the conflict count is equal, TP>1 lanes stack on identical GPU sets, so the remaining GPUs stay whole.
- The existing terms (`collocated`, awake lane count, awake VRAM, free VRAM, indices) follow unchanged as tie-breakers. Feasibility is still gated on the current free VRAM, since the lane has to start now.

New score: `(conflicts, misaligned, collocated, awake_lane_count, awake_used_mb, -free_mb, indices)`

## Tests

New tests in `logos-workernode/tests/test_lane_manager.py`:
- `test_auto_place_aligns_tp2_lane_with_existing_tp2_lane`: the case from the issue. TP=2 lane A sleeps on `0,1`, TP=1 lane C is awake on `0`, and the new TP=2 lane B goes to `0,1`. The old score picked `1,2`, so this test fails on `main`.
- `test_auto_place_prefers_co_residency_over_alignment`: alignment is not applied blindly. If C cannot share a GPU with a TP=2 shard, B goes to `1,2`, so B and C can still be loaded together.
- `test_auto_place_keeps_sleeping_lane_wakeable`: a TP=1 lane is not placed on a GPU where it could never be awake together with a sleeping lane, even though that GPU holds no awake lane. This test fails on `main`.

All existing auto-placement tests still pass, including the deioma regression with the sleeping-lane residue. The full worker suite has 5 local failures in `test_calibration.py` and `test_model_cache.py`; they fail identically on `main` and are unrelated to this change.

## Out of scope (see #1287)

- The orchestrator's `_pick_cold_load_placement` still picks its eviction GPU set by eviction cost alone. It only decides which lanes to evict; the worker makes the final placement.
- No rebalancing of lanes that are already placed.
