body:
Records why we collect central metrics by allowlist, and what we measured when we asked whether a block list would work instead.

Short version:
MCO does accept a broad matcher, but Prometheus joins the `match[]` selectors with OR, so a negative one next to the existing 227 excludes nothing.\
The docs cover removing single metrics by name and say nothing about patterns.
So we keep the model, not the contents, and write the measurements down for whoever picks this up again.

author: kunwarshivam
body:
## Story

E10-13 slice 5a, tests: the vault's token entry for an Alpaca OAuth connection. Claim: #754. PRD: FR-2.2. HLD: connections spec §5.2 step 4 and infrastructure §5. Decisions: DEC-2624 (new, reserved here, agreed with lane LV), DEC-77.

The token-exchange process (slice 5) writes the token at `connections/{connection_id}/token`, and lane LV's executor reads it. They're different processes in different lanes, and nothing fixed the bytes. DEC-2624 fixes one byte form:

`{"access_token":"<token>","format":1,"scope":["data","trading"],"token_type":"bearer"}`

The token is 1 to 4,096 bytes from `!` to `~`, excluding `"` and `\`, so it never needs escaping and the entry has exactly one byte form. Alpaca documents no expiry or refresh token (U-A3), so the entry has none. If Alpaca later documents a lifetime, that becomes format 2.

What it adds:
- **DEC-2624**.
- **`mandate_connections::token_entry`** with `FORMAT`, `MAX_TOKEN_LEN` and `TokenEntry`. `encode` and `decode` are `todo!()` stubs.
- **`ConnectError::TokenEntryInvalid`** (`token_entry_invalid`).
- **Six tests**, pending E10-13.

## Spec clause → test

| Spec clause or invariant | Test name |
|---|---|
| The entry is exactly its canonical form (item 1) | `the_entry_is_exactly_its_canonical_form`, which also checks that form with the journal's canonicalizer |
| An entry decodes to its token and scopes | `an_entry_decodes_to_its_token_and_scopes` |
| Every other form is refused (item 2): whitespace, member order, a missing or unknown member, format 2 or `"1"`, `Bearer`, an unsorted or wider or narrower or string scope, `expires_in`, and an empty, spaced, escaped, quoted, non-ASCII or over-long token; the longest token is held | `every_other_form_is_refused` (22 cases) |
| A token outside the form is never written | `a_token_outside_the_form_is_never_written` |
| A refusal and a decoded entry name nothing of the token (OPS-1) | `a_refusal_and_a_decoded_entry_name_nothing_of_the_token` |
| Every token of the form round-trips as canonical JSON, checked independently by `mandate-canon` | `every_token_of_the_form_round_trips_as_canonical_json` (256 cases) |

## Dependencies

None. `mandate-canon` and `proptest` are already dependencies of this crate.

## Journal events added

None.

## Not done

- The codec is the stacked PR.
- The token-exchange process that calls `encode`, and the fixture OAuth provider, are slice 5b.
- LV's executor calls `decode`.

## Decisions needed

None.

## Safety checklist (safety-critical changes)

- [x] No floats in money or quantity paths
- [x] No clock reads or randomness in the core
- [x] No `unwrap`, `expect`, or panics on trading paths (the stubs are `todo!()`, per DEC-77)
- [x] Ordering: not applicable
- [x] Replay: not applicable
- [x] No secrets or trading content in logs or notifications (tested: no refusal or debug form shows the token)
- [x] No `x-planned` or `(planned: ...)` marker added to a value the code already serves (DEC-683)

## Checks

- [ ] `cargo xtask check` green. I ran the affected checks rather than the whole command:
  - fmt, `clippy -p mandate-connections --all-targets -D warnings`, markers and typos are clean;
  - 85 tests pass and the 6 pending tests fail at `todo!()`.
  - With the stacked implementation, all 91 pass, and `cargo mutants --in-diff` gives 14 mutants, 13 caught, 1 unviable, 0 missed.
- [ ] Review agent report attached: the coordinator reviews.

body:
## PR Title
AQU-2028-Knowledge base: the Indexing… badge never updates after upload, then turns into a false "Indexing stalled"

## Summary
Closes [AQU-2028](https://linear.app/frontierrandd/issue/AQU-2028/bug-knowledge-base-the-indexing-badge-never-updates-after-upload-then)

Found while QA-walking dev on 2026-10-19. Two files uploaded to Living Memory → Knowledge base kept showing **Indexing…** although the server finished both within 30 seconds (one `ready`, one `ready` without summaries per AQU-2002).

`KnowledgeBaseSurface` read the list once, when the page opened. The 30 s timer from AQU-1376 only advanced the clock so the stall badge could appear; it never asked the server again. A row therefore stayed on "Indexing…" until a reload, and five minutes after upload it turned into a red **Indexing stalled**, with a retry button, for a document that was already indexed.

## Changes
- **Re-read while pending.** While any listed document is `pending`, the surface re-reads the list every 5 s (`PENDING_POLL_MS`). It shows no spinner, skips the read while the tab is hidden, and never stacks a read on one still in flight. The same tick re-checks the stall, replacing the old clock-only timer.
- **Stop when settled.** The interval only runs while a document is pending, so the last settled row ends it.
- **A failed re-read is quiet.** The rows on screen stay; the next tick tries again.
- **Stale reads can't win.** A generation counter is bumped by every read and by upload, re-index and delete. A read that started before one of those is dropped instead of overwriting it.

## Test Checklist

### Automated (run on `dbd7edd31`)
- [x] `npx vitest run src/components/knowledge/KnowledgeBaseSurface.test.tsx`: 15/15. New cases:
  - a pending row settles without a reload, then the list is not read again;
  - a list with nothing pending is never re-read;
  - a failed re-read keeps the rows and settles on the next one;
  - a re-read that left before an upload can't drop the uploaded row;
  - a document that stays pending still shows "Indexing stalled".
- [x] 4 of the new cases fail against the old component, and the stale-read case fails with only the generation guard removed.
- [x] `npx tsc -b --noEmit` clean. eslint: no new findings (the only warning is the existing `set-state-in-effect` on `void load()`).
- [x] Pre-push gate (`scan:secrets` + `test:e2e:affected`).

### Local stack, as `dev` on Dev Project → Living Memory → Knowledge base
- [x] Upload a small `.md`: the row went "Indexing…" → "Indexed without summaries" at 6 s with no reload (locally the summary model can't run). One list GET 5 s after the upload, then none in the next 22 s.
- [x] Try indexing again: "Indexing…" → settled at 6 s with one list GET. No console errors.

### For QA on dev after merge
- [ ] Upload a small `.md` and stay on the page: it settles on **Indexed** within a few seconds.
- [ ] Upload a large `.txt`: it settles on **Indexed without summaries** with its reason, and never turns into "Indexing stalled".
- [ ] Once every row is settled, the network panel shows no more knowledge-list requests.

### Spec
- [x] aquilla-specs `spec/aqu-2028-kb-list-settles` (`0405a4e`): new bullet *The list reports a settled run without a reload (AQU-2028)* under Knowledge base (reference documents) in `04-features/checks-rules-and-living-memory.md`. It's stacked on the unmerged AQU-2002 spec branch.

author: sethgw
body:
Step 1 of rebuilding what Bitwarden's web client did, now that it's gone.

- **Sign up**: \"Create an account\" on the sign-in screen (\`#/signup\`). The server emails a link when it verifies email, or returns a registration token directly when it doesn't; either way you choose a master password (12+ characters, confirmed, optional hint) and land in your vault. New accounts use PBKDF2 with 600,000 iterations, Bitwarden's default.
- **Emailed sign-up links** (\`#/finish-signup/?email&token\`) are checked first; an expired one says so and offers to start again.
- **Organization invitations** (\`#/accept-organization/?…\`): a new person sets a master password and is signed in; an existing account signs in or unlocks with the email filled in. Either way the invitation is then accepted for the account it was sent to, and a mismatch is explained rather than accepted.
- Links live in the URL hash (replaceState, no history entries), so a reload keeps the step. Other Bitwarden links (emergency access, delete recovery) still show the \"not yet\" notice.
- Item and Secrets Manager detail panes are centred again, with gutters on both sides (#7 dropped \`mx-auto\`).

No server changes: these use the existing registration and invitation endpoints.

## Testing
- lint, format, typecheck, 65 unit tests, worker smoke.
- Playwright against a local build: direct sign-up, a signed finish-signup link, an expired link, an invite to a new person, an invite to an existing account (email prefilled, accepted on sign-in; member status becomes Accepted), and an unsupported link.

author: wyckit
body:
Broad topic recall can fill its five-result budget with an overview and similar general notes, leaving useful supporting facts outside the candidate pool. This change retains a bounded wider pool for eligible short topic queries, ranks distinguishing query terms alongside semantic similarity, and selects complementary evidence across direct, expert, and broadcast recall.

The default pool is 20 candidates per namespace, with at most 32 extra candidates for larger requests; the public `k` limit is unchanged. Relevant archives can complement a confident live overview. Existing permissions, minimum similarity, explicit status ordering, conflict diagnostics, and final-only access/resurrection checks still apply. Topic selection requires evidence in distinct sources, so generic environment overviews and short factual questions retain the prior policy. Explicit opt-outs, raw search, MCP schemas, and model/dependency versions are unchanged; there are no additional embedding/model calls.

## Evaluation

Compared with merged #39 (`69dcfe5`), using the same corpus, original labels, defaults, and five-result budget:

| Measure | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Labeled sources on the six original broad queries, each route | 8/18 | 12/18 |
| Facet coverage on the 12-query graded supplement, each route | 58.3% | 80.6% |
| Graded nDCG@5, direct/expert | 0.6075 | 0.7583 |
| Graded nDCG@5, broadcast | 0.5982 | 0.7500 |

The original 30 non-broad questions retain their result IDs and quality metrics. No per-query quality metric regresses in the original evaluation or graded supplement. Caching and retries now return all three labeled sources; retrieval improves to two of three. Existing contradiction/resolution decisions and evidence are preserved; one broad timeout case returns the other unresolved claim first while retaining both in its warning.

The supplement was labeled before implementation, credits alternative useful sources, and includes six paraphrases. Its frozen pre-change baseline and per-query gates prevent aggregate gains from hiding a loss of facet coverage or graded ranking. All 36 query/route observations must cover at least two facets. The original corpus, labels, and baseline remain unchanged. These are inspected regression cases, not a blind holdout: coverage remains incomplete, and the bounded pool, English lexical heuristics, and soft namespace hint need validation on larger real workloads.

## Validation

- Full non-MSA suite: 2,105 tests passed on each of .NET 8, 9, and 10; the final three additional archive guards also passed on each (2,108 unique tests per framework).
- 28 controlled broad-coverage cases cover missing source candidates without graph links, archive mutation rules, filters, opt-outs, short questions, permissions, duplicate IDs, morphology, and bounded candidate counts.
- Real ONNX evaluation reports compared across all three frameworks; existing conflict/resolution suites pass.
- All three NuGet packages build; all 48 pinned-baseline gate checks pass. The pinned gate is a compatibility check, not a new MSA benchmark run.
- The documented focused evaluation command and normal CI include the new cases and upload `recall-realistic-broad-coverage-net*.json` reports.

author: clixmods
body:
## Why
After installing the mod on a server, players who had played there before were unknown to it, so no offline player showed until each one had logged in and out again. On horses, a far rider sat inside the horse, and a player logging off on one left a second horse behind as a distant mob.

## What
- **`WorldPlayers`** (server side): the first time a server shares, it reads the world's `playerdata` folder (position, yaw, dimension, hands and armour, both before and after 1.21.5's `equipment` compound) and names them from `usercache.json` (beside the world, above the saves, or the working folder). Players the publisher already knows keep their entry; at most the 1000 who played last.
- **Far riders**: the server's copy of the mount and its measured seat is taken before a remembered mob found under the rider, whose seat was guessed from two positions of different ages; the seat follows the server's every few seconds.
- **Second horse**: a mount a player takes away when logging off leaves the server's mob list at once, and the client sets the server's older report on it aside and never remembers it when it leaves the world (`MobMemory.takenAway`).
- Changelog (EN/FR) and README.

## Checks
- `WorldPlayersTest` on 1.20.1, 1.20.2, 1.20.4, 1.21.11 and 26.3; compile on Fabric 1.20.2, Forge 1.20.2 and 1.21.11, NeoForge 1.21.1, Quilt 1.20.2 and 1.20.4; CI on every target.
- Client game tests on 1.21.11: `lanshare`, `dedicated`, `restingmount`.
- Not checked in game: a real server with old playerdata, and the horse fixes with two real players.

author: fderuiter
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"fderuiter"} -->
_Requested by **Fred de Ruiter Fredde** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Ube12QdAP2r71oZNhUtAxj?thread=cmsg_01Ube12QdAP2r71oZNhUtAxjSqU13yYzqyqhHYyeEL8MtN)_

Fixes #728.

## Description

Before: a same-repo PR could auto-merge itself. `classify-pr.yml` ran on `pull_request`, so the PR's own workflow file and its own `scripts/classify_pr.py` ran with a write token and persisted credentials. The controller then trusted the `automerge:eligible` label, and it accepted `Required CI` and `automerge/classification` as plain commit statuses, which any workflow with `statuses: write` can post (including one the PR adds).

After: nothing the PR controls is trusted on its own.
- **Classifier workflow** runs on `pull_request_target` from the base SHA with `persist-credentials: false`. It never checks out or runs PR code. It reads the diff through the API as before.
- **Controller** re-runs `classify_pr()` from its own default-branch checkout on files, commits and labels fetched from the API, before it updates a branch or merges. The label is only a pre-filter now. `Required CI` is accepted only as a check run created by GitHub Actions; commit statuses are ignored. The `automerge/classification` status is no longer a gate. It's still posted for visibility.
- **Sensitive paths** now include `scripts/**`, so the classifier, controller and validators can't be changed by an auto-merged PR. `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` are sensitive unless the author is exactly `dependabot[bot]`. That keeps routine Dependabot bumps auto-mergeable, but a `dependencies` label alone is no longer enough. (The workflow's old `login.includes('dependabot')` check was also tightened to an exact match.)
- **`.github/rulesets/main.json`** pins `Required CI` to the GitHub Actions integration (15368). This file is a reference copy: the live ruleset must be changed in **Settings → Rules → Protect Main Branch** for this part to take effect.
- **`docs/auto_merge_policy.md`** documents the trust model.

How it was checked: unit tests cover a self-labelled PR touching `scripts/classify_pr.py` (not merged), a red Required CI (not merged), check runs from a non-Actions app (ignored), the latest Actions run winning, and API-sourced metadata. `tests/test_auto_merge_controller.py` and `tests/test_risk_classifier.py` pass (32 tests), as do ruff, the signature, architecture and import validators, and `docs --check`. The controller now runs as `python -m scripts.auto_merge_controller` so it can import the classifier. A local run of that command imports cleanly and stops at the missing-token check.

Note: because `classify-pr.yml` now runs from the base branch, this PR's own classifier run still uses the old workflow from `main`.

## Auto-Merge Eligibility

- [ ] Low-risk change: security fix to merge tooling, needs human review
- [ ] No sensitive paths modified: touches `.github/` and `scripts/`
- [x] No snapshots or API contract baselines modified
- [x] Tests added/updated as appropriate
- [ ] Safe for automatic merge once required CI succeeds

## Documentation Synchronization Check

- [x] I have updated the docstrings for any new or modified public APIs.
- [x] I have verified that the documentation builds locally without errors.
- [ ] I have included the necessary API reference updates if applicable. (Not applicable.)

## Database & Configuration Check

Not applicable.

## UI, Accessibility & Responsive Layout Check

Not applicable.

author: ashfrancis
body:
Closes the 404 half of INV-3029.

`/v1/changes/coin/{id}` 404'd for every classic asset: the change-summary worker builds entities from the configured aggregate pairs only, so the explorer asset page for USDC-GA5Z… (and every other classic asset) logged a 404.

- After every worker candidate misses, the handler tries `asset_price_snapshot` (the `/v1/assets` listing price) under the same withholding gate.
- `current_value` is the listing's USD price; only the `h1/h24/d7_delta_pct` fields are set. d30, ATH/ATL, streak and the `*_value` fields stay absent because the snapshot doesn't hold them. A worker row still wins.
- **Money invariant:** the snapshot price is already decimals-normalised, so the row carries `Normalized` and `changeSummaryResponse` skips the rescale. `TestHandleChangeSummary_AssetFallsBackToSnapshot` pins a 9-decimals asset served verbatim, with no 100x scaling.
- Rows past the listing's 15-minute age ceiling read as missing (`TestCoinChangeFromSnapshot_FreshRowsOnly`, integration, ran locally: PASS).
- OpenAPI description updated; docs-api, Postman and TS types regenerated.

Not done: real 30d/ATH/ATL for classic assets needs a per-asset USD minute series (option (a) in INV-3029); that stays open.

author: harshcasper
body:
The Makefile CI fails on `apigatewayv2-http-kinesis-integration` since early October. It is the only failing sample in the [latest run](https://github.com/localstack-samples/localstack-terraform-samples/actions/runs/38311907073) now that the license problem is fixed:

```
API Response: {"ShardId":"shardId-000000000000","SequenceNumber":"4967940745588605767925297472063743257610882932624536371"}
Smoke test failed: The response does not contain the expected fields.
```

The smoke test required `EncryptionType` in the PutRecord response. Kinesis returns `EncryptionType` only for encrypted streams, and this sample's stream is not encrypted. LocalStack's parity test for this exact integration (HTTP API, `Kinesis-PutRecord`, recorded against AWS) shows AWS answering with `ShardId` and `SequenceNumber` only. The test passed while LocalStack returned `"EncryptionType": "NONE"`; LocalStack now answers like AWS. The smoke test now checks `ShardId` and `SequenceNumber`.

Tested locally with `localstack/localstack-pro:latest` (2026.10.0): `make test-ci` in the sample deploys the 9 resources and the smoke test passes.

This adds an FDE-specific interview round guide to Getting started.

Each round type that's particular to Forward Deployed Engineer loops is explained by what it tests and how it differs from a standard software engineering loop. Examples: decomposition of a customer's business problem, system design inside a customer's identity and data constraints, and deployment retrospectives. It's free, with no sign-up.

Why it fits here: the list covers skill roadmaps and job-posting analysis. This adds what FDE hiring tests round by round, which the existing interview resources cover only in pieces.

Disclosure: I'm the founder of FDE Dispatch, which publishes the guide.

Happy to change the wording or placement.

author: benhuddart
body:
## Why

The CI `tests` job took about **7m53s** on a recent green run ([run 39277097452](https://github.com/BenHuddart/mufinder/actions/runs/39277097452)): roughly 1m20s of apt and pip installs, 38s of collection and worker start-up, and **5m38s** of pytest on one 4-vCPU runner. The test time is spread thinly across 4,801 tests (the slowest 25 add up to about 2 minutes of worker time), so trimming individual tests can't shorten it much. Splitting the suite across runners can.

## What changed

- **Sharded tests:** the `test-shard` matrix runs the suite as four `pytest-split` groups on separate runners (`make test-shard SHARD=n SHARDS=4`). Each shard uploads its `.coverage.shard-n` file.
- **One coverage gate:** the required `tests` job downloads every shard's data, runs `make coverage` (`coverage combine` then `coverage report`) and enforces the threshold. The threshold now lives only in `[tool.coverage.report] fail_under = 85`. `pytest-cov` reads it there for `make test`, and shards override it with `--cov-fail-under=0`.
- **Work-stealing:** `make test` and `make test-shard` use `--dist worksteal` instead of `--dist load`, so an idle worker takes queued tests from a busy one.
- **uv installs:** the `lint`, shard, `tests` and `docs` jobs install with `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7` and `uv sync --frozen` from the committed `uv.lock`, using uv's cache, instead of `pip install -e`.
- **Docs:** `docs/quality_and_automation.rst` describes the new targets, the sharded CI layout, worksteal and uv. It also corrects the old "2-vCPU runners" claim: the logs show 4 workers.

## Reviewer notes

- **Required check name kept:** branch protection requires `tests` and `docs`. The coverage-combining job is named `tests` and the shards report as `tests (shard n/4)`, so no protection change is needed. `tests` runs with `if: always()` and fails unless every shard succeeded, because a required check that is *skipped* when a shard fails would count as passing.
- **No stored durations:** with no `.test_durations` file, `least_duration` deals tests out one at a time in test-ID order. That already balances the shards to within a few seconds locally (36–39s each), so I didn't commit a durations file that would need regenerating. It can be added later with `--store-durations` if the shards drift apart.
- `fail-fast: false`, so one failing shard doesn't cancel the others and every failure shows up in one run.
- Not changed: `pages.yml`, `preview-build.yml` and `release.yml` still use pip. The release builds install non-editable for PyInstaller, so they're best switched separately.
- The CI installs no longer pre-install `numpy`: `muesr` and `muLFC` resolve to wheels in `uv.lock`. This PR's CI run is the first check of that on a clean runner.

## Verification

- All four shards run locally: 1201 + 1200 + 1200 + 1200 = **4,801 passed**. That matches CI's full-suite count, so no test is dropped or run twice. Wall times were 36–39s per shard, against 122s for the unsplit suite.
- `make coverage` over the four shard files reports **90%** total, the same as the unsplit CI run (90.02%).
- Gates still fail when they should: `coverage report --fail-under=95` exits 2, and a `pytest` run over `tests/domain` alone fails with "Required test coverage of 85.0% not reached", read from the new `fail_under` setting.

## Gates

- Shards locally — 4,801 passed in total
- Coverage 90% (≥ 85%), combined with `make coverage`
- `make docs` — clean; `make lint` — clean; `make harness` — 13 passed
- Docs updated alongside behaviour
- No new `MainWindow` handlers; no persisted names touched

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how CI enforces the 85% coverage gate and splits tests; mis-sharding or combine failures could block merges, but application runtime code is untouched.
> 
> **Overview**
> CI **splits the test suite across four parallel runners** using `pytest-split` (`test-shard` matrix), uploads per-shard `.coverage.shard-n` artifacts, and keeps the branch-protection **`tests` job** to fail if any shard fails and to **`make coverage`** (combine + enforce the 85% gate).
> 
> **Makefile / pytest:** adds `test-shard` and `coverage` targets; switches xdist from `--dist load` to **`--dist worksteal`**; moves the coverage threshold to **`[tool.coverage.report] fail_under`** (removed from pytest `addopts` so shards can use `--cov-fail-under=0`).
> 
> **CI installs:** `lint`, shards, `tests`, and `docs` jobs use **`astral-sh/setup-uv`** with `uv sync --frozen` instead of pip; lint runs **`make lint`**.
> 
> **Deps / lock:** adds **`pytest-split`** to dev extras and `uv.lock`; bumps lockfile package version to **0.6.0**.
> 
> **Docs:** `quality_and_automation.rst` documents sharding, worksteal, uv, and the single coverage gate; corrects runner CPU count to 4-vCPU.

author: cavewebs
body:
Closes #33

## Problem

`packages/widget/vite.config.ts` marked `pusher-js` as `external`, so the built widget kept `await import("pusher-js")`. widget.js runs as a classic `<script>` on the sites that embed it, where a browser cannot resolve a bare module name. The import rejected with `TypeError: Failed to resolve module specifier 'pusher-js'`, the widget fell back to polling, and real-time never started.

## Change

- Bundle pusher-js into the widget. I removed `external` and `globals` from the Vite config and added `pusher-js` 8.4.0 to `packages/widget/package.json`, the same version the root already locks. `inlineDynamicImports` keeps it one file. The lockfile change is three lines in the widget importer.
- Rebuilt and committed `packages/widget/dist/*` and `public/widget.js`.
- New `scripts/check-widget-bundle.mjs` fails if a built file imports or requires a package by name. `build:widget` now runs it, so the build fails if this comes back.
- New `lib/widget-bundle.test.ts`. It checks that the committed widget files have no bare imports and that `public/widget.js` matches `dist/guddesk.umd.cjs`, and it tests the checker itself.

I picked bundling over loading pusher-js from a pinned CDN URL. The build is already a single self-contained file, sites do not have to allow another script origin in their CSP, and self-hosted installs do not depend on a third-party script host. There is also no CORS question: Pusher's WebSocket and the `/api/pusher/auth` call are unchanged.

## Size of public/widget.js

| | raw | gzip -9 |
|---|---|---|
| before | 45,376 B | 15,326 B |
| after | 108,625 B | 34,046 B |

That is about 19 KB more gzipped, which is the size of pusher.min.js. Before this change those bytes were never loaded, because the import always failed.

## Verification

- Headless Chrome, loading widget.js as a classic script with fetch and WebSocket stubbed and a Pusher key in `GudDeskSettings`. The old build never opens a WebSocket. The new build opens `wss://ws-eu.pusher.com:443/app/test-key?protocol=7&client=js&version=8.4.0`.
- `node scripts/check-widget-bundle.mjs` passes on the new files. On the old `public/widget.js` it fails with `imports packages by name: pusher-js`.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, tests (158), lint and typecheck all pass locally.

body:
The operator could not prepare this catalogue because the existing Firebase image bucket uses fine-grained ACLs. Preserve its configuration and generated image URLs by storing private archive copies in a separate operator-only GCS bucket, with both bucket names bound to the migration plan checksum.

The authorized launcher accepts `-ArchiveBucket` during Prepare; Check/Apply use the saved binding and reject old unbound plans. Verify matching project numbers, uniform access and enforced public-access prevention on the archive, plus no public bucket IAM. Copy from durable local backups without source ACLs or Firebase tokens; verify checksums and anonymous denial before publication/deletion. Missing/404 is not accepted as private-copy evidence. Recheck privacy before generation-conditional deletion. Retained/shared artwork stays in the original bucket. Private asset records include their bucket, and manual future imports read it explicitly and create separate campaign copies.

Match the website's actual image fields and normalized item-ID/imageBaseId fallback. Obsolete `image` metadata is preserved verbatim in the original archive, rather than fetched as arbitrary external content or treated as required rendered artwork. Active missing/external references and explicit missing imageBaseId still block. Skip only the exact zero-byte `dnd-item-images/` folder marker, leaving it untouched; other unexpected objects remain blocking. Preflight includes aggregate resolution counts without tokens or links.

Retry only transient Firestore GET responses (429/502/503/504), at most three retries with bounded backoff. Never automatically replay POST/DELETE operations or authorization failures. Open backup flush handles with `r+` so Windows FlushFileBuffers succeeds without truncating files. Preserve private-output ACL verification and durable flush requirements.

Includes the read-only Storage metadata diagnostic from #136, an offline aggregate reference diagnostic, a reproducible Windows ZIP/checksum, and PowerShell instructions to create only the new private bucket and prepare a fresh plan. No client access or Firestore/Storage rules changes are enabled; this is an operator-only archive. Project administrators retain administrative access.

Validation: local suite: 45 tests, 43 pass, 2 Windows-only skipped. Independent extracted-package tests pass locally. Real Firestore-emulator transactions pass for migration, exact original/template preservation, retained art, safe restart, private campaign import and import retry; Storage calls there use deterministic contract doubles. Native Windows and Ubuntu CI pass for the checkout and independently extracted ZIP. The owner also ran live read-only preparation: 659 items, 605 Storage images, 658 item matches, 1 item without stored fallback, zero unresolved references, ready=true and productionWrites=0.

No production deployment, bucket changes or production migration were performed by Codex. The owner created the separate bucket locally. No rules deployment is required for this operator-only archive.



Latest reliability/visibility changes: retry safe POST batchGet and beginTransaction responses as well as GET (never replay commit), identify failing RPCs without logging request/body values, and make Check probe a transaction read with no document writes. Every migration stage now reports its label and a 15-second heartbeat, with source/backup/copy counters. Local request/migration tests pass; real Firestore-emulator transactions pass after injected 503s at both transaction start and batch read, including restart and campaign import. Latest native CI pending.

body:
## Summary

- Prefer the fully verified OmniRoute 3.8.50 runtime bundled with the Windows portable app when starting a new local gateway, while continuing to reuse a healthy shared Brahma/OmniRoute gateway.
- Capture bounded, redacted gateway stdout/stderr and include startup diagnostics when readiness times out.
- Show the in-app OmniRoute window immediately with a startup status, then switch to the dashboard on success or show safe diagnostics on failure.
- Make the Windows smoke-test timeout settle even when orphaned children keep stdout/stderr pipes open.
- Terminate the complete Electron process group in screenshot test cleanup and increase CI job timeouts to match measured cold-run durations.
- Keep local-model proxy requests counted as in-flight until the downstream HTTP response finishes or disconnects; give the swap test a realistic idle interval to avoid a slow-runner race.

## Motivation

The installed app waited roughly 48 seconds for OmniRoute readiness before creating the window, so a gateway startup stall appeared as severe UI lag with no window. The previous implementation discarded process output. The smoke-test and screenshot jobs also showed stale runner states consistent with child processes surviving parent cleanup.

## Verification

The prior full run exposed one Ubuntu socket disconnect in `local-model-proxy.test.ts` while swapping models; the current head fixes the downstream-response/idle-unload race and relaxes the test-only idle interval. On the current head, formatting, lint, both typechecks, script checks, localization guards, and the high/critical dependency audit pass. The cross-platform test suites and fresh screenshot/package validation are still running; do not merge until they finish.

This PR supersedes #13. It carries the same fix commit lineage so its workflow runs use a fresh concurrency group rather than the stalled previous branch.

author: brazol
body:
## Summary

Setting a session description blocks while WebRTC waits for an audio session reconfiguration, which can take a few hundred milliseconds. These calls ran on the platform main thread, which since Flutter 3.29 also runs the Dart UI isolate. Joining a call ([FLU-1018](https://linear.app/stream/issue/FLU-1018/setappleaudioconfiguration-stalls-the-ios-main-thread-on-join)) and starting to publish as a host ([FLU-1020](https://linear.app/stream/issue/FLU-1020/host-go-live-stalls-the-ui-during-publish-setup)) froze the UI. Any other call into the same peer connection factory was blocked meanwhile.

## Changes

- **Per-connection serial queue.** These methods now run on a serial queue per peer connection, in call order, and reply on main:
  - `createOffer`, `createAnswer`
  - `setLocalDescription`, `setRemoteDescription`, `addCandidate`
  - `getLocalDescription`, `getRemoteDescription`
  - `getSenders`, `getReceivers`, `getTransceivers`
  - `getStats`
- **Close and dispose.**
  - `peerConnectionClose` / `peerConnectionDispose` remove the connection right away. They close it on a dedicated serial close queue, behind the calls already queued for it, so no in-flight call runs against a closed connection.
  - `-[RTCPeerConnection close]` is synchronous and slow with media running, so it no longer blocks main.
  - `disposePeerConnectionFactory` closes any connections still open the same way, with the normal cleanup, and waits for pending closes before releasing the factory.
  - Engine detach also finds connections that are still closing.
- **Replies always on main.** Description, candidate and stats completions previously called `result()` directly on WebRTC's signaling thread. They now go through `FlutterRTCReplyOnMain`.
- **Remote track bookkeeping on main.** `remoteTracks`, `remoteStreams` and the volume caches are now updated on main in `didAddReceiver`, `didAddStream`, `didRemoveStream` and `didRemoveReceiver`. Main is where they're read (`trackForId`, `setVolume`, playout pause/resume, close cleanup), which removes a race with the signaling thread. These updates are queued before the `setRemoteDescription` reply, so Dart sees remote tracks registered by the time `setRemoteDescription` returns.
- **Event sinks.** The peer connection and data channel event sinks are read atomically.

author: nikrause
body:
## What

`@le-space/orbitdb-storage-bridge` 0.17.0 → 0.22.0 in `app/` and `bridge/`.

Nothing Belege calls changed its shape (`createAlephBackend`, `createAlephPin`, `createAlephAuthorizer`, `listAlephStores`, `waitForMessage`, `buildAppBackup`). The 0.19/0.20 behaviour changes (`allowPlaintextReads` default, `mergeIncrements` head union, FORGET result buckets) touch functions Belege does not use.

What changes is the install: the bridge made `@storacha/client` an optional peer, so the 28 `@storacha/*`, `@ucanto/*`, `@web3-storage/*` packages and `dotenv` leave the dependency graph.

## One thing worth knowing about pnpm

The old lockfile had `@storacha/client` resolved (as the bridge's dependency), and pnpm satisfies an optional peer from whatever is already in the graph — so a plain `pnpm install` after the bump kept the whole Storacha subtree. The lockfile here drops that resolution by hand (the bridge's snapshot no longer carries `(@storacha/client@…)`). Verified:

- a fresh `pnpm add @le-space/orbitdb-storage-bridge@0.22.0` in an empty project resolves no Storacha package;
- after `rm -rf node_modules` and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `node_modules/.pnpm` holds 0 Storacha directories.

pnpm leaves the now-unreferenced `@storacha/*` entries in the lockfile; they install nothing. `pnpm dedupe` would remove them but also bump Helia and friends, which is not this PR.

## Verified

- `pnpm -C bridge test`: 478 pass, 2 skipped, 0 fail
- `pnpm -C app test:unit`: 148 files, 1109 tests pass
- `pnpm -C app check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings

Also fixes the stale `WEBAPP_SLUG` comment and the `save_json` docstring, and adds a note to `OUTPUT_DIR` that it's a bucket key. ⚠️ **The generator must be re-pushed** to each workspace for this to take effect.

body:
## Fix

Keep the stale-selection invariant; improve its diagnostics rather than changing admission. A custom WS client minted a new `act.selectionId` after selecting a session. The session was still hosted, but the action no longer identified the connection's current selection claim.

- Stale refusals now name `selected.selectionId` and `act.selectionId` and explain how to reuse the claim. IDs are JSON-quoted; an absent selection is `null`. The existing dispatch path includes this detail in both its warning and wire error.
- Document the per-connection reuse contract beside `act` in `shared/wire.ts`, including `start: {}` for restarting a stopped session.
- Add a focused ClientSessions regression: a fresh action ID is refused without reaching Pi; the echoed select ID succeeds. Also cover an absent selection. Existing replaced-selection and stopped-session restart tests remain intact.

**Why this approach:** no first-party product bug was found. `web/src/lib/client.ts` centrally supplies `state.selectionId`; UI commands omit that field by type. Existing `Client.test.ts` covers reuse and ready-attachment gating. `extensions/piano-sessions/SessionDispatch.ts` sends create/select, not act. No client rewrite or relaxed guard is warranted. Preserves **INV-05** selection correlation and **INV-02** restart behavior; no migration or wire shape change.

## Evidence

Tested on macOS arm64, Node v24.19.0, revision `2c067e8` (browser run used the same production code before commit; only test formatting changed afterward). Scratch processes used their own database, throwaway Git folder, Pi history and fake Pi; no model calls or user's running instance. Scratch processes/data were cleaned up.

- **Before:** `node --test --import ./test/setup.ts --test-name-pattern 'act reuses the selection claim' test/ClientSessions.test.ts` failed because the refusal only said `Selection changed; inspect the current session before acting.` and omitted the selected/action IDs.
- **After:** all 12 ClientSessions tests pass; full `npm test`: **941 passed**, 0 failed. `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass (including the commit hook).
- **Running-system reproduction through agent-browser:** open a saved session and submit from the UI (restart succeeds). On another WS connection, person-select with `selected-claim`, wait for `selected` with `hosted: true`, then act with `fresh-act` and `start: {}`. Observe:

  ```text
  Selection changed; inspect the current session before acting. selected.selectionId="selected-claim"; act.selectionId="fresh-act". Reuse the selectionId from the current select or create_session; do not mint a new id for act.
  ```

  Resend with `selectionId: "selected-claim"`: observe `session:submission` and `echo: Matching claim admitted` in the UI. Fake Pi's received prompts contain only the browser submission and matching-claim submission, never the mismatched prompt. Runtime check passed in 4.5s.

Browser script stays uncommitted at `.scratch/act-selection/repro.mjs`; retained outputs are under `.scratch/act-selection/`. Screenshot and observed wire output are attached in the evidence comment. Scope limitation: fake Pi verifies admission/dispatch and browser rendering, not a live provider call or the external steer helper.

author: dkgoutham
body:
## What changed and why

### Payouts that strand tokens

A withdrawal to the pool's own address used to succeed. The token transfer moved nothing, but the pool still lowered its notes total by the amount plus the fee, so those tokens were stuck: no claim or withdrawal could reach them. Paying the pool's token contract, or another pool on the same token, strands tokens the same way.

Both pools now refuse a payout to themselves or their token with `Error::InvalidPayee` (code 24), on withdrawals and in `claim_fees`. A pool can't know the deployment's other contracts, so the SDK refuses a withdrawal to any of them with `Error::WithdrawalToContract`. It checks before planning, so no Consolidate step is paid for first, and again before proving each payout step, raw `transact` included. The admin console explains code 24.

### One home for the balance rule

A transaction balances when inputs plus deposit equal outputs plus withdrawal plus the pool fee. The SDK checked this only inside the proof builder, as plain `anyhow` text, after building the Merkle and membership inputs (on the web, inside the prover worker). So the CLI and the Advanced form each kept their own copy.

Now `transact::check_balance` returns `Error::NotBalanced { gap }`, and a raw `transact` step runs it before building anything. The new `check_transact` (`checkTransact` on the web) runs the deposit limits, the recipient check and the balance check without building a proof. The CLI drops `validate_balance` and shows the gap in tokens. The Advanced form drops `advanced-balance.js`, calls `checkTransact` before its dialog, and now refuses a spent input note itself.

## Breaking changes

- Contracts: `pool` and `pool-gvk` add `Error::InvalidPayee` (24). A withdrawal or claim paid to the pool or its token now fails with 24. Code 23 now covers only a negative claim or one above the fees collected. Testnet needs a redeploy; running the fee stack's redeploy from this branch covers both.
- Native SDK: `Error` gains `WithdrawalToContract` and `NotBalanced { gap }`. The enum isn't `#[non_exhaustive]`, so an exhaustive `match` needs both. Code that matched the old `Error::Other("not balanced: …")` text should match `NotBalanced`.
- Web SDK: `PoolRefusal.code` adds `'NOT_BALANCED'`, with `gap` as a signed decimal string in base units. `withdraw` and `transact` now reject a recipient that is a deployment contract.

Part of #695

## Summary

Neutral prose for downstream integrations and the bundled knowledge service, plus the reviewed Meta Forge installer fixes from `fix/094-deployment-test-stable-package` and the console Access change from #667, merged in so that all of them land together after one CI run.

### Neutral wording

Code identifiers are unchanged: file and module names, functions, flags, config keys, environment variables, wire keys, paths and the byte-pinned test fixtures keep their existing spelling.

- Installer prose, Guide prompts and labels, user-facing messages, web UI text and the knowledge-service template README describe the knowledge service and the downstream example applications neutrally. Tests that assert those strings follow.
- The design reference's source rows describe the downstream modules they draw on instead of citing repository paths.
- Archived proposals and design notes use neutral wording for an internal review channel and an additional consumer, and one long dash becomes a hyphen.

### Forge installer fixes

- Animation diagnostics report `renderMs`, `copyMs`, `parentRafAgeMs` and `deadlineOvershootMs` in whole milliseconds. A plain clock difference could show floating-point error, such as 3.0000000000000284 for a 3 ms render, which also made two frontend tests fail now and then. The renderer hash pin is regenerated for the changed renderer.
- A visual review that an earlier version left running no longer strands its slot when the animation renderer changes. Slot custody (reconciling the active-review index, and releasing the slots of a runtime owner that ended) reads saved receipts from any renderer. Every path that reuses review evidence still refuses a receipt from another renderer.
- Test-only: the fake deployment packages use fixed zip entry dates, so the same build packaged twice keeps its digest. This fixes an intermittent `test_deployment.py` failure.
- Test-only: the failed-cleanup status wait settles only on a status read that starts and ends with no deployment task. A read that overlaps the task's final cleanup write gets a conservative projection by design, and the old wait could accept it. This fixes an intermittent backend failure in `test_deployment_failed_cleanup.py`.
- Test-only: the restored-owner drain test in `test_visualization_operations.py` waits up to 30 s, not 0.5 s, for its background tasks to settle after the held read is released. The assertions after that wait check state, not elapsed time. Under parallel load the 0.5 s bound failed in 32 of 96 runs and the 30 s bound in none.
- CHANGELOG, Unreleased / Fixed: the diagnostics entry, and the review slot entry, which says that visual reviews saved by an earlier Forge must be run again.

This PR also carries #667 at its head `d1bdb05f`: the console Access panel keeps its edit controls available while it re-reads the access configuration in the background. #667 describes the change and its tests. author: brandon-fryslie
body:
A YAML bulk file reorders issues in one `lit import`. Each document,
create or update, that states `rank: top` joins the file's ordering, and
the ordering is handed in file order to one `RankSet`, so the file orders
issues exactly as `lit rank set <ids in file order>` would: whole or not
at all, no new rank keys minted, and a re-import of a landed order writes
nothing.

- The ordering is written after the creates and edges and before any
  update, so an order `RankSet` refuses (an epic ranked with its own
  child) applies no update. Updates can neither reparent nor re-rank, so
  nothing in the ordering depends on them.
- A batch refused at an update names what stays written:
  `BulkApplyResult.Kept` lists the applied updates and the order kept,
  leaving out the creates the rollback deletes.
- An update document may state only `rank: top`; then it writes no field
  change and takes no reason. `top` is the one value.
- `ValidateRankSetIDs` accepts one id (a lone `rank: top` document is
  `lit rank <id> --top`); `lit rank set` still requires two on the CLI.
  `FrameRepresentatives` starts its common-ancestor search at the issue's
  parent, which a lone chain needed.
- `lit import` reports the order through `printRankSet`, shared with
  `lit rank set`; its event carries `import.created`, `import.updated`,
  `import.ranked`.

Replaces the separate `tuxery-web-preview` Worker with [Worker Previews](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/previews/) of `tuxery-web` itself.

- `wrangler.jsonc`: `env.production`/`env.preview` removed (top level is production); new `previews` block with observability (Previews don't inherit it). Stale "no canonical redirect" comment fixed (#102 added the www → root 301).
- `deploy.yml`: `main` runs `wrangler deploy`; PRs run `wrangler preview --name pr-<n> --json` → `pr-<n>.preview.tuxery.store`, URL read from the JSON for the sticky comment. New `cleanup-preview` job deletes the Preview when the PR closes (100 Previews per Worker on the free plan).
- Previews send `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` (Cloudflare adds it on `workers.dev` only, not on custom domains).
- `push-cloudflare-secrets.sh` and README: Preview secrets go to the Previews Base config (`wrangler preview base-config secret put`). Already set in the dashboard (preview-tuxery Turso DB).

After merge and one working Preview: delete the `tuxery-web-preview` Worker in the dashboard.

This PR's own run is the test: its Preview URL should appear in the comment, and serve the preview DB's catalog.

author: bradrlaw
body: Follow-up to the 225W soak test: ran the same probe at the V100's full stock 250W cap on idx2. Result: still no throttling (peak HBM 84C), but the card spent 72% of the soak pinned at the power cap vs 35% at 225W -- only ~1C of margin left to the ~85C throttle point, and cooldown time nearly doubled. Conclusion: 225W is the better choice if the production cap is ever raised, since it keeps real thermal margin; 250W works but runs at the edge. No config change -- idx2 stays at 175W.

author: webdevayo
body:
### PR Description

    Closes #456
    
    ### Summary
    Adds `examples/verify-all.sh`, an executable shell script that automates
  the verification procedure described in [`docs/verifying.
  md`](docs/verifying.md). It verifies every documented asset against the
  live on-chain safety registry, reading the chain as the source of truth.
    
    For each asset listed in `docs/deployment.md`:
    1. **Derives the SAC address** for the network (`stellar/soroban contract
  id asset` or standard library fallback).
    2. **Reads the attestation from the registry** via JSON-RPC simulation
  (`getLedgerEntries` for `get_safety`).
    3. **Re-scans the asset** live using `./assay attestation -raw -preimage-
  version <version> <code-issuer>` to verify that the scan completed and is
  not undetermined.
    4. **Recomputes the hash** under the recorded preimage encoding version
  (`v1`/`v2`/`v3`).
    5. **Compares** live on-chain `(severity, flags, evidence_hash)` against
  the re-scanned values.
    6. **Reports a distinct verdict** per asset, followed by a summary of
  counts.
    
    ### Outcomes & Exit Code Mapping
    - **`VERIFIED`**: Chain data was read successfully, and the recomputed
  live scan matches the on-chain registry parameters.
    - **`MISMATCH`**: Chain data was read successfully, but one or more
  parameters (severity, flags, or evidence hash) do not match.
    - **`INCONCLUSIVE`**: The check could not be completed (undetermined scan,
  network/RPC error, or missing on-chain entry). Never reported as a pass or
  mismatch.
    
    **Exit Codes:**
    - `0`: All documented assets verified
    - `1`: At least one mismatch found (`MISMATCH` takes priority over
  inconclusive)
    - `2`: No mismatches, but at least one inconclusive
    - `64`: Invalid usage or configuration error
    
    ### How to Run
    ```bash
    # Basic run against testnet
    ./examples/verify-all.sh

    # With options
    ./examples/verify-all.sh --bin ./assay --deployment docs/deployment.md --
  timeout 30 --attempts 3

  ### Verification & Testing

  • Clean shellcheck run on examples/verify-all.sh and across the repository
  (find . -name '*.sh' | xargs shellcheck -S warning).
  • Tested against the live testnet deployment.
  • Verified all distinct outcomes and exit codes:
      • Exit 0 on matching chain state (VERIFIED)
      • Exit 1 on evidence/flag differences (MISMATCH)
      • Exit 2 on unreachable RPC endpoint (INCONCLUSIVE)
      • Exit 64 on usage errors, empty tables, and malformed rows

author: adclz
body:
- **53 fuzz_ide crashes, none a bug.** Since #88 every input is read beside the library `Lib`, and answers point into it: workspace symbols, "'Half' is declared here", a definition. The harness checked every position against the input's text and never read the `uri`. It now holds both documents and reads each location in the file it names: an object's `uri`, a link's `targetUri`, a call's `from`, a workspace edit's keys. A file the server has not open is a finding. The three smallest inputs are regressions.
- **The triage replayed nothing.** download-artifact v8 extracts a lone matching artifact straight into `path`, so a night where one target crashed had no `fuzz-crashes-*` folder (16 and 19 October). Each target now uploads the folder above its own, so the files are `<target>/crash-…`, and the triage downloads with `merge-multiple: true` into one layout.

author: miguelmedeiros
body:
Straight to dev.

## What
On the Linux Desktop, a file over HyperDHT is no longer paced by a word back from the runtime for every 16 KiB chunk: the runtime says only when a connection's socket is full and when it has room again, so a file goes about as fast as before the runtime started answering sends, with its backpressure kept.

In the released version: yes. The per-frame answer came with "a HyperDHT send is answered once its socket has room" (#2443) and its follow-up (#2509), both in every release since 1.3.0.

## Contract changes (read closely)
Desktop-internal only (sidecar <-> Rust <-> page, no wire or WISP change):
- `native/transports/hyperdht/sidecar.mjs` no longer emits `{type:"sent", endpoint, id, seq}` for each frame. It emits `{type:"full", endpoint, id}` once when a connection's socket holds more than `SEND_ROOM` (64 KiB) after a send, and `{type:"room", endpoint, id}` once it drained to `SEND_ROOM`. A frame it could not send is still `{type:"error", command:"send", id, seq}` (the frame that filled the socket, if the connection closes before it drains; any frame sent to a closed connection).
- `apps/desktop/src/hyperdht.rs` forwards `full` / `room` to the page as `{type:"full"|"room", id}` instead of `sent`; `unsent` is unchanged. `paired_hyperdht_send` keeps its signature (`seq` still names a frame for `unsent`).
- `apps/ui/src/desktop/nativeTransports.ts`: a HyperDHT frame counts against the send budget until Rust answered the invoke (it answers once queued for the runtime), as Iroh's does. While the runtime says `full`, a file's quarter of the budget (30 KiB) counts as well, so a file waits and a message or ping still fits; `room` gives it back.

## Skim
- Tests (`packages/browser/test/hyperdhtSidecar.test.ts`, `hyperdhtSidecarRoom.test.ts`, `apps/ui/src/test/desktop/nativeBinary.test.ts`, Rust `runtime_tests`): the per-frame `sent` expectations removed, the page model of the room test moved to the new contract. In the room test, the page model frees a frame's budget in a `setImmediate` after the pipe write, not in the write's own callback: a write the kernel takes at once calls back in the same turn, so the model wrote on without reading `full` (up to 96 chunks, 1.5 MiB, between two `full`, against 27-34 deferred) and in CI the sidecar's socket passed `MAX_BUFFERED` (2 unhandled "exceeds its frame budget" errors). The real page hears Rust's answer as a message of its own, after the words before it. The test also ignores the sidecar's errors once it is over (afterAll stops the contact first).
- Comments in `endpoint.mjs` and `hyperdht.rs`.
- `docs/changelog/unreleased/desktop-hyperdht-file-speed.md`.

## Your call
- Why not a bigger send budget (tried first): with four chunks in flight instead of two, a 64 MiB file was no faster on a quiet host (out 19.5 s vs dev 18.4 s, before both answers came in 15.0 s), and the receive side regressed as much, which a send budget does not touch. The time goes into the extra crossing per chunk (each `sent` is a `webview.eval` on the page's main thread), not into the round trip's latency.
- Bound: between the socket passing `SEND_ROOM` and the page hearing `full`, the page keeps sending for one trip of that word (it frees a frame once Rust queued it). That is far below the endpoint's `MAX_BUFFERED` (2 MiB), past which a send throws and the chat reconnects. Per-frame accounting bounded it to the page's 120 KiB budget; the trade is speed for a looser (still bounded in practice) cap.
- Rejected: coalescing `sent` (with two to four chunks in flight there is rarely more than one to coalesce), and having Rust answer the invoke only once the runtime wrote the frame (that was the version that doubled a file's time).

## Reversibility
Revert the commit. Nothing is stored; the sidecar ships inside the app, so Rust, page and sidecar always match.

## Evidence
- Unit tests fail on dev and pass with the change: `nativeBinary.test.ts` (on dev: times out waiting for the send to be answered), `hyperdhtSidecar.test.ts` ("says once that a socket is full and once that it has room": on dev, no `full`, a `sent` per frame), `hyperdhtSidecarRoom.test.ts` (on dev: fails). With the change: 3/3 and 11/11 pass, no unhandled errors.
- `npm run typecheck`, eslint on the touched files: clean. Rust (`cargo fmt --check`, `clippy -D warnings`, `cargo test hyperdht`): clean; 12 hyperdht tests pass.
- Desktop A/B on a 4-core Linux host, three debug builds: **old** = dev with #3440, #2509 and #2443 reverted (before the per-frame answer), **dev** = 9b3db1e93, **fix** = dev + this change. Linux Desktop (Xvfb) <-> CLI bot, 64 MiB each way over HyperDHT, Fallback off, local Pkarr relay + HyperDHT testnet on loopback. 4 interleaved rounds in two orders, 8 transfers per direction per build, ms from the pick/send to the other side's stored file:

  | build | Desktop out: median / mean | Desktop in: median / mean |
  |---|---|---|
  | old | 29.7 s / 30.5 s | 25.7 s / 25.8 s |
  | dev | 36.9 s / 36.0 s (+24 %) | 30.9 s / 30.7 s (+20 %) |
  | fix | 30.7 s / 31.2 s (+3 %) | 28.4 s / 28.3 s (+10 %) |

  Desktop CPU per 64 MiB out (app + WebKit + sidecar): old ~6.0k ticks, dev ~7.1k, fix ~6.2k. This host is slower than the one that first measured the gap (software GL under Xvfb), but the ratios match: dev was 23-25 % slower there, and the fix takes back almost all of it on the way out and half of it on the way in.

  Raw (ms/ticks per transfer):
  ```
  old: out 30472/6081 35456/7010 29598/6029 29446/5725 29736/6000 29480/5822 30501/6185 28978/5735
       in  24738/5059 27330/5733 26032/5135 27607/5703 25372/5155 26192/5522 24224/4999 25269/5367
  dev: out 37179/7231 37630/7251 36659/7207 40674/7982 32636/6595 30510/6028 34470/6934 38278/7566
       in  28074/5782 34361/7207 31804/6194 32939/6702 28570/5806 31967/6482 28129/5732 30020/6348
  fix: out 33023/6517 29947/5870 29763/6078 34581/6987 30961/6316 28637/5649 32498/6482 30510/5993
       in  27331/5505 29172/6128 25194/5222 29583/6205 27584/5493 30603/6324 26771/5429 30399/6257

author: roodboi
body:
Linear: HACK-1132 (WU19, unit F16). Scoped migration with preview, replacement verification and rollback.

## Final behavior

New `hack setup migrate` subcommand. It moves one scope at a time from standalone Hack skill and rule files to the skills-only `hack` plugin (the #305 layout).

- **Preview (default, read-only).** Lists every standalone target in the selected scope (`--path`, `--global`, `--all-scopes`) and clients (`--claude`, `--codex`, `--cursor`; default all) with one action:
  - `remove`: Hack-owned (W11 classifier: current or known earlier render) and the replacement plugin is verified or explicitly skipped.
  - `blocked`: Hack-owned, but the replacement is not verified.
  - `preserve`: customized, unknown, or reached through a symlink. Each has a closed, value-free reason.
  - `absent`.

  Targets: the Codex `hack-cli`/`hack-init` skills, the Claude Code `hack-init` skill, the Cursor `hack.mdc` rule, and the shared `~/.ai/skills/hack-cli`. The shared skill follows Claude Code or Codex.
- **Replacement verification** reads configuration only (`src/agents/plugin-replacement.ts`):
  - Claude Code: the nearest settings file must enable `hack@hack-dance` (project `settings.local.json`, then project `settings.json`, then user). `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` must also list an installed copy that carries the `hack-cli` and `hack-init` skills.
  - Codex: `[plugins."hack@hack-dance"] enabled = true` in the project or user `config.toml`.
  - The global scope counts only user-level configuration.
  - Cursor is `not-inspectable`, so it needs `--skip-plugin-check cursor`. `--skip-plugin-check <clients>` accepts `claude`, `codex`, `cursor` or `all`.
- **`--apply` is all or nothing.**
  - It refuses with exit 1 and writes nothing when any target is blocked, a scope root is unresolved, or a file can't be read for backup.
  - Otherwise it first commits a 0600 manifest under `$HACK_HOME/agent-migrations/<id>.json`. The write is fsynced, then renamed into place. The manifest holds the exact bytes, sha256 and mode of each file.
  - It then removes each file only if its bytes still match the backup. Removal uses the W11 owned-remove path, and an empty skill directory goes with its file.
  - A file edited in between is reported as `changed` and left in place, with exit 1.
  - When nothing is Hack-owned, apply writes no manifest.
- **`--rollback-manifest <manifest>`:**
  - Restores each entry into an empty path with exclusive create, then sets the recorded mode.
  - Never overwrites. Identical bytes are reported as `already-present`; anything else is `conflict` (exit 1) and left unchanged.
  - Idempotent, and it recovers an interrupted apply.
  - Refuses the whole manifest, restoring nothing, if any entry's path is not exactly a known target under its root, its digest does not match, or its bytes are not a Hack render for that target.
- Claude primer hooks, MCP entries and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` sections are never touched.
- `--json` returns the usual `{ok, data}` envelope. Messages never include file contents.
- `setup-sync.ts` now exports `listOwnedFileTargets` so migration and sync share one path/surface table.

Docs: `docs/integrations.md` (new "Migrate standalone files to the plugin" section, and the switching guidance now points to it), `docs/cli.md`, the `tests/e2e/README.md` freeze description, and a regenerated `docs/reference/cli.md`. No consumer guidance or render changes, so there are no fingerprint or revision updates.

## Validation (local, macOS, source CLI)

- `tests/plugin-migration.test.ts` (15 tests). Temp project and HOME roots are passed explicitly, so the process HOME is never touched. Covered:
  - preview leaves hashes and modes byte-identical
  - blocked apply refuses with no writes
  - verified apply, then rollback restores exact bytes and mode; a second rollback reports `already-present`
  - incomplete Claude install copy
  - project-local disable overrides a user enable
  - Codex disabled, malformed and other-plugin configs
  - project-only config does not verify user-scope duplicates (all-scopes apply refused)
  - Cursor skip
  - client filtering
  - symlinked skill dir preserved
  - interrupted apply recovered by rollback
  - edit between backup and removal reported as `changed`
  - rollback conflict leaves the user file alone
  - tampered manifests (path, bytes, target, digest, non-Hack bytes) and a missing manifest refused with no writes
  - unresolved scope root refused
- `tests/setup-migrate-command.test.ts` (4 tests). Runs the source CLI through `privateCliEnv` with private HOME and HACK_HOME, and covers preview JSON, refused apply, skip-verified apply, rollback, flag conflicts and `--skip-plugin-check` parsing.
- Flag name: the rollback flag is `--rollback-manifest`, not `--rollback`. The CLI parses argv once against the union of every command's options, keyed by long name. A value-typed `setup migrate --rollback` retyped the boolean `config adopt --rollback`, so `config adopt --rollback --json` took `--json` as its value and failed with a usage error. That failed all ten `native-compose-adoption-*-worktrees` docker E2E scenarios in CI run 39280939414. `tests/cli-command.test.ts` now requires each long option to keep one value type across the command tree, and checks that `config adopt --rollback --json` still parses as two booleans.
- `agent-surface-freeze` e2e: added `setup migrate --all-scopes` and `setup migrate --all-scopes --apply --skip-plugin-check all`, twice each. Ran locally with `bun tests/e2e/run.ts --only=agent-surface-freeze`: pass, all customized seeded surfaces byte-identical, positive control intact.
- Required local checks:
  - `tests/integration-ownership.test.ts`, `tests/cli-spawn-env-isolation.test.ts`, `tests/cli-reference-docs.test.ts`, `tests/cli-help.test.ts` and `tests/integration-sync.test.ts` pass.
  - `bun run --cwd packages/cli typecheck`: 0 errors.
  - `bun run --cwd packages/cli check`: 0 errors. Its 34 warnings come from files this PR does not change.
  - `bunx ultracite check` on the changed files is clean.
  - `bun run privacy:check` passes.

## Negative controls (mutation proofs)

Each mutation below was applied alone. The named test file failed, and the source was then restored:

- apply ignores blocked targets
- Claude installed-copy check skipped
- Claude settings precedence reversed
- Codex `enabled` forced true
- global scope reads project Codex config
- symlink preservation removed
- byte recheck before removal removed
- rollback overwrites a conflict
- manifest path validation removed
- manifest digest validation removed
- rollback accepts non-Hack bytes
- restored mode ignored
- manifest not committed before removal (caught by the interrupted-apply test)
- customized files treated as owned
- `--skip-plugin-check` accepts unknown names
- refused apply exits 0
- `--rollback-manifest` accepts extra flags
- `setup migrate` flag named `--rollback` again (value-typed): both new `tests/cli-command.test.ts` guards fail

## Remaining gaps (host-bound)

- Replacement verification is configuration evidence, not loading evidence. A verified status does not prove a fresh client session loads the plugin. The command and docs tell the operator to check that first.
- The Codex plugin cache layout is not inspected, so only `config.toml` enablement is checked. The Claude `installed_plugins.json` shape is the v2 registry form (array or object, both accepted), and this PR does not re-observe it against the current client release.
- Cursor plugin installs are not inspectable; Cursor migration always needs an explicit skip.
- No real client home or user/global migration was run; all evidence comes from temp fixtures. The new freeze rows also need their first hosted CI pass.
- Concurrent `setup migrate --apply` runs are not serialized. Each removal rechecks bytes and ownership, which leaves the same single read-then-unlink window documented for W11.
