body:
Fixes the `latest` alias gate that failed release run [39271038207](https://github.com/xjoker/garage-ui/actions/runs/39271038207) (tag `20261019.1`, commit `20be70e`) even though `:latest` and `:20261019.1` both pointed at `sha256:2a0784fe9a511239fbd055f30f294216711cbdc17a119cdbf2cbad597927a0bd`. Linear: SAF-49.

## Root cause (with evidence)

`scripts/verify-image-tag-alias.py` read each digest with
`docker buildx imagetools inspect REF --format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'` and threw away stderr and the exit status.

1. **The release job runs Buildx v0.25.0, not the runner image's v0.38.0.** `docker/setup-buildx-action` is pinned to `version: v0.25.0` and installs it as `~/.docker/cli-plugins/docker-buildx`. Job log:
   `2026-10-19T14:45:29.7923085Z github.com/docker/buildx v0.25.0 faaea65da4ba0e58a13cd9cadcb950c51cf3b3c9`
2. **Buildx v0.25.0 does not run a template that starts with `{{.Manifest`.** In `util/imagetools/printers.go` at v0.25.0, `case strings.HasPrefix(format, "{{.Manifest"):` prints the text summary (`Name:` / `MediaType:` / `Digest:` / `Manifests:`) instead of running the template. v0.38.0 narrowed this to an exact `{{.Manifest}}` (`isWholeManifestTemplate`), so the command works on newer Buildx, which hid the problem locally. `{{range .Manifest.Manifests}}` in `publish.sh`'s platform check starts with `{{range` and is not affected.
3. **Reproduced with the same binary** (release asset `buildx-v0.25.0.linux-amd64`, checksum verified, commit `faaea65` as in the job log), reading the public image anonymously:
   - `--format '{{.Manifest.Digest}}'` exits 0 and prints the text summary for both tags. v0.38.0 prints `sha256:2a0784…`.
   - The summaries differ in their `Name:` line (`…:20261019.1` vs `…:latest`), so the version and alias "digests" can never be equal: on v0.25.0 the gate can never pass.
4. **Why the log said `unavailable` and not the summary text:** each read's timeout was `min(10, remaining)`, and only the last loop iteration was reported. The last iteration usually starts with less than one read's time left, so it times out (or is skipped when `remaining <= 0`), returns `""`, and the message shows `unavailable`. Running the original script with v0.25.0 for 6 s and 11 s gives the exact CI message `(version=unavailable, alias=unavailable)`, while every complete read in those runs returned the summary text. With 7–10 s it prints the summary instead. Same mechanism, different timing.
5. Corroboration: the earlier shell version of this check (`a901e52`, same template, `2>/dev/null`) also failed in run 38870091068 (`20261016.3`), on the same Buildx v0.25.0.

Not the cause: the package is public (anonymous token and manifest reads work), tokens and login are fine (the same job pulled and inspected `:20261019.1`), and GHCR serves the index with the Docker manifest-list media type (`Docker-Content-Digest` matches for both tags).

Not verifiable after the fact: the original script discarded stderr, so the runner's last reads cannot be confirmed as timeouts rather than registry errors. Either way, the earlier reads could not have matched.

## Change

`scripts/verify-image-tag-alias.py` only (plus its tests and a CHANGELOG line). `publish.sh` and `ci.yml` are unchanged. The SAF-46 follow-ups below are separate commits.

- Read each tag with `docker buildx imagetools inspect --raw REF` (same tool, same `docker login` credentials) and use `sha256:` + SHA-256 of the exact bytes the registry serves. That is the manifest digest by definition, and it does not depend on Buildx's template handling. The bytes must parse as an image index or manifest. The v0.25.0 text summary or any other output is reported as unreadable.
- Each failed attempt logs one line with the reason for each tag: the digest, or `unavailable (transient|permanent: exit status N: <stderr summary>)`, `no response within 20 seconds`, or `output is not a manifest: …`. Stderr is collapsed to one line, truncated, and redacted (`Bearer`/`Basic` credentials; `key=value` and `%3D` forms of any key ending in `token`, `secret`, `password`, `passwd` or `api_key`, such as `refresh_token=`, `id_token=`, `client_secret=`; the same keys as JSON string fields, such as `"token": "…"`; `password:` values; URL userinfo; JWTs; `ghp_`/`github_pat_` tokens). See *Review round 1 fixes*.
- Transient errors (timeouts, 5xx/429, network errors, `not found` while the alias propagates, and anything not classified) are retried with exponential backoff (3, 6, 12, then 15 s max) within the same 300 s limit. Errors that waiting cannot fix stop early and fail: `Unauthorized`/`Forbidden`/`denied` answers (a bare `401`/`403` number is not matched), missing `docker`, bad flag or reference, and output that is not a manifest after a successful Buildx run.
- One read is capped at 20 s instead of being shortened by the remaining time, so the final message reports a real reading, not an artificial timeout. No new attempt starts after the deadline. An attempt that is already running can finish up to 2 × 20 s past it.

## Why the gate is not relaxed

- It passes only when **both** tags were read in the **same attempt** and give the **same non-empty** digest (`if last_version.digest and last_version.digest == last_alias.digest`).
- A mismatch keeps polling and then fails with both digests in the message. A tag that cannot be read never counts as a match and fails at the deadline, or immediately for permanent errors.
- The overall timeout is still 300 s and `publish.sh` still runs `gh release edit --draft=false` only after this exits 0.

## Tests

- `scripts/check-release-version.sh` (the existing home of these tests): the old tests patched `inspect_digest` and never saw real Buildx output. They are replaced by a fake `docker` on `PATH` that serves scripted answers, plus a fake clock:
  - equal digests → pass (digest = SHA-256 of the served bytes);
  - different digests → fail after the timeout, message has both digests and no `unavailable`;
  - stale alias that converges → pass;
  - unreadable: 401 with a `Bearer ghp_…` in stderr → fails at once, reason logged, token redacted; v0.25.0 text summary → `output is not a manifest`; 503 forever → fails with the 503 reason after backoff 3/6/11 s; read timeout → `no response within …`; `docker` missing → fails at once;
  - 503 then success → pass, attempt 1 logged with the 503;
  - static guard: the script uses `--raw` and no `--format`.
  - Mutation check: the suite fails against the original script, against a gate that treats two unreadable digests as equal, against a gate that ignores the alias, and with redaction removed.
- Real GHCR, anonymous: the fixed script on `ghcr.io/xjoker/garage-ui:20261019.1` vs `:latest` prints `Verified … (sha256:2a0784fe9a511239fbd055f30f294216711cbdc17a119cdbf2cbad597927a0bd)` with Buildx v0.25.0, v0.38.0, and 0.13.1. `--raw | sha256sum` equals GHCR's `Docker-Content-Digest` for both tags.
- Local `registry:2` on 127.0.0.1 (nothing was pushed to any public registry), Buildx v0.25.0 and v0.38.0:
  - multi-arch Docker manifest list copied from `20261019.1`, `latest` = version → pass;
  - hand-written OCI image index (`application/vnd.oci.image.index.v1+json`, amd64 + arm64) on two tags → pass;
  - `latest` ≠ version (single-platform index `sha256:021ccde5…` vs `sha256:2a0784fe…`) → fail with both digests;
  - alias tag missing → fail with `not found` reason;
  - alias stale, retagged after ~7 s → pass on attempt 4;
  - the original script on the identical-digest case with v0.25.0 → fails (bug reproduced).
- `shellcheck scripts/*.sh`: no new findings (30 pre-existing, identical to `main`). `actionlint` 1.7.12: clean. `ruff check` and `pyflakes` on the script: clean.

**Not verified on a GitHub runner:** CI is disabled and no release was triggered. Runner-specific parts (authenticated `docker login` with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the `docker-container` builder created by setup-buildx) were not exercised. `--raw` uses the same resolver and credentials as the

author: sudokmaar
body:
## Blueprint

Sign-off gate for clinical gene panels built on the HGNC REST API (rest.genenames.org). It starts from a Webhook (JSON body with `panel_name` and `symbols`), a weekly Schedule or a manual run. DuckDB splits the list and maps Excel dates such as `2-Sep` back to the legacy symbol (SEPT2). A `Loop` sends one `search` request per 100 symbols with an OR query limited to `status:Approved`. An `If` then runs a second `Loop` only for symbols that did not match, with exact `fetch` calls on `prev_symbol`, `alias_symbol` and `symbol`. DuckDB classifies each input as APPROVED, CASE_FIXED, RENAMED, ALIAS, AMBIGUOUS (more than one gene), WITHDRAWN, EXCEL_DATE, NOT_FOUND, INVALID or DUPLICATE (same HGNC id as an earlier row). It compares the result with the last run for the panel, stored in KV. Findings go to a WARN log and Slack (`allowFailure: true`), and a `Fail` task blocks sign-off while anything needs a curator. Flow outputs: a summary, a per-symbol report CSV and a corrected panel CSV. The default symbols are a sample panel; every classification comes from the live API.

Run on Kestra 2.0.5 (OSS, local), eleven executions against the live HGNC API, no API key needed. Baseline with the 20 default symbols: 8 approved, 6 corrected (SEPT9 to SEPTIN9, GBA to GBA1, KIAA0196 to WASHC5, MRE11A to MRE11, ATP5A1 to ATP5F1A, palb2 to PALB2), 2 duplicates (C10orf2 is TWNK), 4 blocking: HER2 (alias of ERBB2), AIP1 (alias of six genes), 2-Sep (maps to SEPTIN2) and NOTAGENE1. The gate failed as intended. A re-run reported 0 changes. With the stored state for GBA and SEPT9 set back to older approved values, the next run reported "GBA -> RENAMED GBA1, was APPROVED GBA". An edge panel flagged A12M1 as withdrawn, `foo$bar` as invalid, 1-Jan as an Excel date with no gene behind it, and MARCH1 as renamed to MARCHF1. A clean cardiomyopathy panel passed, and so did a webhook submission (KIAA1109 renamed to BLTP1). Without `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` the findings still appear in the WARN log and the CSVs.

## Checklist

- [x] I ran this flow on Kestra 2.0 and it calls the real system named in the title (no hard-coded or simulated results)
- [x] Every `type:` exists on [kestra.io/plugins](https://kestra.io/plugins)
- [x] The file is in `flows/`, its `id` matches the filename, and the `extend` block has all 9 fields from the README
- [x] `tags` and `subTags` come from the README taxonomy, `demo` is `false`
- [x] Secrets use `{{ secret('NAME') }}`, nothing is hard-coded

author: amirali2agh
body:
## Summary

Fixes the three game-engine correctness issues from the review epic: turn rotation on a
partial roster (#10), per-player-count track offsets (#11), and the stale dice value on turn
change (#13). Every behavioural change is covered by a test that failed before the fix.

## #10 — 4-player turn rotation with fewer than four players

- `_rotate_turn` derives the rotation from `len(state["players"])`. The non-diagonal
  `[0, 3, 1, 2]` order only applies while all four seats are occupied, so the existing
  `test_rotate_turn_uses_requested_four_player_order` stays green.
- A stale or out-of-range `current_turn` is clamped instead of raising `ValueError` from
  `turn_order.index()`.
- Every seat lookup now goes through `_current_player_index`, which clamps too.
- **Room behaviour (decided with the maintainer):** a room only starts once its configured
  roster is complete. Waiting clients receive `waiting_for_players`; if the roster is still
  incomplete after `MATCHMAKING_TIMEOUT`, the room is cancelled (`room_timeout`, status
  `cancelled`) instead of starting a 4-seat plan with two players.
- `POST /api/rooms/{id}/join` now seats players in the first free slot, so a 4-player REST
  room can actually be completed (previously only slot 2 was writable).

## #11 — two-player track offsets

- New `app/services/board_layout.py` holds one fixed offset per corner
  (red 20, blue 30, green 0, yellow 10) and `track_offsets(player_count)`.
- Two players use facing corners (seat 0 -> index 20, seat 1 -> index 0), so they start
  exactly 20 cells apart instead of 10.
- `_handle_captures` uses those offsets; the resolved per-seat values ship in `sync_state`
  as `track_offsets`, so the client never re-implements the seat plan.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` section 5 now matches the implementation.

## #13 — stale dice on turn rotation

- `_rotate_turn` sets `dice = None` and `dice_rolled = False`, while `last_roll` is kept for
  the client's roll animation and history.

## Tests

- New `test/test_board_layout.py`, `test/test_turn_and_dice.py`, `test/test_room_lifecycle.py`.
- Room and WebSocket tests now drive the real service layer over an in-memory Redis fake
  (`test/conftest.py`) instead of mocking `GameService`, so the bootstrap path is covered and
  the suite no longer depends on a live Redis.
- `pytest -q` -> **52 passed**. `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx vite build` unchanged (no
  front-end files touched).

## Notes

- The engine keeps working for any roster size, but the room layer now guarantees a full
  roster, so the `player_count=4` with 1/2/3 joined cases are covered at the engine level.
- Offsets sent over the wire are additive; older clients that ignore `track_offsets` keep
  working (they just keep their current mapping until the board PR lands).

Closes #10
Closes #11
Closes #13

## Registry rows
- FIX 4453 (owner ruling 10-19: an agent's free time), PR2a of 2: the engine cycle. PR1 (#3177) landed the labels. PR2b follows with the 4 owner verbs/routes, the usage label on spend records and the cycle spend filter.

## What now works, and where
- **An owner-set free-time policy per agent.** New `crates/oneiron/src/dreamer_runner/free_time/policy.rs`:
  - fields: total budget per cycle, a daily local time in an IANA zone, and an optional pinned split;
  - a revision check, so a write is refused unless it names the revision the owner's surface showed;
  - Vault read/set/clear, with the owner revalidated inside the write;
  - `FREE_TIME_WHEN_UNSET = Disabled`: no cycle until the owner sets one.
- **The cycle** (`free_time/cycle.rs`):
  - It opens once per owner-set boundary, on the home node only, from the existing Timer + Macro pass (`dreamer_wake/driver.rs`), with its due time merged into the timer's Macro deadline (`oneiron-driver tick/timer.rs`).
  - Its root spend scope opens under the cap the owner set, through the existing spend lease (`agent_dispatch/spend_lease.rs`: a keyed guard-delta and root close, with no second spend store). A pinned split carves each item.
  - Missed days collapse into one cycle. The cycle ends at its next boundary or when the policy is cleared.
- **Two items per cycle** (`free_time/items.rs`; new `dreamer_consolidation/resident_for_human.rs`; host `ai_host/dreamer/free_time.rs`):
  - **for_human**: a proposal-only resident run (`CallPurpose::AutonomyForHuman`) that lands its suggestion as a Proposed claim.
  - **own_time**: the resident's reflection (`resident_dream.rs` takes the cycle and writes its receipt in the landing commit), or a Rested choice with zero spend.
  - Each runs on the resident's own served model or the weaver's ladder, on an attributed run, with its guard capped at what the scope has left.
- **Receipts and the floor** (`free_time/receipt.rs`):
  - an engine-stamped terminal receipt per item: Completed, Rested, Failed or Cancelled, with its spend;
  - the pure `free_time_floor`: complete && for_human && own_time, and Unknown when a receipt row does not read;
  - the agent's short note on the cycle (`FreeTimeCycle.owner_note`, from the for_human reply block, secret-masked). The diary stays private. Nothing scores, limits or nudges own time.
- **Nightly reflection is kept** (`dreamer_wake/recipe_wake.rs`). The nightly enqueue skips a resident only when it has a policy and its clock has passed a first boundary; its reflection is then the cycle's own_time item. Every resident without a policy dreams nightly exactly as before, and clearing a policy brings the nightly reflection back.
- **New families**, Named, in `side_table/decls/vault_meta_d_e.rs` + `restore_class/vault_meta_d_l.rs`: policy and clock are LIVE; cycle (Authored), item and receipt are CONTENT.
- **Egress:** for_human is a new AutonomyForHuman call, gated as extraction. No existing call moves into a gated label.

## Seams (Engine-approved 10-19 14:2x)
- L06 Y4: `llm/run_admission/admission.rs` (an immutable optional `RunAttribution` on RunInner, `with_attribution`, `attribution()`) and its `mod.rs` export.
- L06 X2: `oneiron-server models/mod.rs` `ModelRuntime::attributed_run`.
- L09 Q3/Q4: `agent_dispatch/spend_lease.rs` `record_guard_spend_in_txn`, `close_root_spend_scope_in_txn`.
- L14 L/L2: `oneiron-driver tick/timer.rs`. The due boundary is a Macro deadline under the digest home; for_human is classed Macro.
- Shared declarations: `side_table/decls/vault_meta_d_e.rs`, `restore_class/vault_meta_d_l.rs`.

`cargo check --locked --workspace --all-features` on head 79303437453e (signed merge of origin/main): `## CHECK rc=0 head=79303437453e`, fleet job 1020-003440-b4f2 on gce-grad, 13m53s, 0 errors.

files: scripts/rotate-overlays-prove.mjs, src/components/game/Chat.tsx

Closes #861

## Root Cause Analysis
Investigation identified two distinct mechanisms causing `rotate-overlays-prove` to intermittently fail with `Timeout 120000ms exceeded waiting for chat-sheet to be visible`:

1. **Opener Precondition & Click Drop**:
   - Following viewport rotation or fixture updates, React re-renders `ChatControls`. Clicking without waiting for button layout settling and visibility led to dropped click events or element detachment during the click action.
   - **Fix**: Implemented `openChat(p)` in `scripts/rotate-overlays-prove.mjs`, which awaits opener visibility, verifies computed bounding box stability (`width >= 40 && height >= 40`), confirms `visibility !== "hidden"` and `!disabled`, allows two `requestAnimationFrame` cycles for React commit, and retries the click once if `chat-sheet` does not mount within 2 seconds.
   - Also ensured CDP safe-area insets are applied prior to `setViewportSize` to eliminate transient notch crunching, and waited for post-rotation `--active-offer-height` measurements to sync with the DOM before geometric assertions run.

2. **Resize-Driven Unmount on Orientation Changes (`Chat.tsx`)**:
   - In `src/components/game/Chat.tsx`, a `ResizeObserver` monitors sheet height and auto-minimizes chat if `height < 128` px after a 500ms debounce.
   - During rotation from portrait (360×640) to landscape (640×360), before the trade toast finishes its re-measurement in landscape, the CSS variable `--chat-sheet-height` temporarily computed to ~113px (< 128px). Under CPU contention or frame delay, the 500ms debounce timer expired before the landscape layout settled (to ~189px), unmounting the active chat session.
   - Per `docs/research/visual-audit.md`: *"A sheet that stays below 128 px for 500 ms minimizes while preserving its draft. Transient rotation heights do not close it."*
   - **Fix**: Added a `window.addEventListener("resize")` listener in `Chat.tsx` tracking `lastWindowResize` and increased the debounce to 1000ms. If `Date.now() - lastWindowResize < 1000`, transient reflow frames from orientation changes are ignored, while genuine persistent tiny viewports remain safely protected.

body:
AR now keeps the camera behind a compact AR/compass header, up to three directional labels and an expandable nearby panel. Selecting a label or list row opens the same place; Details and Map retain the cached summary, and Directions creates one single-use intent for the existing fresh-GPS walking preview. Rapid double taps cannot create duplicate intents.

The screen retains sensor freshness/quality gates, explicit paid Places actions, camera-denied and heading/GPS list fallbacks, translated recovery, and provider credits outside the moving sheet. Badges reserve measured header/sheet space and clip against the animated sheet position. No dependencies, provider fields, server contracts, native configuration or AR engine changed.

Validation:
- `npm run check`: typecheck, zero-warning lint, 346 tests across 36 files.
- Targeted AR: 62 tests across 5 files; real HeroUI, production query defaults and locale resources, native/network boundaries mocked.
- `npm run check:android`, `npm run export:android -- --max-workers 2`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- New tests cover header/compass fallback, bounded CJK badges, panel expansion and resize, pinned credits, localized camera failure/retry, double presses, single-use route handoff and no duplicate calls across lifecycle/remount.

Android device/UAT is pending: no `adb`, APK installation, native render screenshot or physical sensor/live-provider test was available. The supplied Stitch image was used as a visual reference; no rendered screenshot or outdoor accuracy claim is made. There are no reticles, object-recognition claims, shutter/zoom controls, fabricated place data or invented walking times.

See [design notes](docs/design/clean-explorer/AR_CAMERA.md) and [validation evidence](docs/validation.md) for component boundaries, intentional reference differences and device acceptance cases. This PR targets `main` and must remain unmerged until explicitly requested.

Independent review findings were addressed with two RED→GREEN regressions for delayed native sheet readiness and expanded-state restoration after a one-detent viewport. The installed SDK reactive-index hook is exercised by the native test driver. Final full checks and Android export were rerun after the fixes.

author: henalecam
body:
Rodada agendada do loop de melhorias. Base: `main` (0144cc4). Não conflita com o #26 (loop-10), que mexe em busca, impressão e páginas de serviço. **Não será mesclado sem pedido do Henrique.**

Não mexi em: modelo 3D do hero, depoimentos, CNPJ, links de demonstração, preços, nomes e logos de clientes.

## O que mudou

### 1. fix(cases): altura real das capturas do Scheduly e do Diconta
Esse problema estava anotado nas observações do backlog. Em `content.ts`, a captura do Scheduly constava com 900 px de altura, mas tem 2326 px. Por isso o card dele em /casos não rolava a página no hover, e a janela "Ver a página inteira" reservava um espaço de 1440×900 para uma imagem de 1440×2326. O Diconta constava com 2700 px e tem 2132. Agora o card do Scheduly rola no hover como os outros (confira na captura abaixo).

### 2. perf(cases): celular recebe a captura já recortada nos cards
Os cards de /casos mostram só o topo da página. A captura inteira só serve para a rolagem no hover, e o celular não tem hover. Agora o card usa um `<picture>` (`getImageProps` do Next):
- com `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`, recebe a captura inteira, como antes;
- nos outros casos, recebe `*-top.jpg`, o recorte de 1440×846 criado no ciclo 15.

Os cards deslizáveis da seção Casos da home no celular nunca rolam a captura, então sempre usam o recorte.

| Capturas de casos baixadas (390 px, DPR 3, rolando a página toda) | antes | depois |
|---|---|---|
| `/casos` | 322 KB | **134 KB** |
| `/` (home) | 282 KB | **145 KB** |
| `/casos` e `/` a 1440 px | 150 / 72 KB | 150 / 72 KB (igual) |

A imagem de LCP de /casos no celular passou a ser `diconta-top.jpg`: 60,0 KB → 25,9 KB a 1080w. O alerta "image delivery" do Lighthouse em /casos deixou de aparecer. A nota de performance simulada ficou na faixa do ruído (86 → 84): ela oscila com o cache do otimizador de imagens local.

### 3. chore(cases): aviso em dev quando a altura declarada não bate com o arquivo
Em `npm run dev`, /casos lê a altura real de cada JPEG (marcador SOF, sem dependência nova) e avisa se `shot.height` não bate com ela. Testei com 900 no Scheduly e apareceu o aviso `content.ts: scheduly shot.height is 900, the capture is 2326 px tall`. Isso não roda em produção.

## Como verifiquei
- `npm run lint` e `npm run build` passaram.
- Bytes de imagem medidos com Playwright + CDP (`Network.loadingFinished`), antes e depois, na mesma máquina.
- Capturas a 390 px (com e sem `prefers-reduced-motion`) e a 1440 px, incluindo o hover do Scheduly rolando até o rodapé. A 1440 px, o `currentSrc` continua sendo `scheduly.jpg` inteiro.
- axe (WCAG 2.2 AA) em /casos a 390 e 1440 px: 0 violações. Sem erros no console.

## Observações para o dono
- O fade/zoom dos cards do celular mudou de leve: o recorte tem proporção 1,70 e o card 1,60, então as laterais perdem cerca de 3% de cada lado. Nas capturas não deu para notar diferença.
- Continua pendente a decisão sobre os logos de clientes: o brasão do PR (146×176) aparece a 46×55 px e é o único alerta de entrega de imagem da home.

## Backlog atualizado
Atualizado no Project "Henaweb" (`claude/backlog-melhorias.md`), rodada 11.

author: kausiala
body:
## Summary

- **Bearer tokens are stored hashed.** `access_token.token` (the plaintext, primary key) is replaced by `token_hash`, the SHA-256 hex digest of the token (primary key, so indexed). A new `HashedDatabaseStrategy` / `HashedAccessTokenDatabase` (`api/new/auth/strategies/database.py`) mints the token, stores its digest and returns the token once; every lookup hashes the presented value and compares digests with `hmac.compare_digest`. `hash_access_token` lives beside the model in `db/models.py`. Plain SHA-256 rather than a keyed hash, as the brief allows and as recovery codes already do: the token is a 256-bit server-generated secret.
- **Migration `a7d3c91e5b26`** hashes the stored tokens in place (`encode(sha256(convert_to(token, 'UTF8')), 'hex')`), so every token already issued keeps working, then drops the plaintext column. Its downgrade deletes every row, because a digest gives no token back.
- **Default lifetime 90 days** (was 360), per MAS-201. Device-bound agent tokens keep their 30-day lifetime and renewal.
- **The file-converter token is minted per request** (MAS-201, option A). The server used to read the token back out of the row and give it to the converter on every upload, which hashing makes impossible. `get_access_token` now mints one for each upload or peak request (a bulk upload shares one across its files), valid for 30 days (`FILE_CONVERTER_TOKEN_LIFETIME_SECONDS`, enforced in the strategy on both the bearer and the socket path via `AccessTokenConfig.lifetime_for`). Each mint first reaps that user's converter tokens past that age. `ensure_access_token`'s keep-and-renew logic is gone, and so are the pre-mints at sign-in, on promotion to editor, on a password change and at pairing, because a token minted there could never reach an upload. A demotion and a password change still revoke the user's converter tokens. `get_access_token` now refuses any other service, since the server holds no token it could hand out.
- `remove_access_tokens` deletes rows directly. A database-token logout only ever deleted the row, and it needs the plaintext.
- Docs: the SDK getting-started page gets a "When your token expires" section (90 days, how to rotate), the settings pane's help text says the same, and `docs/maintaining.md` no longer says a password change reissues the converter token. Changelog fragment under Security.

## Why

MAS-75 / #1719: the CDN IP allowlist comes off per site in milestone 2. Before then, a leaked database dump should hand out no working credential, and a leaked token should stay useful for a bounded time. The lifetime and the converter design are the owner's answers in MAS-201.

## Verification

- `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 uv run pytest server/backend/tests -q`: 5986 passed, 7 skipped (before the final rebase). After the rebase: migrations, auth, pairing and unit/auth suites, 747 passed.
- New seeded migration test `tests/migrations/test_hash_access_tokens.py`. It seeds tokens in clear at the previous revision and upgrades. Each row must then be found by `hash_access_token(<token>)`, with owner, service and `created_at` unchanged, and no column may hold the token. The downgrade restores the column and leaves no rows. This covers the Verify line "a token issued before the migration still authenticates after it" and "the stored row holds no plaintext".
- `test_converter_token_on_upload.py` (rewritten) checks:
  - each upload gets its own token, stored as a digest, and the token authenticates on HTTP and socket;
  - a mint reaps only tokens past 30 days;
  - a converter token is refused at 31 days (HTTP 401, socket `InvalidTokenException`) while an SDK token of the same age still works;
  - an SDK token works at 89 days and gets the usual 401 at 91. This is the Verify line "an expired token answers 401 with the existing refusal shape";
  - other services are refused;
  - a guest is refused.
- New `test_converter_token_on_account_changes.py` checks that a promotion mints nothing, a demotion revokes, a password change revokes and mints nothing, and the demo seeder stores digests. `test_pairing.py` now checks that a paired machine account holds only its device token. `test_login_flow.py` checks that a sign-in mints no converter token and leaves held ones alone.
- Mutation check: each behavioural line was reverted one at a time in a scratch worktree and the covering tests rerun. Killed:
  - the digest in the context lookup, the adapter, `write_token` and both labelling UPDATEs;
  - the per-service age check, `lifetime_for`, and the 90-day constant;
  - the reap and its age argument;
  - the other-service and guest refusals;
  - the row delete in `remove_access_tokens`;
  - a re-added mint at sign-in, promotion, password change and pairing;
  - the demotion revoke, the seeder's digest, and the device-renewal keep list.

  **Survives:** removing the `compare_digest` re-check, because the indexed equality has already matched the digest, so no test can tell them apart. It is there for the brief's "compares in constant time". The adapter's `max_age` filter is kept for the fastapi-users interface, but our strategy no longer passes it.
- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .`, `uv run python tooling/changelog.py check`, `uv run mkdocs build --strict`: clean.

## Not verified

- The backend suite ran on the agent host's dev stack, not on the LAN agent host the brief names.
- The security suite's token controls against staging: not run (no access from here).
- Not run end to end with a real file converter. Converter uploads in flight across the upgrade keep working if their pre-migration token is under 30 days old. An older token is refused when the converter writes back, as is any SDK token older than 90 days; the changelog says so.
- Frontend: only the help-text string changed; no unit tests run for it.

## Follow-ups

- The demo seeder still writes a fixed file-converter token that nothing uses now. It is harmless, and it lapses after 30 days unless the demo restarts.
- Design notes under `docs/dev/` (`ai_layer.md`, `mfa_totp_plan.md`, `device_identity_plan.md`) still say "360-day". They are historical records and were left alone.

Fixes MAS-75

author: chinmayyk
body:
Found with a soak test between the real Mac daemon and the Linux daemon.

**Bug.** The desktop daemon (Mac, Windows, Linux) loaded its own clipboard history from the same `history.json` that the engine keeps, and both saved on every clip. Each save replaced the file with that copy's list.
- A clip copied on this computer was recorded only by the daemon's copy. It vanished from disk as soon as a clip arrived from another device, because that one was recorded and saved by the engine's copy.
- Reproduced on the Linux daemon: copy locally, receive a clip from the Mac, restart, and the local clip is gone.
- The two copies also shared one temp file, and under bursts they failed each other's saves with `renaming history file: No such file or directory`.

**Fix.** The daemon now uses `Engine::history_store()`, so each process has one history store. History already ignores an immediate repeat of the same item, so the engine and the daemon both recording a received clip still makes one entry.

**Side effect.** The history limit in Settings (default 50) now also applies to what's kept on disk. The engine's copy used to keep up to 500 there, although the apps only ever showed the limit.

**Checks**
- On the Linux daemon after the fix: the local clip survives a received one and a restart. 100 clips in a burst caused no failed saves.
- New test `history_store_test`.
- All `linkall-core` tests pass, and clippy is clean.

author: javilianes8
body:
Release 1.0.0: the public API of 0.2.0 is declared stable.

API changes (all listed in CHANGELOG.md and GUIDE.md):
- `parse(None)` gives empty `Preferences`.
- `Preferences.get` and `Preferences.applied` raise `TypeError` for a name that is not a `str`.
- Error messages quote at most 40 characters of the input; `TypeError` messages name the type.
- Public classes report `preferhdr` as their module; pickles name no private module (0.2.0 pickles still load).
- The command exits 1 without a traceback when its output pipe closes and cuts huge usage errors.

Tests added: grammar compiled from the fetched RFC 9110 text and erratum 4439, IANA registry, RFC 8144 examples and errata statuses, the standard library and parse-prefer-header 1.0.0 as oracles, PyPI 0.2.0 as an oracle, seeded fuzzing, linear-time and bounded-message checks, pinned signatures, and an e2e test that upgrades the PyPI release in place.

Docs: GUIDE.md, README badge, rationale versus existing tools, absolute links. Packaging: version 1.0.0, Production/Stable.

Details and results: CERT-1.0-REPORT.md.

author: jleybourne
body:
> Builds on #155 (v3 fix pack), so GitHub also lists those commits here. Only the last commit is new:
> - `758d082` feat(mods): check and apply plugin updates (#146)
>
> To review just this change: https://github.com/jleybourne/discopanel/compare/v3-fixes...feat/146-plugin-updates

Closes #146

There was no way to see whether installed plugins or mods had newer
builds, or to update them, short of downloading each jar by hand.

The Mods/Plugins tab gets a "Check for updates" action. Every jar in the
mods/plugins folder (and its _disabled twin) is identified exactly by
file hash, never by file name:

- Modrinth: POST /v2/version_files by sha512, then
  /v2/version_files/update with the server's loaders, Minecraft version
  and release channel (release, optionally beta). Paper-family servers
  map to paper/spigot/bukkit (purpur first on Purpur, folia only on
  Folia); mod loaders reuse the existing dialect facets. A version that
  ships several jars is only used when exactly one reads like the
  installed file.
- CurseForge: the murmur2 fingerprint only shortlists; a jar counts as
  identified when file length and CurseForge's sha1 match too, and a
  print shared by several files is ignored. Newer files are listed for
  the server's version and their loader tags checked locally (Quilt
  takes Fabric builds, NeoForge takes Forge builds). Used only with an
  API key or through the index, as for the existing name sweep.

Results are rechecked locally (loader, game version, channel, listed)
and never offer a build older than the installed one. Jars no source
knows are reported as unknown source. Verdicts are cached for ten
minutes and file digests per path/size/mtime, both in bounded caches;
lookups go through the shared indexer client, so pacing, retries and
the configured User-Agent apply.

The server data dir is mounted into the game container, so plugin code
controls everything in it. The update path is built around that:

- Jar folders are opened as os.Root after an lstat; a plugins or mods
  folder that is a link is refused, and nothing is opened, renamed or
  removed through a path that could leave the folder. Jars are read
  from an fd and must be regular files, links are never hashed.
- Backups and their index live in panel storage,
  {data_dir}/mod-updates/<server id>/<folder>/, outside the server dir
  and removed with the server. Rollback reads only from there.
- The new jar is written through an O_EXCL part file handle in the
  target folder (hidden, non jar name), mode 0644, chowned to the
  folder owner when the panel runs as root, synced and renamed into
  place. The old jar is copied from its fd into the backup store first,
  so the folder never lacks a working copy. Nothing else is written
  under the data dir.
- Downloads go only to cdn.modrinth.com, edge.forgecdn.net,
  mediafilez.forgecdn.net or the configured index host, over https,
  with same-host redirects only, a size cap from the published size
  (256 MB without one), and the published checksum checked twice. A
  failed check never reports the digest of what arrived.
- ApplyModUpdates rechecks on the server (clients never pass urls or
  file names), takes at most 256 distinct ids (repeats would overwrite
  the real backup), and accepts only plain .jar names that clash with
  no other entry (the plain file name check moves to pkg/files).

Jars a modpack or the Modrinth projects setting reinstalls are shown but
not updated, and modpack servers get a warning that pack installs may
replace updated jars. A stored enable/disable choice follows the file,
one backup generation per file allows RollbackModUpdate, and running
servers pick the new jars up on restart, which the UI says.

New RPCs carry mods read (check) and mods update (apply, rollback)
permissions. A MOD_UPDATE activity kind records each change.

pluGET was suggested in the issue, but bundling it would add a Python
runtime to the image, a second licence and a separate tool to maintain,
and it would duplicate the Modrinth/CurseForge clients the panel already
has. Native hash lookups also avoid guessing projects from file names.
Hangar and SpigotMC are not consulted: Hangar's hash lookup could not
be verified and Spigot offers no file hash API.

author: ryancinsight
body:
Slice 1 of KW-NEURO-RESIDUALS (residual findings from the #958 judge rounds): items 1–3.

1. Expose `PowerLawDispersion::Omitted` in the GPU PSTD runner and the simulation PSTD dispatch.
2. Correct the causal-only y = 1 error text in absorption init and name its tolerance.
3. One spectral operator per kernel: uniform operators exist only when the exponent is uniform, built on the half spectrum; a near-uniform exponent resolves to the midpoint of its range for τ, η, the operators and thermal coupling alike.

Later slices on separate PRs: Rayleigh polar order check and tests (4, 5, 9), example split (7), `ElementShape::Rect` consolidation (6), benchmark smoke job (8).

**Judge rounds (head 2c9153b5f):**
- **Collapse rule.** A near-uniform field collapses to its midpoint only when `strata::collapses_to_uniform` admits it. Under causal dispersion this also requires `tan(πy/2)`, whose first-order change is π·d/|sin πy|, to stay within the operators' 1.125e-5 bound. A causal field straddling y = 1 therefore keeps each voxel's exponent instead of evaluating tan at its pole. The top stratum representative is the field maximum.
- **New tests.** `exponent_straddling_unity_collapses_only_without_dispersion`, `exponents_above_the_top_representative_are_reproduced`, and host-only kwavers-gpu tests in `runner/absorption.rs` showing that `Omitted` zeroes only η.
- **CI coverage.** CI runs no kwavers-gpu tests, a pre-existing gap filed as KW-GPU-HOST-TESTS-UNRUN (#962). These tests ran locally with `--features gpu` and in the pre-push gate.
- **Docs.** ADR 135 records the decision. The book's memory figures are corrected (≈4·N³, 538 MB).

**Merge hold:** the CI gate is red on `main` because of RUSTSEC-2026-0367/0368/0369 (KW-DEP-ZIP-ADVISORY, #962).

## What changed

- "Add a precinct": a repository whose `LAWMAN.md` passes lint is proposed at weight 1, and the row stays editable. A new draft always takes weight 0 until its pull request merges.
- After `config.yaml` is written, a weight above zero runs the resume steps of "Raise a weight". "Raise a weight" now offers the resume whenever an edit sets a weight above zero and a job is paused, so a declined offer comes back.
- The install summary names only the jobs still paused. README, `docs/constitution.md` and `references/explain.md` say the same.
- Version 0.16.5 and its CHANGELOG entry.

## Why

Weight 0 keeps a precinct whose constitution has not merged from wasting patrol slots. A constitution that already passes lint has nothing to wait for. With five such repositories, an install left every job paused until five runs of "raise a weight". The resume offer used to come only at the very first weight, so declining it once left the jobs paused with no way back.

## Verification

- `bun run check`: clean. `bun test`: 1068 pass, 0 fail.
- A walk of the install for five passing constitutions, for a draft plus a passing constitution in both orders, and for the menu job on an installation with a weight.

author: animusin
body:
## About The Pull Request

Adds persistent account PQ, RCP and Karma with signed `Respect = PQ + RCP / 4 + Karma`. Default Kindred access is Fledgling 10, Neonate 20, Ancilla 40 and Elder 60. Preference editing, job assignment, applied age and discipline budgets share the gates; existing over-age sheets are retained for correction. Garou use their existing Renown-derived rank ladder at Respect 10/20/30/40/50/60 for Cub/Cliath/Fostern/Adren/Athro/Elder. Renown and Auspice editing, job admission and applied startup rank enforce the same cap; older over-cap sheets can be lowered stepwise. Corax has no implemented rank ladder and remains unchanged.

**New player antagonist admissions require Respect 10** when used with [PR #6](https://github.com/Animusin/crimson-grid/pull/6): Sabbat crusade, stationary Tzimisce, Hunters and real antagonist datum grants all use the same server-side policy. The threshold is configurable independently of age gates. Already accepted living antagonists may finish their round after a score drop; a fresh admission must qualify again. The two PRs compile independently through an optional admission signal.

PQ follows Ratwood-2.0's commend bands and giver history: below 100, a new giver adds 1 and repeats add nothing; from 100, new/repeat givers add 0.5/0.05, with automatic praise capped at 500. RCP grants once per completed round after 45 active living minutes, weighted across transformations: humans 1, ghouls/kinfolk 0.5, other supernaturals 0. Admin adjustments retain separate audited scores. The existing JSON database now marks queued saves so destruction flushes pending awards.

A stable character ID locks the sheet after its first successful job spawn. Cosmetics stay free; stats, quirks and discipline allocation unlock for 3 Karma, other identity settings for 5, or another 2 after buying the stats permission. Payment and permission persist atomically; only a successful spawn consumes permission. The menu shows Respect and age access after spending. Taught discipline identities survive respec at zero dots within the ordinary allocation budget. Deleting a character is free and discards its learned knowledge; a replacement gets a new ID while account scores remain.

Kindred start on Humanity unless their actual initial job is Sabbat or their age is Elder. Current Paths and ratings persist per character. Learning another Path requires mutually accepted lessons in three distinct rounds with the same teacher and actual degeneration of the original Path to zero. A brief initiation frenzy leads to 1–3 dots in the teacher's Path, determined by a saved teaching roll and limited by the teacher's rating. Interrupted attempts retain lessons and the roll. Preview stat objects cannot overwrite the live persistent Path. Path changes, lessons, initiation and taught discipline identities honor the existing canonical-round, original-slot/GUID and original-body save rules; noncanonical lessons explain why no permanent progress can be recorded. Actual in-round Embrace now initializes Path persistence under the existing character ID; teacher lookup safely skips lobby players and observers.

Default player-kill Karma is −1 per attributed death. Explicitly bound summons charge their owner; owned NPC victims remain NPCs. Matching murder objectives waive the penalty using death-time target snapshots and atomic finite quotas. A minion's own explicit orders authorize only that minion's attacks. Non-target kills and arbitrary objective text retain the penalty.

Positive Karma uses bounded account ledgers:

| Source | Default | Limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Locally witnessed say-log/custom emote text | +0.1 per 1500 distinct characters | Five-minute interval, ten awards per round |
| Medical packs | +0.1 per 20 real damage restored | Once per patient per round |
| Successful restorative surgery | +0.1 / (1 + prior pair awards) | Persistent one-hour surgeon/patient cooldown |
| Business defense, with [PR #1](https://github.com/Animusin/crimson-grid/pull/1) | +1 | Once per point/opposing faction, two awards per round |

Medical packs and surgery share ten medical awards per account per round. Failed, harmful and ineffective operations earn nothing.

## Why It's Good For The Game

Connects peer feedback, mortal participation and useful activity to vampire progression while preserving each component for review and tuning. Character knowledge survives paid edits, and degeneration cannot be erased by reopening preferences.

[DECISIONS.md](https://github.com/Animusin/crimson-grid/blob/feature/player-quality/modular_vcg/modules/player_quality/DECISIONS.md) distinguishes user decisions, configurable defaults and remaining design questions. [EVENT_AUDIT.md](https://github.com/Animusin/crimson-grid/blob/feature/player-quality/modular_vcg/modules/player_quality/EVENT_AUDIT.md) records covered summon bindings, objective families and surgeries. Positive objective-completion rewards, sin-table changes, Humanity growth and in-round werewolf progression remain outside this PR. Poison, traps and other uninstrumented indirect deaths may remain unattributed; collusion is bounded rather than fully detected.

## Validation

BYOND 516.1666 normal build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. All 28 focused progression groups pass, including canonical/original-body save boundaries, a real spawn/mind/slot/possession lifecycle, optional antagonist admission at negative/zero/fractional/exact-threshold Respect, trusted account identity, disabled policy and unknown accounts. Existing score, surgery, summon/objective, Garou rank, JSON persistence, respec and Path regressions remain covered. All 95 combined focused engine groups pass on Westfield with the other five PRs, without runtime exceptions. Production TGUI, TypeScript, includes and 3096 define checks pass.

The learned-discipline lifecycle fixture explicitly uses Brujah and its native starting allocation: a randomized True Brujah could naturally own Temporis and falsely fail the zero-dot taught-choice assertion. This correction changes test setup only.

## Changelog

:cl:
add: Require Respect 10 for new player antagonist admissions with the round-style system.
add: Persistent PQ, RCP, Karma and weighted Respect with Kindred access at 10/20/40/60 and Garou ranks at 10/20/30/40/50/60.
add: Character identity locks, paid respecs, free cosmetic edits and persistent taught knowledge.
add: Persistent Paths and consent-based three-night initiation after degeneration.
add: Summon-owner kill attribution, explicit objective-target exceptions and restorative surgery rewards.
admin: View and adjust account scores with required reasons and audit logs.
/:cl:

author: lakerfan901
body:
Refs #95 (closed by #93); UI now reads the server valuation fields.

## Summary

- **Server figures only.** The register, asset detail, `/fleet` and the GPU SPV lead page read `basis`, `capitalized_costs`, `accumulated_book`, `nbv_book`, `accumulated_tax`, `nbv_tax`, `valuation_as_of` and `capex_events` from `GET /api/fleet/assets` and `/[id]`.
- **As-of on every fetch.** Every request sends `?as_of`. It is the user's local date by default (the route's own default is the UTC date). The register and the asset page have an **As of** date control; it only sends a complete, real date, because the route 400s on anything else. `valuation_as_of` is shown beside the figures.
- **No depreciation in the UI.** `components/gpu/fleet-math.ts` no longer imports `lib/gpu/depreciation`. What remains: `fleetTotals`, which adds up the server fields, plus the row-action and gate helpers. `assetFigures`, `assetSchedule` and the "booked = purchase_entry_id" NBV path are gone.
- **Tax book.** The register has a second column pair, "Tax book" (accumulated, NBV), with totals. The asset page's **Book and tax** card shows both rows and names the tax method (Q7).
- **Asset page.** The month-by-month schedule table is gone. In its place: the server's book and tax figures, and a **Capitalized costs** table of `capex_events` (month, amount, source ref, posted).
- **Planned and unbooked (agreed with the lead).** `valueAssets` reports a planned or unbooked asset at its full basis with nothing depreciated. An asset with status `planned`, or one whose purchase entry is not linked, is therefore kept out of the book and tax totals, and its basis is shown in the Planned column, captioned Planned or Unbooked. The lead is raising with gpu-P1 whether the route should report 0 for unbooked assets. If it does, the `purchase_entry_id` half of this rule can go.
- **#94 review lows:**
  - (a) Capex key per dialog mount. The real `CapexDialog` makes two distinct crypto keys across two openings and none while closed. Within one opening the key survives re-renders, and a retry after a 409 reuses it. I mutation-checked this: a per-render key fails the re-render test.
  - (b) Event times are validated before `localToUtc`, which throws a RangeError on a bad value. An invalid From or To is now a form message before the form goes busy, and busy is cleared in a `finally`.

## Tests

`tests/gpu-fleet-ui.test.tsx` has 59 tests:
- Register cells and totals come from fixture valuation fields that are deliberately not derivable from the row.
- The Tax book heading and `valuation_as_of` render.
- Disposed, planned and unbooked assets are kept out of the totals.
- `as_of` is in the path for the register, one asset and a named vehicle, and a 400 comes back verbatim.
- The asset page's Book and tax card and the capex events table render.
- The two guards above.

The client 5,025 / 6,150 / 8,400 and month-60 schedule assertions are removed; they belong to `lib/gpu/depreciation.test.ts`.

Checks:
- `npx vitest run`: 575 files, 5961 tests, all pass.
- `npm run lint`: 0 errors and 219 warnings, the same count as main.
- `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` pass.
- `git diff --check` is clean.

## Browser QA
1. On a GPU SPV with assets, open Fleet. Book NBV and Tax book NBV match the route's figures. A planned asset shows only under Planned.
2. Change **As of** to an earlier date. The figures and the "Valued as of" line change.
3. Open an asset. Check the Book and tax card and the Capitalized costs list (capitalize a cost and it appears with its source ref).
4. Record an event with an impossible time, for example by editing the field value. A message shows and the form is not left busy.

> Changes how fleet NBV and tax figures are displayed and totaled across register, overview, and lead pages; incorrect off-books or as-of handling could misstate balances, though logic is server-sourced and heavily tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> GPU fleet UI now shows **book and tax figures from the ledger** via `GET /api/fleet/assets` with **`?as_of`** (user local date by default), instead of client-side depreciation in `fleet-math`.
> 
> **Register, `/fleet`, and GPU SPV lead** aggregate server fields (`basis`, `nbv_book`, `nbv_tax`, etc.), add **Tax book** columns, and treat **planned / unlinked-purchase** assets as off-books (basis in Planned, excluded from book/tax totals). **As of** date controls on register and asset detail only commit valid dates.

author: flamurmaliqi
body:
## Summary

Linear: [VAY-2272](https://linear.app/vayadacom/issue/VAY-2272) (Marketplace removal step 5, parent VAY-2259). Platform step P3, decision 6 of the approved step-5 plan. It is a separate PR from the CloudFront permission (#587) because it changes retention for **every app**.

`vayada-media-production` is versioned, and today only `staging/` expires old versions. So when the media cleanup or the VAY-2272 purge deletes a photo or PMS attachment, the file stays in the bucket as an old version forever. This PR adds two lifecycle rules:

- under `public/` and `private/`, old (noncurrent) versions expire 30 days after they stop being current;
- the delete markers they leave behind are removed too (`expired_object_delete_marker`);
- current objects never expire. The staging rule is unchanged.

Effect for every app: a replaced or deleted hotel image, room photo, PMS attachment or creator file can be restored from S3 for 30 days, then it is gone. Flamur approved this knowing it applies to all apps.

It also adds `scripts/test-media-version-retention.mjs` (run by Terraform Validate), which pins the three rules, and documents the retention in `docs/environments.md`.

## Validation

- `node --test scripts/test-media-version-retention.mjs`: 3/3 pass (2 of the 3 fail without the new rules)
- `terraform fmt -check infra/media.tf`: clean
- Terraform Plan on this PR: the resource list and the `Plan:` line are reported to the coordinator from the job log (expected: one in-place update of `aws_s3_bucket_lifecycle_configuration.private_profile_media`).

## Risk

- S3 applies lifecycle rules asynchronously. The first run after apply removes every old version that is already more than 30 days noncurrent, so any deletion older than 30 days can no longer be undone from S3.
- Rollback: revert. Versions S3 has already expired cannot be brought back.

author: lukas-dev-client-agent[bot]
body:
Implements part of the OpenSpec change **`metadata-lookup`** (tasks 1.4, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3). The change stays open: 2.4 (refresh job through tagging, protected fields create conflicts) waits for `tag-editing`.

## What
- **Licenses (1.4):** MusicBrainz Server GPL-2.0-or-later (separate deployment, HTTP API only); `musicbrainz-docker` declares no license (linked only, nothing copied); core data CC0, supplementary data and Live Data Feed CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, token free for non-commercial use. Recorded in `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md` and `docs/architecture/musicbrainz-mirror.md`.
- **Lookup clients (2.1)** in `server/anthology/metadata_lookup/`: MusicBrainz (release, recording, ISRC, disc ID, search), Cover Art Archive, AcoustID.
  - Persistent cache (`lookup_cache`, migration 0008): entities 30 days, searches 7 days, not found 1 day.
  - Rate limits 1/s (MusicBrainz, CAA) and 3/s (AcoustID) **across server processes**: slots are reserved in `lookup_schedule` with a compare-and-swap update (works on PostgreSQL and SQLite).
  - Interactive lookups before background ones; 429/503 back off (Retry-After or 2 s doubling up to 60 s) and retry instead of failing; User-Agent with version and contact.
- **Mirror (2.2):** `ANTHOLOGY_MUSICBRAINZ_URL` – no rate limit, health check every minute (`musicbrainz-mirror` in the `services` stream), per-request fallback when it is down or cannot answer (e.g. text search without indexes).
- **Estimate (2.3):** `GET /api/v1/metadata-lookup/status` (admins): queued requests, estimated duration, mirror status, recommendation above 24 hours; domains report backlogs via `register_backlog`.
- Settings in compose/Quadlet, `docs/install.md`, `server/AGENTS.md`; `packages/api-types` regenerated.

## Design notes
- The token bucket of the design became a database slot schedule, because an in-memory limiter would multiply the rate with several server processes (`design.md` updated).
- A message broker (RabbitMQ) was considered and rejected for now; reasons in `design.md`.

## Non-functional requirements
None affected; lookups never block the UI.

## Local results
- Server: SQLite 241 passed, PostgreSQL 249 passed; ruff clean.
- Client: lint clean, 83 tests passed. `openspec validate --all --strict` OK.
- Known pre-existing flake on SQLite (`clean_db` "database is locked", also on `main`) – fixed separately.

author: joheras
body:
## Summary

Adds everything needed to run the ophthalmology benchmark on a second, public dataset: [PALM](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.c.6224616.v1) (pathologic myopia, Fang et al., *Sci. Data* 2024). Reviewers will ask for a second dataset and an unbiased model selection, and this PR covers both.

- **`benchmarks/palm/prepare_palm.py`**: reads the PALM release (Figshare with `Classification Labels.xlsx`, or the 2019 challenge with `P*/N*/H*` names) and writes it in the MVTec layout:
  - `palm-val`: validation set, used to choose the configuration
  - `palm-test`: test set, used to report the chosen configuration
  - `palm-lesion` (optional, `--lesion-masks`): PM test images with lesion masks, for pixel-level metrics
  - Every category fits on the 187 non-PM training images. Other options: `--crop-fov` for the field-of-view ablation (images and masks cropped the same way), `--copy` (symlinks by default), and a `manifest.csv` with device and centring.
- **`configs/palm_benchmark.yaml`**: the same grid as the myopia benchmark (15 extractors, 2 preprocessings, 12 detectors, 19 Anomalib models), plus myopia-specific text prompts in two modes: text-only (true zero-shot) and text + 1-NN. It also has commented-out runs at 448–512 px for the Anomalib resolution ablation.
- **`benchmarks/palm/select_on_validation.py`**: chooses the configuration on `palm-val`, reports its AUROC on `palm-test` next to the oracle, adds a per-family selection, and gives the Spearman correlation between validation and test.
- **`benchmarks/palm/README.md`**: the steps.

## Testing

- Simulated PALM with the Figshare layout (400/400/400, Excel labels, inverted BMP masks): the preparation script gives the expected counts (187/189/211 and 187/187/213) and correct masks, and `--crop-fov` crops masks the same way as images. The 2019 naming is read from the filename prefixes.
- imgad (from `src/`) loads the three categories (140 masks in `palm-lesion`) and builds the 15 detectors in the YAML. A benchmark with the tests' model-free extractor ran 216 runs with no failures, and the selection script ran on its `results.csv`.
- Not yet run on the real PALM download.

author: agasattila-agent
body:
Fixes #22: on FreeBSD, and with every FUSE 2 build, a directory listing through the mount did not report the source's inode numbers. **Stacked** on #23, which re-enables the test for this and skips it on FreeBSD. See "Stack" at the end. Nothing has been opened, pushed or commented upstream.

## Commit

| Commit | |
|---|---|
| `69267ef` | **readdir: report the source's inode numbers without readdirplus** (#22) |

## Cause

`bindfs_readdir()` passed a `struct stat` to libfuse's `filler` only in readdirplus mode. Without one, libfuse's high-level API reports `FUSE_UNKNOWN_INO` (4294967295) as the inode number of every entry.

- **FreeBSD:** its fusefs has no readdirplus, so it always got that value.
- **FUSE 2:** the libfuse 2 high-level API never uses readdirplus, so FUSE 2 builds are affected on every platform. The test never ran there, first because of #13 and then because it was limited to FUSE 3.
- **`stat()`** was never affected, because `getattr` reports the source's inode numbers (`use_ino`).

Reproduced locally on Linux with a FUSE 2 build:

```
$ ./readdir_inode mnt
4294967295 .
4294967295 ..
4294967295 file
4294967295 dir
```

## Fix

Without readdirplus, bindfs now passes a `struct stat` holding the entry's `d_ino` and file type (`DTTOIF(d_type)`) from the source's `readdir()`. Those are the only two fields libfuse uses in that mode. With `--resolve-symlinks`, a symlink entry gets the stat of its target, which bindfs already computed but did not pass on.

**Side effect:** entries now carry their file type. On FUSE 2, `d_type` used to be `DT_UNKNOWN` (0) for every entry; it is now `DT_DIR` and `DT_REG` as on the source, checked locally.

**Test:** "preserves readdir inode numbers" is no longer limited to FUSE 3 or skipped on FreeBSD. It still skips libfuse 3 up to 3.10.1, which has the readdir bug the test already excluded.

## Validation

**Local** (Linux, non-root, built with `-Werror`): the full suite passes with FUSE 2 and FUSE 3. On FUSE 2 the readdir test now runs and passes; before the fix it would have seen 4294967295.

**CI** on `69267ef` (run 39297678340)

| Job | Result |
|---|---|
| Vagrant FreeBSD 14 | pass, the readdir test runs and passes as root and non-root |
| Linux build-and-test, 4 combinations, including FUSE 2 | pass, the test passes on all of them |
| macOS fuse-t, gcc and clang | pass, the test passes |
| Vagrant: Debian 12, Ubuntu 20.04/22.04/24.04, Rocky 9 | pass |
| Vagrant Debian 11 | fails while setting up the VM, as on `master` (#19, removed by #26) |
| Spelling check | pass |

## Stack

This PR sits on #23, next to #11. Neither depends on the other, and they merge without conflicts in either order (checked with `git merge-tree`).

| Order | PR | Branch | Based on |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | #24 | `fix/fuse-version-detection-in-tests` | `master` |
| 2 | #23 | `fix/renameat2-and-readdir-inode-test` | #24 |
| 3 | #11 | `feature/file-filter` | #23 |
| 3 | #28 | `fix/readdir-inode-numbers` | #23 |

It targets #23's branch, so it shows only its own commit. After #23 is merged into its integrate branch, retarget this PR to that integrate branch.

Not to be merged automatically. `fix/readdir-inode-numbers-integrate` (created from `master` `51d00ea`) is the candidate branch for a possible upstream submission after review.

author: thxzzzzz
body:
## ELI5

When Agent sleep puts an idle agent to sleep, a script can only bring it back by making Orca show that workspace, which yanks you away from whatever you were looking at. Orca can already wake sleeping agents quietly in the background, but only when a phone asks. This PR lets the CLI ask too: `orca worktree wake` wakes them without touching your screen, and `orca worktree sleep` is the matching Sleep action.

## What Changed

- **Before:** to give work to a slept agent from the CLI, you ran `orca file open … --focus` or `orca terminal switch`, and the desktop jumped to that workspace. There was no CLI for Sleep either, although a `worktree.sleep` RPC existed.
- **After:**
  - `orca worktree wake --worktree <selector> [--json]` resumes the workspace's slept agents in hidden panes. The desktop keeps showing what it showed. The result's `sleepingAgentWake` is `requested`, `not-applicable`, `unsupported-headless` (headless `orca serve` has no renderer holding the sleep records), or `not-delivered` (the desktop dropped the request, e.g. while reloading). `not-delivered` exits non-zero.
  - `orca worktree sleep --worktree <selector> [--json]` requests the workspace Sleep action. With a desktop window, the renderer performs it after the command returns.
- **Mechanism:**
  - The wake decision that mobile activation made inline is now a shared `requestSleepingAgentWake` on the runtime. It asks the host renderer to wake via `notifier.resumeSleepingAgents`, or reports `unsupported-headless` when there is no window and a background-wakeable record exists.
  - A new `worktree.wake` RPC (`permission: 'workspace'`, same `WorktreeSelector` params as `worktree.sleep`) calls it for any caller. It resolves the repo through host routing, so the headless check reads the sleeping records of the host the worktree runs on.
  - `resumeSleepingAgents` on the notifier returns the renderer send result. A dropped send becomes `not-delivered` for `worktree.wake`; mobile activation keeps reporting it as `requested`, because published phone clients know only the original three values.
  - The renderer side is unchanged. It is the same `wakeSleepingAgentsForWorktreeInBackground` path, which mounts slept panes hidden with `suppressNavigation: true`. As there, finished agents in a workspace the user explicitly slept (`restoreOnTabOpenOnly`) still resume only when their tab is opened (#11598). The help text and docs say so.
  - `worktree.sleep` moved next to `worktree.wake` in `worktree-sleep-wake-methods.ts`, which keeps `rpc/methods/worktree.ts` under the line limit.
  - Mobile activation behaves as before; it now calls the shared helper.

## Why

I drive agents in Orca workspaces from a chat bot. Each task gets a workspace, and follow-ups are sent with `orca terminal send`. Every follow-up to a slept agent stole my Orca window.

Alternatives I tried or considered:
- **`--focus` / `terminal switch`:** these work, but steal the user's view.
- **Close the slept tab and relaunch the agent:** close it with `terminal close --tab` (which drops its sleep record), then start `claude --resume <id>` with `terminal create`. This also works without focus, but the caller must know the provider and session id, it replaces the user's tab, and it cannot handle an agent that shares a split tab.
- **Add a "no navigation" flag to `worktree.activate`:** activation also hydrates mobile session surfaces and has mobile-specific semantics. A dedicated wake call is smaller and clearer.

body:
PR 5b of noir-lang/noir#14004, and the last documentation PR in the series. After it, `just stdlib-doc-inventory --check` passes: all **479** public stdlib items have a doc comment and a `noir` example that CI runs.

## What changed

The files are `meta/typ.nr`, `type_def.nr`, `function_def.nr`, `module.nr`, `item_visibility.nr`, `trait_def.nr`, `trait_impl.nr` and `mod.nr`. `trait_constraint.nr` and `unresolved_type.nr` were already complete.

- **`FunctionDefinition`, `TypeDefinition`, `Module`, `TraitDefinition`** get their definitions the way user code does, through an attribute such as `#[check] pub fn add(...)` with `comptime fn check(f: FunctionDefinition)`. The 30 builtins that had no doc take their descriptions from the markdown reference under `docs/docs/libraries/standard_library/meta`. Behaviours I found while testing are now written down:
  - `named_attribute_args` returns arguments only for comptime attribute macros. A tag such as `#['tag(1)]` has none.
  - Calling a function after `disable` is a compile error carrying the given message. The `# Security` note from the markdown page is carried over.
  - `Module::location` is the module's name for an inline `mod foo { ... }`, but the start of the file for `mod foo;`.
  - `add_abi` only has an effect on a type inside a `contract`. Its example is a `contract`.
- **`Type`** and its `ArrayType`, `IntegerType` and `DataType` decompositions: each `as_*` shows a match and a near-miss that returns `none`. The `get_trait_impl` and `implements` examples were tagged `rust`, so nothing ran them. They're now `noir`, and the `get_trait_impl` one had a broken `assert(x, 1)`, now `assert_eq`. `fresh_type_variable`'s example function is now `main`, so it runs.
- **`TypeGeneric`, `StructField`, `ItemVisibility`**: examples use a `Pair<T, let N: u32>` struct with `pub`, `pub(crate)` and private fields.
- **`mod.nr`**: `unquote`, `type_of`, `error`, `warn`, `DeriveFunction`, `derive`, `derive_via` and `make_trait_impl`.
- **Summaries are one line each**, so the `nargo doc` search index shows a whole sentence.
- Example scaffold items that only exist for an attribute to inspect are `pub`, so they don't produce unused-item warnings. The examples whose subject is visibility keep their private items.

## Docs site

- `// docs:start`/`docs:end` regions that the markdown reference includes contain no `///` lines, so the reference pages show the same code as before.
- The `derive` tutorial in `docs/docs/language/comptime.md` was one region spanning `DeriveFunction`, `HANDLERS` and `derive`, two of which now have doc comments. It's now two regions, `derive_example` (the alias and the handler map) and `derive_example_body` (`derive`), with a sentence between the two includes. The `//` tutorial comments inside them are unchanged. `derive_via`'s doc sits above its region.
- The site reads stdlib sources at the latest release tag and falls back to master for a region the tag doesn't have. So until the next release, the published tutorial shows the old `derive_example` region (which includes `derive`) followed by the new `derive_example_body`, and `derive` appears twice. It resolves at the next release.

## Also changed

`scripts/check_stdlib_doc_examples.py` treats `contract` as a top-level item, so an example can define one.

## Checks

- `just stdlib-doc-inventory --check` passes.
- `scripts/check_stdlib_doc_examples.py`: 472 examples pass, 2 ignored. The only remaining warnings in its output are the ones the `warn` examples emit on purpose, the visibility examples, and two older `BoundedVec` examples.
- `nargo fmt --check` and `nargo doc --check` on the stdlib are clean, and every intra-doc link resolves in the generated HTML.
- The LSP suite (354 tests) and the stdlib `meta` tests pass. No `nargo_cli` snapshot points at these files.

The last PR in the plan is PR 6, which runs `stdlib-doc-inventory --check` in CI.

Refs noir-lang/noir#14004

author: cruisercohen
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A finished sub-agent run's record no longer reads as running.

`create_agent_folder` (`subagent_persistence.py`) writes `"status": "running"` into every run's `state.json`, and no ending writes the field back (a completed ending rewrites the file only to record `result_complete`); the outcome is recorded only in the sibling `tombstone.json`. So the folder of every finished run, stopped ones included, still says `running`. Someone looking at the sub-agent folders after a `409 slot_subagents_running` (#17158) finds dozens of "running" children that are not running.

## Why it matters

The record misleads the person diagnosing a stuck slot: it points at children that ended long ago, and the recorded `pid` cannot settle it because it may since belong to an unrelated process.

## Not a goal

- Recording the ending in `state.json` instead (the tombstone already records it, and a second copy would be one more whole-file rewrite at the run's end).
- Rewriting records written before this change; they keep the stale value until their folder is pruned.
- The `pid` field, the doctor check for stranded rows (#22247) and the 409 body (#22248).

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: finished runs read as running. Root cause: the field is a constant written once at creation, and no code reads it; every reader takes how a run ended from the tombstone (`classify_persisted_ending`: its `outcome`, then its `cause`). The issue offered two fixes, keeping the field current or not writing it. Not writing it removes the misleading value with no new write site; keeping it current would add a whole-file `state.json` rewrite at every kind of ending (delivery, stop, error, boot reconcile), and the file's write model (`test_subagent_state_write_model`) admits a new write site only off the event loop.

- `subagent_persistence.py`: `create_agent_folder` no longer writes `status`, with a comment saying why.
- `docs/system-specs/modules/subagent.md`: the run-folder layout says `state.json` carries no run status and where the ending is read from.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: no code reads `state.json`'s `status`, and a record that still carries it is read exactly as before.

Readers of `state.json` on origin/main @ 02eeb00d15, none of which reads `status` (paths under the package root):
Reader: subagent_persistence.py:classify_persisted_ending -- subagent -- takes the ending from the tombstone's outcome then cause; test_a_stopped_run_does_not_read_as_running
Reader: subagent_persistence.py:list_orphans -- release -- decides by tombstone presence; its one consumer, the orphan reconcile in subagent_manager/monitoring.py, reads id and pid and never status
Reader: taskq/migrate.py:legacy_subagent_records -- release -- reads id, parent_session, task, agent, max_turns, memory_store, started and provider
Reader: subagent_manager/admission/taskq_bridge.py:taskq_artifact_probe -- subagent -- reads the tombstone and result_complete
Reader: dashboard/messaging_api/run_views.py:api_spawn_status -- chat -- the persisted fallback reads task and started and sets done itself
Reader: subagent_manager/continuation.py:_keep_recorded_on_disk_impl -- subagent -- reads keep only

## Tests

Failing first on origin/main (3 cases), passing with the fix:

- `test_subagent_persistence_spawn_lifecycle.py::TestSpawnCreatesFolder::test_spawn_creates_agent_folder`: after the spawned run has ended, its `state.json` does not read `running` and carries no `status` (it used to assert `running` on the finished run, pinning the defect).
- `test_subagent_persistence.py::TestCreateAgentFolder::test_a_stopped_run_does_not_read_as_running`: the folder a user stop leaves reads `stopped` through `classify_persisted_ending` and its `state.json` says nothing that contradicts it.
- `test_subagent_persistence.py::TestCreateAgentFolder::test_creates_state_json`: a new record carries no `status`.

Run locally: the 126 test files that touch `state.json` or `subagent_persistence` (8792 passed). One failure, `test_home_pin_survives_monkeypatch_undo.py::test_the_guard_accepts_a_scratch_home`, fails the same way on main's code on this host (its scratch home resolves into the live data home here), so it is environmental. black, isort, flake8 and mypy on the touched files; the comment-history, brand, harness-parity, feature-map and docs-lint gates.

## Manual verification

N/A: unit coverage sufficient. The lifecycle test reads the `state.json` a real spawn writes after its run ends.

## Related Issues

Fixes #22245

Open #22087 splits `subagent_persistence.py` into modules; this one-line change will need carrying into the split file by whichever lands second.

## Pattern harvest

Not generalizable: one constant field written at creation and never maintained; no other run-record field is written once and read as current.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: angyedz
body:
## Stage 1 QEMU proof — stacked on Stage 0 / PR #8

This draft PR implements a **disposable, offline QEMU-only** proof of two concurrent Linux execution environments sharing the same kernel. It is based on `codex/user-environment-foundation`, not merged into `main`.

### Implemented and tested

- Build an Alpine 3.22 **persistent ext4 user rootfs** populated with BusyBox `/sbin/init`, OpenRC runlevels, an ordinary `veyrauser` account, and a guest-only sudo test rule.
- A **trusted guest system supervisor** first prepares rootfs ownership, spawns an unprivileged launcher (outside UID 100000), installs constrained subordinate UID/GID mappings (inside 0–65535 → outside 100000–165535), then launches a **separate PID 1**, independent mount/network/IPC/UTS/user namespaces, and a true pivot into that root.
- An intermediate private tmpfs root is needed for `pivot_root` when the QEMU system booted from initramfs rootfs.
- Ordinary inner UID 1000 writes to its home; parent verifies outside ownership UID 101000.
- **Real `sudo` inside the user namespace** elevates that user to inner UID 0 while the resulting file is owned by **outside UID 100000**, never initial namespace UID 0. The trusted parent does **not** deny `setgroups`, which user-side sudo needs.
- A test OpenRC service writes a persistent boot-count: the same ext4 image survives two separate QEMU boots, with counter 1 then 2.
- Source: `tests/stage1-user-supervisor.c`, `scripts/veyra-stage1-qemu-init.sh`, `tests/fixtures/*`, `tests/test-stage1-user-openrc-qemu.py`, and QEMU CI workflow.

### Evidence

- [QEMU Stage 1 two-boot, inner sudo and persisted state PASSED](https://github.com/angyedz/Veyra-Linux/actions/runs/39308988112).
- [Integration CI including ShellCheck PASSED](https://github.com/angyedz/Veyra-Linux/actions/runs/39306876896).
- The QEMU test **explicitly asserted the mapped sudo marker on both boots**; that updated run completed successfully. The final documentation-only workflow change will be checked separately.
- Detailed [Stage 1 prototype design and limitations](https://github.com/angyedz/Veyra-Linux/blob/codex/stage1-user-rootfs-openrc/docs/STAGE1-USER-ROOTFS.md).

### NOT DONE — do not merge as production-ready

This is an early, test-only demonstration, **not** a full installed Veyra environment or a general security audit. It has no real login/SDDM, production user sudo/polkit policy, vpkg packages, Wayland/KDE, per-user VPN/veth/DNS, verified inherited-FD/device rules, host control bridges, A/B integration or automated user environment recovery. The QEMU guest supervisor has initial namespace root but only in a disposable VM. Inner sudo NOPASSWD is only a test fixture.

Do not enable in Veyra's installer/default boot or merge these changes into main without additional review and test gates. The user-env version of KDE is still **system-owned but user-executed**; Plasma coherence with A/B remains later work.
