## WTC-11 hiPSC nucleoli (NPM1) single-cell drug perturbation dataset

🔗 **Dataset page:** https://registry.opendata.aws/allen-cell-imaging-collections/
⬇️ **Download:** https://allencell.s3.amazonaws.com/aics/NPM1_single_cell_drug_perturbations/
📄 **Paper:** [Interpretable representation learning for 3D multi-piece intracellular structures using point clouds](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02729-9)

1,025 single-cell 3D spinning-disk confocal crops of WTC-11 hiPS cells with endogenously mEGFP-tagged nucleophosmin (NPM1, nucleolar granular component), imaged after treatment with 16 drugs or DMSO control. Each cell comes with the raw structure crop, a 3D nuclear segmentation and a 3D nucleoli segmentation from the Allen Cell and Structure Segmenter, plus a manifest with drug condition and train/valid/test split.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Modality** | spinning-disk |
| **Dimensionality** | 3D volumes · channels: 1 |
| **Voxel / pixel size** | 108 × 108 × 290 nm (x × y × z) |
| **Data format** | tiff |
| **Size** | 5.5 GB (confirmed from a complete file listing) · 1025 images/volumes |
| **Sample** | Homo sapiens · WTC-11 hiPS cells (AICS-50, endogenously mEGFP-tagged NPM1) treated with 16 drugs or DMSO, imaged at 100x two hours after treatment |
| **Annotations** | semantic-segmentation · dense coverage · automatic · format: Per-cell 3D TIFF masks: single_cell/nucleus (nuclear segmentation) and single_cell/struc_classical (nucleoli segmentation); raw crops in single_cell/struc_raw |
| **ML tasks** | segmentation, classification · splits provided: yes |
| **Access / license** | open · custom (https://www.allencell.org/terms-of-use.html) |
| **Hosted at** | other aics/NPM1_single_cell_drug_perturbations |

**Notes:** Public S3 prefix s3://allencell/aics/NPM1_single_cell_drug_perturbations/: manifest.csv lists 1,025 cells (train 717, valid 154, test 154; 16 drugs plus DMSO) with single_cell/{nucleus,struc_classical,struc_raw}/<CellId>.tiff. Per the paper, nucleoli were segmented with the Allen Cell and Structure Segmenter (classical workflow) and nuclei with a UNet trained on bright-field, so labels are automatic with manual selection of nuclei. Voxel size is the FOV acquisition size from the paper (0.108 um xy, 0.29 um z); crops were not checked in TIFF headers. Terms: Allen Institute terms of use (research or noncommercial use); no SPDX licence. Different from allen-hipsc-single-cell-image-dataset. enricher: size 5,528,673,252 B from full S3 listing (was null); nucleoli masks (struc_classical) are on a different grid than raw crops.

### Technical inspection

Deepest check: **sample**

| Role | Files | Axes · shape | dtype | Compression | Values | Labels | Alignment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| raw | `single_cell/struc_raw/*.tiff` · tiff | zyx · 27×120×108 (varies) | float64 | none | 0–1 · rescaled | — | not-applicable: Single-channel 3D crop per cell (tifffile 'shaped' TIFF, shape stored without axis names; z is the 27-page axis). Shape varies per cell (second sample 27x126x78). |
| label | `single_cell/nucleus/*.tiff` · tiff | zyx · 27×120×108 (varies) | int64 | none | 0–1 | binary · 1=nucleus | same-grid: Pairs with struc_raw by CellId file name (manifest columns crop_raw / crop_seg_nuc); identical shape to the raw crop. |
| label | `single_cell/struc_classical/*.tiff` · ome-tiff | zyx · 97×129×117 (varies) | uint8 | deflate | 0–255 | unknown · None=nucleoli | unknown: Pairs by CellId (manifest column crop_seg) but on a different grid than raw/nucleus (97x129x117 vs 27x120x108; 97x135x87 vs 27x126x78 for a second cell; z ratio ~3.6, xy ~0.93). No resampling or physical size stated in the README, manifest, paper or OME header. Values mostly 0/255 with 51 distinct values (95% zero), so possibly an interpolated binary mask. |

🧪 **Quick-test sample** (5.6 MB): One cell (CellId 0000b617-...) raw NPM1 crop, its nuclear mask and its nucleoli segmentation
- `https://allencell.s3.amazonaws.com/aics/NPM1_single_cell_drug_perturbations/single_cell/struc_raw/0000b617-c508-4fb9-8531-4bf3e68e4420.tiff`

```

single_cell/nucleus/          1035 files  2.7 GB   <CellId>.tiff
single_cell/struc_classical/  1035 files  37.2 MB  <CellId>.tiff
single_cell/struc_raw/        1025 files  2.7 GB   <CellId>.tiff
```

**Inspection notes:** Listing of the full S3 prefix (3,097 files, exact sizes). Probed one file per folder; sampled two cells (0000b617-..., 000b2dd6-...); value ranges are from these samples. author: omni-resolve-agent[bot]
body:
## Related issue

Resolves OMNI-10430 (Linear). It has no mirrored GitHub issue.

## Summary

When a runner's Databricks login lapsed, a codex-native Chat session stayed at "Working…" after the next message. Chat now ends that turn with an error carrying the policy hook's reason.

- **Cause.** The `UserPromptSubmit` policy hook could not refresh the runner's token, so it failed closed and Codex blocked the prompt. Two separate problems each kept Chat hanging: the forwarder ignored Codex's `hook/completed` event, and it posted turn status over HTTP with the same lapsed credentials.
- **Turn error.** A `userPromptSubmit` run blocked with the fail-closed reason (`is_fail_closed_request_reason`) becomes the turn's terminal error, reusing the `error` path's duplicate and stale-turn checks. Other prompt blocks are unchanged.
- **Delivery.** Runner-launched Codex forwarders send their own session's `external_session_status` over the runner's authenticated tunnel; other `TunnelEventClient` users keep the default. Sub-agent statuses stay on HTTP: a reused sub-agent row can keep a stale runner binding after a host runner relaunch, and tunnel ingestion would drop its status, while the HTTP path still applies it. Status falls back to HTTP while the tunnel is down. A status the server answers with `busy` (sent before anything is applied) stays queued on the tunnel with the durable-item backoff, rather than exhausting the forwarder's three quick attempts. A status whose ACK is lost or whose ingest failed may already be applied, so it returns to the forwarder's bounded retry. The server and runner now share the `busy` code.

Related: #8818 is a claude-native draft for this report. #9328 handles codex-native prompt blocks in the forwarder only, and the Repro test still fails without the tunnel. Whichever of the two lands second must reconcile the `hook/completed` handlers.

## Test Plan

Base `8dfed9969`, head `bbeb5fc27`. Stand-in: a local server, a fake Databricks CLI whose login lapses, and a mock model. No Databricks-hosted server or real OAuth refresh was used.

- `tests/e2e_ui/chat/test_codex_native_policy_auth_lapse_notice.py` (the Repro test with the real Codex CLI, kept as coverage): on base no error appears within 90 s; on this branch the expanded error must contain "policy evaluation unavailable". Rerun on `bbeb5fc27` and `b2226779a` (databricks-sdk 0.67.0) and on `3eb757af1` with databricks-sdk 0.115.0 (CI's version) and 0.67.0. Its fake profile now names a loopback workspace host, because SDK 0.115's host-metadata probe retried the placeholder host for minutes and kept the runner offline in CI. The original Repro version also passes. With the tunnel wiring removed it fails, because lapsed HTTP auth rejects the status post.
- `tests/harnesses/codex_native/forwarder/test_turn_errors.py`: a fail-closed block posts one failed status (fails on base). Routing blocks, unblocked runs and tool hooks still finish through `turn/completed`.
- `tests/runner/transports/ws_tunnel/test_event_delivery.py`: status uses the tunnel only for an opted-in client's own session (a sub-agent session's status uses HTTP), falls back to HTTP while the tunnel is down, returns to its producer after a lost or failed-ingest ACK, and stays queued through four `busy` ACKs until the server applies it. The busy case fails on the previous dispatcher, and the sub-agent case fails without the session check.
- `tests/harnesses/codex_native/test_codex_native.py`: the supervised forwarder restricts tunnel delivery to its own session's status (fails without that argument).
- The codex-native, runner tunnel and native-launch, claude-native and policy-hook suites pass, as does the claude-native CLI-upgrade e2e test. On `bbeb5fc27`, the codex-native, native forwarder, CLI auth and runner launch suites (2,234 tests) and the tunnel suites (318) pass. On `b2226779a`, the runner-tunnel and server tunnel/session suites (846 tests) also pass.

## Demo

- [ ] Visual demo attached below
- [x] Non-visual evidence provided below or in Test Plan
- [ ] Not applicable — no behavioral change

The captioned clip `recordings/omni-10430/after-chat-hang.mp4`, recorded on `bbeb5fc27`, is in the Resolve artifact bundle `resolve-bundle-39290285229`. I couldn't attach it: this session's GitHub credential rejects uploads ("unsupported authentication type") for both video and PNG stills. Could a maintainer attach it here? It shows Working… for about 30 s of hook retries, then the error banner.

## Validate the fix live

The fix runs in the runner, so use the PR build against a Databricks-hosted server reached through a Databricks CLI profile:

```
gh pr checkout 10851
uv run omnigent claude --server <your Databricks-hosted Omnigent URL> -p 'Reproduce and validate a bug fix. In web Chat, start a Codex session, send "hello" and wait for the reply. Break token refresh for the runner profile (for example `databricks auth logout --profile <profile>`), then send "are you still there?". Before this fix, Chat stayed at "Working…" with no error. Confirm that within about a minute "Working…" ends and the expanded error banner shows "Omnigent policy evaluation unavailable" with the refresh failure. Sign in again and confirm the next message gets a reply. Report whether each step behaves correctly.'
```

Without such a server, run the stand-in test: `uv run pytest tests/e2e_ui/chat/test_codex_native_policy_auth_lapse_notice.py -v` (needs `codex` and `tmux` on `PATH`).

author: einioville
body:
## Summary

`frontend_v2` moves to Qt 6.12 (#52). Why: Qt 6.12 is an LTS line, and its Canvas2D and QML live preview fit work we already do. Along the way, the move exposed a Qt Location bug that left map tiles blank.

```diff
 Build
~  qt_standard_project_setup(REQUIRES 6.12), links Qt Canvas Painter
+  --qml-preview / -QmlPreview: opt-in QT_QML_DEBUG build for the QmlPreview MCP server,
+  passed on every configure so it never sticks in a later plain build
~  build-frontend.sh: QTDIR or ~/Qt kit only when >= the REQUIRES version (a stale QTDIR is skipped)
 Trips map (items/trip/TripMap.qml)
~  route overlay: Canvas2D (GPU) instead of Qt Quick Canvas (CPU raster + upload every pan frame)
+  AppConfig asks for desktop GL 3.3 core, else ES 3.0, before any window: Canvas2D has no
+  GL 2.x shaders and crashes on Mesa's default 2.1. App.gpuCanvas false -> Qt Quick Canvas.
+  TESLA_HOMEDASH_GPU_CANVAS=0 forces the fallback
 Maps (items/tesla/BasemapSwitch.qml, BasemapPlugin.qml)
+  a pixel pan a second after Qt resets the map type: requests tiles a Qt Location bug left blank
~  shared tile cache 50 -> 300 MiB: at 50 MiB the MML imagery deleted EOX's tiles on every start
 Docs
~  CLAUDE.md §3.2, README, docs/wsl-dev-environment.md: Qt 6.12 with Canvas Painter + Multimedia
+  frontend_v2/CLAUDE.md: QML live preview; core/CLAUDE.md: the GL context guard
```

**The Qt Location bug.** When a tile request is cancelled and the same tile is requested again before Qt delivers the cancelled reply's queued `finished()`, `QGeoTileFetcher::finished()` matches the stale reply by tile, not by request. It completes the new request with no data, and throws the real reply away when it arrives. Our maps trigger this at startup. A map that picks EOX's satellite type before its provider file has loaded (always the Weather view's radar map) gets switched by Qt to its first type (Street) when the file loads, and `BasemapSwitch` switches it back, cancelling and re-requesting the tiles in flight. The radar showed the tile under the home location grey on every start. The fix in Qt is one line, verified against a rebuilt Qt Location 6.12.0; a report with a reproducer is drafted for Qt's Jira. Our workaround needs no Qt changes.

## Verification

Checked on the WSL box (Qt 6.12.0), offscreen through the LD_PRELOAD probe with the fake backend. Screenshots were shared in the session.
- Every view renders on the 3.3 core context; the log reads `OpenGL: core 3.3 context for Canvas2D`.
- The Trips route draws identically on Canvas2D and on the fallback (`TESLA_HOMEDASH_GPU_CANVAS=0`, log `Qt's default context`).
- Radar map: before, the tile under the place stayed grey on every start. After, a logging hook showed the tile lost to the bug and fetched again one second later, and the map is complete. Another map recovered the same way, and nothing was requested from Qt's built-in tile servers during Qt's brief switch to Street.
- `build-frontend.sh`: tested with a stale `QTDIR`, a correct one, none, an explicit missing kit, an explicit 6.11 kit, a `QTDIR` at a 6.11 kit, and only an old kit installed.

To check by hand:
1. `./scripts/build-frontend.sh --run` in a terminal opened before the Qt switch: it says `QTDIR=… is not a Qt 6.12+ kit` and builds with 6.12.0.
2. Trips view: open a trip and pan or pinch. The route should follow smoothly.
3. Weather view with an empty EOX cache (`rm ~/.cache/QtLocation/5.8/tiles/osm/osm_100-l-2-*`, then start the app): no grey square on the radar.

Not on the Pi (none yet). The Windows box needs the 6.12 `msvc2022_64` kit; `build-frontend.ps1` takes the newest kit already. #53 was closed separately ("keep all four graph settings").

Refs #52 (stays open until the Pi runs 6.12)

author: kcnyu
body:
kcn (2026-10-20): 「把用到minimax m3 flash的thinking都改成默认adaptive或者high，如果前者不支持就改成high即可。」「我们只打算用3.1不用考虑minimax其他的」. Authority: MiniMax's own Anthropic API reference (Anthropic SDK page on platform.minimax.cn; the URL is in `docs/operations/models.md`).

## What the reference says for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `thinking` omitted / `{"type":"adaptive"}` | thinking on |
| `{"type":"disabled"}` | HTTP 400 |
| `output_config.effort` | `low` / `medium` / `high` / `xhigh` / `max`; omitted = `max`; `none` = 400 |

Checked against the live endpoint on 2026-10-20 (the account's Token Plan was exhausted, HTTP 429/2056, but parameters are validated before quota): `disabled` -> 400 `requires adaptive thinking`; effort `none` -> 400; effort `bogus` -> 400 `allowed: low, medium, high, xhigh, max`; effort `high`/`xhigh`, adaptive without effort, and `type=enabled` all passed validation (429).

## Changes

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `[models.flash] params.thinking` -> `agents.defaults.models` | `high` (clamped to adaptive with a warning) | `adaptive` |
| `[models.m3]` (rollback to MiniMax-M3) | present, `high` | removed (only M3.1 is used) |
| `talk.consultThinkingLevel` (host, now owned via `[openclaw.talk]`) | `medium` | `adaptive` |
| `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` (host, now owned via `[openclaw.agents.defaults]`) | `high` | `high` (applies only to models without `params.thinking`: deepseek, luna, sonnet) |
| `[chains.cron] thinking` | `max` | `max`, kept on purpose (see below) |
| clawock client thinking call on M3.1 | `{"type":"enabled","budget_tokens":…}`, adaptive only when an effort was passed | always `{"type":"adaptive"}`; `output_config.effort` only when asked (none = endpoint default `max`) |
| `WEEKLY_LLM_THINKING_EFFORT` | `medium` | `high` |
| unknown `thinking_effort` | sent, endpoint 400s three times | `ValueError` before the request |

Why the cron chain stays `max`: OpenClaw's cron executor resolves one level for the turn and re-clamps it per fallback candidate. The MiniMax hops offer only off/adaptive, `gpt-6-luna` offers low…max with no `adaptive`, so no level is exact for both. `adaptive` would clamp Luna to `medium` (against the 2026-09-13 "Luna max as backstop" policy, pinned in `test_strategy_crons_request_max_reasoning_clamped_per_candidate`). On the MiniMax hops OpenClaw (with the host patch) sends `{"type":"adaptive"}` and no effort, which the endpoint runs at `max`, so the label also matches the depth actually run.

Unchanged on purpose: the influencer filter's `thinking_disabled` call (adaptive + effort `low`, #2202): it asks for as little thinking as possible, not for the default, and its 16K output budget is sized for that.

## Tests

`tests/test_model_registry.py`: every MiniMax model is M3.1 with `params.thinking == "adaptive"`, the talk consult level is `adaptive`, and MiniMax-only chains can only say `adaptive`; `[openclaw.*]` keys are rendered and reported as owned sections. `tests/test_llm_chain_budget.py`: request shapes for M3.1 with/without effort; invalid efforts refused before the request.

Local: `pytest tests/test_model_registry.py tests/test_llm_chain_budget.py tests/test_cron_contracts.py tests/test_brief_fallback_token_budget.py tests/test_docs_index.py tests/test_openclaw_upgrade_skill_contract.py tests/test_llm_workflow_deadlines.py` -> 114 passed; `ruff check` on touched files clean. A temporary revert of flash to `high` and of talk to `medium` each turned the new contract test red.

Host rollout after merge: back up `openclaw.json`, `sync_models.py --apply`, gateway restart with no cron in flight, `--effective`. No cron payload change.

author: teflocarbon
body:
New scenario for the host-follower bug family: the coupler-interaction check that the stage 1 audit left as an in-game check nobody ran (docs/design/host-local-session.md, `HostOwnClient`). Scenario files only; no mod code.

In-game: ONLY="host-chain-screw" (player host only: gate kind `player`; a dedicated host has no player to work the chain).

## What it covers
Before stage 1, the host's screw used in a state the mod didn't expect (the Start fallback in `CouplerChainInteractionPatch`, `Client/Trains/CouplerChainInteractionPatch.cs`) went to the server through the host's own client. The server applied it to the host's own coupler a second time (`Common_ReceiveCouplerInteraction`): the screw button and knob stopped taking input, and the coupler stayed marked in use (`NetworkedTrainCarServer`'s `frontInteracting`/`rearInteracting`).

## Steps
1. The host spawns a DE2 and a wagon coupled near its own player (`setup.cs`), and the client teleports next to the coupling to watch.
2. The host uncouples them by hand and couples them again: manual-uncouple's `uncouple.cs` and `couple.cs`, run on the host.
3. `screw.cs` (host): loosens and tightens the hooked chain twice through its screw button (vanilla's `OnScrewButtonUsed`, which the mod's postfix reports). Then it runs the mod's postfix on the other car's chain, which isn't on the hook. That is the Start path, invoked as Harmony runs it, so it's deterministic.
4. `state.cs` on both games. Checks:
   - coupled, in one trainset;
   - the chain tight;
   - the same chain states on both games;
   - every chain's screw button and knob taking input (`S`/`K`);
   - on the host, neither car's end marked in use by its server half.

Uses `dvmp_checked`, so a failed eval prints its error. Added to gate.sh (after manual-recouple-lag) and docs/testing.md.

## Checked
Every probe compiles against `split/client-server`'s build (`dvmp eval` against a session with no games), including the manual-uncouple probes it reuses. Not run in game. If it fails on today's split branch, that's a real bug, not the scenario.

author: plissb
body:
Closes #385

## What

Dev (`test.dfm.bitbi.io`) writes Parquet row groups of **8 MiB** instead of the 16 MiB default, so Bit BI's reader — which decodes a row group whole and refuses one above six million cells (their question 67) — takes every table. In `fyt-new`'s checkpoint of 2026-10-06 the widest table, `nsfwork`, closed its groups at 177 355 rows, about 6.2 million cells.

- `k8s/overlays/dev/configmap-patch.yaml`: `DELTA_PARQUET_ROW_GROUP_BYTES: "8388608"`, with the reason and the consequences beside it. Only the split changes — the rows are the same, a writer holds half the buffer, the footer carries about twice the row groups, compression is a little worse.
- `application.yml`'s default (16 MiB) and the stage/prod overlays are **untouched**.
- New guard `ParquetRowGroupDeploymentTest` (fast gate, every file under `k8s/`, reusing `S3OrphanSweepDeploymentTest.declaredValues`): dev sets exactly 8 MiB in one spelling; the key is the placeholder `application.yml` binds; the value is below the default; no other manifest sets it, in the placeholder or the relaxed-binding spelling (`DELTA_PARQUET_ROWGROUPBYTES`).
- `.githooks/pre-commit`: the `k8s/*` branch runs the new guard with the other manifest guards.
- `ParquetScratchCeilingBudgetTest` does not read this key — unchanged.

## Tests and mutation

- The guard was **red first** on the dev case (key not yet set), green after.
- **Mutation**: `DELTA_PARQUET_ROW_GROUP_BYTES: "8388608"` appended to `k8s/overlays/stage/configmap-patch.yaml` reddens `noOtherManifestSetsTheRowGroup`.
- `kubectl kustomize` renders dev, stage and prod; the dev render carries the key.
- `./gradlew test -PexcludeIntegration` and `./gradlew integrationTest` green.

## Documentation

- `docs/delta-client-v2-guide.md` ("Row-group budget"): needed, done — dev at 8 MiB and why.
- `docs/bitbi-integration.md` ("Download Baseline Files"): needed, done — row groups are per deployment, by bytes; dev 8 MiB.
- Recent Changes in `CLAUDE.md` and `AGENTS.md`: needed, done (`dev-row-group-8mib`).
- `docs/cr-*.md`: not needed — no design change, the CR's "byte limit, lower the key" decision is applied as written.

## Not in this PR (human steps)

- Deploy with a `deploy-dev/*` tag; snapshots are rewritten by the next nightly build, already-written batch/delta files keep their groups.
- After the first night: `nsfwork`'s largest row group ≈ half (≈ 90 000 rows) — check on the file; tell Bit BI the date.

No production code, REST, gRPC, proto, DTO, migration (V61 stays next), `specs/NNN-*`, configuration-key, metric, S3-key or frontend change.

author: boquan-fang
body:
# Goal

Fix the Rust binding Config builder. It shouldn't reload system root CA after we pin a private CA.

## Why

Users can use s2n-tls with their PKI which provides CA by their wish. They do so by calling the `wipe_trust_store` to clear the trust store and then set their own CA. However, the current code has a bug where the system CA will still be loaded after the user set their own CA. This happened when the builder is actually building the `Config`. The problem is that our `wipe_trust_store` rust binding function doesn't clear the `load_system_cert` flag:
https://github.com/aws/s2n-tls/blob/c04774553668754c5f9d56695e5dc3f974f09b76/bindings/rust/extended/s2n-tls/src/config.rs#L179-L183

When they actually call builder.buid(), the flag is still true and the system root CA will be loaded:
https://github.com/aws/s2n-tls/blob/c04774553668754c5f9d56695e5dc3f974f09b76/bindings/rust/extended/s2n-tls/src/config.rs#L1152-L1157

## How

The `wipe_trust_store` function should set the `load_system_cert` flag to false.

## Callouts

This wouldn't matter if the application is actually using the system root CA or just manually calling `set_system_load(false)`.

It's important to know that our C counterpart will set the flag to false, so I think it make sense to match that behavior.
https://github.com/aws/s2n-tls/blob/c04774553668754c5f9d56695e5dc3f974f09b76/tls/s2n_config.c#L510-L517
https://github.com/aws/s2n-tls/blob/c04774553668754c5f9d56695e5dc3f974f09b76/tls/s2n_x509_validator.c#L146-L153

## Testing

I add a `wipe_turst_store_prevents_loading_system_certs` test. The test will wipe the trust store and ping a trust pem that is not trusted. Then we assert on whether the test would emit a S2N_ERR_CERT_UNTRUSTED error after the config is build and handshake has terminated. 

Without the fix, the test wouldn't error, because it would reload the system cert and the handshake will succeed.

author: or4cl3void
body:
## Problem

A connection's clause 5.3 pending queue (`Session::queue_i_frame`) had no size limit. Concrete case: a malicious or broken master connects to an outstation, never sends STARTDT, and answers every TESTFR. The connection stays Stopped forever, t1 never fires, and every spontaneous event the application hands over is pushed into the queue for good, so memory grows without end.

A redundancy group has the same problem in two places: after a failure it keeps every ASDU in `held` until a STARTDT act that may never come, and `left_behind` keeps growing across repeated failures while the application makes no replay decision.

## Fix

- New constant `link::MAX_PENDING_USER_DATA = 16384`. That is about 4 MiB per connection at the 249-octet maximum ASDU, far above any k window (normally 12).
- New variant `QueueError::Full`. `Session::queue_i_frame` returns it once the queue is at the limit.
- `RedundancyGroup::send_user_data` returns `GroupError::Queue(QueueError::Full)` once the group holds that many ASDUs in total that are not confirmed or decided on yet (held data, plus each member's queue mirror, unconfirmed frames and left-behind data). The replay inside `retransmit_unconfirmed` skips this check, because that data was counted already.
- Nothing is dropped. The caller gets the error and keeps the ASDU. The tokio drivers already pass these errors up with `?`. The server never uses the session queue (it has its own bounded event buffer and sends only into an open window), so it needed no change.

## Test

`tests/link.rs`: `a_connection_that_is_never_started_refuses_data_beyond_the_limit` queues `MAX_PENDING_USER_DATA` ASDUs on a connected, Stopped session and checks that the next one gets `QueueError::Full`. Without the fix it fails (`Ok(())` instead of `Err(Full)`).

## API change

This is a breaking change, but a small one: `QueueError` gets a new variant, so an exhaustive `match` on it outside the crate no longer compiles. I made the limit a constant rather than a `LinkParams` field, because `LinkParams` is a plain struct with public fields that callers build as struct literals, and a new field would break all of those.

author: richardqdd
body:
## Why

The Spec registry (`/spec`) took 4–5 s for a reviewer and showed everything at once: the sync form, the run log, write problems, the relations switch, the waiting frames and the full edit history. Before rendering anything it listed **every frame ever made** and the server counted all ~24,700 of their rows — to show two waiting frames, a Changes column that was always "—" (it read `item_counts`; the server sends `item_count`), and the edit history.

## What

**Overview** (default), in Richard's priority order; each section is its own Suspense boundary, so the header and tabs appear at once and sections fill in as their read returns:

1. **Waiting for review**: draft frames only. Reuses the sidebar's read (`listDraftChangesets` is now memoised per request, so layout + page make one call). Readiness looks up only the drafts' own prerequisites (`approvedFrames`, from #894). Rows: frame + one line on what it changes, source in words ("Sync (Sanity)", "Spec System edit"), real change count, status, Review →.
2. **Needs attention**: failed syncs (dismissable) and approved changes not written to Sanity. **Nothing rendered when there are none.**
3. **Recent activity**: latest 3 syncs (drift lines on the latest finished one only) and the 3 most recently approved frames (`?state=approved&order=approved&limit=3`, so the server counts 3 frames).

**Header**: Sync Changes (dataset, SKUs, button) in one row; while a sync runs it is disabled and the page refreshes itself.

**Tabs**, read only when opened: **Edit history** (Spec System edits, 15 at a time, Show more) and **Settings** (relations owner switch, unchanged).

Removed `spec-sync-panel.tsx` (its parts are in the header / sections). The run filters moved to `lib/spec/sync-runs.ts` with tests. `listSyncRuns` is memoised per request (header, attention and recent share one read).

## Also: shared loading states (review feedback)

- `components/loading/page-skeleton.tsx` (admin-wide, on the repo-wide `Skeleton` primitive): `PageSkeleton` shaped like the page it stands in for (`table` · `detail` · `map` · `sections` · `list` · `article`), `SectionSkeleton` for parts that load on their own, `InlineLoading` (spinner + line) for client-side loads.
- Every admin route has its own `loading.tsx` (before: only `/spec`, a generic list every Spec page inherited).
- Registry section fallbacks, Spec Map panel, configurator, rule editor and rules view use the shared pieces instead of plain "Loading…" text.

## Depends on

pakfactory.com-server #354 for `order=approved` and the cheaper write-problems check. Without it the page still works; "Recently approved" is then newest-created first.

## Tests

- `pnpm test` 47 pass (new `sync-runs.test.ts`); `tsc` clean; eslint clean on the changed paths.
- **Not yet seen in a browser**: the local admin needs a password sign-in. To check before merging, sign in at http://localhost:4001 and I'll walk the page; otherwise I'll check it on staging after deploy and re-time it (before: ~4 s server, 4–5 s for a reviewer).

## Summary

body:
## Por qué «no se aplicó» la v0.03.3.2

La v0.03.3.2 está en `main` y compila, pero la app son dos cosas: el Python (dashboard) y el binario Rust (bandeja, notch, avisos). «Actualizar y reiniciar» y `brain update` solo traen el Python; el binario instalado seguía siendo el viejo: notch cuadrado con botones, avisos del notch y del sistema a la vez, clic que abre el menú y el ícono con la versión anterior.

## Qué cambia

- **La app se actualiza sola**: el shell compara su versión con la que informa el dashboard (`/api/app` ahora trae `version`); si el código es más nuevo, avisa, se cierra y corre `brain app-update` (`BRAIN_APP_ONLY=1 install.sh` / `install.ps1`: solo baja la app del último release), que la reabre. Sin bucles (`data/app_update.json`, 6 h), no toca builds de desarrollo. `brain app-update` también sirve a mano.
- **El título del menú sigue la versión** que informa el dashboard.
- **Notch animado por CSS** (resorte en la GPU, no la ventana redimensionada cuadro a cuadro): sale del notch físico en macOS (hombros cóncavos), cae desde arriba sin notch y debajo del panel en Windows/Linux. Encabezado con nombre + campana con globito; el aviso es una tira de 2 renglones; el grafo entra nodo por nodo, late en lo que cambió y manda chispas. Cierre automático (no con el puntero encima), se abre en la pantalla del puntero, clic en un nodo abre el grafo.
- Linux: el menú suma «Notch…» (la bandeja no da eventos de clic). Ventana `resizable(true)` porque GTK ignora `set_size` en una no redimensionable.
- Versión `v0.03.3.3`, changelog, docs, README, SECURITY, CLAUDE, `chat.APP_GUIDE`, tests.

## Verificado

- `pytest` 97 passed; `check_site`; `cargo fmt/clippy -D warnings/test` en Linux; `cargo check` para Windows.
- App real bajo Xvfb: aviso en el notch sin notificación del sistema, ventana que se achica, clic → grafo con nodos reales; auto-actualización con descarga del release real y sin bucle.
- **No probado**: macOS y Windows con ventana real (lo compila el CI).

## Después del merge

Publicar el release `v0.03.3.3` (el workflow arma `.dmg`, `.AppImage`/`.deb` y `setup.exe`) y volver a correr el instalador una vez; las apps anteriores a esta versión no saben actualizarse solas.

author: srbino
body:
Fixes #3783.

## What changes

**`hooks/use-websocket.ts`**
- While a retry is scheduled the status is `"connecting"` with a new `reason` field (`"retrying"`, or `"restart"` after close 1012/1001). `onerror` no longer sets `"error"` before a close that will be retried.
- New status `"offline"`: past the fast budget (8 attempts, ~2 min) with reason `"unreachable"`, retrying every 30 s; or `"browser-offline"` when `navigator.onLine === false`, waiting for `online`.
- Retries at once on `online`, `visibilitychange` to visible, window `focus` and `retry()`. `retryNow` is renamed to `retry` and wakes every socket in the tab through a window event.
- Unchanged: the auth paths (null ticket, 4401, `session_revoked`) and `WsUnavailableError`.
- `isRealtimeDown(status, reason)` is the shared "is the connection down" test.

**UI** (`components/layout/realtime-outage.ts` holds the shared vocabulary and the 4 s grace)
- App banner and chat bar: nothing for 4 s, then neutral "Reconnecting…" (plus " · N messages queued"), "Crewship is restarting · reconnecting…" or "You're offline · Crewship will reconnect when you're back". The warn "Can't reach Crewship · retrying every 30 s" with Retry now comes only after the fast budget. There is no "Reconnected" flash.
- The chat bar joins the app banner queue (kind `offline`), so a screen shows one indicator. The chat header `ConnectionBadge` is removed (file deleted).
- New `neutral` banner tone (chip-neutral tokens).
- System status pill and popover: amber "Reconnecting" while the socket retries, even if the engine poll has failed. Red only for `unreachable`. Browser offline is amber.
- Dashboard offline and the Issues offline state use `isRealtimeDown` with the same 4 s grace (was 3 s on `disconnected`/`error` only).
- Page document sync failure says "Reconnecting…" instead of "Disconnected".

**Backend:** not changed. The hub sends no close code on shutdown: `Hub.Run` returns on ctx.Done, and x/net/websocket's `Close()` always writes 1000 (`defaultCloseStatus` is private). A deploy therefore reaches the browser as 1006, and the "restarting" wording shows only if a proxy sends 1012/1001. Sending 1012 would mean writing raw close frames; that is not a small change.

## Tests
- New: `hooks/__tests__/use-websocket-reconnect.test.ts` (fake timers: status during backoff, no error flicker, 1012/1001, 30 s retries after the budget, immediate retry on online, visibilitychange, focus and retry(), browser offline, 4401 still terminal).
- New: `components/layout/__tests__/realtime-reconnect-banners.test.tsx` (every banner state, the 4 s grace, no Reconnected, one indicator with chat + app).
- Red-first additions in `status-pill.test.ts` and `dashboard-page.test.tsx`.
- Updated for the intended change: `use-websocket{,.cov,-retry-now}.test.ts`, `app-banners.test.tsx`, `chat-feedback-boundaries.test.tsx`, `connection-contrast.test.tsx`, `use-page-document.test.tsx`.
- e2e `chrome-states.spec.ts` (the phone test now runs `page.clock` past the fast budget to reach Retry now) and `harbor2-dashboard.spec.ts` are updated but **not run locally**.

Self-review only; no other reviewer.

author: mattcerisano
body:
## Why

After using the Drive Tracker: the studio only needs to know **who has each drive** and **which drives are free to go out**. Drive types and return dates were extra bookkeeping nobody wanted. And since Matt and Tommy are the co-owners, a drive "in the office" is really with one of them.

## What changed

- **No drive types.** The Editor SSD / Transfer filter and the Type field in the drive form are gone.
- **No return dates or reminders.** The "Expected back" field, overdue flags, the Overdue stat and the Copy reminder button are all removed. Drives that are out still show how long they've been out, without a warning color.
- **"In office" is now "Available", with Matt or Tommy.**
  - **Returned** (and **All returned**) asks *Back with Matt* or *Back with Tommy*.
  - **Add drive** asks who has it now.
  - **Move to Tommy** / **Move to Matt** in a drive's menu switches it between the two of you.
  - **Found** and **Back in service** also ask which of you has it.
- **Who has what** now has two sections: drives *Out* grouped by holder, then *Available* split into *With Matt* and *With Tommy*. Each owner always gets a card, even when empty. Any older drive with nobody set shows in a third card.
- **Stats:** Available (with the Matt / Tommy split), Out now, and Value out.

## Reviewer notes

- **No migration needed.** For an available drive, the owner keeping it is stored in `holder_name`, the same field that names who has it while it's out. The unused `kind` and `expected_back` columns stay in the table. Returning a drive clears `expected_back`.
- Drives already marked "in office" before this change have nobody set and show under "In the office, nobody set". Use **Move to Matt / Tommy** to assign them.
- The owners list is `OWNERS = ['Matt', 'Tommy']` in `src/lib/drives.ts`.
- Verified: 221/221 tests passing, `tsc` and eslint clean, and the UI harness reports no layout findings at 390, 768 and 1440 px. I also checked screenshots of the Available section on phone and desktop. I haven't clicked through the Returned / Move to menus against the real database.

_Requested by **Jagadeesh** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GoT7NgXMGjukewUnst5qkH?thread=cmsg_01GoT7NgXMGjukewUnst5qkHABxxc1Ag7xZWrPMag4R92y)_

Before: faces are found and told apart by OpenCV's YuNet and SFace only. There is no way to try Qwen-Image-Edit or Wan 2.2 on the family's photographs.

After: the AI models page offers **Finding and grouping faces, more accurate (ArcFace)**, InsightFace's `buffalo_l` pack (289 MB from the project's GitHub release, pinned whole by SHA-256; only `det_10g.onnx` and `w600k_r50.onnx` are kept), and `face_model` on the Advanced settings page (`sface` or `arcface`) chooses which pair the next scan uses. Switching has every photograph looked at again; confirmed names are kept by position, and grouping only compares faces found by the same recogniser. `tools/try_faces.py` compares both pairs on a folder of photographs. `tools/try_image_edit.py` (Qwen-Image-Edit, 4-bit model, about 30 GB) and `tools/try_living_photo.py` (Wan 2.2 TI2V-5B by default, the I2V-A14B experts from 4-bit files with `--model a14b`) are try-outs for the Mac; nothing of them is in the app yet.

The ArcFace models' licence is non-commercial research use only; the page, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES and the guide say so. The user chose them for the household's own library.

How: `faces_arcface.py` decodes SCRFD's nine outputs (anchors by stride, NMS) and aligns each face to ArcFace's five-point template, both through ONNX Runtime on the processor. `FaceEngine` takes a `model` and drives either pair through one shape (detector rows of box, landmarks, score; a recogniser that aligns and embeds one row), so the quality gate, crops, pass and policy are shared. `facematch.Thresholds` gives ArcFace's 512-value embeddings their own bars (same 0.30, auto 0.52, cluster 0.48, link 0.36); rows carry their model, `unpack` reads a BLOB only at the asked width, `plan_regroup`/`load_people` take the model id (the table's majority when not given, as from a worker), and changing `face_model` calls `db.reset_face_pass`. Archives in the catalogue may now be zips. Verified here with the real models on `tests/data/face.jpg`: one face, 512-value unit embedding, the mirrored and one-third-size copies at 0.96 similarity, about 280 ms a photograph on four cloud cores.

author: iguanacucumber
body:
Closes #405

## Changements

- pronote: le rafraîchissement de session est atomique

### Le défaut

`ClientBase._refreshing` était un `var Boolean` nu (ni `@Volatile`, ni CAS). Le job de fond (`PeriodicSyncWorker.doWork()`) et la lecture de l'interface tombant en erreur EN MÊME temps, les deux lisaient `false` et déclenchaient **deux** `refresh()` concurrents :

- deux `Communication` (deux cookies, deux compteurs de requêtes) ;
- le champ `communication` finissant sur celle qui avait fini la dernière ;
- chaque `login()` postant sur la `communication` courante → requêtes entrelacées, clé AES mélangée.

Le serveur répondait alors `G=25` (« Exceeded max authorization requests ») ou la session restait à moitié initialisée. Le `@Synchronized` de `Communication.post` ne sauvait rien : le refresh se fait HORS de ce verrou.

### Le correctif

- `Client.post` et `Client.refresh` partagent le **moniteur du client** (`@Synchronized`) : le refresh ne peut donc pas se chevaucher avec une requête, et `communication`/`attributes`/la clé AES ne sont **jamais** permutés pendant qu'une requête est en vol. Le perdant de la course **attend** le rafraîchissement et rejoue sa requête sur la session neuve (aucune erreur ne remonte à l'appelant).
- `ClientBase._refreshing` (booléen nu) → `RefreshGate` : une porte **CAS** (`compareAndSet(false, true)`) qui n'admet qu'UN rafraîchissement à la fois et se relâche dans le `finally` (un refresh raté ne bloque pas les suivants).
- L'état de session est **publié** (`@Volatile` sur `communication`, `attributes`, `funcOptions`, `encryption`) : les lecteurs hors verrou (ping de garde, pièces jointes) voient la session neuve.

Kotlin pur, stdlib seule (`java.util.concurrent.atomic`) : aucune dépendance ajoutée.

## Vérifications

- `make check` : OK (10 étapes, `android-compile` inclus — la compilation Kotlin réelle a bien produit `RefreshGate.class`)
- `tests/unit/kotlin-refresh-gate.test.ts` : Kotlin **exécuté** — N threads lâchés en même temps sur la porte → **un seul** gagnant ; la porte se rend après un échec.
- `tests/unit/kotlin-pronote-client-parity.test.ts` : Kotlin **exécuté** contre le stub PRONOTE — deux requêtes concurrentes sur le même client → **un seul** handshake de refresh, les deux fils réussissent, et le fil de requêtes est **identique** à celui de la référence TS `pronotets` (parité comportementale : la référence est mono-thread).
- `tests/architecture/pronote-refresh.test.ts` : garde de source — plus de drapeau non atomique, `post`/`refresh` synchronisés, porte relâchée dans le `finally`.
- Le test de concurrence **échoue sur l'ancien code** (fil de requêtes divergent : les deux requêtes partaient avant le refresh) — vérifié 3/3.
- Invariant ajouté : `docs/architecture/INVARIANTS.md` (I17).

Before: the first page was a spinning 3D logo over a wallpaper with two buttons, "Modo 3D" and "Modo 2D". It did not say what the tool is for, split it by technology instead of by subject, and loaded three.js and a typeface just to draw the logo. Inside, the 2D labs had a sidebar of their own and the live code page had a header of its own, so going from a lab to the matching challenges meant going back to the start.

After: the home page states the proposal next to a screenshot of the live code, explains the three steps (explore a lab, program the scene, check the math) and lists four topics: Transformações, Câmera e projeção, Luz e cor and Curvas. Each topic links to its 2D lab and to its challenge trail, and shows how many challenges of that trail are done ("2 de 5 feitos"). The labs and the live code now share one bar at the top: the VisuGraph name goes back to the home page, a topic menu switches topics, and **Explorar | Programar** switches between the topic's lab and its trail. Luz e cor shows its two labs as tabs. A step a topic does not have yet (Câmera has no lab, Curvas has no challenges) is shown dimmed, with the reason. In the live code, picking another topic opens the first open challenge of its trail without reloading, and the same menu leads back to the free editor. In study mode the bar shows only the name, so a recorded session cannot leave the live code.

Each 2D lab has its own address (`index-2d.html#coordenadas`, `#cores`, `#phong`, `#curvas`), and `index-3d.html?livre` opens the live code without the stored challenge, which is where "Editor livre" on the home page goes.

How: `src/js/topics.js` is the single list of topics, labs and trails, and `src/js/topicbar.js` draws the bar on both pages from it. `navigation.js` shows the lab named in the address and keeps the two in sync; links to another lab of the same page only change the hash, so each lab keeps its state, also where the host drops `.html` from the address. The sidebar and its buttons are gone. `src/live/app.js` mounts the bar with handlers that open a trail or the free editor in place, and redraws it whenever the open challenge changes. `src/live/progress.js` reads the progress entry the live code page already writes, and `src/js/home.js` fills in the count on each topic. Both headers are exactly 48 px tall (a fractional height put the coordinate lab's canvas on a half pixel), the labs' bar stays at the top while a lab scrolls, and below 1520 px the live code bar shows only the icon and drops the "Tema" label, so it still fits on one row at 1366 px. The screenshot is a lossless WebP because `.gitattributes` sends PNGs to LFS, which is disabled on this repository.

> 이 PR은 정본 문서 `PRD.md`(§3.1 「용어 정의 — CII · DWT · GT」 문단·표·각주) · `TEST_PLAN.md`(§3.19 · §14.2 · 합계)를 수정합니다.

## Summary
- `#2395` **결정 3(2026-10-17)** — 도구 없이 답하는 용어 질문(DWT 정의가 틀림)에 대해, 화면 예시에 있는 용어 **CII · DWT · GT**의 정의를 `PRD`에 먼저 적고 같은 글자를 챗봇 지시문의 용어 풀이(`chat_explain.GLOSSARY`)에 싣는다.
- ⚠️ **정의 출처의 원문 대조는 사람 몫으로 남아 있다**(`AGENTS §2.1`) — PRD 각주에 「원문 대조 확인: 미완 — 사람 대조 대기」를 적었다.

## 관련 이슈
Refs #2395 — 결정 3을 처리한다. 결정 1(Z.ai 첫 응답 시간 조사)이 남는다.

## 변경 사항
- `PRD.md` §3.1 끝 — 정의 표와 출처 각주 `[#2395]`(MEPC.352(78) §2.4·§4 · MEPC.412(84)가 대체한 §4.2와 각주 1·2 · MEPC.328(76) Reg 2 정의 .15 — IMO 공개 PDF 기계 추출 인용). 1969 톤수협약 원문은 받지 못해 GT의 「무게가 아니라 공간의 크기」는 **(정황)** 표시. 변경 이력. 굵은 제목 문단이라 절 신설이 아니어서 버전 유지
- `services/chat_explain.py` — `CII_MEANING` · `DWT_MEANING` · `GT_MEANING`을 `GLOSSARY`에 추가
- `tests/test_chat_explain.py` — **IT-CHAT-100**: PRD 표 행과 GLOSSARY가 글자 그대로 같고, 정의에 숫자가 0건(수치 가드 — 풀이 속 숫자를 모델이 인용하면 답이 폐기된다)
- `TEST_PLAN` — §3.19 IT-CHAT-100 · §14.2 `test_chat_explain.py` 10 → 11 · 합계 실측(268 · 3660 · 4874)

## 구현 결정 (리뷰 필요)
- 정의 문장에 숫자를 넣지 않았다(1,025 kg/m3 · 1969 · CO₂의 2) — 기존 IT-CHAT-046·047이 풀이의 숫자를 막는다. 원문 숫자는 PRD 각주에만 인용했다(PRD는 지시문에 실리지 않는다).
- DWT 정의 출처는 MARPOL Annex VI Reg 2가 아니라 개정 G1 §4.2 각주 1이다 — Reg 2에서 deadweight 정의 항목을 찾지 못했다.
- 원문은 「relative density of 1,025 kg/m3」로 적는다(상대밀도인데 단위가 붙음) — 정의 문장에는 값을 쓰지 않아 영향이 없고 각주에 적었다.

## 테스트
- [x] `ruff check`(CI 대상) 통과
- [x] `test_chat_explain.py` · `test_llm_guard.py` 55 통과(재실행) · `test_chat_tools.py` 포함 101 통과
- [x] 돌연변이 — 정의의 「뺀」을 「더한」으로 바꾸면 IT-CHAT-100 실패
- [ ] 사람의 원문 대조(인쇄면) — PR 머지와 별개로 남는다

body:
## Por qué se seguían borrando
Con #44 los celulares con la versión nueva ya no pisaban los barrios. Pero un celular con el panel abierto desde antes (por ejemplo, el de la impresora) sigue corriendo la versión vieja hasta que se recarga. Esa versión reescribía la lista vieja de barrios cada vez que se guardaba cualquier ajuste guardado en el mismo lugar: sopas, proteínas, agotados, eliminar un pedido, etc.

Además, si guardar un barrio fallaba, el panel lo quitaba sin mostrar ningún error.

Lo reproduje en el navegador con un Supabase simulado: sin tabla, el barrio agregado desaparece cuando otro celular guarda ajustes con la lista vieja.

## Qué cambia
- **Tabla propia `zones` (`app/supabase/barrios.sql`, ejecutar una vez):**
  - Cada barrio es un registro aparte. Agregar, cambiar el precio o quitar toca solo ese barrio, así que ningún otro guardado, venga de la versión que venga, puede deshacerlo.
  - Al crearla se llena con los barrios que tiene hoy el panel, en el mismo orden. Si nunca se configuraron, usa la lista original de 28.
  - Recupera los barrios que tienen pedidos y se habían perdido, con el último nombre y precio cobrado. Deja fuera "Otro" y los nombres repetidos.
  - Volver a ejecutar el archivo no cambia nada: no revive barrios quitados a propósito.
  - Permisos: cualquiera la lee (los clientes ven los barrios) y solo el dueño la cambia.
  - Se agregó a Realtime, así que los cambios llegan en vivo a todos los celulares.
  - `schema.sql` incluye lo mismo para proyectos nuevos.
- **App (`supabaseStore`):**
  - Lee los barrios de la tabla, y cada barrio se agrega, cambia o quita de forma individual.
  - Mientras no se haya ejecutado el SQL, sigue usando la lista anterior, como hoy.
- **Panel:** si guardar un barrio falla, muestra el error en vez de desaparecerlo.

## Pruebas
- Build y lint limpios, 53 pruebas unitarias.
- **Pruebas SQL:**
  - Anónimo y cliente pueden leer los barrios pero no agregar, cambiar ni quitar.
  - El dueño agrega, cambia el precio y quita.
  - Guardar otros ajustes con una lista vieja adentro no toca los barrios.
- **Migración sobre una copia del esquema actual,** con 2 barrios en los ajustes y pedidos de un barrio perdido, un "Otro" y un nombre repetido:
  - Quedan los 2 barrios en su orden más los 2 recuperados, con su último precio.
  - Al volver a ejecutarla, no revive un barrio quitado.
- **Navegador con Supabase simulado:**
  - Con la tabla, el barrio agregado sigue ahí después de que un celular viejo reescribe los ajustes, y un fallo al guardar muestra el error.
  - Sin la tabla, la app sigue funcionando como antes.

## Paso manual
Después de unir, ejecutar **una vez** `app/supabase/barrios.sql` en Supabase → SQL Editor.

body:
## Résumé
- **Pourquoi « que peux-tu faire ? » tombait dans « Pouvez-vous préciser ? Je n'ai pas trouvé de résultat »** :
  - `usesGeneralConversation` n'acceptait que les phrases débutant par une liste très courte (`comment `, `pourquoi `, `qu'est-ce que `, `quelle est `), et `conversationalRequest` ne gérait que `bonjour` et `merci`.
  - Du coup, `que peux tu faire ?` était envoyé à `searchSpotlight` comme s'il s'agissait du nom d'un salarié, renvoyait 0 fiche et affichait le message d'échec de recherche.
- **Ce que corrige cette PR** :
  1. **Réponses conversationnelles naturelles sur le rôle et les capacités de l'assistant (`src/services/assistantConversation.js`)** :
     - Gère naturellement `que peux-tu faire ?`, `tu fais quoi ?`, `qui es-tu ?`, `à quoi tu sers ?`, `comment tu fonctionnes ?`, `peux-tu m'aider ?`, ainsi que les échanges courants (`comment ça va ?`, `ça va ?`, `ok`, `d'accord`, `super`, `au revoir`, `bonne journée`).
  2. **Réponses conversationnelles sur les modules En-Check (`src/services/assistantDialogue.js` & `src/services/assistantExplanation.js`)** :
     - Explications naturelles sur les **pauses** (planifiées, hors planning, temps réel), les **plannings** et les **absences/congés** avec raccourci direct vers la page concernée.
     - Élargissement des formulations naturelles comprises pour les explications métier (`c'est quoi une sortie présumée ?`, `comment tu calcules les retards ?`, `c'est quoi le nombre de pointages ?`).
  3. **Routeur conversationnel élargi (`src/services/assistantRouting.js` & `src/components/AssistantDock.jsx`)** :
     - Prise en charge des formulations conversationnelles ouvertes (`que ...`, `quel ...`, `peux-tu ...`, `pouvez-vous ...`, `est-ce que ...`, `propose ...`, `rédige ...`, `résume ...`, `conseille ...`) et des relances dans un fil général actif (`history.length > 0`).
     - Remplacement du message rigide *« Pouvez-vous préciser ? Je ne peux pas encore répondre librement à tous les sujets »* par une réponse conversationnelle fluide.

## Vérifications
- `npm test` (31 fichiers, 268 tests passés)
- `node --test tests/edge/*.mjs` (55 tests passés)
- `npx eslint src/components/AssistantDock.jsx src/services/assistantConversation.js src/services/assistantDialogue.js src/services/assistantExplanation.js src/services/assistantRouting.js`
- `npx eslint src --config eslint.gate.config.js`
- `npm run build`

author: apple-df
body:
## 变更摘要

修 Android 出包链路的三处独立问题，并同步文档。

### 1. 版本比较改为归一后再比

`requirements.txt` 是 uv 导出的 PEP 440 拼写（`maafw==5.15.0b1`），而内核 tag 与 MaaFramework release tag 是发布原文（`3.13.15-maafw5.15.0-beta.1` / `v5.15.0-beta.1`）。原来三处都按字符串精确比较，预发布钉版会被判成「内核还没发配对」而降级回上一个正式版，下载地址还会拼成不存在的版本。

新增 `maafwVersionKey()` 把三种拼写归一到同一 key，接入三处：

| 位置 | 原来 | 现在 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `pickPackagingCore` 精确配对 | `pairings.includes(requested)` | 归一 key 比对 |
| `coreTagFor` tag 匹配 | 正则转义做字面匹配 | 归一 key 比对 |
| `AGENT_CORE_TAG` / `maa-project.json` 一致性 | 字符串不等即告警 | 归一 key 比对 |

顺带移除不再使用的 `escapeRegExp()`。

### 2. 出包前按 lock 重导 requirements.txt

依赖变更（Dependabot 的 uv 更新）只改 `uv.lock`，而 `sync:runtime` 与 APK 的 `build_agent_bundle.py` 都从导出的 `requirements.txt` 装依赖。不重导就会拿旧钉版出包，**且不会有任何报错**。

`release.yml` 的 `package` job 与 `android-build.yml` 的 `build` / `abi-split` 两个 job 在消费 `requirements.txt` 之前跑 `uv export --frozen`；`pyproject` 与 lock 不一致时直接失败，不静默用旧 lock。

`android-build.yml` 的两个 job 原先没有 `setup-uv`，一并补上。

### 3. Android 包关闭前台模式

前台模式在手机主屏上跑，屏幕实际分辨率与比例和 720P 资源对不上。改为 `foreground: false`：`MAFW_FOREGROUND_ALLOWED` 随之为 false，首页不再渲染运行模式开关，已存的前台设置回落到后台。`presets` 只留与 PI controller 的 `display_short_side: 720` 一致的那一档。

**代价**：只剩后台虚拟屏，`BackgroundModePrecheck` 在 API 29 以下直接 Block，Android 10 以下的机器跑不起来。

### 4. 文档同步

- `docs/*/develop/android.md`：把「前台/后台两种模式」改写成「只提供后台模式」，说明关掉前台的原因与代价
- `docs/*/manual/newbie.md`：系统要求从 Android 9.0 改为 Android 10，Android 用户备注补一句「只提供后台模式」

## 影响范围

| 文件 | 改动 |
| :--- | :--- |
| `tools/android-packaging.mjs` | +58/−22，版本归一 |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | +5，重导 requirements |
| `.github/workflows/android-build.yml` | +12，重导 + setup-uv |
| `Android/profile.yaml` | +10/−4，关闭前台模式 |
| `docs/{zh,en}/develop/android.md` | 运行模式章节重写 |
| `docs/{zh,en}/manual/newbie.md` | 系统要求表 |
| `maa-project.lock.json` | 受管文件基线 |

不影响桌面端出包、pipeline、资源包与 agent 代码。

**用户可见**：Android 包不再提供前台模式，系统版本要求提高到 Android 10（API 29）。

## 验证

- `maafwVersionKey` 8 条用例全部通过：`5.15.0-beta.1` / `5.15.0b1` / `v5.15.0b1` → `5.15.0b1`；`5.15.0-rc.2` / `5.15.0-rc2` → `5.15.0rc2`；`5.15.0-alpha.1` → `5.15.0a1`；正式版 `5.14.2` / `v5.14.2` → `5.14.2`
- `node tools/android-packaging.mjs` 在本仓库输出 `3.13.15-maafw5.14.2` / `v5.14.2`，无降级、无 warning
- 两个 workflow 经 PyYAML 解析通过，job 结构不变（`android-build.yml`: library-resources / build / abi-split；`release.yml`: package / git_cliff / android-apks / release）
- `pnpm check` → exit 0
- `pnpm docs:build` → 渲染 58 页成功

## 检查清单

- [x] 我已阅读并遵守 `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [x] PR 范围清晰，没有混入无关格式化或重构
- [x] 用户可见行为或流程变化已同步文档
- [x] 我没有提交本地缓存、构建产物、调试文件或大体积模型文件

## Sourcery 总结

修复 Android 打包版本解析和依赖同步问题，并统一采用后台模式进行 Android 打包。

Bug Fixes:
- 在选择配对的 Android 核心版本以及验证版本一致性时，统一 MaaFW 版本的拼写形式，避免预发布版本发生错误回退并生成无效的制品 URL。

Enhancements:
- 禁用 Android 前台模式，并统一使用 720P 虚拟后台显示器进行打包；将最低支持的 Android 版本提升至 10。

Build:
- 在发布和 Android 打包任务开始前，根据冻结的 uv 锁文件重新导出 requirements.txt；如果项目依赖与锁文件不一致，则任务失败。

CI:
- 在 Android 构建任务中添加 uv 环境配置，以便在打包时导出依赖。

Documentation:
- 更新 Android 开发文档和新手文档，说明应用仅在后台运行，并注明 Android 10 是最低要求。

Chores:
- 更新 Maa 项目锁文件的基线。

<details>
<summary>Original summary in English</summary>

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix Android packaging version resolution and dependency synchronization while standardizing the Android package on background mode.

Bug Fixes:
- Normalize MaaFW version spellings when selecting paired Android cores and validating version consistency, preventing incorrect fallback and invalid artifact URLs for pre-release versions.

Enhancements:
- Disable Android foreground mode and standardize packaging on a 720P virtual background display, raising the minimum supported Android version to 10.

Build:
- Re-export requirements.txt from the frozen uv lockfile before release and Android packaging jobs, failing when project dependencies and the lockfile diverge.

CI:
- Add uv setup to Android build jobs so dependency exports are available during packaging.

Documentation:
- Update Android development and newcomer documentation to describe background-only operation and the Android 10 minimum requirement.

Chores:
- Update the Maa project lockfile baseline.

</details>

author: vladroja
body:
## Defecto detectado en producción
`SR_MANTENIMIENTO` heredaba `can_schedule=True` del permiso de ejecución PM (`can_pm_execute`); podía reprogramar por botón, drag & drop y PUT directo `/api/maintenance-planner/tickets/:id/schedule`. También las rutas legacy `PUT /api/tickets/update/:id` y `PUT /api/tickets/compromiso/:id` aceptaban fecha compromiso para SR.

## Cambio
- `backend/app/maintenance_planner/service.py::_can_schedule_maintenance`: distingue programación de ejecución PM; roles `SR_MANTENIMIENTO`, `AUX_MANTENIMIENTO`, `TECNICO` quedan sin programación, manteniendo lectura/ejecución. `COORDINADOR_MANTENIMIENTO` y `COMPRAS` con grant explícito y sucursales mantienen programación; administradores también. `MANTENIMIENTO` conserva el flujo legacy de diagnóstico estructurado para no romperlo.
- `backend/app/utils/tickets_maintenance_permissions.py`: un grant incidental no habilita a SR/AUX/TECNICO para coordinar.
- `backend/app/utils/maintenance_ticket_update_guard.py`: bloquear `fecha_solucion` y alteraciones del historial de fechas por las rutas legacy de Tickets para usuarios sin permiso de coordinación, sin bloquear cambios de estado puramente técnicos.
- Frontend: `can_schedule=false` oculta botón Cambiar fecha, deshabilita CDK drag y bloquea drop a nivel método; textos aclaran permiso de programación y no invitan a arrastrar a usuarios de lectura.

## Regresión/seguridad
- Pruebas negativas con SR: permiso de programación `False`, `schedule_ticket` 403 sin mutación ni query, board visible pero no programable, legacy PUT fecha/historial 403, incluso grant incidental.
- Prueba positiva: SR mantiene `can_pm_execute` y actualización técnica de estado sin fecha.
- Pruebas positivas para coordinación de Yuliana y conservación de flujo legacy MANTENIMIENTO.
- Guardas estáticas frontend de las tres entradas: fecha inicial, botón y arrastre.

No requiere migración. No desplegar automáticamente en producción.

body: ## Summary Portal checks included every open application in Applied or Interviewing, even when that application's organization had no career portal to open. A null, empty, or whitespace-only careers URL is now treated as no portal, so those applications are left out of the check. Applications that have a portal, including a URL with only surrounding whitespace, are still checked on the same interval as before. Offers and closed applications stay out of the check. body:
## Summary

- Each language Lymi writes in its own format now publishes it from one core export, `LanguageOut`: a public, cacheable `GET /api/languages`, a `languages` map in MCP `list_decks` for the learner's deck languages (plus one INSTRUCTIONS line), `/docs/languages` built at site build time, and the enrichment guide's pronunciation and example lines. The `pronunciation` and `example` schema descriptions point to that format instead of naming languages. Supported-languages slice 4b.
- Korean becomes a configured language: pronunciation is the pronounced form in Hangul only where it differs from the spelling (학교 → 학꾜), replacing Revised Romanization; notes give Sino-Korean roots (學 학: 학생, 학년) and are on by default for Korean decks; Korean speech now uses a native ElevenLabs voice by default: Hyunbin, chosen from the library's native Korean voices (see Voice choice).
- Enrichment prompt v6, with before-and-after recorded runs over 12 new Korean fixtures: v5 793/815, v6 842/845. Korean pronunciation goes from 5/14 to 14/14 (text) and 1/4 to 4/4 (empty); notes filled from 14/19 to 19/19. The one remaining Korean miss gives 聯 for 연락's root instead of the standard 連.

## Screenshots

![The docs page, built from the language records](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1495dcd4-d55f-4702-a61b-c090a479f6e3)

![A Korean card enriched locally, after the reveal: 학꾜 and its roots](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f8cd5cc8-8adf-4cb3-a937-3b3492c0e9da)

## Voice choice

Six native Korean ElevenLabs library voices, each run through Lymi's settings (eleven_v4, stability 1) on ten words with sound changes: 학교, 학년, 국물, 같이, 좋다, 읽다, 신라, 연락, 맛있어요 and 사랑. Logged out, the library lists only its top three voices per sort, so these are the most-used native voices plus the newest; this API key lacks `voices_read`, so nothing past that was searchable.

| Voice | Accent | Words recovered by gpt-4o-transcribe / whisper-1 | Loudness across words (LUFS) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Hyunbin** (chosen) | Seoul, ElevenLabs high-quality tier | 10/10 · 10/10 | −17.6 to −21.8 |
| Chris (listed before, never default) | Seoul, high-quality tier | 10/10 · 10/10 | −22.7 to −28.5 |
| Anna Kim | Seoul, high-quality tier | 9/10 · 9/10 (사랑 heard as 사람) | −17.8 to −24.6 |
| Hyuk | standard, high-quality tier | 9/10 · 9/10 (사랑 heard as 사람) | −17.8 to −22.4 |
| Apollo | standard, community | 10/10 · 10/10 | −21.9 to −27.3 |
| Minchul | standard, community | 10/10 · 10/10 | −17.9 to −23.5 |

Hyunbin is a Seoul speaker, every word came back right from both transcribers, and its level is the most even, so one Korean word is not noticeably quieter than the next. Kateryna listened to Hyunbin and Chris on 학교, 학년, 국물 and 같이 and kept Hyunbin.

## Instrumentation

Question: does Korean's new prompt hold up, that is, do learners keep the pronounced Hangul and roots the AI writes? `enrichment_finished` (Worker, `services/enrichment.ts`) and `ai_text_corrected` (Worker, `services/cards.ts`) gain an optional `languages`: the sorted primary subtags of the cards that gained text or were corrected, up to 20, never text. Read with `prompt_version`, Korean corrections can be compared before and after v6. A failed run and a run with no landed field leave it out; existing chart properties are unchanged. Unit tests cover the enriched and corrected paths (`services/enrichment.test.ts`, `services/cards.test.ts`); documented in `docs/analytics.md`. `GET /api/languages` reuses the request metric every route already writes, and `list_decks` reuses `mcp_tool`, so neither needs a new event.

## Verification

- `pnpm verify:changed`: all web tests pass. Its two unhandled `oauth_resource` errors came from the new route test, which made requests before any sign-up and let Better Auth's background seeding race; it now signs up first, and the race no longer reproduces. `routes/add.test.ts` timed out locally under heavy load and passes 7/7 with a longer timeout.
- `pnpm deploy:check`: passes
- `pnpm test:e2e:chromium`: 84 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed: `writes-offline.spec.ts`, the known offline-writes flake being fixed separately
- Local request: `GET /api/languages` without a session answers 200 with `cache-control: public, max-age=3600` and ja, zh, ko.
- `/docs/languages` rendered on the local site (screenshot above).
- Verify skill, new `korean` feature, PASS with no console errors or 5xx: `/tmp/lymi-evidence/kateryna-language-format-and-korean/korean-local-e16888ba, before the rebase` (local, real enrichment).
- `apps/web/src/server/ai/speech.test.ts` routes `ko-KR` to ElevenLabs with Hyunbin first; every candidate voice generated all ten clips through the AI Gateway.
- Frozen phone contracts and `check:cache-shape` pass in `verify:changed`; the change adds a route and an MCP field only.

## Follow-ups

- The Chinese record must carry the new `format` field when zh moves out of the configured table; a pinyin engine adds its `EXAMPLE_NOTATION` entry.
- A fluent reader should review Korean's guide text, as the proposal asks for each prompt.

author: mrucker
body:
Stacked on #4: review and merge that first, then this PR will retarget to `main`.

## What

Each release now uploads **three zips**:

| Asset | Contents |
|---|---|
| `protocol.zip` | Unchanged: everything, exactly as the app downloads it today |
| `media.zip` | All images, videos and audio (`jpe?g png gif webp svg mp4 m4v mov webm mp3 m4a wav ogg`) at their release paths, plus `media-cache.tsv` |
| `text.zip` | Everything else (JSON etc.) |

Together, `text.zip` and `media.zip` hold exactly the same files as `protocol.zip`. That leaves the app free to download them separately later and skip unchanged media.

**Reusing processed media.** Before processing, the action:

1. Hashes (SHA-256) each image over 100 KiB and each `.mp4`, using the files' actual content. Callers may modify files before the action runs, so git's hashes aren't used. This takes about 0.4s for leia's 824 MB.
2. Downloads `media.zip` from the newest earlier non-draft release that has one (it checks the 30 most recent). It uses that zip only if its `media-cache.tsv` was written by a byte-identical `action.yml`, so any change to the action, settings included, causes a full reprocess.
3. Copies the already-processed file for every unchanged image or video and processes only the rest. Restored files are never re-encoded.
4. Installs vips and/or ffmpeg only if something is left to process.

Other changes:
- The two rename steps are now plain bash, so the `rename` package is no longer installed.
- **New input `reuse_media`** (default `'true'`). Set it to `'false'` to always process everything; `media.zip` is still built.

## Tested with real releases

The test used a private throwaway repo, `digital-trails/protocol-leia-test`: a copy of protocol-leia 0.5.2 whose workflow points at this branch.

| Release | Scenario | Reused | Processed | Job time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| test-1 | Cold, no earlier `media.zip` | 0 | 538 images + 4 videos | 2m59s |
| test-2 | Nothing changed | **542** | none; vips/ffmpeg not installed | **36s** |
| test-3 | 1 image altered, 1 video trimmed, `Added.JPG` added | 540 | 2 images + 1 video | 1m28s |
| test-4 | `action.yml` changed (comment only) | 0: earlier cache correctly rejected | 539 images + 4 videos | 2m35s |

Each release's downloaded assets were checked:
- **Every release:** `text.zip` + `media.zip` equal `protocol.zip` exactly (same 8,898–8,899 files, same bytes), and every `media-cache.tsv` entry is present in `media.zip`.
- **test-2 vs test-1:** all 8,898 files byte-identical.
- **test-3 vs test-2:** exactly three files differ (`images/190.jpeg`, `images/added.jpg`, `videos/video3.mp4`). The new upper-case image came out lower-case and resized (650x975).
- **test-4 (fresh) vs test-3 (cached):** all 8,899 files byte-identical, so a reused file is exactly what fresh processing would produce.

## Notes / risks

- **When anything changed, install time dominates.** In test-3, installing vips + ffmpeg took 39s against about 7s of processing.
- **The first release after upgrading is a full run,** because no earlier release has a `media.zip` yet. The same applies after any change to `action.yml`.
- **About 40 MB extra upload and storage per release for leia,** since `media.zip` + `text.zip` duplicate `protocol.zip`'s contents.
- **The cache trusts earlier releases' `media.zip`.** Replacing it by hand needs repo write access. Cache paths containing `..` are ignored.
- **Each release page now shows `media.zip` and `text.zip`.** If anything enumerates release assets rather than fetching `protocol.zip` by name, check it.

body:
« Une histoire de transparence avec le thème qui passe par-dessus » — la feuille des amis ouverte depuis l'accueil, sous Le Sommet, au téléphone Android (le retour du propriétaire du 19 octobre 2026 ; précisé ensuite : « le décor reste visible à travers la feuille, tant qu'elle est ouverte »).

## 1. Une feuille ouverte retire le décor du thème (le bug signalé)

**Cause.** Le décor d'un thème vit dans des couches fixes plein écran (`html::before`, `body::before`, `body::after`, `#root::before`, `#root::after`). Sous Le Sommet : la montagne, ses lanternes, ses drapeaux, le voile de nuit et la neige — cinq grands calques, animés pour la plupart, à la densité du téléphone. Ils prennent la mémoire des tuiles ; la feuille ouverte par-dessus n'en a plus : Chrome ne la dessine pas, ou à moitié, et le décor reste à sa place.

**Reproduit** dans Chromium, carte graphique émulée (SwiftShader) et mémoire graphique bornée à celle d'un téléphone (`--force-gpu-mem-available-mb=64`, 412 × 915 à la densité 2,625 — environ 115 Mo à la densité 3,5) : une seconde après le toucher, la feuille n'était pas dessinée du tout (l'accueil et la montagne à sa place), à 24 Mo à moitié ; Velours, au même budget, la dessinait entière. Le Chromium sans écran des rendus, qui a toute la mémoire qu'il veut, ne le montrait pas.

**Correction** (`client/src/styles.css`) : tant qu'une feuille, une carte, un dialogue ou le coffre est ouvert (`.carte-voile`, `.dialog-backdrop`, `.coffre-scene`), ces couches se retirent :

```css
:root[data-theme]:has(.carte-voile, .dialog-backdrop, .coffre-scene)::before,
… body::before, … body::after, … #root::before, … #root::after { content: none !important; }
```

Assombri aux trois quarts par le voile et couvert presque partout, le décor ne s'y voyait guère ; il revient à la fermeture. Rejoué au même budget de 64 Mo : la feuille entière, le haut de l'écran assombri ; à 48 Mo, tout est dessiné en 2,5 s. Les 35 thèmes photographiés (feuille et carte d'un ami) : rien d'étrange sans le décor.

## 2. La carte d'un ami ne laisse plus lire la liste au travers

Sous **25 thèmes sur 35**, la carte d'un ami — touchée dans la feuille — était translucide : on lisait la liste au travers (« Un prénom… », Zoé, Tom). Un dialogue (`Dialog.tsx`), de même. Chaque thème repeint `.card` d'un sélecteur (0,3,0) plus fort que le sol de la carte (0,2,0) et d'un dialogue (0,1,0), d'un verre de 82 % (Neige) à 95 % (les Heures, l'Horloge, la Plage) ; le 5 octobre, seule la carte **à fond** en avait été écartée.

```css
:root .card.dialog:not(.carte-fond) { background-color: var(--bg-raised); }
```

Le sol seul se reprend : dégradé, fêlures, bordure et ombre du thème restent. Mesuré dans Chromium thème par thème : fond plein sous les 35.

## Tests

`server/test/feuilles.test.ts`, deux épreuves, qui échouaient avant leur correction :
- aucune règle de thème ne repeint le sol d'un dialogue ou de la carte d'un joueur aussi fort que lui, aucune celui d'une feuille ; `--bg` et `--bg-raised` pleins partout (« aurore.css : … (300) repeint le sol d'un dialogue, plus fort que lui (100) ») ;
- toute couche fixe d'un thème est de celles qui se retirent sous une feuille ouverte (« la règle qui retire le décor sous .carte-voile, .dialog-backdrop, .coffre-scene »).

Tests voisins verts (`feuilles`, `fonds`, `design`, `themes`, `maintenance`, `loge`, `decors-peints`, `notes-pour-claude`, `documentation`, `emojis`), typage vert ; `npm run verify` relancé sur le dernier commit.

## Documenté

Les pièges dans `.claude/rules/css.md` et `.claude/rules/themes.md` ; la recette pour rejouer la mémoire d'un téléphone dans la skill `regarder-le-rendu` ; la ligne de `feuilles.test.ts` dans `docs/contribuer/tests.md`.

The owner (2026-10-19, q_dffcd44d): Tynn answers every failed auth with the
404 a path that does not exist gets, so attackers cannot probe what exists
(Tynn #827). Genie read only 401/419 as "the session is gone"; with Tynn
answering 404, an expired session would have shown as a string of errors with
Genie still claiming to be signed in.

A 404 is ambiguous on purpose, so TynnAccount.request() does not guess: a 404
while signed in asks /api/v1/me once. It answers who the session belongs to
(still signed in: the 404 was a path that is not there), or Genie shows signed
out. Tynn unreachable for that check leaves the state unchanged. 401/419 keep
their meaning, so this is safe before and after Tynn changes.

Tests first, seen red on omarchy-test (a 404 from an ended session left Genie
signed in and never asked /me); CONTROL: a 404 for a missing path with the
session live stays signed in. Full suite on omarchy-test: typecheck 0, 592

author: kodaksax
body:
## Summary

The sign-up form's live username check could never see a taken name. `isUsernameUnique` queried `profiles` directly, but every `profiles` SELECT policy is own-row only (`auth.uid() = id`) on **staging and production** (checked read-only). Signed out at sign-up, and signed in during onboarding, the query returned no row and no error, so every name showed "@x is available". `/auth/register` then answered 409 "Username already taken", and the form showed both messages at once. 3 of 6 agents hit this in the 19 Oct Shoal `poster-conversion` run (follow-up from SBA-06, review PR #931).

## Changes

1. **`public.is_username_available(text)`**: new migration `20261019195723_is_username_available.sql`, named after the production ledger version; staging recorded `20261019194109`, and the header notes both.
   - `SECURITY DEFINER`, `SET search_path = ''`, `STABLE`.
   - Compares case-insensitively (`lower(username)`), matching register's rule.
   - Ignores the caller's own row (`auth.uid()`), so a signed-in user re-checking their current name sees it as free.
   - Returns `NULL` for malformed input (not 3–24 of `[A-Za-z0-9_]`), so "can't be a username" is never confused with taken or free.
   - `REVOKE ALL … FROM PUBLIC`, then `GRANT EXECUTE` to `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role` explicitly.
   - It reveals only whether a name exists. That is already public (profiles, bounty cards) and already answered by register's 409, so the only change is when the answer arrives.
   - It also adds `idx_profiles_username_lower` with `IF NOT EXISTS`. Production already has it, so it's a no-op there; staging didn't.
2. **RLS manifest:** a new `is_username_available(text)` entry (`forbid_execute: [PUBLIC]`, `require_execute: [anon, authenticated]`). `scripts/rls-policy-check/rules.js` gains `require_execute`, so a future "revoke from anon" hardening pass fails CI instead of quietly re-breaking sign-up.
3. **Client** (`lib/services/userProfile.ts`): `isUsernameUnique` calls the RPC first. If the RPC is missing (a backend without the migration) or returns `NULL`, the old direct query and local fallback run as before, so nothing is worse on any backend.
4. **Sign-up form:** a 409 "username taken" flips the live hint to "taken", so the form can no longer show "available" under a "taken" banner.
5. **`/auth/register`:** its `.ilike()` now escapes `_`. Unescaped, `_` is a wildcard, so `jo_n` matched an existing `john` and was refused after the live check had said it was free. `.limit(1)` stops `.maybeSingle()` erroring (500) if case variants of a name both exist; the unique index is case-sensitive.

**Ships server-first.** Old builds keep their old (blind) behaviour, and nothing breaks for them. The client change is **OTA-safe** (JS only, no fingerprint inputs) and rides the 2.1.3 build or the first OTA after it.

## Deploy order (please read before merging)

| Step | Staging | Production |
|---|---|---|
| Migration | ✅ `20261019194109`, verified | ✅ `20261019195723`, applied 2026-10-19 on "go" and verified |
| `auth` Edge Function | not deployed | deploys automatically on merge, **but see below** |

**Production RLS check is red on `main` for a different reason.** `function search_bounties_nearby(…8 args…) is missing`: SBA-02's migration `20261019210000` is on staging only. The same single failure appears on `main`'s 18:42Z run, before this PR. On this branch (dispatch run 39315423035) it is still the **only** failure, and the new `is_username_available` entry passes. Because `deploy-edge-functions.yml` runs that check before deploying, **Edge Function auto-deploys from `main` stay blocked**, including this PR's `auth` change, until `20261019210000` is applied to production. The RPC and the client change don't depend on the `auth` deploy.

## Testing

- [x] **Staging, as the real client roles** (one transaction, rolled back):
  - signed out: existing name → `false`; the same name in UPPERCASE → `false`; fresh name → `true`; `a b` / `ab` → `NULL`;
  - signed out, raw `profiles` rows visible → **0** (the old bug, reproduced);
  - the owner checking their own name → `true`; another signed-in user checking it → `false`;
  - grants: `anon`, `authenticated`, `service_role`, **no PUBLIC**; `prosecdef = true`; `search_path=""`.
- [x] `node scripts/check-rls-policies.js` against staging: **OK, live policies match the manifest.** The two "baseline entry no longer present" warnings were already there.
- [x] Unit tests:
  - `username-uniqueness.test.ts`: a taken name reads as taken even when the caller can't read that profile; a free name reads free (trimmed); `NULL` falls back. The existing fallback tests run against a mock that answers like a backend without the RPC (PGRST202).
  - `rls-policy-check.test.ts`: losing a `require_execute` grant fails the check.
  - `sign-up-failure-analytics.test.tsx`: a 409 username flips the hint to taken. **It fails with the fix removed.**
- [x] `npm test`: 434 suites, 5,784 tests pass.
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` / `npm run lint`: no new problems. The same 9 tsc errors and 2 lint errors (`app/bounty/[id]/cancel.tsx`) exist on `main`.
- [x] `deno check supabase/functions/auth/index.ts`: passes.

## Done when

1. ✅ **Done 2026-10-19.** Production, read-only, as the real roles. Signed out: an existing name, and the same name in uppercase, → `false`; fresh → `true`; malformed → `NULL`; the old direct query sees 0 rows. The owner sees their own name → `true`; another user → `false`. Grants are `anon`, `authenticated` and `service_role`, no PUBLIC; `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path=""`. To re-check:
   ```sql
   BEGIN READ ONLY;
   SET LOCAL ROLE anon;
   SELECT public.is_username_available((SELECT username FROM public.profiles LIMIT 1)) AS existing_should_be_false,
          public.is_username_available('zz_no_such_user_8841') AS fresh_should_be_true;
   ROLLBACK;
   ```
   (`SET LOCAL ROLE anon` hides the `profiles` row from the inner SELECT; run the inner SELECT first as the service role and paste the name in.)
2. **The RLS check passes on production** (`rls-policy-check.yml`, production job). The new entry already passes; the job turns green once SBA-02's `20261019210000` is on production (see above).
3. **PostHog:** `auth_signup_failed` with `reason = 'username_taken'` falls to ~0. Baseline for the last 60 days is 11 failures: **10 from Shoal** (Windows, headless) and **1 real user** (Android). The real-user count is tiny; the clearer signal is the next Shoal `poster-conversion` run showing no "available, then taken" finding.

## Affected areas

- [x] Authentication / Onboarding
- [x] Infrastructure / Config (migration, RLS manifest and checker, Edge Function)

## Security checklist

- [x] No secrets or credentials committed
- [x] User input is sanitised before use or storage (format-checked in SQL; parameterised)
- [x] No new sensitive data written to logs
- [x] RLS / auth guards in place for any new data access. The RPC returns one boolean and no row data; it is `SECURITY DEFINER` with an empty `search_path`, has no PUBLIC grant, and its required grants are pinned in the manifest.
