Clerk sign-in returns to `app.vaettir.app/projects?__clerk_synced=false`, then fails with the edge's 502 response. A sanitized live runtime probe confirmed that Next generates the exact Clerk satellite handshake with an HTTP return URL after TLS termination, and the edge rejects that handshake endpoint.

Restore the HTTPS forwarded context before Clerk runs, only for cryptographically attested bodyless workspace requests. Permit document GET redirects to the exact `clerk.vaettir.app/v1/client/handshake` endpoint with one absolute HTTPS return to the requesting workspace and path. Preserve cookie directives and private caching controls; reject other provider paths, tenant returns, ambiguous parameters, API requests and writes. Existing auth protection, pending sessions and POST body streams are preserved.

Validation: web TypeScript and changed-source lint pass; 20 targeted checks pass across the installed Clerk SDK handshake, signed ingress, actual middleware handler and edge redirect controls. The SDK fixture forbids network calls. Pinned Wrangler 4.151.1 entry-only dry run passes. Full exact-source [CI 39338099057](https://github.com/Skaldandstone/Vaettir/actions/runs/39338099057) passed, including production artifacts and historical upgrade/restore gates. The original 1,449,941-byte job log is retained locally with SHA-256 d4a09a995d02aa79d8b64b0a37313ca85b184bb4730e5e8c6fda51494efdf54a. Deployed as immutable Web54 (image 8e7a03fa89f0db91accb9695e6eb1a02010add6c43bbb81c0ae66b5b9b4cf517), with all 50 layers, 642 native tuples and 133 static files verified. API52/b766 is unchanged. The matching entry Worker was deployed with existing secret bindings retained. Actual Chrome sign-in succeeded at app.vaettir.app, and Skald sandbox acceptance passed at skaldandstone.vaettir.app: exact owner, synthetic project, foreign-workspace refusal, reload, full sign-out and fresh Google sign-in. author: majorsilence
body:
## Problems on Android (and any single-view head with a pixel ratio above 1)
1. **No `ToolStrip`/`MenuStrip` drop-down or other popup was visible.**
   - `IWindowBackend.Location` is a screen point in device pixels: it's what `PointToScreen` returns, and `MenuItem.ShowDropDown` places the drop-down with it. `MajorsilenceFormsSingleViewHost` set it directly as `Canvas.Left/Top` on the root Canvas, which uses device-independent units.
   - Every popup therefore landed at `RenderScaling` times its intended position. On a Pixel 7 emulator (scale 2.625), the File menu opened at x = 659 on a screen 411 units wide.
   - Browsers at a pixel ratio of 1 hid this. It is likely also why the combo box drop-down "never showed" (#438).
2. **Dialogs sat at the top left.** `GetScreens` returned nothing on single-view rows (it only knew desktop windows), so a dialog had no screen to centre in.
3. **Drop-downs near a screen edge ran off it** (a toolbar's right-hand Sync menu on a phone).
4. **Message boxes ran off the screen.** `MessageBoxForm` wraps text at 560 units whatever the screen. A phone is about 410 wide, so the box and its buttons ran off the right edge.

## Fixes
- **Popup position:** the single-view `Location` setter converts the screen point through the root's `TopLevel`, the inverse of the host's own `PointToScreen`. The getter still returns the screen point.
- **A screen for single view:** the root host reports itself as the screen. Its bounds are its area in screen coordinates, and its working area is that less the safe area (status bar, cut-outs).
- **Scale before attaching:** a popup or dialog not yet in the visual tree takes the root's scale instead of 1, so its size, and therefore its centring, is right before it is shown.
- **Drop-downs stay on screen:** `MenuDropDown.Show` pulls a drop-down back inside its screen's working area, as WinForms does. `DropDownDirection_places_the_drop_down_on_the_named_side` moves its form off the screen's corner, since it checks direction arithmetic rather than screen edges.
- **Message box width:** `MessageBox` fits the box within the owner's screen (`MessageBoxForm.FitWithin`), never wrapping narrower than 160 units.

## Verified
- **Android 16 emulator (Pixel 7):**
  - In the Gallery's MenuStrip sample, File opens directly under its button, and File > Save updates "Last action: File → Save".
  - In Majorsilence.Recital, the Theme menu opens and applies Sepia, and the bottom bar's menus open upwards.
- **Tests:**
  - `DropDownOnScreenTests`: a right-aligned Sync menu on a 411-wide screen stays on it. Without the fix it spans 357..552.
  - `MessageBoxFitsScreenTests`: on a 411 × 880 headless screen a long message box stays on screen with both buttons inside (it is 548 wide without the fix). A desktop screen keeps the usual width.
  - The main suite passes: 7,952 passed, 4 skipped.

body: ## Summary Rolls the file-metadata header from [001-project-file-metadata-spec](.meta-project/specs/001-project-file-metadata-spec.md) out to every remaining eligible file. Insertion is done by a deterministic script (`tools/metadata/apply-headers.mjs`) so it can be re-run. `check:file-metadata` now **fails when an eligible file has no header**, in addition to rejecting malformed ones. Default clipping behavior is unchanged. Headers are comments / front matter only. ## Kind of change - [x] Other (repo hygiene / metadata) - [x] CI / build - [x] Docs ## Checks - [x] Default clipping behavior is unchanged unless this change is explicitly opt-in - [x] No site-specific hardcoding (domains, selectors, or one-page special cases) - [x] Tests added or updated when behavior changed - [x] Live snapshots considered (or N/A for CI/docs-only work) — N/A: comments/front matter only; live snapshot workflow is not affected ## Safari / Swift - [x] `xcode/**`, `*.swift`, Safari scripts, or the workflows that drive them changed, and the macOS jobs are expected to run Swift files and `xcode/build-safari-app.sh` received comment headers after the Xcode file banner / shebang. Analyze (swift) and the Safari wrapper job must run and pass on this PR. ## What landed - Shared exclusion + eligibility list: `tools/metadata/rules.cjs` (the spec now points here). - Repeatable inserter: `tools/metadata/apply-headers.mjs` (`--dry-run` supported). - `created` / `updated` from git history (first and last commit dates, ISO). `owner` left `""`. `status: adopted` for live files. - Placement after shebang, `'use strict'`, `// @ts-check`, license / Xcode banners; blank line before Go `package`. - CSS uses `/* meta: */` because `//` is not a CSS comment. - `.mjs` / `.cjs` treated as JS; `.ps1` uses `#` comments. ## Files given headers (this PR) 188 existing files via the apply script, plus 2 new tools files written with headers: | usage | count | | --- | ---: | | test | 88 | | source | 76 | | script | 14 (12 applied + apply-headers.mjs + rules.cjs) | | workflow | 4 | | doc | 5 | | config | 3 | 17 files already had valid headers from #18 (spec, templates, SECURITY, two build presets, version/metadata scripts and their tests). Re-running the apply script is a no-op. ## Skipped (grouped) | Reason | count | examples | | --- | ---: | --- | | comment-less format, binary, or lockfile | 67 | `manifest.json`, `package-lock.json`, icons, fonts, `providers.json` | | vendored or minified | 37 | `src/popup/lib/**`, `Readability.js`, `turndown*.js`, `*.min.js` | | Xcode-generated | 20 | `project.pbxproj`, plists, entitlements, storyboard, schemes, xcassets | | GitHub-schema or PR template | 7 | issue forms, `config.yml`, `release.yml`, `dependabot.yml`, `FUNDING.yml`, PR template | | golden markdown fixtures | 6 | `src/tests/fixtures/e2e-markdown/**` (front matter would break snapshot compares) | | license or comment-less dotfile | 5 | `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, `.nvmrc`, `.node-version` | | README.md (all copies) | 4 | root, `native/`, `xcode/`, `src/tests/` | | CHANGELOG.md | 1 | generated narrative | ## Spec changes Only clarifications / gap fixes in `001-project-file-metadata-spec.md`: 1. Authoritative exclusion list is `tools/metadata/rules.cjs`. 2. `check:file-metadata` fails on **missing** headers for eligible files. 3. Parse rule skips shebang, `use strict`, `@ts-check`, and a leading license/Xcode banner; Markdown front matter without `usage` can fall through to ``. 4. `.mjs` / `.cjs` are JS; `.ps1` is a `#` language; CSS must use `/* */`. 5. Golden Markdown under `src/tests/fixtures/e2e-markdown/` is excluded. 6. Xcode-generated extensions and vendored paths are listed explicitly. 7. Every `README.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded, not only the repo-root copies. 8. Folded YAML (`>`) in front matter (Cursor `SKILL.md`) is accepted by the checker. ## JSON sidecars (not in this PR) **Recommendation: do not add sidecars yet**, except maybe later for a short allow-list if we truly need machine-readable metadata on those files. | | | | --- | --- | | **Pros** | Covers `manifest.json`, `package.json`, lockfiles, locale catalogs, `go.mod`, icons without breaking parsers. | | **Cons** | Doubles path count; easy to drift from the real file; AMO / web-ext / Xcode copy steps must ignore `*.meta.yaml` or they leak into packages; little value on generated lockfiles and images. | | **Candidates if we do it later** | `src/manifest.json`, `src/package.json`, `native/go.mod`, maybe `providers.json`. Skip lockfiles, `_locales/**/messages.json` (generated-ish catalogs), and binaries. | ## Build / packaging - Headers are comments. Firefox/Chrome/Safari trees copy them as comments. `web-ext lint` reports 0 errors. - Debug `esbuild` sourcemap rewrite (existing) strips `//` comments, so debug packages do **not** carry JS headers. Release copies keep them. Neither path injects headers into `manifest.json` or concatenated page context. ## Local verification - `npm run check:file-metadata` — 205 headed files, 0 missing - `npm run lint:js`, unit (595), integration (90), `check:version-sync`, `test:build-artifacts` - `web-ext lint -s .build/firefox` — 0 errors - `npm audit` — 0 vulnerabilities - `actionlint` v1.7.12 — clean - `go test ./...` (native) — pass - Playwright Chromium could not be downloaded here (cdn.playwright.dev TLS reset). E2E is deferred to CI. ## Follow-ups - Optional sidecars for the small JSON allow-list above, if we want metadata on manifests. - Preserve comments through the debug esbuild pass if we want headers in debug packages (not required). - Nested READMEs stay excluded; switch them to HTML comments if we want headers without GitHub-special front matter.

author: yogthos
body:
`(Math/atan2 0 0)`, `(Math/log 0)` and `(Math/pow 0 -1)`, and the same calls through `clojure.math`, threw ArithmeticException because the exact argument reached the Chez op unconverted. Only the result was turned into a double. The JVM answers 0.0, ##-Inf and ##Inf. The double-parameter methods now convert their arguments first. floorDiv, floorMod and the *Exact methods keep their long arguments. Both hosts pick this up, since Gambit includes java/math.ss.

Checked against Clojure on the JVM, including Math/pow over exact args, Math/rint of a ratio and clojure.math/floor of a bignum. Two corpus rows were added.

Untyped `(/ x y)` throwing on a 0.0 divisor is unchanged on purpose. Numbers.divide(Object, Object) does the same on the JVM.

author: yhw1630
body:
## Summary

This is platform-integration pi3, the last pp-ledger change before pp-node can run a ledger role (pi4, in pp-browser).

**A role tells its host when it's listening.**
- **Why:** a host's mesh (pp-cpp-mesh `MeshHost`) refuses any open for a protocol nothing serves. So the host should advertise `AmpLedgerServer::protocolIds()` only while the ledger's handlers are actually bound.
- **API:** `Server::setOnListening`, exposed as `RoleRunner::Options::onListening`. It runs on the role's thread:
  - `true` once `startAmpServer` has bound the handlers;
  - `false` at stop, just before the handlers are removed.
- **Restarts:** a restart (a rewind) unbinds and then binds again, so the host sees `false` and then `true`.
- **How pp-node will use it:** advertise on `true`, withdraw on `false`, both through `MeshHost::SetAppProtocols`. The example in `PLATFORM_INTEGRATION.md` shows this wiring.

**pi3 is done.**
- The mesh moved to pp-cpp-mesh v1.0.0. pp-node stayed in pp-browser, as an app on the mesh, rather than moving with it as the design assumed.
- PHASES, DESIGN and CURRENT_STATE are updated to match, and `PLATFORM_INTEGRATION.md` shows the host wiring.
- In passing, the doc said `RoleRunner` is in `pp::server`; it's in `pp`, and the doc now says so.

**Pin:** pp-cpp-common v1.1.0 → v1.2.0, matching pp-browser's pin.

## Test plan

- [x] Build with tests passes; all 626 tests pass. The hosted-relay `RoleRunner` test now checks the host sees exactly `true` then `false`, and that `true` comes once the listener is up.
- [x] Smoke passes: L0, L1, LATEJOIN

Note: building locally, pp-ledger's CMake silently used a stale sibling `../pp-cpp-amp` checkout until I passed `PP_CPP_AMP_SOURCE_DIR`. pp-cpp-mesh deliberately has no sibling fallback; pp-ledger could drop it too.

author: amirali2agh
body:
Closes #30

## Summary

`README.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` were the only entry points for this project
and both were broken: a truncated title, code fences that swallowed prose and
commands, a wrong test count, a completely missing frontend, no environment
reference, and an architecture doc whose JSON blocks were not fenced and whose
board facts had already drifted. This PR rewrites the README and repairs the
architecture reference, then adds the two missing repository documents.

## README

* Title fixed (`ensch` -> `Mensch Multiplayer Game`), broken fences removed.
* Documents **both** halves of the repo: the FastAPI/Redis backend and the
  React/Vite client, with an architecture diagram and a file map.
* Quick start for Docker Compose *and* local development, with prerequisites.
* Full environment-variable table (every key read by `app/config.py`).
* The rules the engine actually enforces: yard/track/home ranges, roll of 6 to
  enter, overshoot rejection, captures, extra roll on 6/capture, three-six rule,
  auto-pass when blocked, win = every piece inside 40..43, 44 unreachable.
* Test gates and the fact that the suite needs no running Redis.
* No hard-coded test count.
* License section carried over from #28.

## ARCHITECTURE.md

* Proper fences and `##` headings throughout (it previously had literal
  `code`/`JSON`/`Bash` lines instead of fences and unclosed blocks).
* Correct board facts: track `0..39`, home `40..43`, yard `-1`, goal `44` is
  never reachable; corner offsets `(20, 30, 0, 10)`; two-player seats on facing
  corners (`track_offsets == [20, 0]`).
* `match_found` documents `pieces_count` as required, matching the server.
* `next_round` described as rematch with the same roster/settings (not as a
  score-preserving new round).
* New sections: chat action, full `sync_state` field reference, reconnect and
  forfeit flow, **Redis key + TTL table**, **error-message table**, and the
  debug-only `/api/dev` surface.
* Stale typo ("o enter the matchmaking queue") and the orphan
  `code`/`Code` block removed.

## New files

* `CONTRIBUTING.md` — branch/PR flow, the four gates, test-first rule for bugs,
  line-ending warning, security rules.
* `docs/deployment.md` — reverse-proxy topology, systemd unit, environment file,
  Caddy example, go-live checklist, upgrade procedure. Host names are examples;
  the real production paths stay out of this public repository.

`.env.example` already existed and already documents every variable, so it was

author: nicolasaunai
body:
## Issue

Relates to #1466: PR 2 of 3, stacked on #1471.

## What this implements

After #1471 the electron velocity uses the charge flux $\sum_s q_s\mathbf{F}_s$. The mass-weighted bulk velocity $\mathbf{V}_i$ and the mass density only feed diagnostics: ion inertia enters the dynamics only through the pusher. Their communication between patches and levels is removed.

## Design

- New fluid diagnostic `charge_flux` for the ions as a whole (h5 and VTK), read by pharesee as `CFx`, `CFy`, `CFz`.
- Removed for $\mathbf{V}_i$: border max, coarsening sync, patch-ghost refill and its old-time copy `ViOld_`.
- Removed the border max of the mass density. The charge density keeps its border max, sync and patch-ghost refill.
- The patch-ghost refill of the charge density is now a plain refiner and `NiOld_` is removed: a same-level schedule never time-interpolates, so the old copy was never read. Both old copies were left over from `fillIonMomentGhosts`, disabled in #1083.

Visible in diagnostics:

- On coarse regions covered by a finer level, the written $\mathbf{V}_i$ is the coarse level's own value, not the coarsened fine one.
- Ghost nodes of $\mathbf{V}_i$ and of the mass density are no longer made consistent between patches.

Names (`charge_flux`, `CFx`) are open to discussion.

## Tests

- `test_field_coarsening_via_subcycles` checks the charge flux instead of the bulk velocity.
- `charge_flux` is in `dump_all_diags`: h5 restart and VTK diagnostics tests write it.
- `test_validation.py`: a per-population `charge_flux` diagnostic is rejected.
- Full debug ctest passes except `py3_diagnostics` and `py3_init-1d-fields`, which fail locally only because the MHD module `cpp_1_Linear_VanLeer_Rusanov_false` is not built.

<!-- /orca-pr-loc -->

## ELI5

If you have a very large pile of agent transcripts (on the order of 150,000 files in one agent's folder), opening the Session History **Workspace** or **Project** tab failed with an error instead of listing your sessions. The code that gathers the candidate files handed the whole list to JavaScript as separate arguments to one call, and JavaScript has a ceiling on how many arguments one call can take. This PR adds the files one at a time instead, so the size of your history no longer matters.

## What Changed

- **Before:** a scoped Session History scan (Workspace or Project tab) over one agent folder with more files than JavaScript's argument ceiling threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` while building its list of candidate files, before any limit or parse cap could apply, so that view showed an error instead of sessions.
- **After:** the same scan lists the in-scope sessions normally. Nothing changes for normal-sized histories: the same files are considered in the same order, and the walk still checks every candidate (no new cap).

Mechanism: `src/main/ai-vault/session-scanner-scope-walk.ts` built its candidate lists with `list.push(...otherList)`. Spreading an array into a call passes every element as a separate argument, which has a hard engine limit. Both sites in that file now append one item per `push`:
- the walk over every discovered file (the reported site, unbounded by design because the Workspace tab must find older sessions past the recency cap);
- the per-folder agent candidates (bounded by the scan limit, but an "unlimited" scan passes no limit, so it is unbounded too).

The same pattern in the session search index's deleted-file sweep (`src/main/ai-vault-search/session-search-deleted-sources.ts`), which hands over every not-yet-checked indexed path at once, now assigns the remaining slice directly. That list can be the whole index when a folder is unmounted, so it has the same ceiling at the same history size.

## Why

The ticket asked for an iterative append that keeps the walk exhaustive, not a cap on how many candidates are considered; a cap would hide older in-scope sessions again, which is the problem #29977 fixed. Per-item appends are already the pattern this codebase uses for the same engine limit in other transcript listings (Codex session file listing, Claude usage transcript discovery). Other `push(...)` sites in the scanner append fixed-size batches or capped issue lists and can't reach the limit.

## Plan and review path

Plan: replace each variadic `push(...list)` that can receive a history-sized list with a per-item append (or a direct assignment where the target is always empty), keep the walk exhaustive and its order unchanged, and pin it with one test above the engine limit.

Review path: **full**. The reviewer rejected the light-path claim because `retireDeletedSessionSearchSources` removes saved search-index rows; the saved-data criterion applies even though the replacement returns the same unchecked paths. The loop includes an independent correctness review, architecture challenge, dedicated performance and compatibility review, CI on the non-draft head, and main-versus-branch Electron QA of Workspace, Project and search.

## Linked Issue

Tracked in STA-11092 (regression from #29977).

## Visual Proof

Full hidden Electron QA passed on M4Air for head `82b02ee72fe5d7ad28c2a900c69a5857ac9228ed` versus main `7e75a86caaa0a01a0e2f95bd04fabc2fdab6917e`, using identical 1,007-transcript input. Workspace, Project and folder lists included the older real session past the recency cap; search, View Log, deletion refresh and a real resumed reply worked. Setup/default tabs matched. [All eighteen paired full-window screenshots and review result](https://github.com/stablyai/orca/pull/30905#issuecomment-6284923554).

## Testing

- New test in `session-scanner-scope-walk.test.ts`: a scoped scan over 200,000 candidate files with one real in-scope Codex rollout. It fails on `main` with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` and passes with this change.
- `session-scanner-scope-walk.test.ts` (8/8) and `session-search-deleted-sources.test.ts` (18/18) pass.
- Full PR workflow: blocked by inherited main tunnel-manager file length and formatting failures in run 39340258655, attempt 2. Formatting fix #30918 merged; tunnel-length fix #30925 is still draft and unmerged. Typecheck did not execute after preflight failed. A successful full workflow on the final integrated head remains required.

- [x] Manually tested through hidden Electron QA on the admitted M4Air machine
- [x] Automated tests added/updated, or explained why not below

## Agent skill upstream boundary

- [x] Not applicable, or this change copies or mechanically translates no upstream skill-installer source, tests, fixtures, registry entries, path tables, comments, or documentation.

## Notes

Platform-independent array handling in the main process; same behavior on macOS, Linux, Windows, WSL and SSH hosts (the scanner runs on the execution host). No saved schema, wire or ordering change; saved search-index retirement keeps the same decisions.

author: varshith-kali
body:
*Issue #, if available:* #4771

*Description of changes:*

Problem: A template with `Resources: {}` passes cfn-lint with exit 0, while CloudFormation `ValidateTemplate` rejects it. E1001 already flags a missing `Resources` key, so the empty section was a false negative in the same rule.

Root cause: The base template schema (`src/cfnlint/data/schemas/other/template/configuration.json`) declares `"required": ["Resources"]` but gives the `Resources` property an unconstrained `{}` schema. Likewise, the Resources section schema used by E3001 (`src/cfnlint/data/schemas/other/resources/configuration.json`) caps at `maxProperties: 500` but sets no lower bound. Neither schema rejects an empty object.

Fix: Add `"minProperties": 1` to the `Resources` property in the base template schema. This makes E1001 fire on `Resources: {}`, consistent with the existing E1001 finding for a missing `Resources` key. The keyword is not mapped in E1001's `rule_set`, so the error is attributed to E1001 itself, matching how `required` and `additionalProperties` violations are reported. Only E1001 consumes this schema, so the blast radius is limited to templates with an empty `Resources` section (which CloudFormation rejects anyway).

Verification:
- Red (before fix): `cfn-lint` on a template with `Resources: {}` exited 0 with no findings.
- Green (after fix): it reports `E1001 expected minimum property count: 1, found: 0` at the `Resources` key and exits 2. A template missing `Resources` still reports `'Resources' is a required property`, and a valid template with a resource still passes clean.
- Tests: updated `test_base_template.py` counts (base.yaml 1 to 2, base_date.yaml 1 to 2, base_null.yaml 2 to 3) and `test_json_schema.py` expectations for the new error; added a `test_empty_resources` regression test. Full unit rule suite: 1943 passed. The module suite failures (missing `defusedxml`, network dependent graph/pricing tests) are pre-existing environment issues, verified identical on the pristine tree. Integration `test_good_templates` passes.

body:
Adds **Graph** to every cluster's Flux section: a layered drawing of the cluster's Flux objects.

- Edges run from what an object needs to the object: `dependsOn` solid, source references (GitRepository, OCIRepository, HelmRepository) dashed. A HelmRelease's HelmChart is not drawn as its own node; its edge resolves through the chart to the repository, the same `FluxObject::source` the object page uses. A `dependsOn` target that does not exist shows as an offline "not found" node.
- Nodes carry the status glyph and colour. Clicking a node opens the object. Arrow keys (or right-click) select one, Enter opens it, Escape clears the selection.
- With a node selected, a panel shows the same object (kind, namespace, name) on every cluster that has it side by side: status, revision, source, dependencies and reason. Values that differ from this cluster's are shown in the warning colour, and clicking a cell opens that cluster's object.
- The layout is pure and lives in `flock_core::flux_graph`. It uses longest-path layers, and a dependency cycle is broken at the edge that closes it. Long edges pass through placeholder slots so they never cross a node. Barycenter sweeps order each layer, with ties broken by key, so the same input always gives the same picture whatever order the objects arrive in.
- The graph page reports the combined Flux watch state, so it shows loading and error states the same way the Flux lists do.

author: rorygraves
body:
Follow-up to K1 (#2045) and D4 (#2051), part of #2044.

**Deleting marker (K1).** Before the first descendant delete, the cascade commits a copy of the root's latest checkpoint with the new `Checkpoint.deleting = true`, under the root's claim (fenced commit, parent = latest). `start`, `recover`, `resume`, `fork` (from it) and `updateState` refuse a marked thread with the new `GraphError.ThreadDeleting` before any claim. `deleteThread` goes ahead on it, and running it again finishes the delete. `updateState` is refused too, because its commit would drop the marker. A thread with no descendants gets no marker.
- Why a checkpoint field and not a store flag (see 4.41): there's no `Checkpointer` SPI change, schema step or contract case, because every store already applies fenced, parent-checked commits atomically and admission already reads the latest checkpoint. A new `CheckpointStatus` would have touched every status match. The field goes into format 8, which hasn't been released yet, so there's no format bump. migration.md's format-8 line now names it.

**Late nested subscriber (D4).** The event hub remembers each child a run announces (`RunContext.childStarted`, which sends `TaskStarted`) until the call's runner returns. It also forgets them when the run's claim is released. A `subscribe(..., nested = true)` attaching meanwhile is given that `TaskStarted` and then one `Nested(child, LiveGap(0))`, under the hub lock, ahead of the child's further events.

**Settled-child window (D4, spec update).** The hub keeps a child until its call's `TaskEnded` is handed over (token-matched) or the run releases the thread, so a late nested subscriber attaching after the child settled but before the call commits gets `TaskStarted`, the gap, then `TaskEnded` (NestedStreamSpec).

**Retention at a Blocked parent (K1, spec update).** The fenced terminal retention pass also runs once a blocked run's closing checkpoint is stored; never at a failure (ChildThreadSpec: a Blocked parent keeps only `childRetention`).

Tests (written first, failed before the fix):
- `DeletingMarkerBehaviours` on in-memory and SQLite: an injected failure after the first child delete leaves the root refusing all five admissions, in the same runtime and after a restart, and a second `deleteThread` finishes it. A delete with no children writes no marker.
- `NestedStreamSpec`: a subscription attached mid-child gets `TaskStarted`, then `Nested(child, LiveGap(0))`, then the child's text. A subscription made before the child starts gets no gap.

`agent/test` and `agentCheckpointSqlite/test` pass locally. Design records 4.41 and 4.47 are amended. There's no CHANGELOG entry because both slices are unreleased.

Closes #2074

Before: the health check covered only the pm2 apps. The personal site, a Next.js app on port 3001 that pm2 doesn't manage, wasn't checked at all.

After: the check also confirms that port 3001 answers on the server and that https://tmcdonald.ca loads from outside, and it prints the server's hostname and IPs at the top of the report. If the site is down, the run fails.

How: `3001` joins the localhost port loop, a `hostname`/`hostname -I` block is added, and there's a new runner-side step that curls the public site. Everything stays read-only.

Tested on this branch with a manual run, which passed. Port 3001 returned 200, and https://tmcdonald.ca returned 200 in 0.49s from the runner.

Merging redeploys JobOS once.

author: zac-kyoti
body:
Thank you for merging #779. This follow-up moves BLACKPYRAMIDS_303's pin from `7d9e121` to `5af46f8` for one fix found on the unit.

## The fix

On the octabam form from #779, switching a BLKPYRAMD track to another machine (STATIC, FLEX, …) and back reset BLKPYRAMD's knobs to their defaults. Every stock machine keeps its own.

- **Cause:** while the track is BLKPYRAMD, the knobs live in FLEX's bytes, where the page editor and the renderer read them. On leaving, FLEX's own values went back and nothing kept BLKPYRAMD's.
- **The fix:** on leaving, the eleven knobs are kept in NEIGHBOR's twelve unused bytes (a mark, then one value a byte, each ≤ 127 for stock's validator). Coming back takes them from there. A track with no mark gets the defaults, as before.
- **A related bug, also fixed:** on another machine's track, SRC SETUP's BLKPYRAMD row edited FLEX's SETUP bytes. It now shows and edits the kept values.
- **Unchanged:** a stock OS still opens the project with the track as FLEX.

The runtime grows from 31,512 B to 32,364 B. `reference` is updated in the author's manifest, and the build still compares the linked unit with it byte for byte. Detours, pokes and the DSP words are unchanged.

## Changes here

- **Submodule pin:** `modules/blackpyramids-303/upstream` `7d9e121` → `5af46f8`.
- **`THIRD_PARTY.md`:** the pin on the Zac-Kyoti row (the mount count is unchanged).
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** an Unreleased entry.
- **The module's `README.md` and manifest:**
  - the pin;
  - the runtime size;
  - the hardware record and `proof_note`: this octabam form is now flashed.
- **`docs/site/usage/blackpyramids-303.md`:** one note on knobs kept across machine changes.
- **`README.md`:** regenerated (`make docs`, the proof column).

## Hardware

This octabam form (`remixes/test/blackpyramids-303`) on the author's MKI, 19 Oct 2026:
- **Before the fix:** the #779 build worked well, except for the reset above.
- **With the fix:** every check passes:
  - the knobs are kept away and back, on both pages;
  - they are kept after a save and a power cycle;
  - the other machine's settings are untouched;
  - SRC SETUP's BLKPYRAMD row edits the kept values.

The flashed image's MAIN OS is byte-identical to `make bus REMIX=test/blackpyramids-303` on this branch (`26a1c285…`).

## Measured

The author's emulator check (`tools/ot303/verify_ot303.py` upstream) gains four cases:
- STATIC → BLKPYRAMD, WAVE turned, → STATIC → BLKPYRAMD;
- all eleven knobs set, → FLEX → back;
- the row edited on a STATIC track;
- the FLEX round trip, now expecting the defaults kept in NEIGHBOR's bytes and every other Part byte as stock.

Result: ALL GOOD on this image, with the voice, the sequencer and the reverbs as before.

## Gates

On `70e78920` (current main), with pin `5af46f8`:
- `make docs` (README regenerated), `make verify-docs`: 67 modules, 80 remixes, 0 problems.
- `mkdocs build --strict --config-file docs/site/mkdocs.yml`: pass.
- `scripts/refhash.sh check`: ALL 24 CASES BIT-IDENTICAL.
- `make reach RUN=1 KEEP=1 TESTS=1`: every gate passed (`make emu-get`, `verify_docs`, `make check-shared` for blackpyramids-303 and octabam-core, `check_shards`).
- `make bus REMIX=test/blackpyramids-303`: the runtime matches the author's build at 0x40a955e0 (32,364 B); the image is the one flashed.

author: maureranton
body:
Ports the pure logic behind streaming tool-call rendering:

* `ui/chat/message/StreamingJsonDocument.kt` — prefix-aware JSON parser (zero imports)
* `ui/chat/message/StreamingToolArgumentHints.kt` — bounded tool-card hints + subject normalization (zero imports)

Both compile **verbatim** in the golden stand. `ToolKind` is lifted declaration-for-declaration by `extract_tool_kind.py` because `ToolPresentation.kt` drags kotlinx.serialization and ChatMessage along; the enum is regenerated before every compile and never retyped.

## Port

`agora::core::streaming_json` (`core/src/streaming_json.cpp`) keeps every cursor, `errorOffset`, length and slice in **UTF-16 code units**, like the JVM — `errorOffset` is a UI cursor into the UTF-16 argument string, and the 120-unit subject truncation counts units too. The document is parsed from `std::u16string` and converted to UTF-8 only at the `describe`/`Hints` boundary; `describe()` reproduces the Kotlin data-class `toString()` byte for byte.

## Stand

`core/tools/golden/streaming-json-document/` — 133 scenarios / 133 frozen traces (`PARITY OK` twice). Pinned: document statuses and exact error offsets, multi-root documents, open leaves with partial content, string escapes (including `\u` surrogate pairs), UTF-16 offset counting (`"🙂\q"` → 4, `"é\q"` → 3), JSON number grammar edges, every `ToolKind` hint branch, the 4096-unit prefix boundary (destination appears/disappears), and subject normalization (`\s+` = ASCII incl. vertical tab/form feed, Kotlin trim incl. NBSP, 120/121-unit edges with astral input).

Documented boundaries: ASCII `\u` hex digits and number-continuation digits (Kotlin routes them through Unicode-aware `Character.digit`/`Char.isDigit`; no JSON encoder emits exotic forms); `normalizeToolSummarySubject`'s `require(maxCharacters > 0)` precondition (app always passes a positive width); unpaired surrogates print `?` like the JVM encoder.

## Verification

* `core/tests/streaming_json_parity_test.cpp`; full suite **73 tests, 0 failures**.
* Negative controls: each plausible bug (control bytes accepted, CR not whitespace, leading-zero digits, consumed keyword mismatch, smaller prefix limit, missing read gate, truncation at exact max, JVM-only trim, dropped invalid status branch, dropped entry on bad colon, byte-based normalize length, count without complete array) makes the parity test fail.
